Tarutius.opening: a Roman proper name : L. Tarutius Firmanus, a celebrated astrologer, Cic. Div. 2, 47, 98 .

tasconĭum.opening: a white , clayey kind of earth , Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 69 .

Tasgetĭus.opening: a prince of the Carnutes , Caes. B. G. 5, 25 .

tăsis.opening: , = τάσις, a straining , tension , exertion : vocis = intentio, Mart. Cap. 9, 939 .

tăt.opening: interj. , an exlamation of surprise, what! strange! Tat! ecquis est? Plaut. Truc. 3, 1, 18 ; cf. tatae.

tăta.opening: Gr. τέττα; Sanscr. tātas, = papa . A name by which young children, speaking imperfectly, call their father, as with us, dad , daddy , Varr. ap. Non. 81, 5 ; Inscr. Orell. 2813 sq. ; 4943 .— A bringer up , rearer ,…

tatae.opening: interj. , an exclamation of surprise, so! the deuce! Sa. Fac tu hoc modo. St. At tu hoc modo. Sa. Babae! St. Tatae! Sa. Papae! St. Pax! Plaut. Stich. 5, 5, 31 ; cf. tat.

Tătĭus.opening: , T., a king of the Sabines , who afterwards reigned jointly with Romulus , Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 947 P. (Ann. v. 113 Vahl.); Cic. Rep. 2, 7, 13 ; Liv. 1, 10 sq. ; Prop. 4 (5), 2, 52 . — Hence, , , adj. , of Tatius :…

Tattaeus.opening: sal, the name of a marsh in Phrygia, Plin. 31, 7, 41, § 84 ; 31, 9, 45, § 99 .

tau.opening: the name of the Greek T, Aus. Idyll. Lit. Monos. 18 : et signa tau super frontes virorum gementium, Vulg. Ezech. 9, 4 (al. thau).

Taulantĭi.opening: a people of Illyria , Mel. 2, 3, 11 ; Plin. 3, 22, 26, § 144 ; Liv. 45, 26, 14 .—Hence, , , adj. , Taulantian : incola, Sil. 15, 294 ; Luc. 6, 16 .

Taum.opening: an arm of the sea in Britain , now the Firth of Tay , Tac. Agr. 22 .

Taunus.opening: a mountain range in Western Germany ( between Frankfort and Mayence ), now called Taunus , or the Höhe , Mel. 3, 3, 3 ; Tac. A. 1, 56 ; 12, 28 .

taura.opening: , = ταῦρα, a barren , hybrid cow , a free-martin , Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 6 ; Col. 6, 22, 1 ; cf. Fest. pp. 352 and 353.

taurĕus.opening: adj. taurus , of a bull or ox , of oxen , taurine (mostly poet. ). Adj. : vincla, i. e. taurean bands (a poet. expression to denote glue ), Lucr. 6, 1071 : terga, bulls ' hides , Verg. A. 9, 706 ; also, meton., for a…

Tauri.opening: the Taurians , a Thracian people , living in what is now Crimea , who sacrificed foreigners to Diana , Mel. 2, 1, 11 ; Cic. Rep. 3, 9, 15 ; Ov. P. 3, 2, 45 .— Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Taurians , Taurian…

taurĭcornis.opening: adj. taurus-cornu , bull-horned , tauricornous , an epithet of Jupiter, Prud. στεφ. 10, 222.

taurĭfer.opening: adj. taurusfero , bull-bearing , i. e. bearing , feeding , or supporting bulls : campi, Luc. 1, 473 .

taurĭformis.opening: adj. taurus-forma , bull-shaped , tauriform , an epithet of the river Aufidus, Hor. C. 4, 14, 25 .

taurĭgĕnus.opening: adj. taurus-gigno , bull-born , i. e. begotten by or proceeding from a bull , Att. ap. Macr. S. 6, 5 fin. (Trag. Fragm. v. 463 Rib.).

Taurĭi lūdi.opening: games at Rome in the Circus Flaminius, held in honor of the infernal gods , Varr. L. L. 5, § 154 Müll.; Liv. 39, 22 ; Fest. pp. 350 and 351 Müll.; Serv. Verg. A. 2, 140 .—Hence, Taurium aes, quod in ludos Taurios…

Taurīni.opening: a people of Northern Italy , near the modern Turin (Augusta Taurinorum), Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 123 ; Liv. 21, 38 sq. ; Tac. H. 2, 66 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Taurini , Taurine : saltus, Liv. 5, 34 :…

taurīnus.opening: adj. taurus , of or belonging to bulls or oxen , bull ' s- , taurine (mostly poet. ): vultus (Eridani), Verg. G. 4, 371 : frons, Ov. F. 6, 197 : gluten, Lucr. 6, 1069 : sanguis, Plin. 28, 9, 41, § 147 : fel, id. 28, 9,…

Tauris.opening: an island near Illyria , Auct. B. Alex. 45, 1 sq.

Taurisci.opening: an Alpine tribe in Pannonia , Plin. 3, 25, 28, § 148 ; 3, 19, 23, § 133 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Taurisci : gens, Plin. 3, 20, 24, § 134 .

Tauriscus.opening: the name of a Greek actor , Cic. de Or. 3, 59, 221 .

taurŏbŏlĭcus.opening: adj. taurobolium , of or belonging to a sacrifice of a bull (taurobolium): ARA, Inscr. Orell. 2328 .

taurŏbŏlīnus.opening: id. , one who has sacrificed a bull to Cybele , Inscr. Orell. 2353 .

taurŏbŏlĭor.opening: v. dep. n. [id.]. Lit. , to make a sacrifice of a bull (taurobolium; late Lat.): matris deum sacra accepit et tauroboliatus est, Lampr. Heliog. 7 ; Inscr. Orell. 2351 .— Transf. : TAVROBOLIATA PETRA, set up to…

taurŏbŏlĭum.opening: a sacrifice of a bull in honor of Cybele , Inscr. Orell. 1899 sq. ; 2322 sq.; 2130 al.

Taurŏīs.opening: , = Ταυρόεις, a fortress belonging to Marseilles , situated on the seashore in Gallia Narbonensis, now Tarento; acc. Tauroenta, Caes. B. C. 2, 4 : Tauroin, Mel. 2, 5, 3 .

Taurŏmĕnĭum.opening: ( ), , , a town in the eastern part of Sicily , now Taormina , Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 88 ; Cic. Att. 16, 11, 7 . — Called also , Ov. F. 4, 475 . — Hence, , (the o long in Sid. Carm. 9, 163 ), adj. , of or belonging to…

taurophthalmon.opening: , = ταυρόφθαλμον, the ox-eye , a kind of rosemary , App. Herb. 79 .

Taurŏpōlos.opening: an appellation of Diana , who, under this name, had a temple at Amphipolis, Liv. 44, 44, 4 Weissenb. ad loc.

Taurŭbŭlae.opening: an island near Naples , Stat. S. 3, 1, 129 .

taurŭlus.opening: dim. taurus , a little bull , Petr. 39 .

taurus.opening: = Gr. ταῦρος; Sanscr. sthūrus; Goth. stiur; Germ. Stier , a bull , bullock , ox , steer. Lit. , Varr. R. R. 2, 5 ; Col. 6, 20 ; Plin. 8, 45, 70, § 176 ; Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 66 ; Cic. Div. 2, 16, 36 sq. ; Caes. B. G. 6, 28…

Taurus.opening: a Roman proper name : M. Taurus, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1 .

tautŏlŏgĭa.opening: , = ταυτολογία, a repetition of the same meaning in different words , tautology , Mart. Cap. 5, § 535 ; Charis, p. 242 P.

tax.grammar: an onomatopee, expressing the sound of blows
tax.opening: , Engl. whack : tax tax tergo meo erit: non curo, my back will get whack, whack, Plaut. Pers. 2, 3, 12 (Ritschl reads tuxtax).

taxātĭo.opening: taxo , a rating , valuing , appraisal , estimation. In gen. (cf. aestimatio): ejus rei taxationem nos fecimus, Cic. Fragm. Or. pro Tull. 7: intra pecuniam versabitur taxatio, Sen. Ben. 3, 10, 2 : hoc super omnem…

taxātor.opening: id. , a reviler , taunter , abuser : scenici taxatores dicuntur, quod alter alterum maledictis tangit, Fest. s. v. taxat, p. 356 Müll.

taxĕa.opening: , the Gallic name for lard , Afran. ap. Isid. Orig. 20, 2, 24 (Com. Fragm. v. 284 Rib.); Arn. 7, 229 .

taxĕōta.opening: , = ταξεώτης, a magistrate ' s assistant , Cod. Just. 1, 3, 53 .

taxĕus.opening: adj. taxus , of the yewtree , of yew-trees : silva, Stat. S. 5, 5, 29 .

taxĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of the yewtree , yew : venenum, supposed by some of the ancients to be toxica, Plin. 16, 10, 20, § 51 .

Taxilae.opening: the name of a people in India , Plin. 6, 20, 23, § 78 .

taxillus.opening: acc. to Cic. Or. 45, 153, the primitive whence talus , a small die , Pompon. ap. Prisc. p. 615 P. (Com. Fragm. v. 190 Rib.); Vitr. 10, 8, 2 .

taxim.opening: adv. tango; lit. by touching; cf. sensim , gently , little by little , by degrees , gradually (ante - class.), Varr. ap. Non. 47, 27 ; 550, 18 ; Pompon. ib. 178, 20 (Com. Fragm. v. 23 Rib.); Lucil. ib. 169, 32 .

Taximagŭlus.opening: a king of Kent , Caes. B. G. 5, 22 .

taxo.opening: v. freq. a. tago, tango , to touch sharply , to feel , handle (post-Aug.; but cf. taxatio; syn.: tango, tracto). Lit. (very rare): taxare pressius crebriusque est quam tangere, unde procul dubio id inclinatum est, Gell.…

taxōnīnus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to a badger , badger. : adeps, Marc. Emp. 36 .

taxus.opening: a yew , yew-tree. Lit. , Plin. 16, 10, 20, § 50 ; Caes. B. G. 6, 31 ; Verg. E. 9, 30 ; id. G. 2, 113 al. — Considered, on account of its poisonous berries, as a tree of the infernal regions, Ov. M. 4, 432 ; Sil. 13, 596…

Tāўgĕtē.opening: , = Ταϋγέτη, a daughter of Atlas and Pleione , one of the Pleiades , Verg. G. 4, 232 ; Ov. M. 3, 595 ; id. F. 4, 174 ; Cic. Arat. 35 (269); Hyg. Fab. 155 .

Tāўgĕtus.opening: , = Ταΰγετον, a ridge of mountains in Laconia , Mel. 2, 3, 4 ; Plin. 2, 79, 81, § 191 ; Cic. Div. 1, 50, 112 ; Prop. 3, 14 (4, 13), 15; Luc. 5, 52 ; Claud. B. G. 193 ; called also , , , Verg. G. 2, 488 ; Stat. Achill.…

Tazata.opening: an island in the Caspian Sea , Plin. 6, 17, 19, § 52 .

tĕ.opening: , e. g. tute, tete; v tu.

Tĕānum.opening: the name of two Italian towns. Teanum Apulum, a town in Apulia , now Civitate , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 103 ; Cic. Att. 7, 12, 2 ; 7, 13 , b, 7; id. Clu. 9, 27 . — Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Teanum , Liv. 9, 20, 4 ;…

Tĕāte.opening: a town on the Adriatic Sea , near Corfinium , now Chieti , Sil. 8, 521 ; 17, 454 . — Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Teate , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 106 .

teba.opening: , an old Latin term, in Varro's time still used among the Sabines, signifying a hill : lingua prisca et in Graeciā Aeolis Boeotii sine afflatu vocant colles tebas: et in Sabinis, quo e Graeciā venerunt Pelasgi, etiam…

techna.opening: ( , Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 23 Lorenz ad loc.; id. Poen. 4, 1, 1 ), , , = τέχνη, a wile , trick , piece of craft or subtilty , artifice , cunning device (ante-class.): tum igitur ego deruncinatus, deartuatus sum miser Hujus…

technĭcus.opening: , = τεχνικός, a teacher of art , technologist , Quint. 2, 13, 15 .

Technŏpaegnĭon.opening: , = Τεχνοπαίγνιον (a game of art), the title of a poem by Ausonius.

Tē^cmessa.opening: a daughter of king Teuthras , and mistress of Ajax , the son of Telamon , Hor. C. 2, 4, 6 ; Ov. A. A. 3, 517 .

tēcŏlĭthos.opening: , = τηκόλιθος (stonedissolver), a stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 36, 19, 35, § 143 ; 37, 10, 68, § 184 ; Sol. 37 med.

tectē.opening: adv. , v. tego, P. a. fin.

tectĭo.opening: f [tego], a covering : limpidae lanae, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 5, 58 : lanarum, id. ib. 3, 21, 200 .

tectŏnĭcus.opening: adj. , = τεκτονικός, of or belonging to building , architectural , tectonic : formae, designs or plans of a building , Aus. Idyll. 10, 298 .

tector.opening: tego , one that overlays walls with plaster , stucco , etc., a plasterer , pargeter : villa tua, quam neque pictor neque tector vidit umquam, Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 9 ; Cic. Planc. 25, 62 ; Front. Aquaed. 117 ; Vitr. 7, 3…

tectōrĭŏlum.opening: dim. tectorium , a little plaster , parget , or rough-cast , Cic. Fam. 9, 22, 3 .

tectōrĭum.opening: , v. tectorius, I. B. and II. B.

tectōrĭus.opening: adj. tego , of or belonging to covering or to a cover. In gen. (very rare): paniculum, thatch, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 18 . — Hence, Subst. : , , , a covering , cover , Cato, R. R. 11, 2 . — In partic., that belongs to or…

Tectŏsăges.opening: a people in Gallia Narbonensis, between the Pyrenees and the Rhone , Mel. 2, 5, 2 ; Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 37 ; Caes. B. G. 6, 24 ; called also , , Liv. 38, 16 ; 16, 24 ; Aus. Clar. Urb. Narb. 9 .

tectŭlum.opening: dim. tectum , a little roof , Hier Ep. 117, n. 9.

tectum.opening: tego . Lit. , a covering. A roof : quojus (villae) Deturbavit ventus tectum ac tegulas, Plaut. Rud. prol. 78 : de tecto deturbavit tegulas, id. ib. 1, 1, 5 . tecta domorum, Lucr. 2, 191 ; Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 4, § 14 :…

tectūra.opening: tego , a covering over , overlaying with a wash, plaster, etc.: parietum, Pall. 1, 15 and 17.

tectus.opening: Part. and P. a. of tego.

tēcum.opening: , i. e. cum te; v. tu.

Tēdignĭlŏquĭdes.opening: te-dignaloquens , a comically-formed proper name , Plaut. Pers. 4, 6, 22 .

Tĕgĕa.opening: ( , Stat. Th. 11, 177 ), , = Τεγέα, a very ancient town in Arcadia , now Paleo - Episkopi , near Tripolitza , Mel. 2, 3, 5 ; Plin. 4, 6, 10, § 20 .— Poet. for Arcadia , Stat. Th. 11, 177 ; Claud. B. G. 576 .— Hence, or…

tĕgĕs.opening: tego , a covering , mat : quae fiunt de cannabi, lino, junco, palmā, scirpo, ut funes, restes, tegetes, Varr. R. R. 1, 22, 1 ; so Col. 5, 5, 15 ; 12, 52, 8 ; Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 112 ; Mart. 11, 32, 2 ; 11, 56, 5 ; Juv.…

tĕgĕtārĭus.opening: ψιαθοποιός, ψιαθοπλόκος, Gloss. Gr. Lat., a mat-maker [teges].

tĕgĕtĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little mat : tegeticulae cannabinae, Varr. R. R. 3, 8, 2 ; 2, 11, 8 ; Col. 8, 9, 3 ; Mart. 9, 93, 3 .

tĕgĭle.opening: tego , a covering , cover , App. M. 9 , p 222, 28 (al. tegillo).

tĕgillum.opening: dim. tegulum , a small covering , a hood or cowl , Plaut. Rud. 2, 7, 18 ; Varr. ap. Non. 179, 4 ; cf.: tegillum cuculiunculum ex scirpo factum, Fest. p. 366 Müll.

tĕgĭmen.opening: , and (in obliq. cas. usu. syncop. tegminis, etc.), tego , a covering , cover (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; in Cic. in prose only once, as a transl. from the Greek; syn.: operculum, integumentum): mihi…

tĕgo.opening: v. a. Gr. στέγω, to cover; τέγος, στέγος, roof; Sanscr. sthag-, to hide; Germ. decken; Engl thatch , to cover (syn. operio). Lit. In gen.: amica corpus ejus (Alcibiadis) texit suo pallio, Cic. Div 2, 69, 143 : capite se…

tēgŭlae.opening: (less freq. and mostly poet. , also in sing. : , ae; v. the foll. ), tego , tiles , roof-tiles , a tiled roof (class.; cf. imbrex). Plur. : tempestas venit, confringit tegulas imbricesque, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 28 ; so,…

tēgŭlĭcĭus.opening: adj. tegulae , covered with tiles : ATTEGIA, Inscr. Orell. 1396 .

tĕgŭlum.opening: tego , a covering , roof , thatch (very rare): tegulo aquaticarum harundinum domos suas operiunt, Plin. 16, 36, 64, § 156 : scirpi fragiles ad tegulum tegetesque, id. 16, 37, 70, § 178 .

tĕgŭmentum.opening: (collat. forms and ), , tego , a covering , cover. Lit. (class.; cf. tegmen): tegumenta corporum vel texta vel suta, Cic. N. D. 2, 60, 150 ; so, tegumentum, id. Fin. 5, 11, 32 ; Liv. 1, 43, 2 ; 9, 19, 7 ; 9, 40, 3 ; 22,…

tēla.opening: prob. contr. from texia, from texo; cf. ala, from axilla; mala, from maxilla, Cic. Or. 45, 153 , a web. Lit. : texentem telam studiose ipsam offendimus, Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 44 : Penelope telam retexens, Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 95…

tĕlămo.opening: or , , , = τελαμών (a bearer, supporter); in architecture, a male figure that supports an entablature; in the plur. : telamones, Vitr. 6, 10 fin.

Tĕlămo.opening: or , , , = Τελαμών, an Argonaut , son of Æacus , brother of Peleus , and father of Ajax and Teucer , Hyg. Fab. 14 ; 89 ; 97 ; Val. Fl. 1, 354 ; Ov. M. 7, 476 sq. ; 11, 216 sq.; Cic. N. D. 3, 32, 79 ; id. Tusc. 3, 18, 39…

telānae fīcus.opening: a kind of black fig , Cato, R. R. 8, 1 ; Plin. 15, 18, 19, § 72 ; Macr. S. 2, 16 .

Telchīnes.opening: , = Τελχῖνες, a fabled family of priests in Rhodes , famous for their magic arts , Ov. M. 7, 365 ; Stat. Th. 2, 274 .

Tēlĕbŏae.opening: , = Τηλεβόαι, a people in Acarnania , noted for robbing travellers , Plaut. Am. prol. 101 ; 1, 1, 56 ; 1, 1, 95 al. A colony of them afterwards inhabited the island of Capreae: Teleboūm Capreas regna, Verg. A. 7, 735 ;…

Tēlĕbŏas.opening: a centaur killed by Nestor at the marriage of Pirithous , Ov. M. 12, 441 .

Tēlĕgŏnus.opening: , = Τηλέγονος, son of Ulysses and Circe , who , when he came to Ithaca , killed his father without knowing him; on his return he founded Tusculum , Hyg. Fab. 127 ; Hor. C. 3, 29, 8 ; Prop. 2, 32 (3, 30), 4; Ov. F. 3, 92…

Tēlĕmăchus.opening: , = Τηλέμαχος, the son of Ulysses and Penelope , Hyg. Fab. 127 ; Ov. H. 1, 98 ; 1, 107 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 40 ; Cat. 61, 229 .

Tēlĕmus.opening: , = Τήλεμος, the name of a soothsayer , Ov. M. 13, 770 ; Hyg. Fab. 128 .

tēlĕphĭon.opening: , = τηλέφιον, a kind of herb resembling purslane : Sedum telephium, Linn.; Plin. 27, 13, 110, § 137 .

Tēlĕphus.opening: ( ), , , = Τήλεφος. A king of Mysia , son of Hercules and the nymph Auge. He was wounded before Troy by the spear of Achilles, but was afterwards oured by its rust, Ov. M. 12, 112 ; 13, 171 ; id. Tr. 5, 2, 15 ; Hor. A.…

Tĕlĕsĭa.opening: a town of Samnium , now the village Telese , Liv. 22, 13 ; 24, 20 .

Tĕlestes.opening: the father of Ianthe , Ov. M. 9, 716 .

tĕlĕta.opening: , = τελετή, initiation , consecration , App. M. 11, p. 268 sq. ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 10, 9; 10, 23; 4, 31.

Tĕlethrius.opening: a grassy mountain of Eubœa , Plin. 25, 8, 53, § 94 .

Tĕlĕthūsa.opening: the wife of Ligdus and mother of Iphis , Ov. M. 9, 682 sq.

tĕlĕtus.opening: , = τελετός (perfect), one of the Æons , Tert. adv Val. 8.

telicardĭos.opening: or , , , a precious stone , called also muchula, otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 68, § 183 .

tēlĭger.opening: adj. telumgero , dart - bearing , an epithet of Cupid, Sen. Herc. Oet. 543 .

tēlĭnum.opening: , = τήλινον, a costly ointment prepared from the herb telis, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 13 ; Tert. Pall. 4 med.

telirrhizos.opening: or , , , a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 68, § 183 .

tēlis.opening: , = τῆλις, the herb fenugreek Trigonella foenum Graecum, Linn.: foenum Graecum quod telin vocant, Plin. 24, 19, 120, § 184 .

Tellēna.opening: a town of Latium , now Toretta , Liv. 1, 33 ; called also , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 68 (Sillig).

Tellūmo.opening: a god among the Romans , the personified productive power of the earth , answering to Tellus as a goddess, Varr. ap. Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 23 fin. — Called also , , Mart. Cap. 1, § 49 .

tellūs.opening: (-ŭs short, Mart. Cap. 5, § 584 ), , perh. root tollo, to bear , the earth , opp. to the other planets or to the sea, the globe (a word belonging almost entirely to poetry). Lit. In gen.: ea, quae est media et nona,…

telluster.opening: adj. tellus , of or belonging to the earth , terrestrial : tellustres silvicolaeque divi, Mart. Cap. 7, § 729 .

Telmessus.opening: , or , , , = Τελμησσος or Τελμισσός, a town in Lycia , near to Caria , at the head of the Glaucus Sinus , now Makri; it was famed for the skill of its inhabitants in divination, Cic. Div. 1, 41, 91 ; Mel. 1, 15, 3 ;…

tĕlōnārĭus.opening: telonium , a tollgatherer , collector of the customs , Cod. Th. 11, 28, 3 fin.

tĕlōnĭum.opening: ( ), , , = τελώνιον, a toll-booth , custom-house , Tert. Idol. 12 ; id. Bapt. 12 ; Vulg. Luc. 5, 27 .

tēlum.opening: for texlum; root τεκ-, of τίκτω, to beget; τυκ-, τυχ-, of τυγχάνω, to hit, chance upon; v. texo; cf. τόξον, a bow , a weapon used for fighting at a distance; a missile weapon , missile , as a dart , spear , javelin ,…

Temarunda.opening: a Scythian name of the Palus Mæotis , Plin. 6, 7, 7, § 20 .

Tĕmĕnītis.opening: , = Τεμενῖτις (Polyb. c. 27, 7): porta, a gate of Tarentum, Liv. 25, 9, 9 (v Weissenb. ad loc.).

Tĕmĕnos.opening: , = τέμενος, τό, a place at Syracuse sacred to Apollo; hence, , , , = Τεμενίτης, an epithet of Apollo , Cic. Verr 2, 4, 53, § 119 ; Suet. Tib. 74 . — , , = Τεμενῖτις, a fountain at Syracuse , Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 89 .

tĕmĕrārĭus.opening: adj. temere . That happens by chance , accidental , casual (so very rare; cf. fortuitus): sed quid hoc, quod picus ulmum tundit? hau temerarium'st, Plaut. As. 2, 1, 14 : non temerarium est, ubi dives blande appellat…

tĕmĕrātor.opening: id. , a violator , ravisher (post-Aug.), Stat. Th. 11, 12 ; id. Achill. 1, 600 ; Cod. Just. 12, 53, 2 .— A forger , Dig. 48, 10, 29 .

tĕmĕrē.opening: (ante-class. collat. form , Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 1010 p.; Att. ap. Non. 516, 5 ; Trag. Fragm. v. 96 Rib.), adv. Sanscr. tamra, darkening; timira, dark; hence, blindly; cf.: timor, temeritas , by chance , by accident , at…

tĕmĕrĭtas.opening: f [temere]. Hap. chance , accident (so rare but class., cf.: fortuna. casus): in quibus nulla temeritas, sed ordo apparet, Cic. N. D. 2, 32, 82 quid enim sors est? Idem propemodum, quod micare, quod talos jacere, quod…

tĕmĕrĭtūdo.opening: temere , rashness , heedlessness , temerity (ante-class. for temeritas), Pac. ap. Non. 181, 23 (Trag. Rel. v. 149 Rib.).

testĭcŭlus.opening: dim. 2. testis , a testicle. Lit. , Auct. Her. 3, 20, 33 ; Juv. 6, 339 ; Mart. 3, 24, 5 ; Cels. 7, 18 .— Transf. , as a designation of manly vigor , manliness : haec fierent, si testiculi vena ulla paterni Viveret in…

testĭfĭcātĭo.opening: testificor , a bearing witness , giving testimony , testifying , testification (Ciceron.; whereas testatio is found in the jurists and in Quint.; v. testatio, I.). Lit. : si ejus rei testificatio tolleretur, Cic. Verr.…

testĭfĭcor.opening: v. dep. a. [1. testisfacio].— To bear witness , give evidence , attest , testify (class.; esp. freq. in Cic.; cf. testor). Lit. : haec cum maxime testificaretur, in vincula conjectus est, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 7, § 17 .—With…

testĭmōnĭālis.opening: adj. testimonium , of , belonging to , or serving for evidence , testimonial (late Lat.). Adj. : comparatio, Tert. adv. Psych. 16 fin. — Subst. : , , (sc. litterae), testimonials , Cod. Th. 7, 20, 12; 7, 21, 4; Veg.…

testĭmōnĭum.opening: testor , witness , evidence , attestation , testimony (oral or written): qui falsas lites falsis testimoniis Petunt, Plaut. Rud. prol. 13 : testimonii dictio, Ter. Phorm. 2, 1, 63 : quorum egregiam fuisse virtutem…

testis.opening: a testicle , Plaut. Mil. 5, 28 ; 5, 33 : dexter asini testis in vino potus, Plin. 28, 19, 80, § 261 : testes pecori ad crura decidui, id. 11, 49, 110, § 263 ; so in plur. , Lucil. ap. Non. 235, 5 ; Hor. S. 1, 2, 45 .—In…

testĭtrăhus.opening: adj. 2. testistraho , that drags his testicles : aries, Laber. ap. Tert. Pall. 1 (Com. Rel. xx. Rib.).

testor.opening: v. a. 1. testis . To be a witness , speak as witness , to bear witness , give evidence , depose , testify , attest any thing. Lit. (very rare, and not in Cic.; cf. testificor): confiteor: testere licet: signate…

testu.opening: or , , testa , a vessel or lid which was placed over food, etc., to be cooked, and then covered with hot coals, usually of earthenware. Lit. : in foco caldo sub testu coquito leniter, Cato, R. R. 75 : sub testu, id. ib.…

testŭātĭum.opening: testu , a cake baked in an earthen cup , cup-cake , Varr. L. L. 5, § 106 Müll.

testūdĭnĕātus.opening: and , , adj. testudo, II. B. , arched , vaulted : tectum, Col. 12, 15 ; Vitr. 2, 1 med. : cavaedium, id. 6, 3 .

testūdĭnĕus.opening: adj. testudo, I. and-II. , of or belonging to a tortoise; made of tortoise-shell : gradus, a tortoise-pace , snail ' s pace , Plaut. Aul. 1, 1, 10 : lyra, made of or overlaid with tortoise-shell , Prop. 4 (5), 6, 32 ;…

testūdo.opening: testa , a tortoise. Lit. , Pac. ap. Cic. Div. 2, 64, 133 ; Plin. 9, 10, 12, § 35 ; 32, 4, 14, § 32 ; Cic. N. D. 2, 48, 124 ; 2, 52, 129 ; Liv. 36, 32, 6 ; Sen. Ep. 121, 9 ; Phaedr. 2, 6, 5 al. —Prov.: testudo volat, of…

testŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small potsherd. Lit. , Col. 11, 3, 3 .— Transf. An earthen lamp , Ser. ap. Diom. p. 511 P. — A voting-tablet used by the Athenians , Nep. Arist. 1, 2 (cf. testa, II. C.).

teta.opening: a kind of dove : columbae, quas vulgus tetas vocat, Serv. Verg. E. 1, 58 .

tĕtănĭcus.opening: , = τετανικός, one affected with tetanus (cramp in the neck), Plin. 20, 22, 87, § 239 ; 26, 12, 81, § 130 ; 32, 10, 41, § 120 .

tĕtănōthrum.opening: , = τετάνωθρον, a cosmetic for removing wrinkles (pure Lat. tentipellium), Plin. 32, 7, 24, § 73 (dub.; Jahn, et tetanis).

tĕtănus.opening: , = τέτανος, a stiffness or spasm of the neck , tetanus , Plin. 23, 1, 24, § 48 ; 31, 10, 46, § 122 ; Scrib. Comp. 101 (in Cels. 4, 3 , written as Greek).

tĕtartēmŏrĭa.opening: , = τεταρτημοπία, a fourth in music, Mart. Cap. 9 , §§ 930 and 959.

tĕtartēmŏrĭon.opening: , = τεταρτημόριον, a fourth of the zodiac, Plin. 7, 49, 50, § 160 ; Hyg. Limit. p. 173 Goes.

tĕthălassōmĕnon.opening: (sc. vinum), = τεθαλασσωμένον, wine mixed with sea-water , Plin. 14, 8, 10, § 78 .

Tēthys.opening: , = Τηθύς, a sea-goddess , wife of Oceanus , and mother of the seanymphs and river - gods; acc. Tethyn, Ov. F. 5, 81 : Tethyos neptes, id. ib. 5, 168 ; Verg. G. 1, 31 ; Cat. 64, 29 ; 66, 70 .— Transf. , the sea , Ov. M.…

tē^trăchordos.opening: adj. , = τετράχορδος, ον, having four strings or notes. Adj. : machina, a water-organ, Vitr. 10, 13 . — Subst. ( ), , , a chord of four notes , a tetrachord. Lit. , Vitr. 5, 4 ; Mart. Cap. 9 , §§ 935 and 941; Macr. S.…

tē^trăcōlon.opening: , = τετράκωλον, a period consisting of four members , Sen. Contr. 4, 25 fin. ; 5 praef. med.

tē^trădĭum.opening: , = τετράδιον, the number four , a quaternion , tetrad , Col. 3, 20, 3 ; Sen. Contr. 5 praef.

tē^trădōros.opening: adj. , = τετράδωρος, ον, of four palms or hand-breadths , Plin. 35, 14, 49, § 170 ; Vitr. 2, 3 .

tē^trădrachmum.opening: and , , , = τετράδραχμον, a silver coin of four drachmas among the Greeks, Cass. ap. Cic. Fam. 12, 13, 4 .—Form tetrachmum, Liv 34, 52, 6; 37, 58, 4; 37, 46, 3; 39, 7, 1 Weissenb.

tē^trăgnăthĭus.opening: , = τετράγναθος (having four jaws), a kind of poisonous spider , Plin. 29, 4, 27, § 87 .

Tetragŏnis.opening: a town in Asia , near the Caucasus , Plin. 6, 24, 25, § 92 .

tē^trăgōnum.opening: , = τετράγωνον, a quadrangle , tetragon , Aus. Ecl. de Ratione Puerp. 21 and fin. ; Mart. Cap. 6, § 712 .

tē^trălix.opening: , = τετράλιξ, a plant , heath , = erice, sisara, Plin. 11, 16, 15, § 42 (al. tetradice); 21, 16, 56, § 95.

tē^trămĕtrus.opening: , = τετράμετρος, a verse of four metrical feet , a tetrameter , Ter. Maur. p. 2430 P.; Diom. p. 506 ib. al.

tē^trans.opening: ( gen. plur. , heterocl., tetrantorum, Vitr. 3, 3 med. ), , = τετρᾶς. A fourth part , a quarter : columnarum, Vitr. 4, 2 ; 4, 3 : circini, a quadrant, id. 10, 11 .— Among surveyors, the place where two lines meet , Hyg.…

tē^trăo.opening: , = τετράων, a heath-cock , moor-fowl , Plin. 10, 22, 29, § 56 ; Suet. Calig. 22 med. ; Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 13 fin.

tē^trăpharmăcum.opening: , = τετραφάρμακον. A plaster composed of four ingredients , Veg. Vet. 4, 28 med. (in Cels. 5, 19, 9 ; 5, 26, 35 , and Scrib. Comp. 211 , written as Greek).— A mess of four kinds of food , Spart. Hadr. 21 ; Ael. Ver. 5;…

tē^trăphŏros.opening: adj. , = τετράφορος, of four bearers : tetraphori phalangarii, four bearers carrying any thing together , Vitr 10, 8, 7.

Tē^traphȳlĭa.opening: a town of Athamania in Epirus , Liv. 38, 1 .

tē^trăplăsĭus.opening: adj. , = τετραπλάσιος, fourfold : ratio, Mart. Cap. 9, § 953 .

tē^traptōta.opening: , = τετράπτωτα, words which occur in only four cases , tetraptotes , Diom. 1 ; Prisc. 5 ; Isid. 1, 6, 43 .

Tē^trăpūs.opening: , = τετράπους (four-footed), the title of the eighth book of Apicius , which treats of the dishes prepared from quadrupeds.

tē^trarches.opening: , = τετράρχης, a ruler who governed the fourth part of a country , a tetrarch; in gen., the title of a petty prince , Cic. Att. 2, 9, 1 ; id. Phil. 11 , 12, 31; id. Balb. 5, 13 ; id. Mil. 28, 76 ; id. Deiot. 9, 27 ;…

tē^trarchĭa.opening: , = τετραρχία, the dominions of a tetrarch , a tetrarchy , Cic. Deiot. 15, 42 ; id. Div. 1, 15, 27 ; Auct. B. Alex. 78, 3.

tē^tras.opening: , = τετράς, the number four , a quaternion , tetrad , Tert. adv. Val. 7 ; 8 ; Mart. Cap. 7, § 734 .

tē^trăsēmus.opening: adj. , = τετράσημος, of four syllables , quadrisyllabic : pes, a poetical foot of four syllables, Mart. Cap. 9, § 987 .

tē^trastĭchos.opening: adj. , = τετράστιχος, containing four rows or lines. Adj. : porticus, Treb. Gall. 18. — Subst. : , , , a poem of four verses , a tetrastich , Quint. 6, 3, 96 Spald. N. cr.; Mart. 7, 85, 1 .

tē^trastȳlos.opening: adj. , = τετράστυλος, having four columns. Adj. : frons loci, Vitr. 3, 2 : cava aedium, id. 6, 3 .— Subst. : , , , a building with four columns , a tetrastyle , Capitol. Gord. 32 ; Inscr. Orell. 2270 .

Tĕtrĭca.opening: a rocky mountain in the Sabine territory , abounding in wild goats , Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 5 ; Verg. A. 7, 713 ; called Tetrica rupes, Sil. 8, 419 .

tē^trinnĭo.opening: v. n. , to utter the natural cry of the duck, to quack , Auct. Carm. Philom. 22.

tettīgŏmētra.opening: , = τεττιγομήτρα, the larva or matrix of the cicada, Plin. 11, 26, 32, § 93 .

tettīgŏnĭa.opening: , = τεττιγόνια, a kind of small cicada , Plin. 11, 26, 32, § 92 .

Teucer.opening: ( nom. Teucrus, Verg. A. 3, 108 ; Lact. 1, 21, 1 ), , = Τεῦκρος. Son of Telamon , king of Salamis , and brother of Ajax , Hor. C. 1, 7, 21 ; 1, 7, 27 ; 1, 15, 24 ; 4, 9, 17; id. S. 2, 3, 204 ; Ov. M. 13, 157 ; 14, 698 ;…

teuchītes.opening: , = τευχίτης, a kind of fragrant rush , Plin. 21, 18, 72, § 120 .

Teucri.opening: , and , , v. Teucer, II. 1. and 2. b.

teucrĭon.opening: , = τεύκριον. A plant , the germander : Teucrium chamaedrys, Linn.; Plin. 24, 15, 80, § 130 (al. Teucria).— The herb spleenwort : Teucrium flavium, Linn.; Plin. 25, 5, 20, § 45 .—Called also , Plin. 26, 7, 19, § 35 .

Teuta.opening: a queen of Illyria , Plin. 34, 6, 11, § 24 . — Called also , Flor. 2, 5, 2 .

Teutāni.opening: a people of the Peloponnesus , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 50 .

Teutātes.opening: a deity of the Gauls , to whom human sacrifices were offered , Luc. 1, 445 ; Lact. 1, 21, 3 .

teuthălis.opening: , = τευθαλίς, a plant , called also sanguinaria and polygonos. Plin. 27, 12, 91, § 113 .

Teuthras.opening: , = Τεύθρας. A king of Mysia , father of Thespius , Hyg. Fab. 99 and 100.—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Teuthras; poet. for Mysian : Caicus, Ov. M. 2, 243 . — , , adj. , of or belonging to Teuthras : turba, the…

Teutoburgiensis.opening: adj. , of or belonging to the citadel of the Teutones : saltus, a forest of Western Germany in which Varus was defeated A. D. 9, Tac. A. 1, 60 .

Teutomatus.opening: a king of the Nitiobriges , Caes. B. G. 7, 31 ; 7, 46 .

Teutŏni.opening: (collat. form , , Caes. B. G. 7, 77 fin. ; Vell. 2, 12, 4 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 67 ; Eutr. 5, 1 sq. ), , the Teutons , a people of Germany , Mel. 3, 3, 4 ; 3, 6, 7 ; Cic. Imp. Pomp. 20, 60 ; Caes. B. G. 1, 33 ; Liv.…

Teutrĭa.opening: an island in the Ionian Sea , Plin. 3, 26, 30, § 151 .

texo.opening: ( inf. paragog. texier, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 69 ), , v. a. root tek-; Gr. ἔτεκον, τίκτω, to beget; Sanscr. takman, child; taksh, to make , to weave (class.; syn. neo). Lit. : texens telam, Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 44 : vestes,…

textĭlis.opening: adj. texo , woven , wrought , textile. Lit. (class.) Adj. : tegmen, Lucr. 5, 1350 : stragulum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 21, 61 : dona, Verg. A. 3, 485 : aurum, Plin. 33, 3, 19, § 63 ; Sen. Med. 372 : picturae, Lucr. 2, 35 ; cf.:…

textor.opening: texo , a weaver , Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 45 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 19, 13 ; Mart. 12, 59, 6 ; Juv. 9, 30 : textorum et textricum cibaria, Dig. 33, 9, 3, § 6 .

textōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to weaving , plaiting , or braiding , textorial (post-Aug. and very rare). Lit. : alvearia opere textorio salicibus connectentur, plaited work, Col. 9, 6, 1 .— Trop. : textorium, inquis, totum…

textrīcŭla.opening: dim. textrix , a little (female) weaver; in apposition: puellae, Arn. 5, 166 .

textrīnus.opening: , a. , adj. contr. from textorinus, from textor . Of or belonging to weaving , textrine. Adj. : ars, the art of weaving , Firm. Error. Prof. Relig. 17: opus, Vulg. Tob. 2, 19 . — More freq., Substt. , , (sc. opus),…

textrix.opening: textor , a female weaver , Mart. 4, 19, 1 ; Inscr. Rein. cl. 9, n. 77; Dig. 33, 9, 3, § 6 ; Tib. 2, 1, 65 ; App. M. 6, p. 181, 25 . — In apposition: anus, i. e. the Fates, App. M. 6, p. 180, 39 .

textūra.opening: texo , a web , texture (very rare). Lit. : aranearum, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 24 : Minervae, Prop. 4 (5), 5, 23. Sen. Ep. 121, 22 .— Transf. , a construction , structure : quam tenui constet texturā (animi natura), Lucr. 3,…

textus.opening: texo, I. B. , texture , tissue , structure ( poet. and in post - Aug. prose). Lit. : haec sunt tenuia textu, Lucr. 4, 728 : capiuntur purpurae parvulis rarique textu, Plin. 9, 37, 61, § 132 ; 18, 7, 10, § 60 .— Trop. ,…

Thabēna.opening: a city of Numidia , Auct. B. Afr 77; its inhabitants are called , , , id. ib. 77

Thabraca.opening: a city of Numidia on the coast of the Mediterranean , Mel. 1, 7, 1 ; Juv 10, 194, Plin. 5, 3, 2, § 22 .

Thāis.opening: , = Θαΐς, a celebrated courtesan of Athens , Prop. 2, 6, 3 ; 4 (5), 5, 43 ; Ov. A. A. 3, 604 ; id. R. Am. 383 sq. — Another at Rome , Mart. 3, 8 ; 4, 12 .— A courtesan in the Eunuchus of Terence , Ter. Eun. 1, 2, 11 ;…

Thala.opening: , = Θάλα, an important town of Numidia , Sall. J. 75, 1 sq. ; Tac. A. 3, 21 ; Flor. 3, 1 .

thălămēgus.opening: , = θαλαμηγός, a state-barge fitted up with cabins , Suet. Caes. 52 (called navis cubiculata, Sen. Ben. 7, 20, 3 ).

thălămus.opening: , = θάλαμος, an inner room , chamber , apartment ( poet. ). Lit In gen.: Pars secreta domus ... Tres habuit thalamos, quorum tu, Pandrose, dextrum, Aglauros laevum, medium possederat Herse, Ov. M. 2, 738 : ferreique…

Thălassa.opening: , = θάλασσα (the sea), the title of the ninth book of Apicius , which treats of sea-fish.

thălassēglē.opening: a plant , called also potamantis, Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 164 .

thălassĭcus.opening: adj. , = θαλασσικός, of or like the sea , sea-colored , sea-green : colos (pallioli), Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 43 ; cf. ornatus, id. ib. 4, 6, 67 ; v. thalassinus.

thălassĭnus.opening: adj. , = θαλάσσινος, sea-colored , sea-green : vestis, Lucr. 4, 1127 ; cf. thalassicus.

thălassĭon phȳcos.opening: , = θαλάσσιον φῦκος , archil or orchil (a sea-plant which produces a reddish dye): Lichen roccella, Linn.; Plin. 26, 10, 66, § 103 .

thălassītes.opening: , = θαλασσίτης, sea-wine , i. e. wine which has been ripened by sinking it in the sea , Plin. 14, 8, 10, § 78 .

thălassŏmĕli.opening: , = θαλασσόμελι, sea-water mixed with honey , used as a beverage, Plin. 31, 6, 35, § 68 ; Ser. Samm. 28, 537 .

Thăles.opening: ( gen. Thaletis, Mel. 1, 17 ; Juv 13, 184; dat. Thaleti, Val. Max. 4, 1 , ext. 7), , = Θαλῆς, a celebrated Greek philosopher of Miletus , one of the seven wise men , and founder of the Ionic sect , Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 3 ;…

Thălīa.opening: (written , acc. to Fest. p. 359 Müll., and Serv. Verg. E. 6, 2 ; so Rib.), , , = Θάλεια. One of the Muses; the Muse of Comedy , Verg. E. 6, 2 ; Ov. A. A. 1, 264 ; of Lyric poetry , Hor. C. 4, 6, 25 .— One of the Graces…

Thălĭarchus.opening: , = Θαλίαρχος, the name given by Horace to the friend to whom is addressed C. 1, 9.

Thalli.opening: a people on the Caspian Sea , Plin. 6, 5, 5, § 17 .

Thallumētus.opening: a slave of Atticus , Cic. Att. 5, 12, 2 .

thallus.opening: , = θαλλός, a green stalk , green bough : cepae, Col. 11, 3, 58 ; Pall. Febr. 24, 4 : Amyclaeus, perh. a myrtlebough , Verg. Cir. 376 ; Vulg. 2 Macc. 14, 4 .

Thalna.opening: a Roman surname of the Juventian gens, Liv. 39, 31 .

Thămўras.opening: a Thracian poet who entered into a contest with the Muses , and , being vanquished , was deprived of his eyes , Prop. 2, 22 (3, 15), 19; Ov. Am. 3, 7, 62 ; id. A. A. 3, 399 ; id. Ib. 274 ; Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 204…

thannum.opening: ( ), , , = θάμνος, a shrub , otherwise unknown, Col. 12, 7, 1 ; Tert. Anim. 32 .

Thapsăcus.opening: , = Θάψακος, a town of Syria , on the Euphrates , now El-Hammam , Plin. 5, 24, 21, § 87 .

thapsĭa.opening: , = θαψία, a poisonous shrub : Thapsia Asclepium, Linn.; Plin. 13, 22, 43, § 124 .—Called , Luc. 9, 919 .

Thapsus.opening: or , , , = Θάψος. A peninsula and city in Sicily , now Magnisi , Ov. F. 4, 477 ; Verg. A. 3, 689 ; Sil. 14, 206 .— A city in Africa Propria , famed for Cæsar ' s victory over the partisans of Pompey , now Baltah , Plin.…

Thăsus.opening: or , , , = Θάσος, an island in the north of the Ægean Sea , off the coast of Thrace , now Thaso , Mel. 2, 7, 8 ; Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 73 ; Cic. Pis. 36, 89 ; Auct. Her. 4, 54, 68 ; Liv 33, 30; 33, 35; Stat. S. 1, 5, 34 ;…

Thaumăci.opening: a people of Thessaly , now Dhomoko , Plin. 4, 9, 16, § 32 ; Liv. 32, 4, 1 ; 36, 14, 12 ; inhabiting the town called , ,

Thaumas.opening: , = Θαύμας, the father of Iris , Cic. N. D. 3, 20, 51 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Thaumas , Thaumantian : virgo, i. e. Iris, Ov. M. 14, 845 .— , , , daughter of Thaumas : Iris, Ov. M. 4, 480 ; called also…

theamēdes.opening: an Ethiopian stone that repels iron; acc. to some, the tourmaline , Plin. 36, 16, 25, § 130 .

theangelis.opening: a kind of plant growing on Libanus , Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 164 .

thĕātrālis.opening: adj. theatrum , of or belonging to the theatre , theatrical : theatrales gladiatoriique consessus, Cic. Sest. 54, 115 : operae, Tac. A. 1, 16 : lascivia populi, id. ib. 11, 13 : ad theatrales artes degeneravisse, id.…

thĕātrĭcus.opening: adj. , = θεατρικός, of or belonging to the theatre , theatric (late Lat. for the class. theatralis): nugae, Aug. Doctr. Chabr. 2, 18 : turpitudines, id. Civ. Dei, 6, 6: operarii, id. Mus. 2, 5 .

thĕātrum.opening: , = θέατρον, a playhouse , theatre (cf.: scena, spectaculum, ludus). Lit. : num theatrum, gymnasia, porticus, etc. ... rem publicam efficiebat? Cic. Rep. 3, 32, 44 : theatrum ut commune sit, id. Fin. 3, 20, 67 : castra…

Thēbae.opening: (collat. form , , Juv. 15, 6 ; Plin. 5, 9, 11, § 60 ), , = Θῆβαι (or Θήβη ), Thebes , the name of several cities of antiquity. —The most considerable were, The city of the hundred gates , in Upper Egypt , now Karnak ,…

Thēbāgĕnes.opening: (MSS. ), , adj. Thebae-gigno , born at Thebes : Ismenias, Varr. ap. Non. 172, 26 .

Thēbē.opening: a female name. A nymph , daughter of the river-god Asopus , Ov. Am. 3, 6, 33 .— Wife of the tyrant Alexander of Pheræ , Cic. Inv. 2, 49, 144 ; id. Off. 2, 7, 25 .

Thēbes.opening: a city in Samaria , Vulg. Judic. 9, 50 ; id. 2 Sam. 11, 21.

thēca.opening: , = θήκη, that in which any thing is enclosed , an envelope , hull , cover , case , sheath , etc. (syn. vagina): grani, Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 1 : efferri sine thecis vasa, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 23, § 52 ; id. Att. 4, 7, 2 ;…

thēcātus.opening: adj. theca , placed in a case or cover , encased : arcus, Sid. Ep. 1, 2 med.

Thelxĭnŏē.opening: one of the first four Muses , Cic. N. D. 3, 21, 54 .

thēlўgŏnon.opening: , = θηλυγόνον (producing females). A species of the plant phyllum, Plin. 26, 15, 91, § 162 .— A species of the Satyrion, Plin. 26, 10, 63, § 99 .— A species of the crataeogonos, Plin. 27, 8, 40, § 62 .

thēlўphŏnon.opening: , = θηλυφόνον, another name of the aconitum, Plin. 25, 10, 75, § 122 ; 27, 3, 2, § 9 .

thēlyptĕris.opening: , = θηλύπτερις, the female plant of the filix ( fern , polypody ), Plin. 27, 9, 55, § 78 .

thĕma.opening: , = θέμα. A subject or topic treated of , a theme (post-Aug.): Scholastici exempla cum dixerunt, volunt et illa ad aliquod controversiae thema redigere, Sen. Contr. 3, 20 fin. ; so id. ib. 3, 28 med. ; Quint. 4, 2, 28 ;…

Thĕmis.opening: , = Θέμις, the goddess of justice and of prophecy , Cat. 68, 153 ; Ov. M. 1, 321 ; 1, 379 ; 4, 643 ; 7, 762; 9, 403; 9, 419; Luc. 5, 81 ; Claud. Rapt. Pros. 1, 107 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 174 ; Schol. Juv. 1, 82 .— The…

Thĕmiscȳra.opening: , = Θεμίσκυρα, a town in Pontus , on the Thermodon , Plin. 6, 3, 4, § 10 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Themiscyra : luci, Amm. 22, 8, 14 .— , , adj. , the same, Plin. 6, 3, 3, § 9 ; 24, 17, 102, § 165 .

Thĕmĭson.opening: , = Θεμίσων, a celebrated physician of Laodicea in Syria , Juv. 10, 221 ; Cels. Praef. al.; Plin. 29, 1, 5, § 6 ; Sen. Ep. 95, 9 .

Thĕmista.opening: a female Epicurean philosopher of Lampsacus , Cic. Fin. 2, 21, 68 ; id. Pis. 26, 63 ; Lact. 3, 25, 15 .

thĕŏlŏgĭcus.opening: adj. , = θεολογικός, of or belonging to theology , theological : doctrina, Amm. 16, 5, 5 : metrum, heroic verse , Plot. 2629 P.

tintinnābŭlātus.opening: adj. tintinnabulum , belled , i. e. wearing a bell or bells : greges, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 .

tintinnābŭlum.opening: tintinno , a bell , signal-bell , e. g. on a door to summon the attendant, on the necks of cattle, etc., Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 162 ; id. Ps. 1, 3, 98 ; Suet. Aug. 91 ; Plin. 36, 13, 19, § 92 ; Juv. 6, 441 ; Mart. 14, 163…

tintinnācŭlus.opening: adj. id. , tinkling , clinking , clanking : educi ad tintinnaculos, i. e. to the manacled malefactors, Plaut. Truc. 4, 3, 8 Spengel ad loc. (acc. to others, the executioners who fastened the chains).

tintinno.opening: ( ), , and , , v. n. reduplicated from tinnio , to ring , clink , clank , to jingle , tingle (anteclass.): tintinnabant compedes, Naev. ap. Fest. p. 364 Müll.; Nigid. ap. Non. 40, 16 : tintinnire janitoris impedimenta…

tintinnum.opening: tintinno , a jingling , tinkling , Ven. Carm. 2, 20, 49.

tīnus.opening: a plant : Viburnum tinus, Linn.; Plin. 15, 30, 39, § 128 ; 17, 10, 11, § 60 : bacis caerula, Ov. M. 10, 98 .

tiphē.opening: , = τίφη, a kind of grain , acc. to Sprengel, Peter ' s-corn , one-grained wheat : Triticum monococcon, Linn.; Plin. 18, 8, 19, § 81 ; 18, 10, 20, § 93 .

tiphўon.opening: , = τίφυον, a kind of narcissus , Plin. 21, 11, 39, § 67 (dub.; Jahn, iphyon).

Tīphys.opening: ( voc. Tiphy), , = Τῖφυς, the pilot of the Argo , Verg. E. 4, 34 ; Ov. H. 6, 48 ; id. Tr. 4, 3, 77 ; id. P. 1, 4, 37 ; Poët. ap. Charis. p. 243 P.

tippŭla.opening: ( ), , , an insect that runs swiftly over the water , the water-spider , water - spinner , Varr. ap. Non. 180, 11 . — Transf. , of any very light object: neque tippulai leonis pondu'st quam fides lenonia, Plaut. Pers.…

Tirēnus pons.opening: a bridge at Minturnæ , Cic. Att. 16, 13 .

Tīrĕsĭas.opening: , = Τειρεσίας. A celebrated blind soothsayer of Thebes , Hyg. Fab. 68 ; 75 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 39, 115 ; id. Div. 1, 40, 88 ; 2, 3, 9 ; id. N. D. 2, 3, 7 ; Ov. M. 3, 323 ; 6, 157 ; Hor. S. 2, 5, 1 ; Stat. Th. 10, 589 .—…

Tīrĭdātes.opening: the name of several kings of Armenia , Hor. C. 1, 26, 5 ; Suet. Ner. 13 ; 30 ; Just. 42, 5 ; Tac. A. 6, 32 sqq.; Plin. 7, 39, 40, § 129 ; 30, 2, 6, § 16 .

tīro.opening: ; in milit. lang., a newly-levied soldier , a young soldier , recruit. Lit. : aetas tironum, Cic. Tusc. 2, 16, 38 : legio tironum, Caes. B. C. 3, 28 ; 3, 29 ; 3, 34 ; Auct. B. Afr. 31, 7; Suet. Tib. 42 ; id. Ner. 19 ;…

Tīro.opening: a Roman proper name. So esp., M. Tullius Tiro, the learned freedman of Cicero , Cic. Fam. 16, 10 ; id. Att. 6, 7, 2 ; 9, 17, 2 (to him are addressed the letters id. Fam. 16, 3 -10; 16, 12-15); Gell. 7, 3, 8 ; 13, 9, 1…

tīrōcĭnĭum.opening: tiro . Lit. In milit. lang., the first military service or first campaign of a young soldier , military rawness or inexperience , = rudimentum (perh. not ante-Aug.): juvenis, Liv. 39, 47, 3 : propter exercitūs…

tīrōnātus.opening: id. , the state or condition of a recruit (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 7, 13, 21.

tīruncŭlus.opening: dim. tiro , a young beginner , little tiro (post-Aug.): ut probarem tibi, quam vehementes haberent tirunculi impetus primos ad optima quaeque, Sen. Ep. 108, 23 : servitia sic tirunculum (vilicum) contemnunt ut senem,…

Tīryns.opening: , = Τίρυνς, a very ancient town in Argolis , where Hercules was brought up , Plin. 4, 5, 9, § 17 ; Stat. Th. 4, 147 ; Serv. Verg. A. 7, 662 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Tiryns , Tirynthian; and poet. , also,…

tis.opening: , i. e. tui, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 42 ; v. tu.

Tīsaeus.opening: , or , , , = Τισαῖον, a mountain of Thessaly , now Bardjora , Liv. 28, 5, 17 ; Val. Fl. 2, 7 .

Tīsăgŏras.opening: , = Τισαγόρας, a brother of Miltiades , Nep. Milt. 7, 5 .

Tīsămĕnus.opening: , = Τισαμενός, a son of Orestes , and king of Argos , Ov. Ib. 346 ; Hyg. Fab. 124 .

Tisanūsa.opening: a town and harbor of Caria , Plin. 5, 28, 29, § 104 ; Mel. 1, 16 .

Tīsĭas.opening: , = Τισίας, a Sicilian who wrote on oratory , Cic. Brut. 12, 46 ; id. Inv. 2, 2, 6 ; id. de Or. 1, 20 ; Quint. 2, 16, 3 ; 3, 1, 8 .

Tīsicrătes.opening: , = Τισικράτης, a sculptor of Sicyon , father of the painter Arcesilas , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 67 ; 35, 11, 40, § 146 .

Tīsĭphŏnē.opening: , = Τισιφόνη (avenger of murder), one of the Furies , Verg. A. 6, 571 ; 10, 761 ; Prop. 3, 5 (4, 4), 40; Ov. M. 4, 481 ; id. H. 2, 117 ; Hor. S. 1, 8, 34 ; Juv. 6, 29 ; Sen. Herc. Fur. 984 . — Hence, , , adj. , of or…

Tissē.opening: a little town in Sicily , now Randazzo , Sil. 14, 267 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Tisse , Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 38, § 86 ; for which: , Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 91 .

Tītan.opening: (collat. form , , v. in the foll. ), , = Τιτάν. Son of Cœlus and Vesta , elder brother of Saturn , and ancestor of the Titans , called or , who contended with Saturn for the sovereignty of heaven , and were , by the…

Tītānŏmăchĭa.opening: , = Τιτανομαχία, the battle with the Titans , Hyg. Fab. 150 in lemm.

Tithoës.opening: an Egyptian king , builder of the labyrinth , Plin. 36, 13, 19, § 84 .

Tīthōnus.opening: or , , , = Τιθωνός, son of Laomedon , consort of Aurora , and father of Memnon; endowed with immortality , and changed at last , after reaching a decrepit old age , into a cicada , Cic. Sen. 1, 3 ; Verg. A. 4, 585 ; Ov.…

tĭthўmălus.opening: ( ), , , = τιθύμαλος, a plant with a milklike sap , spurge (Euphorbia, Linn.), of many species, Plin. 26, 8, 39, § 62 ; App. Herb. 108 ; Ser. Samm. 46, 841 ; 64, 1106 .—A female species, called , , sea-spurge :…

tītillāmentum.opening: titillo , a tickling , for titillatio, Fulg. Myth. 2, 18 .

tītillātĭo.opening: id. , a tickling , titillation : voluptates, quibus quasi titillatic sensibus adhibetur, Cic. N. D. 1, 40, 113 : non est voluptatum tanta quasi titillatio in senibus, id. Sen. 14, 47 ; Hier. Ep. 52, 3 : corporis, Sen.…

tītillātus.opening: id. , a tickling , for titillatio, Plin. 11, 37, 77, § 198 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 6, 26 ; id. Tard. 2, 11, 129 .

tītillo.opening: v. a. , to tickle , titillate. Lit. : sensus, Lucr. 2, 429 : voluptas, quae quasi titillaret sensus, Cic. Fin. 1, 11, 39 ; cf. carnem, Tert. Pud. 22 med. : multitudinis levitatem voluptate quasi titillantes, Cic. Off.…

tītillus.opening: titillo , a tickling , for titillatio, Cod. Th. 8, 5, 2.

Tĭtĭnĭus.opening: ( ), , , a Roman comic poet of the ante-class. period; see the fragments of his writings in Com. Rel. pp. 115-137 Rib.; Varr. ap. Charis. p. 215 P.

tĭtĭo.opening: a burning brand , firebrand (syn.: taeda, fax), Varr. ap. Non. 182, 21 ; 302, 7 ; Cels. 2, 17 ; Hyg. Fab. 171 al. ; cf.: titionem vulgus appellat extractum foco torrem semiustum et exstinctum, Lact. 4, 14 med.

Tĭtĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; e. g. Sex. Titius, a tribune of the people , whose motions so much resembled dancing that a certain dance was named Titius after him , Cic. Brut. 62, 225 ; id. de Or. 2, 11, 48 .— Titius…

tītivillitĭum.opening: a very small trifle , a bagatelle : non ego istuc verbum empsitem (empsiculem, Müll.) titivillitio, Plaut. Cas. 2, 5, 39 ; cf. Fest. p. 366 Müll. N. cr. , and Fulg. Prisc. Serm. 562 .

tĭtŭbantĭa.opening: titubo , a staggering , wavering (very rare): linguae, i. e. stammering, Suet. Claud. 30 ; so too, oris, id. Vit. 6 ; cf. the foll. art., I.

tĭtŭbātĭo.opening: id. , a staggering , wavering. Lit. : in ipsā ebrietate, Sen. Ep. 95, 16 : linguae, i. e. stammering, Macr. S. 7, 6 med. ; cf. the preced. art.— Trop. : titubatio aut offensio, Auct. Her. 2, 8, 12 ; Cic. Inv. 2, 12, 41…

tĭtŭbo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
tĭtŭbo.opening: v. n. and a. , to stagger , totter , reel. Lit. (rare; cf.: vacillo, labo); of drunken persons: Silenus titubans annisque meroque, Ov. M. 11, 90 : mero somnoque gravis titubare videtur, id. ib. 3, 608 ; 4, 26; 15, 331;…

tĭtŭlo.opening: v. a. titulus , to give a title to , to call , name , entitle (postclass.): magos quoque Samaritanorum appellatione titulavit, Tert. adv. Jud. 9 med. ; id. Anim. 13 ; Carm. Judic. Dom. 2; Mart. Cap. 1, § 41 .

tĭtŭlus.opening: (collat. , : HOC TITVLVM, Inscr. Fabr. 8, 47 ; Inscr. Cardin. Dipl. 22), root ti- of τίνω, τιμάω , a superscription , inscription , label , litle; a ticket , bill , placard , notice that a thing is to be sold or let…

Titūrĭus.opening: a legate of Cæsar in the Gallic war , Caes. B. G. 5, 27 ; 5, 29 ; 5, 33 ; Suet. Caes. 25 . — Hence, , , adj. , of Titurius , Titurian : clades, Suet. Caes. 67 .

Titurnĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens, Cic. Fam. 13, 39 .

Tĭtўos.opening: , = Τιτυός, a giant , son of Jupiter , slain by Apollo with arrows for his attempt on the chastity of Latona; and , as a further punishment , as he lay in the infernal regions stretched out over a space of nine jugera,…

Tītўrus.opening: Lit. , the name of a shepherd in Virgil ' s Eclogues , Verg. E. 1 .— Transf. For a shepherd in gen., Verg. E. 8, 55 .— As a designation of Virgil ' s Eclogues , Ov. Am. 1, 15, 25 . — As a designation of Virgil himself,…

Titўus.opening: a river of Illyria , Plin. 3, 21, 25, § 139 ; Flor. 2, 5 .

Tlēpŏlĕmus.opening: , = Τληπόλεμος, a son of Hercules , leader of the Rhodians before Troy , Hyg. Fab. 81, 97 ; Ov. M. 12, 537 .

Tmărŏs.opening: or , , , a mountain in Epirus , Verg. E. 8, 44 .—Called also , Plin. 4, 2, 3, § 6 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Tmaros , Tmarian : Juppiter, Claud. B. Get. 18 .

tmēsis.opening: , = τμῆσις, in grammar, the separation of a word , tmesis (as, Saxo cere comminuit brum; v. cerebrum init. ), Serv. Verg. A. 1, 412 .

Tmōlus.opening: and , , , = Τμῶλος, a mountain of Lydia in which the Pactolus rises , producing excellent wines , now Kisilja Mousa Dagh , Plin. 5, 29, 30, § 110 ; Verg. G. 1, 56 ; Ov. M. 2, 217 ; 11, 151 sq.— Form Timolus, Ov. M. 6,…

tŏcŭlĭo.opening: or , , τόκος, usury , a usurer : neque te in toculionibus habebam, Cic. Att. 2, 1, 12 .

todi.opening: : todi genus avium parvarum. Plautus: cum todillis crusculis, Fest. pp. 352 and 353 Müll.

toecharchus.opening: , = τοίχαρχος, the commander of the rowers , Hyg. Fab. 14 fin.

tōfācĕus.opening: or , , adj. tofus , of tufa , tufaceous : argilla, Plin. 17, 7, 4, § 43 : lapis, Pall. Aug. 9, 2 .

tōfĭcĭus.opening: adj. id. , like tufa , tufaceous : lapides, Capitol. Max. 6 .

tōfīnus.opening: adj. id. , of tufa : metae (circi), Suet. Claud. 21 .

tōfōsus.opening: adj. id. , like tufa , tufaceous , porous : verruca umore, Sid. Ep. 3, 13 .

tŏga.opening: tego , a covering , garment. In gen. (ante-class. and rare): praeterea quod in lecto togas ante habebant; ante enim olim fuit commune vestimentum et diurnum et nocturnum et muliebre et virile, Varr. ap. Non. 541, 2 :…

tŏgātārĭus.opening: togatus , an actor in the Fabula togata, Suet. Aug. 45 (al. togatarum).

tŏgātŭlus.opening: dim. toga, II. B. 2. , a man of humble station , a little client , Mart. 10, 74, 3 ; 11, 24, 11 .

tŏgātus.opening: adj. toga , wearing the toga , clad in the toga , gowned : fovebit Romanos, rerum dominos, gentemque togatam, Verg. A. 1, 282 : ut togatus mandata senatus audiret, Liv. 3, 26, 9 .— Transf. , of a private station :…

tŏgŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little toga : togulae lictoribus praesto fuerunt, Cic. Pis. 23, 55 : picta, id. Att. 1, 18, 6 : trita quidem nobis togula est, Mart. 9, 101, 5 .

tŏlĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. tolero . Pass. , that may be borne , bearable , supportable , endurable , passable , tolerable (class.): amicitiae si tolerabiles erunt, ferendae sunt, Cic. Lael. 21, 78 : tolerabilis conditio servitutis, id. Cat.…

tŏlĕrans.opening: Part. and P. a. of tolero.

tŏlĕrantĭa.opening: tolero , a bearing , supporting , endurance (very rare): rerum humanarum, Cic. Par. 4, 1, 27 : pax vel incuriā vel tolerantiā priorum timebatur, Tac. Agr. 20 ; Sen. Ep. 67, 5 : doloris, Quint. 2, 20, 10 : malorum, id.…

tŏlĕrātĭo.opening: id. , a bearing , supporting , enduring : dolorum, Cic. Fin. 2, 29, 94 .

tŏlĕrātor.opening: tolero , one who endures (late Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 99, 11 .

tŏlĕrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of tolero.

tŏlĕro.opening: v. a. ( dep. collat. form , , acc. to Prisc. p. 800 P.) [lengthened form of the root tol, whence tollo and tuli, kindr. with the Gr. ΤΛΑΩ ], to bear , support , sustain (syn.: fero, patior, sustineo, sino). Lit. (rare…

Tolistobogii.opening: ( ), , , a people of Galatia , whose precise home is unknown , Liv. 38, 15, 15 (Weissenb. Tolostobogiorum); Plin. 5, 32, 42, § 146 ; Flor. 2, 11, 5 .

tollēno.opening: tollo , in mechanic. and milit. lang., a swing-beam , a swipe or swape , e. g. to raise a water-bucket from a well, or to raise a body of men to a level with the enemy's ramparts, Plin. 19, 4, 20, § 60 ; Plaut. Fragm.…

tollo.opening: v. a. ( perf. tollit, Pers. 4, 2 : tollisse, Dig. 46, 4, 13 ) [root Sanscr. tul-, tulajāmi, lift up, weigh; Gr. ταλ-, τελ, in τλῆναι, τάλαντον; cf.: tuli, tlātus (latus), tolerare], to lift or take up , to raise ,…

Tŏlōsa.opening: a city in Gallia Narbonensis, now Toulouse , Mel. 2, 5, 2 ; Caes. B. G. 3, 20 ; Cic. Font. 5, 9 ; Mart. 9, 100, 3 .— Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Tolosa , Tolosan : aurum, plundered by the consul Q. Servilius…

Tŏlumnĭus.opening: A king of the Veientes , Liv. 4, 17 .— A Rutulian soothsayer , Verg. A. 11, 429 ; 12, 258 .

tŏlūtārĭus.opening: adj. tolutim , going on a trot , trotting : equus, Sen. Ep. 87, 9 .— Collat. form , , in the trop. sense: sententiae tolutares, Front. Or. 1 .

tŏlūtĭlis.opening: adj. id. , going on a trot , trotting : gradu vectus, Varr. ap. Non. 17, 26 .

tŏlūtĭlŏquentĭa.opening: tolutim-loquor , a talking on a trot , volubility : o pestifera . . . trux tolutiloquentia, Nov. ap. Nen. 4, 7 (Com. Rel. p. 220 Rib.).

tŏlūtim.opening: adv. from the root tol, whence tollo, tolero, tŭli; Gr. ΤΛΑΩ; prop. lifting up the feet; hence, pregn. , on a trot , full trot (mostly ante - class.): cedit citu', celsu' tolutim, Varr. ap. Non. 4, 20 ; so of horses,…

tŏmācĭna.opening: τομή, a cutting up , a kind of sausage , Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 10 ; cf. tomaculum.

tŏmācŭlum.opening: , contr., , , τομή, a cutting in pieces , a kind of sausage , probably similar to our brain- or liver-sausage , Juv. 10, 355 ; Mart. 1, 42, 9 ; Petr. 31 fin. ; 39 fin. ; v. the preced. art., and cf. Becker, Gallus, 3,…

tŏmē.opening: , = τομή, a cut , separation; in metre, the cæsura , Ter. Maur. p. 2440 P.; Aus. Ep. 4, 90 .

tōmentum.opening: a stuffing for cushions (e. g. of wool. hair, feathers, straw, etc.), cushioning , Plin. 8, 48, 73, § 192 ; 19, 1, 2, § 13 ; 27, 10, 61, § 88 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 167 Müll.; Suet. Tib. 54 ; Tac. A. 6, 23 med. ; Mart. 14,…

Tŏmis.opening: , or , , , = Τόμις or Τόμοι, a town of Mœsia , on the Pontus Euxinus , famous as the place to which Ovid was banished. —Form Tomis, Ov. P. 4, 14, 59 ; id. Tr. 3, 9, 33 .—Form , , Stat. S. 1, 2, 254 ; Claud. Epith. Pall.…

tŏmus.opening: , = τόμος. In gen., a cut , piece , bit : vilis, a cheap piece , i. e. roll of paper , Mart. 1, 67, 3 . — In partic. A part , book , tome of a larger work: feci excerpta ex libris sexaginta in quinque tomis, M. Aurel.…

Tŏmўris.opening: , = Τόμυπις, a Scythian queen , by whom the elder Cyrus was defeated and slain , Just. 1, 8 ; Tib. 4, 1, 143 ; Val. Max. 9, 10 , ext. 1.—Called also or , Front. Strat. 2, 5 ; and , Val. Max. 9, 10 .

tondĕo.opening: (collat. form acc. to the third conj.: OVES TONDVNTVR, Calend. ap. Grut. 138), v. a. for tomdeo; root in Gr. τέμνω, to cut , to shear , clip , crop , to shave , etc. Lit. : barbam et capillum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 58 ; so,…

tŏnesco.opening: v. inch. n. [tono], to resound : caelitum altum tonitribus templum tonescit, Varr. ap. Non. 180, 15 .

tongēre.opening: , quod Praenestini tongitionem dicant pro notione. Ennius: alii rhetoricam tongent, Fest. p. 356 Müll. (Sota, v. 4 Vahl. p. 165).

tŏnĭtrālis.opening: , a false read. for penetralia, Lucr. 1, 1105 .

tŏnĭtrŭālis.opening: adj. tonitrus , thundering , an epithet of Jupiter, App. de Mundo, p. 75, 6.

tŏnī^trŭo.opening: v. a. , to thunder : Deus tonitruat, Hier. in Psa. 76 .

tŏnī^trus.opening: , or , ( gen. tonitrui, Vulg. Marc. 3, 17 ), tono , thunder. Sing. : tonitrum auribus accipiamus, Lucr. 6, 164 ; 6, 171 : tonitrum audire, Plin. 2, 54, 55, § 142 : tonitruum terribile exsistit, id. 36, 13, 19, § 88 ;…

tŏno.opening: (collat. form of third conj.: tonimus, Varr. ap. Non. 49, 21 ), v. n. and a. [root in Sanscr. tan-, to stretch, extend; Gr. τείνω; whence teneo, tendo, tenus; cf. O. H. Germ. donar; Engl. thunder], to thunder. Lit. :…

tonsa.opening: perh. from tundo , an oar ( poet. ; mostly in plur. ; syn. remus). Sing. : in mari magno tenere tonsam, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 356 Müll. (Sota, v. 3 Vahl. p. 164): valida tonsa, Val. Fl. 1, 369 . — Plur. , Enn. ap. Fest. p.…

tonsĭcŭla.opening: dim. tonsa , the name of a small fish , Cassiod. Var. 12, 4 .

tonsĭlis.opening: adj. tondeo , that may be shorn , cut , or clipped. Lit. : villus, Plin. 8, 50, 76, § 203 : facilitas piceae, id. 16, 10, 18, § 40 . — Transf. , for tonsus, shorn , clipped , cut , lopped : tapetes, Matius ap. Gell. 20,…

tonsilla.opening: ( ), , A sharppointed pole which was stuck in the ground to fasten vessels to the shore , Pac. and Att. ap. Fest. p. 356 Müll. ( Pac. Trag. Fragm. v. 218 ; Att. Trag. Fragm. v. 517 Rib.). — In plur. : , , , the tonsils…

tonsĭo.opening: tondeo , a shearing (late Lat.): lanae ex ovium tonsione, Vulg. Deut. 18, 4 ; id. Amos, 7, 1.

tonsĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to shear : oves, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 9 .

tonsor.opening: (TOSOR, Inscr. Fabr. p. 214 , n. 546), , id. . A shearer, clipper , shaver of the hair, beard, nails, etc., a hair-cutter , barber , Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 10 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 58 ; Plin. 7, 59, 59, § 211 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 1,…

tonsōrĭus.opening: adj. tondeo , of or belonging to shearing or shaving , tonsorial : culter, a razor, Cic. Off. 2, 7, 25 ; Petr. 108 : ferramenta, Mart. 14, 36 in lemm. : sella, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 : cultellus, for cutting nails, Val.…

tonstrīcŭla.opening: dim. tonstrix , a little female hair-cutter or barber , Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 58 ; cf. tonstrix.

tonstrīna.opening: tondeo , a barber ' s shop , Plaut. As. 2, 2, 76 ; id. Am. 4, 1, 5 ; id. Ep. 2, 2, 14 ; Plin. 36, 22, 47, § 165 ; 29, 6, 36, § 114 ; 35, 10, 37, § 112 ; cf. Becker, Gallus, 3, p. 136 (2d edit.).

tonstrīnum.opening: ( ), , id. , the act or calling of a barber , Petr. 46 ; 64 .

tonstrix.opening: ( , Charis. p. 30 P.), , id. , a female hair-cutter or barber , Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 51 ; 4, 2, 59 ; 4, 4, 3 ; Mart. 2, 17, 1 ; Inscr. Grut. 594, 3 .

tonsūra.opening: id. , a shearing , clipping; a pruning , trimming : quidam in anno bis tondent (oves) ac semestres faciunt tonsuras, wool - shearings, shearings, Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 8 : primae lana, Plin. 28, 8, 29, § 115 : capillorum,…

tŏnus.opening: , = τόνος. The stretching , straining of a rope: mollior, vehementior, Vitr. 10, 10, 6 . — Trop. Lit. , the sound , tone , of an instrument, Vitr. 5, 4 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 1 med. ; Mart. Cap. 9, § 959 .—Of the tone…

tŏparcha.opening: , = τοπάρχης, the governor of a territory or district , a toparch , Spart. Had. 13, 8 .

trĕmor.opening: tremo , a shaking , quaking , quivering , trembling , tremor. Lit. In gen. (class.; cf. trepidatio); terrorem pallor et tremor consequitur, Cic. Tusc. 4, 8, 19 ; cf id. Ac. 2, 15, 48 : quo tremore et pallore dixit! id.…

trĕmŭlus.opening: adj. tremo . Lit. , shaking , quaking , quivering , trembling , tremulous ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): anus, Plaut. Curc. 1, 3, 3 ; cf.: incurvus, tremulus, labiis demissis, gemens, Ter. Eun. 2, 3, 45 : manus…

trĕpĭdātĭo.opening: f [trepido], a state of confused hurry or alarm , agitation , confusion , consternation , trepidation (not freq. till the Aug. per.): numquae trepidatio? numqui tumultus? * Cic. Deiot. 7, 20 : quae senatūs trepidatio,…

trĕpĭdĭārĭus.opening: adj. trepidus , restless , moving briskly : sed ipsos equos, quos vulgo trepidiarios, militari verbo tottonarios vocant, ita edomant, etc., Veg. 1, 56, 37 .

trĕpĭdo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
trĕpĭdo.opening: v. n. and a. [id.], to hurry with alarm , to bustle about anxiously , be in a state of confusion , agitation , or trepidation (class., but not in Cic.): ut ille trepidabat! ut festinabat miser! Plaut. Cas. 2, 7, 9 ; so…

trĕpĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.] trembling , anxious , timorous : pulli circumstrepere, Gell. 2, 29, 8 .

trĕpĭdus.opening: adj. root in Gr. τρέπω, to turn, put to flight; cf. Lat. torqueo (cf. Fest. p. 367 Müll.); prop. scared; hence , restless , agitated , anxious , solicitous , disturbed , alarmed , in a state of trepidation , etc. (not.…

trĕpit.grammar: vertit, unde trepido et trepidatio, quia turbatione mens vertitur

trĕpondo.opening: neutr. indecl. [tres-pondus; cf. duapondo, under duo], three pounds : ejusdem radicis trepondo, panacis pondo IV., Scrib. Comp. 165 : adipis porcinae, id. ib. 271 ; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 15 .

trēs.opening: (also and ; acc. tres and tris), , num. adj. Sanscr. tri-, trajas; Gr. τρεῖς, τρία; Goth. thrija; Germ. drei; Engl. three . Three : duas, tris minas auferunt, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 7 : tria corpora, Tris species tam…

tressis.opening: tres-as , Three asses, Varr. L. L. 5, § 169 ; 9, § 81 Müll.— To denote a trifle : hic Dama est non tressis agaso, is not worth three coppers, Pers. 5, 76 .

tres-vĭri.opening: three men holding an office together , or associated in public business , a board of three , three joint commissioners; as overseers of prisons, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 3 ; id. Aul. 3, 2, 2 .—As inferior priests: tresviri…

Trēvĕri.opening: ( ), , A people in Gallia Belgica, between the Moselle and the forest of Ardennes , in and about the mod. Treves , Caes. B. G. 1, 37 ; 2, 24 ; 3, 11 ; 6, 8 et saep.; Mel. 3, 2, 4 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 ; Liv. Epit.…

trĭācontăs.opening: , = τριακοντάς, the number thirty , Tert. adv. Val. 49 fin.

trĭangŭlāris.opening: adj. triangulus , of or belonging to a triangle , triangular : anfractus, Mart. Cap. 6, § 579 .

trĭangŭlus.opening: adj. tres-angulus , having three corners or angles , threecornered , triangular. Adj. : sidera, Cic. Div. 2, 42, 89 : forma cutis, Cels. 7, 25, 2 : species (Siciliae), Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 86 : ager, Col. 5, 2, 5 : latera…

trĭārĭi.opening: tres , a class of Roman soldiers who formed the third rank from the front , the triarii , Varr. L. L. 5, § 89 Müll.: etiamsi te sors inter triarios posuerit, Sen. Tranq. 3, 10 ; Liv. 22, 5, 7 : a primā acie ad triarios…

Trĭārĭus.opening: a surname in the gens Valeria. C. Valerius Triarius, a friend of Cicero , Cic. Brut. 76, 266 ; he is introduced as a speaker in Cicero's treatise de Finibus; v. Cic. Fin. 1, 15, 13 sq. — His father was named L. Valerius…

trĭăs.opening: , = τριάς, the number three , a triad , Mart. Cap. 7, § 733 .

trĭātrus.opening: a feast-day among the Tusculans , three days after the Ides , Fest. s. v. quinquatrus, p. 257 Müll.

trĭbacca.opening: (sc. inauris) [tres-bacca], an ear-drop consisting of three pearls , P. Syr. ap. Petr. 55 .

trĭbăs.opening: , = τριβάς (rubbing), a woman who practises lewdness with women , Phaedr. 4, 14, 3 ; Mart. 1, 91 tit.; 7, 67, 1; 7, 70, 1; Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 9 .

Tribocci.opening: ( ), , , a German people on the left shore of the Rhine , in mod. Alsace , Caes. B. C. 1, 51 ; 4, 10 ; Tac. G. 28 ; id. H. 4, 70 .

trĭbōn.opening: , = τρίβων, a threadbare cloak , Aus. Epigr. 53 .

Trĭbōnĭānus.opening: a celebrated jurist in the time of the emperor Justinian , Just. Inst. prooem. § 3, 4.

trĭbrăchys.opening: , = τρίβραχυς, a poetical foot consisting of three short syllables , a tribrach , Quint. 9, 4, 97 .—Called also in Lat. tribrevis, Diom. p. 475 P.

trĭbŭārĭus.opening: adj. tribus , of or belonging to a tribe or tribes : crimen sodalitiorum, i. e. a bribing of the tribes, Cic. Planc. 19, 47 : res, id. ib. 15, 36 .

trībŭlātĭo.opening: tribulo , distress , trouble , tribulation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Jud. 11 ; Aug. in Psa. 125, 2 ; Hier. Ep. 108, 18 .

trībŭlātus.opening: adj. tribulum , pointed , toothed like a threshing-sledge: falciculae, Pall. 1, 43, 8 .

trĭbūlis.opening: tribus , one of the same tribe with another. Lit. (class.): tribulis tuus, Cic. Fam. 13, 23, 1 ; Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 85 ; Cic. Planc. 19, 47 ; id. Rosc. Am. 16, 47 ; id. Vatin. 15, 36 ; Liv. 2, 16, 5 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 13, 15…

trībŭlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. tribulum . Lit. , to press : Θλίβω tribulo, presso, premo. Gloss, Philox.; Cato. R. R. 23, 4.— Trop. , to oppress , afflict (eccl. Lat.): in omnibus tribulemur, Tert. adv. Gnost. 13 med. ; Ambros.…

trībŭlōsus.opening: adj. tribulus . Lit. , full of thorns or thistles (late Lat.): voragines viarum, Sid. Ep. 3, 2 fin. — Trop. , thorny , rough : opus, Sid. Ep. 4, 3 . — Sup. : tribulosissima dissimulatio, Sid. Ep. 1, 7 med.

trībŭlum.opening: ( ), , tero , a threshing-sledge , consisting of a wooden platform studded underneath with sharp pieces of flint or with iron teeth, Varr. L. L. 5, § 21 Müll.; id. R. R. 1, 22, 1 ; 1, 52, 1 ; Plin. 18, 30, 72, § 298 ;…

trĭbŭlus.opening: ( ), , , = τρίβολος, an instrument resting on three of its iron prongs , while a fourth projected upward , thrown on the ground to impede an enemy's cavalry, a caltrop. Lit. : tribulos abjecerunt, Veg. Mil. 3, 24 .—…

trĭbūnal.opening: (moleste diligentibus permittamus et tribunale dicere, Quint. 1, 6, 17 ; yet is found Corp. Inscr. Lat. 206, 24), , tribunus . Lit. A raised semicircular or square platform , on which the seats of magistrates were…

trĭbūnātus.opening: id. , the office and dignity of a tribune , the tribuneship : Cotta, qui tribunatum plebis petebat, Cic. de Or. 1, 7, 25 ; id. Leg. 3, 9, 20 ; so of the office of a tribune of the people , id. Rep. 1, 19, 31 ; id. Lael.…

trĭbūnīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. id. , of or belonging to a tribune , tribunitial : tribunicia potestas, Cic. de Or. 2, 28, 124 ; Caes. B. C. 1, 7 ; Flor. 3, 13, 1 ; Val. Max. 2, 9, 8 : vis, Caes. B. C. 1, 7 ; Sall. H. 3, 61, 12 Dietsch;…

trĭbūnus.opening: tribus, prop. the chief of a tribe; hence, in gen. , a chieftain , commander , tribune. Tribuni aerarii, paymasters , who assisted the quaestors, Cato ap. Gell. 7, 10, 2 ; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 181 Müll.; Fest. p. 2 ib.;…

trĭbŭo.opening: v. a. tribus , to assign , impart , allot , bestow , give , etc. (syn.: do, dono, largior). Lit. : ut ei plurimum tribuamus, a quo plurimum deligimur, Cic. Off. 1, 15, 47 : in tribuendo suum cuique, id. ib. 1, 5, 14 :…

trĭbus.opening: ( dat. and abl. plur. : tribubus, Cic. Rep. 2, 9, 16 ; Liv. 5, 18, 2 ; 23, 12, 16 , etc.; but trebibos, Ephem. Epigr. 2, 208, n. 299; never tribibus; cf. Serv. ad Verg. G. 3, 376 , and v., in gen., Neue, Formenl. 1, 361…

trĭbūtārĭus.opening: adj. tributum , of or belonging to tribute : necessitas, of paying tribute, Just. 32, 2, 1 : solum, subject to tribute, tributary, Plin. 12, 1, 3, § 6 ; so, praedia tributaria sunt ea, quae in his provinciis sunt, quae…

trĭbūtim.opening: adv. tribus , through each tribe , tribe by tribe , by tribes : tributim et centuriatim descriptis ordinibus, Cic. Fl. 7, 15 : legem centuriatis comitiis tulere, ut quod tributim plebes jussisset, populum teneret, i. e.…

trĭbūtĭo.opening: tribuo . A dividing , distributing , distribution (very rare): hanc ἰσονομίαν appellat Epicurus, id est aequabilem tributionem, * Cic. N. D. 1, 19, 50 : tributio fit pro ratā ejus, quod cuique debetur, Dig. 14, 4, 5…

trĭbūtor.opening: id. , a giver , imparter : tributor omnium, App. Trism. p. 92, 27 .

trĭbūtōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or concerning payment (jurid. Lat.): tributoria actio, Dig. 14, tit. 14 .

trīcae.opening: acc. to Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 104, orig. Trīca, ae, f., like Apina, the name of a small town in Apulia; but cf. Sanscr. trkvan, thief; and Lat. tricor, extricare, etc.; hence, prov. , trifles , toys , trumpery , stuff ,…

trĭcămĕrātus.opening: adj. tres-camera , having three chambers (late Lat.). ecclesia, Aug. Civ. Dei , 15, 26: inferiora ar cae bicamerata et tricamerata facies, Ambros. Hexaëm. 6, 9, n. 72.— Subst. : , , , a room divided into three chambers…

Tricca.opening: , and , , , = Τρίκκη, a town of Thessaly , on the Peneus , now Trikala , Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 29 ; Liv. 32, 13, 5 ; Sen. Troad. 824 .—Hence, , , adj. , of Tricca , Avien. Arat. 206 .

trīcēnārĭus.opening: adj. triceni , of or containing thirty : fistula, thirty quarterdigits in diameter, Front. Aquaed. 29 ; 48 : filius, thirty years old, Sen. Excerpt. Controv. 3, 3 fin. : homo, Arn. 2, 58 ; Pall. Aug. 12 ; Front. Aquaed.…

trīcēni.opening: ( gen. plur. tricenūm, Plin. 7, 49, 50, § 164 ; 11, 33, 39, § 113 ), num. distr. adj. [triginta], thirty at a time , thirty each , thirty. Lit. , distributively: lecti, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 26, § 58 : tricenos milites ex…

trīcennālis.opening: adj. tricennium , of or belonging to thirty years , tricennial (late Lat.): incuria, Ruf. in Hier. 1, 11 .—In plur. subst. : , , , a festival celebrated once in thirty years , a tricennial festival , Oros. 7, 28 fin.

trīcennĭum.opening: triginta-annos , the space of thirty years , Cod. Just. 7, 31, 1 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 6 med. ; Cassiod. Var. 1, 18 ; 3, 31 .

trīceps.opening: adj. tres-caput; cf. Cic. Or. 48, 159 . Lit. , having three heads , triple-headed : Cerberus, Cic. Tusc. 1, 5, 10 : Hecate (because she was also at the same time Luna and Diana), Ov. M. 7, 194 .—* Transf. , threefold :…

trīcēsĭmāni.opening: tricesimus , soldiers of the thirtieth legion , Amm. 18, 9, 3 .

trīcēsĭmus.opening: (less freq. , Mart. 1, 16, 3 ; 10, 103, 7 ; Just. 12, 15 ), a, um, num. ord. adj. [triginta], the thirtieth : idem tricesimo post die feci, Cic. Fam. 12, 2, 1 : tertius et tricesimus annus, id. Sen. 6, 19 : sexto…

trīcessis.opening: triginta - as , thirty asses, Varr. L. L. 5, § 170 Müll.

trĭchalcon.opening: , = τρίχαλκον, a coin of the value of three chalci, Vitr. 3, 1 med.

trĭchaptum.opening: , = τρίχαπτον, a fine , soft garment woven of hair , a hairgarment , Hier. in Zach. 3, 14, 14 ; id. in Ezech. 4, 16, 11 .

trĭchĭas.opening: , = τριχίας, a kind of sardine , Plin. 9, 15, 20, § 52 ; 9, 51, 74, § 162 .

trĭchĭăsis.opening: , = τριχίασις, a disease of the eyelids , when the lashes grow inside , Veg. Vet. 2, 15 .

trĭchĭla.opening: a bower , arbor , summer-house , Verg. Copa, 7 ; Col. poët. 10, 378; 10, 394; Inscr. Orell. 4517 ; Caes. B. C. 3, 96 (al. triclinia).—Also, in a contr. collat. form † , , , Inscr. Orell. 2909 : † , , ib. 4337 ; and † ,…

trĭchītis.opening: , = τριχῖτις, a kind of alum , Plin. 35, 15, 52, § 186 .

trĭchŏmănes.opening: , = τριχομανές, a plant resembling adiantum, Plin. 27, 13, 111, § 138 ; 22, 21, 30, § 63 ; App. Herb. 47 .

trĭchordis.opening: adj. , = τρίχορδος, three-stringed : citharae, Sid. Ep. 5, 5 med. ; Cassiod. Anim. 5 .

trĭchōrum.opening: , = τρίχωρον, a room divided into three apartments , Stat. S. 1, 3, 57 ; Spart. Pesc. 12 ; Inscr. Orell. 1595 .

trīcĭes.opening: (also , Auct. B. Afr. 97, 2 twice: , Mart. Cap. 7, § 737 ), adv. num. triginta , thirty times : (pedes) tricies triceni fiunt nongenti, Col. 5, 2, 10 : tricies centenis millibus pondo olei eos multat, Auct. B. Afr. 97,…

trĭcĭnĭum.opening: tres-cano , a song by three voices , a trio : semivolucrum puellarum, of the three Sirens, Symm. Ep. 1, 41 .

Trĭcĭpĭtīnus.opening: a surname in the gens Lucretia; e. g. Sp. Lucretius Tricipitinus, father of Lucretia , Cic. Leg. 2, 4, 10 ; Liv. 1, 59, 8 .— L. Lucretius Tricipitinus, a consul , and conqueror of the Volsci , Liv. 3, 8, 2 ; Fast.…

trīclīnĭarches.opening: or , , , = τρικλινιάρχης, a chief servant who has charge of the table , Petr. 22 ; Inscr. Orell. 794 ; 2952 .

trīclīnĭāris.opening: adj. triclinium , of or belonging to an eating - couch or diningroom. Adj. : gradus, Varr. L. L. 8, § 32 Müll.: apothecae, id. ap. Non. 545, 4 : mappae, id. L. L. 9, § 47 Müll.: lecti, Plin. 37, 2, 6, § 14 : vestimenta,…

trīclīnĭum.opening: , = τρικλίνιον, a couch running round three sides of a table for reclining on at meals , an eating-couch , table-couch. Lit. : triclinio posito cenabimus, Varr. R. R. 3, 13, 2 : sternere, id. L. L. 9, § 9 Müll.:…

trīco.opening: tricae, II. , a mischiefmaker , shuffler , trickster , Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 46 ; Lucil. ap. Non. 8, 24 ; 22, 31 ; Capitol. Ver. 4 .

trĭcoccum.opening: , = τρίκοκκον (that has three berries), a kind of heliotropium, Plin. 22, 21, 29, § 57 .

trĭcōlum.opening: , = τρίκωλον (having three members), a sentence or period consisting of three clauses , Sen. Contr. 2, 12, § 12 ; 4, 25, § 27 .

trīcor.opening: v. dep. n. [tricae], to make or start difficulties; to trifle , dally , shuffle , play tricks (Ciceron.), Cic. Att. 15, 13, 5 : Publilius tecum tricatus est, id. ib. 14, 19, 4 . —Collat. form , reflex., to dally , delay…

Tricorĭi.opening: a people of Gallia Narbonensis, Liv. 21, 31 .

trĭ-cornĭger.opening: adj. tres , having three horns or points : species furcae, of the letter Ψ, Aus. Idyll. 13 technop. Lit. Monos. fin.

trĭcornis.opening: adj. tres-cornu , having three horns , three-horned : boves, Plin. 8, 21, 30, § 73 ; Sol. 52 .

trĭcorpor.opening: adj. tres-corpus , having three bodies , three-bodied , tricorporal : umbra, i. e. Geryon, Verg. A. 6, 289 ; so, Geryon, Sil. 3, 422 ; 13, 201 .

trīcōsus.opening: adj. tricae , full of difficulties or perplexities , full of wiles or tricks , Lucil. ap. Non. 79, 26 (al. strigosus); Inscr. Grut. 50, 1 .

trĭ-cuspis.opening: adj. tres , having three points or tines , three-pointed , three-tineà , tricuspid : telum, i. e. tridens, Ov. M. 1, 330 .

trĭdacna.opening: , = τρίδακνα, a kind of oysters , Plin. 32, 6, 21, § 63 .

trĭ-dens.opening: ( abl. tridenti, Verg. A. 1, 145 ; 2, 418 ; Sil. 3, 53 : tridente, Ov. M. 1, 283 ; 6, 75 ; Plin. 9, 15, 20, § 51 ), adj. tres , having three teeth or tines , three-tined , threepronged , tridented , trident. Adj. :…

trĭdentĭfer.opening: tridens-fero , the trident-bearer , an epithet of Neptune, Ov. M. 8, 595 ; cf. tridentiger.

trĭdentĭger.opening: tridens-gero , the trident-bearer , an epithet of Neptune, Ov. M. 11, 202 ; cf. tridentifer.

trĭdentĭpŏtens.opening: tridenspotens , ruling with the trident , an epithet of Neptune, Sil. 15, 159 .

trīdŭānus.opening: adj. triduum , lasting three days , of three days ' continuance (post-class.): spectaculum, App. M. 10, p. 247, 27 : jejunia, Hier. Ep. 54, 10 : funus, Paul. Nol. Carm. 12, 207 .

trīdŭum.opening: (sc. spatium) [tres-dies], the space of three days , three days : ubi triduom continuom, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 147 : hanc hoc triduom solum sinas Esse hic, id. Cist. 1, 1, 106 : triduom servire numquam te sinam, id. Mil. 4,…

trĭennĭa.opening: (sc. sacra) [triennium], a festival celebrated every three years , a triennial festival , = trieterica sacra, Ov. M. 9, 642 .

trĭennis.opening: adj. tres-annus , three years old : vacca, Vulg. Gen. 15, 9 .

trĭennĭum.opening: (sc. spatium) [id.], the space of three years , three years : biennium aut triennium est, cum virtuti nuntium remisisti, Cic. Fam. 15, 16, 3 ; Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 79 ; id. Most. 2, 2, 10 ; id. Stich. 1, 2, 80 ; 1, 3, 61 ;…

trĭens.opening: tres , a third part , a third of any thing. In gen.: cum sciemus, quantum quasi sit in trientis triente, Cic. Att. 7, 8, 3 : medicaminis, Col. 12, 20, 7 : ut triens ex heminā supersit, Plin. 23, 7, 68, § 133 .—Of…

trĭentābŭlum.opening: triens , a portion of public land assigned to creditors in place of a third part of the public debt : trientabulumque is ager, quia pro tertiā parte pecuniae datus erat, appellatus, Liv. 31, 13, 9 .

trĭentālis.opening: adj. id. , that contains a third of a foot : materia, Vitr. 10, 6 : folia, Plin. 27, 5, 17, § 34 .

trĭentārĭus.opening: adj. triens, II. B. , of or belonging to a third part : faenus, i. e. a third of one per cent. monthly, or, in our manner, four per cent. a year, Capitol. Anton. P. 2 ; Lampr. Alex. Sev. 21, 1 .

trĭentĭus.opening: adj. triens , sold for a third : ager, Liv. 31, 13, 9 .

trĭērarchus.opening: , = τριήραρχος, the captain of a trireme , a trierarch , Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 20, § 52 ; Tac. H. 2, 16 ; Suet. Ner. 34 ; Inscr. Orell. 2652 ; 3595 ; 3603 ; 3615 sq.

trĭēris.opening: adj. , = τριήρης, having three ranges of oars. Adj. : navis, Auct. B. Afr. 44, 2.— Subst. : , , , a ship or galley of three ranges of oar-banks , a trireme , Nep. Alcib. 4, 3 ; Inscr. Orell. 3610 ; 3612 ; 3617 sq.; cf.…

trĭĕtērĭcus.opening: adj. , = τριετηρικός, recurring every three years , triennial : sacra, the festival of Bacchus, Ov. M. 6, 587 ; also called trieterica orgia, Verg. A. 4, 302 . —As subst. : , , , the festival of Bacchus , Ov. R. Am. 593…

trĭĕtēris.opening: , = τριετηρίς. Lit. , a space of three years , three years , Stat. S. 2, 6, 72 ; Mart. 9, 85, 9 ; 10, 53, 3 ; Aus. Caes. 3 . — Transf. , a triennial festival; of the festival of Bacchus, Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 58 ; cf.…

trĭfārĭam.opening: (collat. form , Diom. p. 279 P.), adv. trifarius , triply , in three places (not ante-Aug.): trifariam adortus castra, Liv. 3, 22, 7 : muniebant Romani, id. 5, 26, 7 : distraxere exercitum, id. 26, 41, 20 : epulas…

trĭfārĭus.opening: adj. τριφάσιος , of three sorts or ways , threefold , triple (postclass.): causa morborum omnium, App. Mag. p. 305, 38 : genus, Sol. 27 : linguae, Cassiod. Var. 5, 40 med. : vestigia numerorum in corporibus trifaria,…

trĭfaux.opening: adj. tres-faux , having three throats , triple-throated : latratus Cerberi, Verg. A. 6, 417 .

trĭfax.opening: a kind of long missile weapon , Enn. ap. Fest. p. 367 Müll. (Ann. v. 524 Vahl.); cf. Gell. 10, 25, 2 .

trĭfer.opening: adj. ter-fero , thricebearing , that bears fruit three times a year : ficus, Col. 5, 10, 11 ; cf.: ficus trifero proventu, Plin. 15, 18, 19, § 71 : vites, id. 16, 27, 50, § 114 .

trĭfĭdus.opening: adj. ter-findo , cleft or cloven into three parts , three-cleft , threeforked ( poet. and mostly post-Aug.): hasta (Neptuni), Val. Fl. 1, 641 ; cf.: cuspis Neptuni, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 181 : flamma, i. e. lightning,…

trĭfīlis.opening: adj. ter - filum , having three threads or hairs : calva, Mart. 6, 74, 2 .

trĭfīnĭum.opening: ter - finis , a place where three boundaries meet , Sicul. Flacc. Condit. Agr. p. 6 Goes.; Inscr. Grut. 201, 5 ; Isid. 15, 14, 5 .

trĭfissĭlis.opening: adj. ter - findo , = trifidus, cleft or cloven into three parts , threeforked : forma Ψ, Aus. Ep. 128, 7 .

Trĭfŏlīnus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to Mount Trifolium near Naples (which abounded in grape-vines): ager, Juv. 9, 56 : vina, Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 69 ; Mart. 13, 114, 1 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 212 .

trĭfŏlĭum.opening: ter - folium , threeleaved grass , trefoil , Plin. 21, 9, 30, § 54 ; 21, 21, 88, § 152 .

trĭformis.opening: adj. ter - forma , having three forms , shapes , or natures; threefold , triple , triform ( poet. ): Chimaera, Hor. C. 1, 27, 23 : canis, i. e. Cerberus, Sen. Herc. Oet. 1202 : Geryon, id. Agam. 841 : diva, i. e. Diana…

trĭformĭtas.opening: triformis , triplicity of shape , Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 9 .

trĭ-fūr.opening: ter , a triple thief , an arrant thief : non fur sed trifur, Plaut. Aul. 4, 4, 6 ; cf. trifurcifer.

trĭ-furcĭfer.opening: id. , an arch rogue , arrant knave , Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 47 ; id. Rud. 3, 4, 29 ; cf. trifur.

trĭfurcĭum.opening: trifurcus , any thing of a three-forked shape , App. Herb. 77 .

trĭfurcus.opening: adj. ter-furca , having three forks , prongs , or points , threeforked , three-pronged : surculi, Col. 5, 11, 7 : stirps, id. 5, 10, 7 : semina, id. Arb. 20, 2 .
