tŭdes.opening: (ĭtis, acc. to Fest. p. 253 Müll.), root tud, tundo; Sanscr. tud-, to thrust , a hammer , mallet : tudites malleos appellant antiqui a tundendo, Fest. p. 352 sq. Müll.: fabriles operae tudibus contundere massas…

Tudicĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens: Cn. Tudicius, a Roman senator, Cic. Clu. 70 .

tŭdĭcŭla.opening: dim. tudes , a small machine for bruising olives , Col. 12, 52, 7 .

tŭdĭcŭlo.opening: v. a. tudicula , to stir , stir about (ante- and post-class.), Varr. ap. Non. 178, 30 : cum bene ferbuerit, tudiculabis, Apic. 5, 2 .

tŭdĭtans.opening: Part. [tud, tundo], striking or beating often (ante-class.). Lit. , Lucr. 3, 394 : corpora, id. 2, 1142 .— Trop. , pushing or driving on : tuditantes significat negotium tundentes, id est agentes, Fest. pp. 352 and 353…

Tŭdĭtānus.opening: a surname in the gens Sempronia, Enn. ap. Cic. Brut. 15, 58 (Ann. v. 305 Vahl.); Cic. Sen. 4, 10 ; 14, 50 al. ; cf. Fest. p. 252 Müll.

tŭĕor.opening: ( perf. only post-Aug., Quint. 5, 13, 35 ; Plin. Ep. 6, 29, 10 ; collat. form tūtus, in the part. , rare, Sall. J. 74, 3 ; Front. Strat. 2, 12, 13 ; but constantly in the P. a.; inf. parag. tuerier, Plaut. Rud. 1, 4, 35…

tūfa.opening: a kind of helmet-crest; or, acc. to others, a kind of military standard , Veg. Mil. 3, 5 ; cf. Lyd. Magistr. 1, 8 (hence the Fr. toupet ).

Tugĭo.opening: a jurist in the time of Cicero , Cic. Balb. 20, 45 .

tŭgŭrĭŏlum.opening: dim. tugurium , a little hut or cottage , App. M. 4, p. 147, 34 ; Arn. 6, 191 ; Hier. Ep. 112, 5 .

tŭgŭrĭum.opening: (TEGVRIVM and TIGVRIVM in inscrr.; cf. Inscr. Orell. 1773 ; and ib. Labus), , tego , a hut , cot , cottage of shepherds, peasants, etc., Varr. R. R. 3, 1, 3 ; Afran. and Caecil. ap. Fest. p. 355 Müll.; Cic. Sest. 43, 93…

tŭgŭrĭuncŭlum.opening: dim. tugurium , a little hut or cottage , Hier. Vit. Hil. 9 .

Tuisco.opening: the progenitor of the Germans , honored by them as a god , Tac. G. 2 ; cf. Grimm, Myth. pp. 176 and 318 (2d ed.).

tŭĭtĭo.opening: tueor, II. , a taking care of , keeping , guarding , preserving , defense , protection , preservation; with gen. subj. praetoris, Dig. 7, 4, 1 pr.; with gen. obj. : tuitio sui, Cic. Top. 23, 90 : pudoris, Macr. S. 2, 2…

Tulingi.opening: a German or Helvetic tribe on the Rhine , Caes. B. G. 1, 5 .

Tullĭŏla.opening: dim. Tullia , a pet name for Tullia, the daughter of Cicero , Cic. Att. 1, 3, 3 ; 1, 8, 3 ; 1, 10, 6 et saep.

Tullĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. Esp., Servius Tullius, the sixth king of Rome , Liv. 1, 41 sqq. — M. Tullius Cicero, the renowned statesman and orator. — Q. Tullius Cicero, his brother. — M. Tullius Tiro, a freedman of M.…

Tullus.opening: a Roman prœnomen , e.g. Tullus Hostilius, the third king of Rome , Liv. 1, 22 sqq.; Val. Max. 3, 4, 1 ; 9, 12, 1 : Tullus Cluilius, a Roman ambassador, Cic. Phil. 9, 2, 5 al.

tulo.opening: (tŭli), , v. a. akin with tollo; Gr. τλάω , ante-class. collat. form of fero, to bring , bear , lift up : nisi quid tua facultas nobis tulat opem, peream, Att. ap. Macr. Diff. et Soc. Gr. et Lat. Verb. 6, 14 (Trag.…

tum.opening: adv. demonstr. , of time [pronom. demonstr. stems to-, ta-; Gr. το , seen in ita, tam, etc.; cf. quom or cum], then. Absol. Referring to a time previously specified. To a definite past time. To a period of time in which…

tumba.opening: , = τύμβα ( τύμβος ), a sepulchral mound , a sepulchre , tomb , Prud. στεφ . 11, 9.

tumbŭla.opening: tumba , a little tomb (late Lat.), Aldhelm. Carm. Virg. 889.

tŭmĕ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. tumeo , to cause to swell , to tumefy ( poet. ). Lit. : vis fera ventorum ... Extentam tumefecit humum, Ov. M. 15, 303 : tumefactus pontus, id. ib. 11, 518 .— Trop. , to swell or puff up , to inflate with pride,…

tŭmentĭa.opening: id. , a swelling (late Lat.): capitis, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 10, 74 ; 3, 8, 92 .

tŭmĕo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. tu-, taumi, tavīmi, to be strong; Gr. τύλος, τύλη, lump; Lat. tuber, tumulus, tumor, etc.; cf. O. H. Germ. dūmo; Germ. Daumen; Engl. thumb , to swell , be swollen or tumid , to be puffed out or inflated…

tŭmesco.opening: v. inch. n. [tumeo], to begin to swell , to swell up ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : inflatum mare cum subito penitusque tumescit, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 7, 13: vi maria, Verg. G. 2, 479 : freta ventis, Ov. M. 1, 36…

tūmicla.opening: dim. contracted from tomicula, from tomix . a little rope , a cord : spartea, App. M. 8, p. 213 (p. 575 Oud.).

tŭmĭdĭtās.opening: tumidus , a swelling , tumor (late Lat.): ventris, Firm. Math. 8, 29 med. ; Hier. Ep. 53, 11 .

tŭmĭdo.opening: v. a. id. , to cause to swell (late Lat.), Aug. Spec. 30 .

tŭmĭdōsus.opening: adj. id. , high-swelling : colles, Amm. 21, 10, 3 (al. tumulosi; cf. , however, Ov. Am. 2, 16, 51 , and Tac. A. 2, 23 s. v. tumidus; v. also tumor).

tŭmĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [tumidus], swollen , tumid : gingivula, App. Mag. p. 277, 12 .

tŭmĭdus.opening: adj. tumeo , swollen , swelling , rising high , protuberant , tumid (class.). Lit. : membrum tumidum ac turgidum, Cic. Tusc. 3, 9, 19 : serpens inflato collo, tumidis cervicibus, id. Vatin. 2, 4 : Python, Ov. M. 1, 460…

tŭmor.opening: id. , the state of being swollen or tumid; a swelling , tumor (class.; syn. tuber). Lit. : oculorum tumor, Cic. Tusc. 4, 37, 81 ; so of a tumor , id. ib. 3, 9, 19 ; Auct. Her. 2, 27, 44 .—In plur. : tumores ardentes,…

tŭmōrōsus.opening: adj. tumor , inflated , bloated (late Lat.), Ps.-Aug. ad Fr. Erem. Serm. 12 .

tŭmŭlāmen.opening: tumulus , a sepulchral mound , tumulus , Inscr. Fabr. 634, 290 .

tŭmŭlo.opening: v. a. id. , to cover with a mound , to bury , inter , entomb ( poet. ; syn. humo): neque injectā tumulabor mortua terrā, Cat. 64, 153 : neu sim tumulandus ab illā, Ov. M. 8, 710 ; 15, 716 ; id. P. 1, 6, 49 ; Mart. 11,…

tŭmŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of hills , hilly : locus, Sall. J. 91, 3 .

tŭmultŭārĭus.opening: adj. tumultus , of or belonging to bustle , hurry , or tumult; in milit. lang., of troops brought hurriedly together , raised hastily or suddenly (not ante-Aug., but esp. freq. in Livy). Lit. : tumultuario exercitu…

tŭmultŭātim.opening: adv. id. , in haste , hastily , Sid. Ep. 4, 11 .

tŭmultŭātĭo.opening: tumultuor . A bustling , hurrying , bustle , confusion , tumult (very rare), Liv. 38, 2, 8 .— The irregular swearing of the milites tumultuarii, acc. to Isid. Orig. 9, 3, 55 .

tŭmultŭor.opening: v. dep. n. [tumultus], to make a bustle or disturbance , to be in great agitation or confusion , be in an uproar , raise a tumult : in otio tumultuaris, in tumultu es otiosus, Auct. Her. 4, 15, 21 : non decet…

tŭmultŭōsus.opening: adj. tumultus , full of bustle , confusion , or tumult , restless , turbulent , tumultuous (class.): qui homo tam tumultuoso sonitu me excivit foras? Plaut. Trin. 5, 2, 52 : seditiosa ac tumultuosa vita, Cic. Inv. 1, 3,…

tŭmultus.opening: ( gen. tumulti, Enn., Att., Afran., Turp., and Pompon. ap. Non. 489, 29 sq. ; Plaut. Cas. 3, 5, 22 ; id. Poen. 1, 1, 79 ; Ter. And. 2, 2, 28 ; id. Hec. 3, 2, 21 ; Sall. C. 59, 5 ), Sanscr. tumalas, tumulas, disturbing;…

tŭmŭlus.opening: (late Lat. in the neutr. : HOC TVMVLVM, Inscr. Rein. cl. 20, 197) [tumeo; cf. also tumor and tumidus], a raised heap of earth , a mound , hill , hillock (freq. and class.; cf.: agger, moles). In gen.: terrenus, Caes. B.…

tunc.opening: adv. demonstr. , of time [tum, and demonstr. suffix -ce], then , at that time; but in ante-class. and class. prose tunc is always emphatic, and generally refers to a point of time. In post-Aug. style tunc freq. occurs…

tundo.opening: (v. Neue, Formenl. II. 568), 3 (old collat. form of the perf. tuserunt, Naev. 1, 1 : tunsi, acc. to Diom. p. 369 P.; inf. tundier, Lucr. 4, 934 ), v. a. Sanscr. tu-dāmi, thrust; cf. Gr. Τυδεύς, Τυνδάρεος , to beat ,…

Tūnēs.opening: a maritime town of Africa Propria , now Tunis : Scipio occupat relictum Tuneta, Liv. 30, 9, 16 .— Acc. Tunetem, Liv. 30, 36, 6 .

Tungri.opening: a people of Gallia Belgica, near the modern Tongres , Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 ; 31, 2, 8, § 12 ; Tac. G. 2 ; id. H. 2, 14 sq. ; 4, 16, 55 ; Amm. 15, 11, 7 ; Inscr. Orell. 3399 .—In sing. : , Sil. 7, 682 ; Inscr. Grut.…

tŭnĭca.opening: perh. for tog-nica, from tego , an under-garment of the Romans worn by both sexes , a tunic. Lit. , Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 46 ; 5, 2, 60 ; id. Mil. 3, 1, 93 ; 5, 30 ; id. Pers. 1, 3, 75 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 60 ; id. de Or. 2,…

tŭnĭco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. tunica , to clothe with a tunic. In the verb. finit. only once: tunicare homulum, Varr. ap. Non. 182, 17 .— In part. perf. (freq. and class.): , , clothed with a tunic , Cic. Cael. 5, 11 ; cf. in…

tŭnĭcopallĭum.opening: tunica-pallium , a garment uniting in one the tunic and the pallium , Serv. Verg. A. 1, 648 ; ad Hor. S. 1, 2, 99 ; cf. Non. 537, 33 .

tŭnĭcŭla.opening: dim. tunica . A little tunic , Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 65 ; Turp. ap. Non. 538, 10 ; Varr. ib. 228, 27 .— A little coat , skin , or membrane : oculorum, Plin. 26, 12, 76, § 123 ; 29, 6, 38, § 124 : stellionis, id. 30, 10, 27,…

tŭor.opening: 1. tuor, = tueor , the sight , vision : radios omnis nostri tuoris raritate transmittunt, App. de Deo Socr. p. 48 .

tūrālis.opening: ( ), , adj. tus , of or belonging to incense , incense- : arca, Serv. Verg. A. 5, 745 .

tūrārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or belonging to frankincense. In gen. Adj. : tibiae, incense-flutes , i. e. flutes played upon while the incense was burned at sacrifices, Sol. 5 med. (called also tibiae sacrificae Tuscorum, Plin.…

turba.opening: = τύρβη; cf. Sanscr. turāmi, to hasten; turas, hasty; Lat. turma , a turmoil , hubbub , uproar , disorder , tumult , commotion , disturbance , of a crowd of people (syn. tumultus): praetor ait: cujus dolo malo in turbā…

turbāmentum.opening: turbo , a means of disturbance (very rare): turbamenta reipublicae, Sall. Or. Lepid. 11 : turbamenta vulgi, Tac. H. 1, 23 .

turbātē.opening: adv. , v. 1. turbo, P. a. fin.

turbātĭo.opening: 1. turbo , confusion , disorder , disturbance (perh. not ante-Aug.; cf.: conturbatio, perturbatio): turbam multitudinis hominum esse turbationem et coetum, rixam etiam duorum, Dig. 48, 8, 4 (v. turba init. ): rerum,…

turbātor.opening: id. , a troubler , disquieter , disturber (not ante-Aug.): turbatores vulgi erant tribuni plebis, Liv. 4, 48, 1 ; so, vulgi, id. 4, 2, 7 : plebis (Gracchi et Saturnini), Tac. A. 3, 27 : Germaniae (Arminius), id. ib. 1,…

turbātrix.opening: turbator , she that troubles , disquiets , or disturbs ( poet. and very rare): turbatrix fama, Stat. Th. 4, 369 : pacis, Prud. Psych. 668 .

turbātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of 1. turbo.

turbellae.opening: or , , dim. turba . A bustle , stir , row (only in vulg. lang.): tantas turbellas facio, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 9, 134 ; so id. Ps. 1, 1, 108 ; App. de Deo Socr. p. 48, 20 .—* A little crowd , multitude : populi…

turbĭdo.opening: v. a. turbidus , to trouble , to make turbid , to disturb , obscure (post-class.). Lit. : aquam, Sol. 49 fin. : aër turbidatus, Mart. Cap. 2, § 165 . — Trop. : laetitiam, Mart. Cap. 1, § 67 ; cf.: serenitatem animae,…

turbĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat disturbed or confused : sensus, Prud. Apoth. 276 .

turbĭdus.opening: adj. turba , full of confusion or disorder , wild , confused , disordered (class.; cf.: agitatus, tumultuosus). Lit. : turbida tempestas heri fuit, wild, stormy, Plaut. Rud. 4, 3, 3 : tempestas, Lucr. 4, 169 ; 6, 376 ;…

turbĭnātĭo.opening: turbinatus , a pointing in the form of a cone : piri, Plin. 15, 21, 23, § 85 .

turbĭnātus.opening: adj. 2. turbo , coneshaped , pointed like a cone , conical. In gen.: adamas ... turbinatus in mucronem, Plin. 37, 4, 15, § 56 ; 11, 37, 69, § 181 . — Comp. : turbinatior piris figura, Plin. 15, 15, 17, § 58 .— As adj.…

turbĭnĕus.opening: adj. id. , shaped like a top , cone-shaped : vortex, Ov. M. 8, 556 .

Turbo.opening: the name of a gladiator , Hor. S. 2, 3, 310 .

turbor.opening: 1. turbo , restlessness , unquietness , disturbance , tumult (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 15 , n. 149; 2, 1 med.

turbŭla.opening: dim. turba , a disorderly group , a little crowd of people (Appuleian): turbulae complent totas plateas, App. M. 11, p. 260, 16 ; 11 , p. 159, 27; 4, p. 151, 39.

turbŭlenter.opening: adv. turbulentus , in a turbulent manner , confusedly , tumultuously , etc.: nihil turbulenter, nihil temere facere, Cic. Fam. 2, 16, 7 .

turbŭlentĭa.opening: id. , trouble , disquiet , turbulence (post-class.), Tert. adv. Prax. 29 fin. ; id. adv. Herm. 41 .

turbŭlento.opening: v. a. id. , to trouble , disturb (post-class.): me strepitu turbulentant, App. M. 9, p. 222, 16 ; 2 , p. 120, 9.

turbŭlentus.opening: adj. turba , full of trouble or commotion. Pass. , restless , agitated , confused , disturbed , boisterous , stormy , tempestuous (class.; syn. tumultuosus): tempestas, stormy, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 10, § 26 ; Plaut. Rud. 4,…

turbystum.opening: or , , , a drug used by painters to facilitate the reception of a color , a mordant : scytatum atque turbystum, Plin. 33, 5, 26, § 88 .

turdārĭum.opening: turdus , a place where thrushes are kept , Varr. L. L. 6, § 2 Müll.

turdelix.opening: , icis; of uncertain signif., Varr. L. L. 6, § 2 Müll.

turdus.opening: (collat. form , , , Pers. 6, 24 ; denied by Varr. L. L. 9, § 55 Müll.; cf. id. R. R. 3, 5, 6 ) [cf. O. H. Germ. trosca; Angl. Sax. throsle; Engl. thrush]. Lit. , a thrush , a fieldfare , Plin. 10, 25, 36, § 73 ; Varr.…

turgesco.opening: v. inch. n. [turgeo], to begin to swell , to swell up , swell. Lit. : ne aqua in eorum corpore turgescat, Varr. R. R. 8, 9, 13 : hoc (umore) aetas illa (puerilis) turgescit, Quint. 11, 3, 28 : prima Ceres docuit…

turgĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [turgidus], swollen : ocelli flendo, Cat. 3, 18 .

turgĭdus.opening: adj. turgeo , swollen , inflated , distended , turgid (class.; syn. tumidus). Lit. : membrum tumidum ac turgidum, Cic. Tusc. 3, 9, 19 : oculi, Plaut. Mil. 4, 3, 15 : labra, Mart. 6, 39, 8 : venter, App. M. 6, p. 176, 40…

turgor.opening: id. , a swelling , turgidity (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 2, § 135 ; 5, § 566 .

Tūrĭa.opening: a river in Hispania Tarraconensis, now the Turia or Guadalaviar , Mel. 2, 6, 6 ; Sall. H. 2, 96, 6 Dietsch; 2, 18 ib.—Called also , , , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 20 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or pertaining to Turia : proelium (in…

tūrĭbŭlum.opening: ( ), , tus . Lit. , a vessel to burn incense in , a censer , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 21, § 46 ; Liv. 29, 14, 13 ; Curt. 8, 9, 23 ; Val. Max. 3, 3 , ext. 1; Aus. Idyll. 12, 104 ; Prud. Apoth. 479 .— Transf. , a constellation ,…

tūrĭcrĕmus.opening: ( ), , adj. tuscremo , incense-burning , for burning incense ( poet. ): arae, Lucr. 2, 353 ; Verg. A. 4, 453 : foci, Ov. H. 2, 18 : ignes, Luc. 9, 989 .

tūrĭfĕr.opening: ( ), , adj. tusfero , incense-bearing , that bears , yields , or produces incense : Indus, Ov. F. 3, 720 : regio, Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 104 : Sabaei, Val. Fl. 6, 138 ; cf. Arabes, Claud. III. Cons. Hon. 71 : silvae, id.…

tūrĭfĭcātor.opening: ( ), , turifico , one that offers incense to the gods, i. e. an idolater , Aug. contr. Liter. Petil. c. 103.

tūrĭfĭco.opening: v. n. tus-facio , to burn incense , offer incense (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 87, 2 .—Hence, subst. : ( ), , , one that offers incense (to the gods), a term applied to those Christians who sacrificed to the heathen gods in…

tūrĭlĕgus.opening: adj. tus-lego , incense-gathering : Arabes, Ov. F. 4, 569 .

turĭo.opening: a shoot , sprout , tendril , young branch of a tree, Col. 12, 50, 5 ; Apic. 8, 1 .

Tŭrĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. Q. Turius, Cic. Fam. 12, 26, 1 .— C. Turius, Hor. S. 2, 1, 49 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to a Turius , Turian : hereditas, of Q. Turius , Cic Fam. 12, 26, 2: cassia, a peculiar kind so…

turma.opening: Sanscr. root tvar-, tur-, hasten; v. turba , a division of Roman cav alry, the tenth part of an ala, consisting at first of thirty, and afterwards of thirty-two men; a troop , squadron of horse. Lit. , Varr. L. L. 5,…

turmālis.opening: adj. turma , of or belong ing to a troop or squadron. Lit. , as subst. : , , : T. Manlius cum suis turmalibus evasit, i. e. with those of his squadron or troop , Liv. 8, 7, 1 ; 25, 18, 11 .— Transf. : non sanguine…

turmārĭi.opening: id. , recruiting officers of cavalry , Cod. Th. 6, 35, 3.

turmātim.opening: adv. id. . Lit. , by troops or squadrons : equites se turmatim explicare coeperunt, Caes. B. C. 3, 93 : nostri turmatim in eum devenerunt, Hirt. B. G. 8, 18 : vagantibus circa moenia turmatim barbaris, Liv. 5, 39, 5 :…

turpĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [turpis], ugly , foul , deformed. Lit. : nasus, Cat. 41, 3: res, Varr. L. L. 7, § 97 Müll.—* Trop. : jocus in (rebus) turpiculis et quasi deformibus ponitur, Cic. de Or. 2, 61, 248 .

turpīdo.opening: contr. from turpidudo , baseness , etc., Tert. Cor. Mil. 14 ; Cic. Rep. 1, 2, 2 MSS. (B. and K. turpitudinis; cf. Osann ad loc.).

turpĭfĭcātus.opening: adj. turpisfacio , made foul or filthy , debased , deformed , corrupted; trop.: foeditas turpificati animi. Cic. Off. 3, 29, 105 .

turpĭlŭcrus.opening: adj. m. [turpis-iucrum], making dishonest gain , Aug. Op. Mon. 13 .

turpis.opening: adj. Sanscr. root tarp-, to be ashamed , ugly , unsightly , unseemly , foul , filthy (class.; esp. freq. in a trop. sense; syn.: taeter, foedus, deformis, obscaenus, immundus). Lit. : aspectus deformis atque turpis,…

turpĭtūdo.opening: turpis , ugliness , unsightliness , foulness , deformity (syn. deformitas). Lit. (very rare): an est ullum malum majus turpitudine? Cic. Off. 3, 29, 105 : virtutis laude turpitudinem tegere, App. Mag. p. 283, 9 .— Trop.…

turpo.opening: v. a. id. , to make ugly or unsightly , to soil , defile , pollute , disfigure , deform (mostly poet. ; cf. deformo). Lit. : Jovis aram sanguine turpari, to be defiled or polluted , Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 35, 85 ; 3,…

Turrānĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens, esp., D. Turranius Niger, a friend of Varro and of Q. Cicero , Varr. R. R. 2 , praef. § 6; Cic. Att. 1, 6, 2 ; 6, 9, 2 ; 7, 1, 1 .— M. Turranius, a prœtor , Cic. Phil. 3, 10, 25 .— C.…

turrĭcŭla.opening: . , dim. turris . A little tower , a turret , Vitr. 10, 19 med. — = pyrgus, a kind of dice-box , shaped like a tower, Mart. 14, 16 in lemm.

turrĭger.opening: , gĕra. gĕrum. adj. turris-gero , turret-bearing , turreted. In gen. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): umeri elephantorum, Plin. 11, 2, 1, § 4 : ferae moles, Sil. 9, 560 : urbes, Verg. A. 10, 253 : ripae, Claud. Cons.…

turris.opening: ( acc. turrim and turrem; abl. turri and turre; v. Neue, Formenl. I. 196 sqq.), , = τύρρις . Lit. In gen., a tower : eā ballistā si pervortam turrim, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 59 : apud vetustam turrem, Att. ap. Prisc. p. 761…

turrītus.opening: adj. turris , set , furnished , or fortified with towers , towered , turreted , castled , castellated (mostly poet. ). Lit. Moenia, Ov. Am. 3, 8, 47 : muri, id. P. 3, 4, 105 : castella, Luc. 6, 39 : puppes, Verg. A. 8,…

tursĭo.opening: a kind of fish resembling the dolphin , a porpoise : Delphinus phocaena, Linn.; Plin. 9, 9, 11, § 34 .

turtur.opening: ( fem. turturis marinae os, Dict Cret. 6, 15; Plin. 30, 8, 21, § 68 ), a turtle-dove : Columba turtur, Linn.; Plin. 10, 34, 52, § 105 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 8 ; Col. 8, 9 ; Pall. 1, 25 ; Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 44 ; id. Bacch. 1,…

turtūrilla.opening: dim. turtur , a little turtle-dove; a term applied to an effeminate person, Sen. Ep. 96, 5 .

turunda.opening: A ball of paste for fattening geese, Cato, R. R. 89 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 20 .— A kind of sacrificial cake , Varr. ap. Non. 552, 3 .— A tent or roll of lint for wounds, Cato, R. R. 157, 14 ; Scrib. Comp. 201 .

tūs.opening: ( ), , from θύος, τό incense , frankincense. In gen., Plin. 12, 14, 30, § 51 ; Plaut. Poen. 2, 3 ; id. Trin. 4, 2, 89 ; id. Truc. 2, 5, 27 : accendere, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 35, § 77 ; id. Off. 3, 20, 80 ; Lucr. 3, 327 ;…

Tuscē.opening: adv. Tuscus , in the Tuscar language or manner : dicere, Gell. 11, 7, 4 cf. Varr. ib. 2, 25, 8 .

Tusci.opening: or , , , another name for Etrusci, the inhabitants of Etru ria , the Tuscans , Etruscans , Etrurians , Mel. 2, 4, 2 ; Liv. 2, 51, 1 ; 5, 33, 7 ; 5, 45, 4 ; Cic. Div. 2, 51, 106 al. —Hence, , , , Etruria , the Etruscan…

Tuscŭlānensis.opening: , e; , i; and, , , um; v. 2. Tusculum.

tuscŭlum.opening: ( ), , dim. tus , a little frankincense , Plaut. Aul. 2, 8, 15 .

Tuscŭlum.opening: a very ancient town of Latium , on a hill near the modern Frascati , Liv. 2, 15 sq. ; 6, 33 sq.; Cic. Font. 18, 41 ; id. Div. 1, 43, 98 ; 2, 45, 94 ; Hor. Epod. 1, 29 al. —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Tusculum ,…

tussēdo.opening: tussis , a cough , App. M. 9, p. 222, 38 .

tussĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little or slight cough , Cels. 3, 22 ; Plin. Ep. 5, 19, 6 ; Front. Ep. 1, 2 med.

tussĭcŭlāris.opening: adj. tussicula , of or belonging to a cough , good for a cough , cough- : medicamen, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 17, 172 ; id. Tard. 2, 13, § 77 : herba = tussilago, id. ib. 2, 7, 111 .

tussĭcŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , coughing much , subject to a cough : senilis aetas, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 13, 90 .

tussĭcus.opening: tussis , afflicted with a cough , Firm. Math. 5, 16; Marc. Emp. 20 .

tussiens.opening: one who has a cough : nuces tussientibus inimicae, Plin. 23, 8, 77, § 147 ; 21, 20, 83, § 140 ; 29, 3, 11, § 42 .

tussĭo.opening: v. n. tussis , to cough , to have a cough : forte si tussire occoeperit, ne sic tussiat, Ut cuiquam linguam in tussiendo proferat, Plaut. As. 4, 1, 49 sq. : male, Hor. S. 2, 5, 107 : crebro, Quint. 11, 5, 56 : plurimum,…

tūtācŭlum.opening: 1. tutor , a defence , means of protection , Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 387 .

tūtāmen.opening: id. , a means of defence , defence , protection ( poet. and postclass.): (lorica) decus et tutamen in armis, Verg. A. 5, 262 .— Plur. : domorum aut vestium, Arn. 2, 71 : deposcimus rebus fessis, id. 1, 15 .

tūtāmentum.opening: id. , a means of defence , defence , protection (rare; not anteAug.), Liv. 21, 61, 10 : circumspiciens tutamenta sermonis, App. M. 1, p. 105 ; Vulg. 1 Macc. 14, 37 .

Tūtānus.opening: id. , the name of a Roman guardian deity , who is fabled to have put Hannibal to flight , Varr. ap. Non. 47 fin. ; cf. Becker, Antiq. 4, p. 14; and v. Tutelina.— Plur. : Titanas vobis Tutanos dicitis esse, Commod. 20, 1…

tūtātĭo.opening: id. , a protecting , defending , protection , Firm. Math. 4, 7.

tūtātor.opening: id. , a protector , defender (post-class.): periculosis tutator, egenis opitulator, App. de Deo Socr. p. 52, 12 .

tūtēla.opening: 1. tutor , a watching , keeping , charge , care , safeguard , defence , protection (syn.: praesidium, cura). Lit. In gen.: tutelam januae gerere, Plaut. Truc. 2, 1, 43 : foribus tutelam gerere, id. Trin. 4, 2, 28 :…

tūtēlāris.opening: adj. tutela (post-class.). (Acc. to tutela, I. B.) Of or belonging to guardianship , tutelar , tutelary : causa, Dig. 12, 3, 4 : instrumenta, ib. 27, 7, 8 : anni, Sid. Ep. 4, 24 fin. : praetor, Capitol. M. Aur. 19 fin.…

tūtēlārĭus.opening: tutela, I. A. , one who has the care or custody of a thing, a keeper , warden , curator; of a building, Plin. 34, 7, 17, § 38 : PRAETOR, Inscr. Grut. 363, 2 ; 465, 5 .

tūtēlātor.opening: tutela , a protector , guardian; said of a genius, Mart. Cap. 2, § 152 .

tūtēlātus.opening: adj. id. , that is under protection : genus agri (with in tutelam rei urbanae assignatum), Aggen. Limit. Agr. p. 58 Goes.

Tūtēlīna.opening: or , , id. , a guardian deity , tutelar goddess. Of Rome, Varr. L. L. 5, § 163 Müll.; id. ap. Non. 247, 29 .— Of corn, Tert. Spect. 8 ; Macr. S. 1, 16 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 8; cf. Plin. 18, 1, 3, § 8 ; v. Tutanus.

Tūtĭcānus.opening: the name of a man , Ov. P. 4, 12, 10 sq. (where it is sportively scanned Tūtĭcănumque and Tūtĭcănui, to show that it cannot stand in elegiac verse).

Tutĭenses.opening: an ancient people of Latium , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 69 .

Tutĭlĭus.opening: the name of a rhetorician of Rome , Plin. Ep. 6, 32, 1 ; Quint. 3, 1, 21 ; Mart. 5, 56, 6 .

tūtō.opening: adv. , v. tueor, P. a. fin.

tūtor.opening: ( inf. parag. tutarier, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 41 ), 1, v. dep. a. [tueor], to watch , guard , keep , protect , defend. Lit. (class.; syn. tueor): tutatus est domum, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 196 : rem eri (servus), id. Men. 5, 6, 4…

tūtōrĭus.opening: adj. 1. tutor , of or belonging to a guardian : tutorio nomine regnum administrare, Just. 30, 3, 4 .

tutrix.opening: f [id.], a female guardian , tutrix. Lit. : filiarum suarum, Cod. Just. 5, 35, 3 .— Transf. , of the Muses, Fulg. Myth. praef. fin.

tūtŭbo.opening: v. n. onomatop. , to cry like an owl , to hoot : noctua lucifugax tutubat in tenebris, Auct. Carm. Philom. 41 (al. cucubat); cf. Plaut. Men. 4, 2, 96 .

tŭtŭlātus.opening: adj. tutulus , having or wearing a tutulus, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 44 Müll.; and in Fest. s. v. tutulum, pp. 354 and 355 ib. (Ann. v. 124 Vahl.), Pompon. ap. Non. 19, 16 .

tŭtŭlus.opening: a high head-dress , formed by plaiting the hair in a cone over the forehead , worn esp. by the Flamen and his wife, Tert. Pall. 4 fin. ; cf. Varr. L. L. 7, § 44 Müll.; Fest. pp 354 and 355 ib.; and v. Böttig. Sabina, 1,…

Tūtūnus.opening: , i. q. Priapus , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 11; Arn. 4, 131 and 133.

tūtus.opening: Part. and P. a. of tueor.

tŭus.opening: pron. poss. [tu], thy , thine , your , yours. Lit. In gen.: tuŏs est servus, Plaut. Am. 2, 1, 63 : ex tuā accepi manu, id. ib. 2, 2, 132 : imperium tuom, id. ib. 2, 1, 84 : Me. Quojus nunc es? So. Tuos, nam pugnis usu…

tuxtax.opening: , an exclamation imitative of the sound of blows: tuxtax meo tergo erit, Plaut. Pers. 2, 3, 12 ; cf. Naev. ap. Charis. 2, p. 185 P. (Com. Fragm. v. 6 Rib.), tax pax.

Tўăna.opening: , = Τύανα , a city in Cappadocia , the birthplace of the philosopher Apollonius , now Kiz Hissar , Plin. 6, 3, 3, § 8 ; Amm. 23, 6, 19 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Tyana : incola, Ov. M. 8, 719 .—Collat. form…

Tyba.opening: a village on the Euphrates , now Taibe , Cic. Fam. 15, 1, 2

Tўcha.opening: , = Τύχη (fortuna), the name of a part of Syracuse in the west of the Achradina , called after the temple of the goddess Τύχη , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 53, § 119 ; Liv 24, 21, 7; 25, 25, 5.

Tўchĭus.opening: , = Τυχίος (Hom. II. 7, 220), a celebrated shoemaker of Bœotia , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 196 ; Ov. F 3, 824 .

Tȳdeus.opening: ( ), , , = Τυδεύς , the son of Œneus and Periboea , and father of Diomedes , Verg. A. 6, 479 ; Stat. Th. 8, 664 ; Hyg. Fab. 69 and 70.—Hence, , , , the son of Tydeus , i. e. Diomedes , Verg. A. 1, 97 ; 1, 471 ; 2, 164 ;…

tympănĭŏlum.opening: dim. tympanum , a small drum , a taboret , tambourine , Arn. 6 fin.

tympănista.opening: , = τυμπανιστής , a drummer , taborer , App. de Deo Socr. p 49, 19.

tympănistrĭa.opening: , = τυμπανίστρια , a female drummer or player on the tambourine , Sid. Ep. 1, 2 fin. ; Vulg. Psa. 67, 26 ; Inscr. Orell. 2451 .

tympănītes.opening: , = τυμπανίτης , a kind of dropsy that swells the belly like a drum , tympanites , Veg. Vet. 1, 43 ; Cael. Aur Tard. 3, 8, 101 (in Cels. 3, 21 , written as Greek).

tympănītĭcus.opening: , = τυμπανιτικός , one who is afflicted with tympanites , a dropsical person , Plin. 25, 5, 24, § 60 ; Veg. Vet. 3, 27 .

tympănĭum.opening: , = τυμπάνιον a precious stone shaped like a tambourine , Plin. 9, 35, 54, § 109 ; Dig. 34, 2, 32, § 9 .

tympănīzans.opening: Part. [ τυμπανίζω ], playing on a drum or timbrel , Suet. Aug. 68 fin.

tympănŏtrĭba.opening: , = τυμπανοτρίβης , a taborer , a timbrel-player , a term of reproach for a soft, effeminate person (alluding to the priests of Cybele), Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 49 ; cf. tympanum.

tympănum.opening: (collat. form , Cat. 63, 8 sq. ), , = τύμπανον , a drum , timbrel , tambour , tambourine. Lit. Esp., as beaten by the priests of Cybele, Lucr. 2, 618 ; Cat. 63, 8 sq. ; Verg. A. 9, 619 ; Ov. M. 3, 537 ; 4, 29 ; 4, 391 ;…

Tyndăreus.opening: (trisyl.; but quadrisyl. Ov. H. 8, 31 ; 17, 250 ), ĕï ( , , Hyg. Fab. 77 ; 78 ; Lact. 1, 10, 11 ), , = Τυνδάρευς , a king of Sparta , son of Œbalus , and husband of Leda; he was the father of Castor and Pollux , and of…

Tўphōeus.opening: ( ), , , = Τυφωεύς , a giant , struck with lightning by Jupiter and buried under Mount Ætna , Verg. A. 9, 716 ; Ov. M. 5, 321 sq. ; id. F. 4, 491 ; Hor. C. 3, 4, 53 ; Sil. 14, 196 al. —As a gigantic monster, called…

tȳphon.opening: , = τυφών . A violent whirlwind , a typhoon , Plin. 2, 48, 49, § 131 ; App de Mundo, p. 64, 5.—The same accompanied by lightning, Val. Fl. 3, 130 . Hence, , , adj. : ventus, a typhoon, Vulg. Act. 27, 14 .— A name given…

Tȳphōn.opening: (scanned Tўphōn, Mart Cap. 2, 43), ōnis, another name for the giart Typhōeus , Luc. 4, 595 ; 6, 92 ; Ov. F 2, 461 ; Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 22 ; Hyg. Fab. 152 . Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Typhon , Typhonian :…

tȳphus.opening: , = τῦφος , pride (late Lat.): inentis elatio et typhus qui appellatur a Graecis, Arn. 2, 43 ; 2, 53 ; 2, 56 ; 2, 63; 2, 88; Aug. Conf. 3, 3 ; 7, 9 ; Mart. Cap. 5, § 566 .

tўpĭcālis.opening: adj. typicus , typical (late Lat.), Inc. Visit. Infirm. 2, 4.

tўpĭcus.opening: adj. , = τυπικός , figurative , typical : typicus Moses (Christus), Sedul. 3, 208 : cruor, id. 1, 192 .— Periodical , recurring at intervals : tremor, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 15, 95 : accessiones, id. Tard. 3 , S, 118.

tўpus.opening: , = τύπος . A figure , image , on a wall, Cic. Att. 1, 10, 3 ; Plin. 35, 12, 43, § 151 ; Lampr. Heliog. 3 and 7.— In medic. lang., a form , type , character of intermittent fevers, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 14, 108 ; App.…

tўranna.opening: f [tyrannus], a princess , a female tyrant (with tyrannis), Treb. XXX. Tyr. 31 fin.

tўrannĭcīda.opening: tyrannus-caedo , a killer of a tyrant , a tyrannicide , Sen. Ira, 2, 23, 1 ; Plin. 7, 23, 23, § 87 ; Suet. Tib. 4 ; id. Vit. Luc.; Quint. 5, 10, 36 ; 5, 10, 59 ; 7, 3, 7 ; 7, 7, 2; 7, 7, 5; Tac. Or. 35 .

tўrannĭcīdĭum.opening: id. , the killing of a tyrant , tyrannicide , Sen. Contr. 1, 7 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 72 ; Quint. 7, 3, 10 .

tўrannĭcus.opening: adj. , = τυραννικός , tyrannous , tyrannical : tetrum facinus, crudele, nefarium, tyrannicum, Auct. Her. 2, 30, 49 : leges, Cic. Leg. 1, 15, 42 : ira, Sen. Ben. 1, 11, 2 : crudelitas, Just. 16, 4, 11 : dominatio, id.…

Tўrannĭo.opening: a grammarian and geographer contemporary with Cicero , Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 4, 2 ; id. Att. 2, 6, 1 ; 4, 4 , b, 1; 4, 8, a, 2.

tўrannis.opening: ( acc. tyrannida, Cic. Att. 14, 14, 2 ), , = τυραννίς . The sway of a tyrant , arbitrary or despotic rule , tyranny : o di boni! vivit tyrannis, tyrannus occidit, Cic. Att. 14, 9, 2 ; cf.: sublato tyranno tyrannida…

tўrannoctŏnus.opening: , = τυραννοκτόνος , the killer of a tyrant : nostri tyrannoctoni, Cic. Att. 14, 15, 2 ; 16, 15, 3 .

tyrannŏpŏlīta.opening: , = τυραννοπολίτης , a citizen of a town ruled by a tyrant , Sid. Ep. 5, 8 .

tўrannus.opening: , = τύραννος . In gen., a monarch , ruler , sovereign , king (rare, and mostly poet. ): tyrannusque fuerat appellatus (Miltiades), sed justus ... omnes autem et dicuntur et habentur tyranni, qui potestate sunt perpetuā…

Tўras.opening: , = Τύρας , a river in Sarmatia , now the Dniester , Mel. 2, 1, 7 ; Ov. P. 4, 10, 50 .—Called also , Plin. 4, 12, 26 . § 82.

tўrĭanthĭnus.opening: adj. , = τυριάνθινος , of a cotor between purple and violet : pallium. Vop. Carin. 19 .—As subst. : , ōrum. , garments of a purpleviolet color , Mart. 1, 54, 5 .

Tȳro.opening: , = Τυρώ , a daughter of Salmoneus , Prop. 2, 28, 51 (3, 26, 5); Hyg. Fab. 60 ; 254 .

tȳrŏpătĭna.opening: vox hibrida from τυρός, cheese, and patina , a kind of cheesecake , Apic. 7, 11 fin.

tȳrŏtărīchŏs.opening: , = τυροτάριχος , a dish of salt-fish prepared with cheese , Cic. Fam. 9, 16, 7 ; 9, 16, 9 ; id. Att. 4, 8 , a, 1; 14, 16, 1.— Adj. : patella tyrotaricha, Apic. 4, 2 med.

Tyrrhēni.opening: , = Τυρρηνοί , the Tyrrhenians , a Pelasgian people who migrated to Italy and formed the parent stock of the Etrurians , Verg. A. 11, 171 ; 11, 733 ; Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 50 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the…

Tyrrheus.opening: ( ), , or , , , the shepherd of King Latinus , Verg. A. 7, 485 .—Hence, , , , the sons of Tyrrheus , Verg. A. 7, 484 .

Tyrtaeus.opening: , = Τυρταῖος , an Athenian poet , who flourished about 680 B.C., Hor. A. P. 402 ; Just. 3, 5 .

Tўrus.opening: or , , , = Τύρος (Heb. ). Lit. , Tyre , a famous maritime and commercial city of the Phœnicians , especially celebrated for its purple , now the ruins of Soor , Mel. 1, 12, 2 ; Plin. 5, 19, 17, § 76 ; Curt. 4, 2 sq. ;…

U.opening: (orig. V, v, a modification of the Greek Υ , Marc. Vict. p. 2459 P.), the twentieth letter of the Latin alphabet ( i and j being counted as one), a vowel, which was early distinguished by the old grammarians from the…

Ubĭi.opening: a Germanic people , who in Cœsar's time occupied the territory on the east bank of the Rhine , near the mod. Cologne , but were transferred to the left bank of the Rhine by Agrippa , B. C. 39, Caes. B. G. 1, 54 ; 4, 3 ;…

Ucubis.opening: ( acc. -im; abl. -i), a city of Hispania Baetica. Auct. B. Hisp. 7; 24.

Uffugum.opening: a town in the territory of the Bruttii , now Fagnano , Liv. 30, 19 .

ulcĕrārĭa.opening: (sc. herba) [ulcus], the plant horehound , App. Herb. 45 .

ulcĕrātĭo.opening: ulcero , a breaking out into sores , ulceration; a sore , ulcer , Plin. 34, 11, 27, § 115 (dub.; al. exulcerationes). —In plur. , Sen. Const. 6, 3 .

ulcĕro.opening: v. a. ulcus , to make sore , cause to ulcerate (rare but class.). Lit. : nondum ulcerato Philocteta serpentis morsu, Cic. Fat. 16, 36 : mantica cui lumbos onere ulceret, Hor. S. 1, 6, 106 .— * Trop. : non ancilla tuum…

ulcĕrōsus.opening: adj. ulcus , full of sores , ulcerous (very rare; not in Cic.). Lit. : facies, Tac. A. 4, 57 .— Transf. , of trees, knobby , full of knots , Plin. 17, 14, 24, § 106 .—* Trop. : jecur, i. e. wounded (with love), Hor. C.…

ulciscor.opening: v. inch. dep. [etym. dub.]. To avenge one's self on , take vengeance on , or punish for wrong done (very freq. and class.; cf.: vindico, punio, persequor). With a personal object: ego pol illum ulciscar hodie Thessalum…

ulcuscŭlum.opening: dim. ulcus , a small sore or ulcer , Cels. 5, 28, 15 ; Sen. Ep. 72, 5 ; Plin. 28, 19, 78, § 259 .

Ulĭa.opening: a town of Hispania Baetica, Auct. B. Hisp. 3; Auct. B. Alex. 61; Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 15 .

ullātĕnus.opening: adv. ullus-tenus , in any respect whatever , Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 21 ; Greg. Ep. 2, 8.

ullus.opening: , um; gen. ullīus; dat. ulli ( gen. sing. ulli, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 38 ), adj. dim. [for unulus, dim. of unus], any , any one (usu. in neg. sentences; corresp. with aliquis in affirmations). In negative declarations (so…

ulmārĭum.opening: ulmus , a plantation or nursery of elms , Plin. 17, 11, 15, § 76 .

ulmĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to an elm-tree , of elm , elm- : frons, Col. 6, 3, 6 : cena, Juv. 11, 141 : virgae, i. e. rods for whipping with , Plaut. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 1, 478 : qui tibi subnectabant rure huc virgas…

ulmĭtrĭba.opening: vox hibrida, from ulmus and τρίβω, tero , an elm-rubber, i. e. one that wears out elms , is often beaten with elm-rods , a term of abuse, Plaut. Pers. 2, 4, 7 ; cf. ulmus.

ulna.opening: Gr. ὠλένη; Goth. aleina; Germ. Elle; cf. Ellenbogen; Engl. ell , the elbow. Lit. , Plin. 11, 43, 98, § 243 .— Transf. Poet. , in gen., the arm : tremula patris dormientis in ulnā, Cat. 17, 13 ; Prop. 2, 18 (3, 10), 9;…

Ulpĭānus.opening: : Domitius Ulpianus, a celebrated Roman jurist under the emperors Septimius Severus , Caracalla , Heliogabalus , and Alexander Severus , fragments of whose writings are found in the Pandects; he was murdered in Gaul ,…

ulpĭcum.opening: a kind of leek , Cato, R. R. 71 ; Col. 11, 3, 20 ; 10, 113 ; Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 35 .

Ulpius.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So esp., M. Ulpius Trajanus, the celebrated Roman emperor of that name. —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Ulpius : porticus, Sid. Carm. 8, 8 .

uls.opening: ( ; v. infra ), prep. with acc. [from the pronominal root il, whence ille], beyond; opp. to cis (ante-class.): uls Cato pro ultra posuit, Fest. p. 379 Müll.: ouls lucum facutalem (followed by cis lucum Esquilinum),…

ulter.opening: adj. ( comp. ulterior, us; sup. ultimus) [cf.: uls, ollus, olim; and the advv. ultra, ultro], prop. that is beyond or on the other side. The posit. is not found, but the comp. and sup. are very freq. Comp. : , , farther…

ultĭmō.opening: adv. , v. ultimus, under ulter, II. B. 1. fin.

ultĭmo.opening: v. n. ultimus , to come to an end , be at the last : cum ultimarent tempora patriae, Tert. Pall. 1 fin.

ultĭmum.opening: adv. , v. ultimus, under ulter, II. B. 1. fin.

ultĭo.opening: ulciscor , a taking vengeance , avenging , revenge (not ante-Aug.; cf. vindicta): quamquam serum auxilium perditis erat, tamen ultionem petens, Liv. 31, 24, 1 : ultionem violatae per vim pudicitiae confessa viro est,…

ultor.opening: ulciscor , a punisher , avenger , revenger. In gen. (class.): conjurationis investigator atque ultor, Cic. Sull. 30, 85 : Publius nostrarum injuriarum ultor, id. Brut. 77, 268 ; id. Pis. 10, 23 : exoriare aliquis…

ultōrĭus.opening: adj. ultor , of or belonging to vengeance , avenging (post-class.): mala, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 24 .

ultrā.opening: adv. and prep. ulter . Adv. Prop., on the other side : dextera nec citra mota nec ultra, neither on that side nor on this, neither backwards nor forwards, Ov. M. 5, 186 .— Transf. , in gen., beyond , farther , over ,…

ultrā-mundānus.opening: adj. , that is beyond the world , ultra - mundane (postclass.): ille deus, App. Dogm. Plat. 8, 7 : pater, Mart. Cap. 2, § 185 .

ultrix.opening: adj. ultor , avenging , vengeful. Adj. ( poet. ): ultricesque sedent in limine Dirae, the avenging goddesses , i. e. the Furies , Verg. A. 4, 473 ; cf. Furiae, Claud. Ep. 1, 14 ; and, deae, Sen. Med. 967 : Curae, Verg.…

ultrō^.opening: adv. , to the farther side , beyond , on the other side. Lit. , so most usually in the connection ultro citroque, Cic. Rep. 6, 9, 9 ; id. Ac. 1, 7, 28 ; Caes. B. G. 1, 42 ; Liv. 3, 5, 11 ; Auct. B. Hisp. 21: ultro et…

ultrōnĕĭtas.opening: ultroneus , freewill , voluntariness : ultroneitas, quam libertatem arbitrii dicimus, Fulg. Myth. 3, 6 fin.

ultrōnĕus.opening: adj. ultro , of one's own accord , voluntary (late Lat.): exsilium, App. M. 1, p. 111, 15 : ultroneam te dominae tuae reddis (i. e. ultro, tuā sponte), voluntarily, id. ib. 6 , p. 175, 17; cf. id. Flor. 2, p. 350, 10 ;…

ultrorsum.opening: adv. contr. from ultroversum , farther onwards : pergere, Sulp. Sev. Hist. Sacr. 2, 26 .

ulucus.opening: a screech-owl , = ulula, Serv. Verg. E. 8, 55 (al. alucos).

Ulurtīni.opening: a people of Lower Italy , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 105 .

ulvōsus.opening: adj. ulva , abounding in sedge , Sid. Ep. 1, 5 ; id. Carm. 7, 324 .

umbella.opening: dim. umbra (a little shadow, i. e. meton.), a sunshade , parasol , umbrella , Mart. 14, 28 in lemm.; 11, 73, 6; Juv. 9, 50 .

umbĭlīcāris.opening: adj. umbilicus , of or belonging to the navel , umbilical : nervus, the navel-string, umbilical cord, Tert. Carn. Chr. 20 med.

umbĭlīcātus.opening: adj. id. , navel-shaped , umbilicate : in alvo mediā plerisque umbilicatum, Plin. 13, 4, 7, § 32 .

umbĭlīcus.opening: akin to ὀμφαλός , the navel. Lit. , Cels. 7, 14 ; 6, 17 ; Plin. 11, 37, 89, § 220 ; Liv. 26, 45, 8 ; Auct. B. Afr. 85, 1; Isid. Orig. 11, 1 .— Transf. The umbilical cord , Cels. 7, 29, § 41 .— The middle , centre : dies…

umbo.opening: kindr. with ἄμβων, ὀμφαλός, umbilicus; Germ. Nabel; Engl. navel ; prop. any convex elevation; hence, A boss of a shield, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 3 (Ann. v. 432 Vahl.); Verg. A. 2, 546 : scutis magis quam gladiis geritur…

umbra.opening: etym. dub.; Curt. compares Sanscr. ambara, an encircling , a shade , shadow. Lit. : cum usque quaque umbra est, tamen Sol semper hic est, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 79 : illa platanus, cujus umbram secutus est Socrates, Cic. de…

umbrācŭlum.opening: umbra ( any thing that furnishes shade ). Lit. , a shady place , bower , arbor , Varr. R. R. 1, 51, 2 ; Cic. Fragm. ap. Macr. S. 6, 4 ; Verg. E. 9, 42 .— Transf. , a school : in solem et pulverem, ut e Theophrasti…

umbrālĭter.opening: adv. id. , figuratively , metaphorically , Aug. Ep. 37 fin.

umbrātĭcŏla.opening: umbra-colo , one who is fond of the shade , an effeminate person , a lounger , = umbraticus homo, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 60 .

umbrātĭcus.opening: adj. umbra , of or belonging to the shade , i. e. to retirement , seclusion , or leisure : homo, i. e. who loves to stay in the shade, an idler, lounger, Plaut. Curc. 4, 3, 24 .— Esp., retired , private , contemplative…

umbrātĭlis.opening: adj. id. , remaining in the shade , in retirement , or at home; private , retired , contemplative. In gen.: vita umbratilis et delicata, a dreamy life, Cic. Tusc. 2, 11, 27 : mora segnis et umbratilis, Col. 1, 2, 1 :…

umbrātĭo.opening: umbro , a shadowing : sequebatur columna nubis quasi umbratio Spiritus Sancti, Ambros. Sacr. 1, 6, § 22 .

Umbrēnus.opening: , Publius, a fellowconspirator with Catiline , Cic. Cat. 3, 6, 14 ; Sall. C. 40, 1 sqq.

umbresco.opening: v. inch. n. [umbra], to shadow , become shadowy , darken , Cassiod. Compl. Apoc. 3 .

Umbri.opening: a people of Italy , in the district of Umbria , which was named after them , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 50 ; 3, 14, 19, § 112 ; Liv. 5, 35 ; 9, 37 sq.—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Umbrians , Umbrian : porcus, Cat. 39,…

Umbricĭus.opening: a haruspex in the service of Otho , Tac. H. 1, 27 .

umbrĭfĕr.opening: adj. umbra-fero . Shade-bringing , shade-giving , casting a shade , shady : platanus, Cic. poët. Div. 2. 30, 63: nemus, Verg. A. 6, 473 : rupes, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 11 : Academia, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 13, 22.— (Acc. to…

umbro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
umbro.opening: v. a. and n. umbra , to shade , shadow , overshadow , overspread , cover; to make or cast a shade (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic.). Lit. : (quercus) Umbrabat coma summi fastigia montis, Sil. 5, 488 :…

umbrōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of shade , shady , umbrageous (class.; cf. opacus): locus umbrosior, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2, § 3 : fere aquosissima sunt quaecumque umbrosissima, Sen. Q. N. 3, 11, 4 : fico folium maximum umbrosissimumque,…

umquam.opening: ( ), adv. temp. [etym dub.], at any time , ever (opp. never; cf. aliquando); most freq. in neg. clauses, sometimes also in interrogations and in conditional clauses; but very seldom in affirmations. In neg. clauses.…

uncātĭo.opening: uncatus , a bending inwards , a hooking , curving : unguium, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 32 med.

uncātus.opening: adj. uncus , bent inwards , hooked , curved (post-class.). Lit. : lanceae, Sid. Ep. 4, 20 .— Transf. , bent down , bowed down : ut quidam uncati permaneant, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 3, 57 .— Trop. , hooked , barbed :…

uncĭa.opening: , = οὐγκία (Siculian and Etruscan; v. Müller, Etrusk. 1, p. 309 sq.) [akin to unus, unicus, unio; Gr. οἰνός ], the twelfth part of any thing, a twelfth. Lit. Of inheritances: mortuus Babullius. Caesar, opinor, ex unciā,…

uncĭālis.opening: adj. uncia , of or belonging to a twelfth part , amounting to a twelfth part : asses, i. e. weighing an ounce, Plin. 33, 3, 13, § 45 ; so, uva, id. 14, 3, 4, § 42 : altitudo, of an inch, id. 18, 16, 43, § 146 ; so,…

uncĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a twelfth part , containing a twelfth : heres, i. e. who inherits a twelfth part, Dig. 30, 1, 34 fin. : fenus, i. e. one twelfth of the principal was returned annually as interest, or 8 1/3…

uncĭātim.opening: adv. id. , by twelfths , by ounces. * Lit. : (axungia) datur et phthisicis unciatim, cum vini veteris hemina decocta, donec tres unciae e toto restent, Plin. 28, 9, 37, § 139 .—* Transf. , by a little at a time , little…

uncīnātus.opening: adj. uncinus , furnished with hooks or tenters , barbed : hamata uncinataque corpora, Cic. Ac. 2, 38, 121 .

uncīnus.opening: 1. uncus , a hook , barb (late Lat. for 1. uncus), App. M. 3, p. 135, 39 ; Pall. Mart. 10, 29 ; Vnlg. Exod. 28, 13. —As adj. : hamus, barbed, Paul. Nol. Carm. 20, 270 .

uncĭŏla.opening: dim. uncia , a little ounce , Juv. 1, 40 .

uncĭ-pēs.opening: adj. 2. uncus , having feet bent in , crook-footed , Tert. Pall. 5 .

unco.opening: v. n. , to sound or roar like a bear , Carm. Philom. 50.

unctĭo.opening: ungo , a besmearing. anointing. Lit. : sudatoriae, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 73 : cottidiana, Col. 12, 53, 3 . philosophorum omnes unctionis causā relinquunt, i. e. to go and anoint themselves for wrestling in the palæstra,…

unctĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to besmear or anoint often (ante-class.): se unguentis, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 117 : flavo cinere (crinem), Cato ap. Serv. Verg. A. 4, 698 .

unctĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [unctus, from ungo], somewhat unctuous : pulmentum, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 85 .

unctor.opening: ungo , an anointer , Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 22 ; Mart. 12, 70, 3 ; 7, 32, 6 ; 12, 70, 3 ; Cic. Fam. 7, 24, 2 ; Quint. 11, 3, 26 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 10, 2; Inscr. Orell. 2791 ; Inscr. Grut. 785, 5 .

unctōrĭum.opening: (sc. cubiculum) [unctor], the anointing-room in a bath, Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 11 ; cf. elaeothesium.

unctŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [unctus, from ungo], besmeared , anointed. Adj. : circumtonsi et terti atque unctuli, Varr. ap. Non. 179, 8 .—* Subst. : , , , a little ointment , App. M. 3, p. 139, 2 .

unctūra.opening: ungo , an anointing of the dead: servilis, Cic. Leg. 2, 24, 60 .

unctus.opening: ungo , an anointing , anointment : oleum unctui profer, App. M. 1, p. 113, 3 : cochlearum cinis cum melle unctu sanat, Plin. 30, 10, 27, § 90 (al. linitu).

uncus.opening: adj. 1. uncus , hooked , bent in , crooked , curved , barbed ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: curvus, recurvus): uncus hamus, Ov. M. 15, 476 ; also called unca aera, id. P. 2, 7, 10 : cornua (tauri), Prop. 2, 5, 19…

unda.opening: Sanscr. root ud-, und-, to be wet; whence, uda, water; Angl. -Sax. ydhu, wave; Slav. voda, water; Gr. ὕδωρ, ὑάδες; Goth. vatō, water , a wave , billow , surge (syn. fluctus). Lit. : mare plenum undarum, Plaut. Mil. 2,…

undābundus.opening: adj. undo , full of waves , surging , billowy (post-class.): mare, Gell. 2, 30, 3 : aquae, Amm. 17, 7, 11 .

undātim.opening: adv. undo , in a waving manner , like waves : mensae undatim crispae, Plin. 13, 15, 30, § 96 : crispum marmor, id. 36, 7, 11, § 55 .— In a throng , Amm. 21, 3, 2 .

undĕ.opening: adv. , from which place , whence. Lit. , of place. Correlatively: petere inde coronam Unde prius nulli velarint tempora musae, Lucr. 4, 5 : nec enim inde venit, unde mallem, Cic. Att. 13, 39, 2 : ibi, unde huc translata…

undēcēni.opening: , a false read. for undenis, Plin. 36, 8, 14, § 65 .

undēcentēsĭmus.opening: num. adj. unde-centum , the ninety-ninth : annus, Val. Max. 8, 7 , ext. 11.

undēcentum.opening: num. adj. unus-decentum , ninety-nine : anni, Plin. 7, 60, 60, § 214 .

undĕcĭes.opening: num. adv. [unus-decies], eleven times : hanc summam undecies multiplicato, fiunt, etc., Col. 5, 2, 7 : surrexi unā cenā, Mart. 5, 79, 1 .

undĕcĭm.opening: num. adj. unus-decem , eleven : legiones, Cic. Fam. 6, 18, 2 : milia debeo, Mart. 2, 44, 8 ; Vitr. 3, 1 med. : dies, Macr. S. 1, 13 .

undĕcĭmus.opening: num. adj. unusdecimus , the eleventh : legio, Liv. 30, 18, 10 : annus, Verg. E. 8, 39 : dies, Plin. 11, 54, 118, § 283 .

undĕcĭrēmis.opening: (sc. navis) [undecim-remus], a ship of eleven banks of oars , Plin. 16, 40, 76, § 203 .

undĕcŭmāni.opening: undecimus , soldiers of the eleventh legion , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 107 .

undĕ-cumque.opening: ( ; in tmesi: unde vacefit cumque locus, Lucr. 6, 1017 ), adv. , from wherever , whencesoever , from what place or part soever (post-Aug.): undecumque moti sunt (fluctus), Sen. Vit. Beat. 27, 3 : fluens sanguis, Plin.…

undĕ-lĭbet.opening: adv. , whence you will , whencesoever , from any place whatever , from anywhere (very rare): invenire, Auct. Her. 4, 50, 63 : fascia undelibet super fracturam incipere debet, Cels. 8, 10, 1 . —Also rel. , from whatever…

undēnārĭus.opening: adj. undeni , containing eleven : numerus, Aug. Serm. 51 fin. ; 83 med.

un-dēni.opening: num. distrib. adj. [unus], eleven each , eleven distributively: pariuntur undeni, Plin. 11, 25, 30, § 91 : cubitis, id. 36, 8, 14, § 65 Sillig N. cr. : Musa per undenos emodulanda pedes, i. e. with a hexameter and…

undēnōnāginta.opening: num. adj. unus-denonaginta , eighty-nine : classis undenonaginta navium, Liv. 37, 30, 1 .

undĕoctōginta.opening: num. adj. unus-deoctoginta , seventy-nine : unde-Octoginta annos natus, Hor. S. 2, 3, 118 .

undēquadrāgēsĭmus.opening: num. adj. undequadraginta , the thirty-ninth : volumen, Val. Max. 8, 7 , ext. 10.

undēquadrāgies.opening: or , num. adv. [id.], thirty - nine times : dimicare, Plin. 7, 25, 25, § 92 .

undēquadrāginta.opening: num. adj. unusde-quadraginta , thirty - nine : anni, Cic. Rep. 2, 14, 27 .

undēquinquāgēsĭmus.opening: num. adj. undequinquaginta , the forty-ninth dies, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 12, 35 ; Vell. 2, 17, 3 .

undēquinquāginta.opening: num. adj. unus de-quinquaginta , forty-nine : coronae aureae, Liv. 37, 58, 4 : genera, Plin. 13, 4, 9, § 40 .

undēsexāgēsĭmus.opening: num. adj. undesexaginta , the fifty-ninth : pars, Censor. de Die Nat. 19 .

undēsexaginta.opening: num. adj. unus-desexaginta , fifty-nine : undesexaginta (Carthaginiensium) vivi capti, Liv. 23, 37, 6 : dies, Plin. 36, 15, 24, § 122 .

undētrīcēni.opening: num. distr. adj. [undetriginta], twenty-nine each , twentynine distributively: menses undetricenum tricenumque (dierum) numero alternaverunt, Macr. S. 1, 13, § 4 .

undētrīcēsĭmus.opening: or , , num. adj. id. , the twentyninth : dies, Liv. 25, 36, 14 : in commentariorum undetricesimo, Gell. 10, 5, 1 .

undētrīginta.opening: num. adj. unus-detriginta , twenty-nine : menses, Vitr. 9, 4 : dies, Macr. S. 1, 15, § 6 .

undēvīcēni.opening: num. distr. adj. [undeviginti], nineteen each , nineteen distributively: pedes, Quint. 1, 10, 44 .

undēvīcēsĭmāni.opening: undevicesimus , soldiers of the nineteenth legion : cum quinque cohortibus undevicesimanorum egreditur, Auct. B. Alex. 57, 2; Tac. A. 1, 51 .

undēvīcēsĭmus.opening: or , , adj. undeviginti , the nineteenth : anno undevicesimo post ejus mortem, Cic. Sen. 5, 14 : expleto aetatis undevicesimo anno, Quint. 6, praef. § 4 ; Tac. A. 1, 45 (al. unetvicesimus): die undevigesimo, Col. 8, 5,…

undēvīginti.opening: num. adj. unus-de-viginti , nineteen : undeviginti annos natus. Cic. Brut. 64, 229 : signa militaria, Liv. 23, 46, 4 .

undĭcŏla.opening: unda-colo , wavedwelling , i. e. inhabiting the waves , dwelling in the sea : Naïades, Varr. ap. Non. p. 250, 14 : pistris, Avien. Arat. 808 .

undī^flŭus.opening: adj. unda-fluo , flow ing with waves : amnes, Dracont. Hexaëm. 1, 607.

undĭfrăgus.opening: adj. unda-frango , wave-breaking , that breaks the waves or water : fluctus, Ven. 3 prol.

undĭquĕ.opening: adv. indef. [unde-que, prop. whencesoever; hence], from all parts , sides , or places , from every quarter , on all sides , on every part , everywhere : ut undique uno tempore in hostes impetus fieret, Caes. B. G. 1, 22…

undĭsŏnus.opening: adj. unda-sono , wave-sounding , sounding or roaring with the waves ( poet. ): rupes, Stat. Achill. 1, 198 : saxum, Val. Fl. 4, 44 : Psamathe, id. 1, 364 : dei, i. e. sea-gods, Prop. 3 (4), 21, 18.

undĭvăgus.opening: adj. unda-vagus , wandering in waves (late Lat.): latices, Coripp. Johan. 6, 342: salum, id. ib. 7, 344 : Tethys, Anthol. Lat. 2, p. 303 Burm.

undo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
undo.opening: v. n. and a. [unda]. Neutr. , to rise in waves or surges , to throw up waves , to surge , swell ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : undantem salum, Enn. ap. Non. 223, 24 (Trag. v. 226 Vahl.); cf.: undanti in freto,…

undōsus.opening: adj. unda , full of waves or surges , surgy , billowy : aequor, Verg. A. 4, 313 : Plemyrium, id. ib. 3, 693 : regna, Sil. 5, 21 .— Comp. : fluctus, Sol. 12 fin. — Sup. : torrentes, Aug. Civ. Dei , 27, 11. — Adv. : , in…

undŭlātus.opening: adj. undo, I. B. 2. and II. p. a. , diversified as with waves (like watered stuffs), undulated : togae, Varr. ap. Non. 189, 26 (cited also in Plin. 8, 48, 74, § 195 ).

Unelli.opening: a people in Gallia Lugdunensis, bordering on the Curiosolitœ and Lexovii , whose country formed part of the Tractus Armoricus; their chief city was Constantini Castra, now Coutances , Caes. B. G. 2, 34 ; 3, 11 ; 3, 17 ;…

ungella.opening: ( ), , dim. ungula , a little claw or talon , Apic. 4, 5 ; Marc. Emp. 20 med.

ungo.opening: or , , v. a. root in Sanscr. ang, to besmear; cf. Gr. ἄγος , to smear , besmear , anoint with any fat substance, an unguent, oil, etc. (class.; syn.: lino, linio): unguentis, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 35, § 77 : aliquam…

unguēdo.opening: unguo, ungo , an ointment , unguent , App. M. 3, p. 138, 26 .

unguen.opening: id. , a fatty substance , fat; an ointment , unguent : in aënum caldum unguen indito, Cato, R. R. 79 ; 80 : pingues unguine ceras, Verg. G. 3, 450 : cras. sum, Pers. 6, 40 : pingue, Val. Fl. 6, 360 ; 8, 302 al.

unguentārĭus.opening: adj. unguentum , of or belonging to ointments or unguents , ointment-. Adj. : taberna, Varr L. L. 8, 30, 117; Sen. Ep. 108, 4 ; Suet. Aug. 4 : cella, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 : vasa, Plin. 36, 8, 12, § 60 .— Substt. , , , a dealer…

unguento.opening: v. a. id. , to rub with sweet ointments , to anoint , perfume (in verb. finit. very rare): DEAS VNGVENTAVERVNT, Inscr. Fratr. Arval. Orell. 2271, 391 (cf. Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 35, § 77 ).—More freq. in part. perf. : , ,…

unguentum.opening: ( gen. plur. unguentūm, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 5 ; id. Poen. 3, 3, 88 ), unguo , an ointment , unguent , perfume : non omnes possunt olere unguenta exotica, Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 41 ; 1, 3, 115 sq.; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 25, § 62 ;…

unguĭcŭlus.opening: dim. unguis , a finger-nail : integritas unguiculorum omnium, Cic. Fin. 5, 27, 80 ; Plaut. Ep. 5, 1, 17 ; Sen. Q. N. 6, 2, 5 .—Prov.: a teneris unguiculis, a transl. of the Gr. ἐξ ἁπαλῶν ὀνύχων , from early infancy ,…

unguilla.opening: unguo, ungo , an ointment-box , Sol. 27 fin.

unguĭnōsus.opening: adj. unguen , full of fat or oil , fat , oily , unctuous : unguentum, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 17 : opus, Cels. 5, 26, 20 .— Comp. : nuces, Plin. 23, 8, 77, § 147 .

unguis.opening: ( abl. ungui, Cat. 62, 43 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 19, 46 ; id. C. 2, 8, 4 ; Prop. 1, 20, 39 ; cf. Charis. p. 120 ), cf. Gr. ΟΝΥΧ-, ὄνυξ; Sanscr. nakha , a nail of a person's finger or toe. Lit. , Plin. 11, 45, 101, § 247 ; 10,…

ungŭla.opening: unguis . Lit. , a hoof , claw , talon; of a horse: totam quatit ungula terram, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 1 (Ann. v. 231 Vahl.); Verg. A. 8, 596 ; cf. Cic. N. D. 3, 5, 11 .—Of a swine, Cato, R. R. 158, 1 ; Cels. 2, 17 ; 4, 14…

ungŭlatros.grammar: ungues magnos atque asperos Cato appellavit

ungŭlātus.opening: adj. ungula , having claws or hoofs (post-class.): altero pede ungulatus, Tert. Apol. 16 fin. ; so, aliquis, Mart. Cap. 4, § 378 .

ungŭlus.opening: Oscan; Sanscr. ankami, bend; Gr. ἀγκύλος, crooked; Lat. ancus, aduncus; cf. angulus , a finger-ring , a ring (ante-class.): ungulus Oscorum linguā anulus, Fest. p. 375 Müll.; cf.: (anulum) apud nos prisci ungulum…

Unĭŏnītae.opening: id. , Unionites , Unitarians , a religious sect that denied the Trinity, Prud. Apoth. 246 sq.

Unxia.opening: ungo , the goddess of anointing , Arn. 3, 115 ; 7, 227 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 149 .

Upis.opening: , is. Masc. , the father of the third Diana , Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 58 .— Fem. , the third Diana; acc. Upim, Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 58 .

upŭpa.opening: ἔποψ . Lit. , a hoopoe , Plin. 10, 29, 44, § 86 ; 10, 25, 36, § 73 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 75 Müll.; cf. epops.— Transf. , a kind of hoe or mattock , Plaut. Capt. 5, 4, 7 .

urbānātim.opening: adv. urbanus , after the manner of city people , politely , urbanely : at ego rusticatim tangam, urbanatim nescio, Pomp. ap. Non. 409, 2 , and 166, 31.

urbānĭcĭānus.opening: adj. urbanus ; in milit. lang., garrisoned in the city (of Rome): milites, Dig. 4, 6, 35, § 4 ; Spart. Carac. 4 ; id. Get. 6 (called urbanae cohor tes, Dig. 25, 1, 8, § 9 ).

urbānĭtas.opening: id. , a living in a city , city life. Lit. : desideria urbis et urbanitatis, Cic. Fam. 7, 6, 1 : in urbis urbanitatisque desiderio, id. ib. 7, 17, 1 .— Transf. , city fashion , city manners , both in a good and in a bad…

urbānus.opening: adj. urbs , of or belonging to the city or town , city- , town- (opp. rusticus; cf.: urbicus, oppidanus). Lit. Adj. : nostri majores non sine causā praeponebant rusticos Romanos urbanis, Varr. R. R. 2 , praef. § 1:…

urbĭcăpus.opening: urbs-capio , a city taker , taker of cities : urbicape, occisor regum, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 64 .

urbĭcārĭus.opening: adj. urbicus , of or belonging to the city (post-class.): regiones, Cod. Th. 11, 28, 14: praefectura, Cod. Just. 3, 24, 1 .

urbĭcrĕmus.opening: adj. urbs-cremo , city burning : nubes (of the destruction of Sodom), Prud. Ham. 729 .

urbĭcus.opening: adj. urbs , of or belonging to the city , city- , civic (post-Aug.): res rusticae et urbicae, Gell. 15, 1, 3 : annona, Suet. Aug. 18 : res, id. Ner. 14 : negociatores, id. Caes. 49 : magistratus, id. Aug. 46 :…

Urbĭcus.opening: the name of a poet , Juv. 6, 71 ; Mart. 1, 42, 11 .

Urbigenus pāgus.opening: a canton in Helvetia , perh. the mod. Orbe , in Vaud, Caes. B. G. 1, 27 ; Inscr. Orell. 403 .

vălentŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [valens, from valeo], strong , stout : ut valentual est! Plaut. Cas. 4, 4, 26 .

vălĕo.opening: v. n. kindr. with Sanscr. bála, vis, robur, balishtas, fortissimus; cf. debilis , to be strong. Lit. , of physical strength, vigor, or health. In gen., to be strong , stout , or vigorous , to have strength (cf.: polleo,…

vălĕrĭa.opening: a kind of eagle , called by the Greeks melanaĕtos, Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 6 .

Vălĕrĭānus.opening: ; Licinius, a Roman emperor , A. D. 253-260, father of the emperor Gallienus , Treb. Val. 1 sqq.; after him were named Valeriani aurei, Treb. Claud. 17 .

Vălĕrĭus.opening: (old form , acc. to Fest. s. v. Aureliam, p. 23 Müll.; v. letter R), , ; , , , the name of a Roman gens. The favorite of the people , P. Valerius Publicola, Liv. 1, 58 ; 2, 2 ; 2, 8 ; Cic. Rep. 2, 31, 55 ; id. Leg. 2,…

vălesco.opening: v. inch. n. [valeo], to grow strong , acquire strength (rare; not in Cic.): (puerorum aetas) tali pacto recreata valescat, Lucr. 1, 942 ; 4, 17 : sucus ex quo omne corpus valescit, Ambros. de Noë et Arca, 9, 28.— Trop.…

vălētūdĭnārĭus.opening: adj. valetudo , sickly , infirm , weak , valetudinary (not in Cic.). Adj. : pecus (opp. sanum), Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 15 : fenerator, Sen. Ira, 3, 33, 2 .— Substt. , , , one in infirm health , an invalid , valetudinarian :…

vălētūdo.opening: ( ), , valeo , habit , state , or condition of body , state of health , health , whether good or bad. Lit. In gen.: optimā valetudine uti, Caes. B. C. 3, 49 : valetudine minus commodā uti, id. ib. 3, 62 : integra, Cic.…

Valgĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. T. Valgius Rufus, an epic poet , Tib. 4, 1, 180 ; Hor. S. 1, 10, 82 .— C. Valgius, a rhetorician , Quint. 3, 1, 8 ; 3, 5, 17 .— Valgius, father-in-law of Rullus, Cic. Agr. 3, 1, 3 .

valgus.opening: adj. root varg, to turn awry, twist; Sanscr. vrginas, twisted; cf. ruga, for fruga, and Anglo-Sax. wrinkle , having the calves of the legs bent outwards , bow-legged. Lit. : valgos Opilius Aurelius aliique complures…

vălĭdĭtas.opening: validus , strength of body: validitas et tenuitas, App. Trism. p. 97, 2 : virilis, Ambros. Abr. 2, 11, 84 .

vălĭdus.opening: adj. valeo , strong , stout , able , powerful , robust , vigorous (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cæs.; very rare in Cic.; cf. valens). Lit. In gen.: quasi incudem me homines octo validi caedant, Plaut. Am.…

vallāris.opening: adj. vallum , of or belonging to a rampart : corona, given to him who first mounted the enemy's rampart, Liv. 10, 46, 3 ; 30, 28, 6 ; Suet. Aug. 25 ; Plin. 16, 4, 3, § 7 ; 22, 3, 4, § 6 .

vallātĭo.opening: vallo , an intrenchment (late Lat.), only trop.: medicorum, Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

valles.opening: or (the former, Caes. B. G. 7, 47 ; Verg. A. 11, 522 ; the latter, Ov. M. 3, 155 ; 8, 334 al. ; cf. Fest. s. v. convallis, p. 42 Müll.), , Gr. ἕλος, lowland, Ἦλις; Lat. Veliae, Velitrae , a valley , vale. Lit. : quod…

vallescit.grammar: perierit, dictum a vallo militari, quod fit circa castra, quod qui eo eiciuntur pro perditis habentur
vallescit.opening: Fest. p. 377 Müll. (where Lachm. reads vallessit; cf.: valle feci, Varr. ap. Non. p. 217, 24 ; v. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 191 ).

vallestrĭa.opening: vallis , valleys , vales , Ambros. Hexaëm. 3, 3, 14 al.

vallĭcŭla.opening: ( , Serv. ad Verg. A. 11, 522 ), , dim. valles , a little valley , a glen , dell : vallis deminutivum vallicula facit, Fest. s. v. convallis, p. 42 Müll.: deformes, little hollows, Vulg. Lev. 14, 37 .

vallo.opening: v. a. vallum , in milit. lang., to surround with a rampart and palisades , to palisade , intrench , circumvallate (syn. saepio). Lit. : castra vallantem Fabium adorti sunt, Liv. 9, 41, 15 : castra vallari placuit, Tac.…

Vallōnĭa.opening: the goddess of valleys : collibus deam Collatinam, vallibus Valloniam praefecerunt, Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 8.

vallum.opening: collective of 1. vallus; the line of palisades about an intrenchment; hence , an earthen wall or rampart set with palisades , a palisaded rampart , intrenchment , circumvallation. Lit. , Varr. L. L. 5, § 117 Müll.; Liv.…

vallus.opening: dim. contr. for vannulus, from vannus , a little winnowing-van for grain or provender, Varr. R. R. 1, 52, 2 ; 1, 23, 5 ; id. ap. Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 166 .

vălor.opening: valeo , value : valor, τιμή , Gloss. Lab.

valva.opening: the leaf of a door , a folding-door; sing. rare, Pompon. ap. Non. 19, 23 ; Petr. 96 ; Sen. Herc. Fur. 999 .—Mostly plur. : , , the leaves , folds , or valves of a door , a folding-door , Cic. Div. 1, 34, 74 ; Cic. Verr.…

valvātus.opening: adj. valvae , having folding-doors : valvata et fenestrata triclinia, Varr. L. L. 8, § 29 Müll.; cf.: lumina fenestrarum (in tricliniis), Vitr. 6, 6 : fores, id. 4, 6 fin.

valvŏlae.opening: dim. id. (quasi double-flaps, i. e.), the pod , shell , pericarp , valvules of leguminous plants: fabarum, Col. 2, 17, 7 : lentis, id. 6, 10, 1 ; 6, 4, 3 ; 7, 4, 2 (ap. Fest. p. 375 Müll. masc. valvoli).

Vandălĭi.opening: or or , , , the Vandals , a people in the northern part of Germany in the time of Tacitus , Tac. G. 2 (Vandalii, Halm; Vandilii, Ritter); Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 99 (Vandili, Jan. and Sillig). — Sing. : Vandalus, a Vandal,…

vānesco.opening: v. inch. n. [vanus], to pass away , disappear , vanish ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : incipiunt gravidae vanescere nubes, Ov. Tr. 1, 2, 107 : Ceres in sterilem herbam, id. Am. 3, 7, 31 : spiritus meus in auras,…

vanga.opening: a kind of mattock , or, acc. to others, a spade with a cross-bar to put the foot upon (late Lat.), Pall. 1, 43, 3 .

Vangĭo.opening: a prince of the Suevi , Tac. A. 12, 99 sq.

Vangĭŏnes.opening: Lit. , a German people on the Rhine , about the mod. Worms , Caes. B. G. 1, 51 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 ; Tac. G. 28 ; id. A. 12, 27 ; id. H. 4, 70 ; Luc. 1, 431 ; Amm. 15, 11, 8 .— Transf. , the capital of the…

vānĭdĭcus.opening: adj. vanus-dico , vain - speaking; false - speaking; subst. , a liar (ante- and post-class. and rare): cum probis potius quam cum improbis vivere vanidicis, Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 37 ; Amm. 16, 7, 2 .

Vānĭenses.opening: a people of Gallia Transalpina, Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 130 .

vānĭlŏquentĭa.opening: vaniloquus , empty or idle talk , prating , vaunting (rarely; not in Cic.), Plaut. Rud. 4, 1, 14 : hac vaniloquentiā primum Aristaenum praetorem Achaeorum excitavit, Liv. 34, 24, 1 ; Tac. A. 3, 49 ; 6, 31 .— Plur. ,…

Vānĭlŏquĭdōrus.opening: vanus-loquor. δῶρον , gabble-giver , a facetiously-formed name of a liar, Plaut. Pers. 4, 6, 20 .

vānĭlŏquĭum.opening: vaniloquus , empty or idle talk , gabble , prate , vaunting (late Lat.): seductionis, Aug. Ep. 134, 4 ; 166, 6 .

vānĭlŏquus.opening: ( ), , adj. vanus-loquor , talking emplily or idly , gabbling , prating , i. e., Lying : quia vanilocu's, vapulabis, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 223 .— Ambros. Ep. 63, 7 .— Boastful , bragging , vaunting , Liv. 35, 48, 2 : ore,…

vānĭtas.opening: vanus . Lit. , emptiness , nothingness , nullity , want of reality : nulla in caelo nec fortuna, nec temeritas, nec erratio, nec vanitas inest; contra omnis ordo, veritas, ratio, constantia, Cic. N. D. 2, 21, 56 : ne…

vānĭtĭes.opening: , ēï, id. , emptiness , nullity , folly (late Lat.): plebeia, Amm. 29, 1, 13 .— Esp., vanity , vainglory : ad extollendam ejus vanitiem sidera quoque, si jussisset, exhiberi posse promittens, Amm. 29, 1, 11 .

vānĭtūdo.opening: id. , emptiness , nothingness , vainglory , vanity (ante-class.): ne turpasse vanitudine aetatem suam, Pac. ap. Non. 184, 7 : vera vanitudine convincere, by empty, lying talk, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 37 .

Vannĭus.opening: a king of the Quadi in the time of Tiberius , Tac. A. 2, 63 ; 12, 29 sq.—Hence, , , of Vannius : regnum, Plin. 4, 12, 25, § 81 .

vanno.opening: v. a. vannus , to fan , winnow (ante-class.): frumentum, Lucil. ap. Non. 19, 25 and 27.

vannus.opening: ( abl. heterocl. vannu, Non. 19, 21 ), , a fan , van for winnowing grain, Col. 2, 20, 4 ; App. M. 11, p. 260, 9 ; 11 , p. 269, 2: mystica Iacchi, borne about in the Bacchic festival, Verg. G. 1, 166 .

vāno.opening: v. n. vanus , to utter empty words , Att. ap. Non. 16, 22 ; 184, 2 .

vānus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; cf. vaco , that contains nothing , empty , void. vacant. Lit. (rare; not in Cic.): sed illos Exspectata seges vanis elusit aristis, Verg. G. 1, 226 : leve ac vanum granum, Col. 2, 9, 13 : ne vana urbis…

văpĭdus.opening: adj. vapor , that has emitted steam or vapor , i. e. that has lost its life and spirit , spoiled , flat , vapid. Lit. : vinum, Col. 12, 5, 1 .— Transf. , spoiled , bad. Lit. : pix, Pers. 5, 148 .— Trop. : astutam vapido…

văpor.opening: (ante-class. form , Naev. ap. Non. 487, 10 ; Lucr. 6, 952 ; cf. Quint. 1, 4, 13 ), , Sanscr. kapis, incense; Gr. καπύω, καπνός, smoke; cf. vappa , steam , exhalation , vapor (syn. exhalatio). In gen.: aquarum vapores,…

văpōrālis.opening: adj. vapor , of or belonging to steam or vapor , vapory (late Lat.): tenuitas, Aug. Genes. ad Lit. 2, 5 .— Adv. : , like a vapor , Aug. Genes. ad Lit. 2, 4 fin. ; 3, 10 fin.

văpōrārĭum.opening: id. , a steam-pipe in the Roman baths, which conveyed the heat to the sweating-room, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 1, § 2 ; Sen. Q. N. 3, 24, 3 Haase.

văpōrātē.opening: adv. vaporatus , with heat , hotly , Amm. 24, 4, 17 .

văpōrātĭo.opening: vaporo , a steaming , reeking , steam , vapor (post-Aug.): inundantium aquarum, Sen. Q. N. 6, 11 : urinae impubium, Plin. 28, 6, 18, § 65 : balinearum, a steam-bath, vapor-bath, id. 28, 4, 14, § 55 .—Esp., a fomentation…

văpōrĭfer.opening: adj. vapor-fero , emitting steam , full of vapors or exhalations , vaporous ( poet. ): fornaces, Stat. S. 1, 3, 45 : Baiae, id. ib. 3, 5, 96 : specus, Schol. Juv. 9, 57 .

văpōro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
văpōro.opening: v. n. and a. [vapor] Neutr. , to emit steam or vapor , to steam , reek. Lit. : aquae vaporant et in mari ipso, Plin. 31, 2, 2, § 5 : aquae fontanae vaporantes, Sol. 21 .—* Trop. , to glow , burn : invidiā quoniam, ceu…

văpōrōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of steam or vapor , steaming , vaporous (postclass.): caligo, App M. 9, p. 222, 31: fontes balnearum, id. ib. 5 , p. 165, 24.

văpōrus.opening: adj. id. , steaming , reeking , smoking (post-class.): tus, Nemes. Ecl. 4, 63 : ardor, Prud. στεφ . 6, 115.

vappa.opening: kindr. with vapor; cf. vapidus , wine that has lost its spirit and flavor; palled , flat , vapid wine. Lit. : vitium musto quibusdam in locis iterum sponte fervere, quā calamitate deperit sapor vappaeque accipit nomen,…

vappo.opening: root vap-, to flutter; cf. Gr. ήπίολος, moth , a moth , butterfly , Lucr. (or Lucil.) Fragm. ap. Prob. p. 1450 P. (v. Lindem. Corp. Gram. I. p. 109, n. 32; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 165 sq. ).

vāpŭlāris.opening: adj. vapulo , that gets a flogging : tribunus, facetiously, qs. the head floggee , of a slave, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 22 .

vāpŭlo.opening: v. neutral pass. [perh. root vap-; cf. vappo; prop. to wriggle, flutter; hence], to get a cudgelling or flogging , to be flogged. Lit. : ego vapulando, ille verberando usque ambo defessi sumus, Ter. Ad. 2, 2, 5 ; so…

vāra.opening: A wooden horse or trestle for spreading nets upon; hence, prov.: sequitur varam vibia, one evil follows the other, Aus. Idyll. 12 praef. monos.— A forked pole for spreading nets upon, Luc. 4, 439 ; to support a bough,…

vārātĭo.opening: varo , a bending , winding (late Lat.): fluminis, Auct. Limit. pp. 257 and 285 Goes.

Vardaei.opening: a people in Dalmatia , Vatin. ap. Cic. Fam. 5, 9, 2 ; Plin. 3, 22, 26, § 143 .

Vardŭli.opening: a people of Lusitania , Mel. 3, 10, 7 ; Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 27 ; 4, 20, 34, § 110 .

Vărēnus.opening: a Roman proper name , esp. L. Varenus, who was defended by Cicero , but convicted of assassination , Cic. Fragm. pro Var. 14, p. 5 B. and K.; Plin. Ep. 1, 20, 7 .

Vargŭla.opening: a talkative friend of C. Julius Cæsar Strabo, Cic. de Or. 2, 60, 244 ; 2, 60, 247 .

Varguntēius.opening: , L., a Roman senator who was engaged in Catiline's conspiracy , Sall. C. 17, 3 ; 28, 1 ; 47, 1 ; Cic. Sull. 2, 6 ; 5, 15 .

vargus.opening: Gallic , a vagabond , Eum. Pan. Const. 9, 3 ; Sid. Ep. 6, 4 .

Vărĭa.opening: A small city of the Sabines , now Vicovaro , Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 3 ; Phaedr. 5, prol. 14 .— A town in Appulia , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 100 .

vărĭābĭlis.opening: adj. vario , changeable , variable (post-class.): aër, App. de Mundo, p. 58, 31.

vărĭantĭa.opening: id. , a difference , diversity , variety (Lucretian; cf.: varietas, vicissitudo): rerum, Lucr. 1, 653 ; 3, 318 .

vărĭānus.opening: adj. varius , divers-colored , variegated : uvae, a particular kind so called, Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 29 .

vărĭātim.opening: adv. vario , in various ways , variously : dici, Gell. 5, 12, 9 ; Apic. 4, 1, § 120 .

vărĭātĭo.opening: id. , a difference , variation : sine variatione ullà, Liv. 24, 9, 3 .

vărĭātus.opening: , um. Part. of vario.— P. a. , diverse , manifold , varied : lyra concentu variatior, App. Flor. p. 357 fin.

vārĭcātor.opening: varico , one that walks with his legs spread apart , a straddler : praevaricator est quasi varicator, qui diversam partem adjuvat, proditā causā suā, Dig. 3, 2, 4, § 4 ; 47, 15, 1 .

vārĭco.opening: v. n. 1. varicus , to spread the legs apart , to straddle : varicare supra modum et in stando deforme est et accedente motu prope obscenum, Quint. 11, 3, 125 : vallum, quod eā varicare nemo potest, i. e. can stride over…

vărĭcōsus.opening: adj. varix , full of dilated veins , varicose : centuriones, Pers. 5, 189 : haruspex, Juv. 6, 397 : Arpinas, i. e. Cicero, Sid. Ep. 5, 5 (cf. Quint. 11, 3, 143 ; and Vatin. ap. Macr. S. 2, 3 ).—* Adv. : , full of…

vărĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small varix , Cels. 5, 26, 32 .

vārĭcus.opening: adv. id. , with feet spread apart , straddlingly , App. M. 1, p. 108, 19 .

vărĭĕgo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
vărĭĕgo.opening: v. a. and n. varius-ago (post-class.). Act. , to make of various sorts or colors , to variegate : figuras alius alio scientius, Aus. Idyll. 13 praef. : balteus miris coloribus variegatus, App. Flor. p. 346, 15 : navis…

vărĭĕtas.opening: varius , difference , diversity , variety (class.; used alike in sing. and plur. ): varietas Latinum verbum est, idque proprie quidem in disparibus coloribus dicitur: sed transfertur in multa disparia: varium poëma,…

Varīni.opening: a German tribe on the Baltic Sea , Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 99 ; Tac. G. 40, 3 .

vărĭo.opening: v. a. and varius . Act. , to diversify , variegate , change (class.). Lit. : (principia) omne genus gignunt variantque colores, Lucr. 2, 759 : maculis ortum (sol), Verg. G. 1, 441 : caeruleis corpora guttis, Ov. M. 4,…

vārĭtus.opening: adv. , a false read. for varicus, App. M. 1, p. 108, 19 .

vărĭus.opening: adj. , diverse , different , manifold , changing , varying , various (cf.: diversus, distinctus). Lit. Of color, etc., variegated , party-colored , mottled , etc.: arietis lingua nigra aut varia, vestis, Varr. R. R. 2,…

Vărĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; esp., Q. Varius of Sucro , in Spain , called Hybrida , a tribune of the people A.U.C. 663, Cic. de Or. 1, 25, 117 ; id. Brut. 49, 182 ; 62, 221 ; Val. Max. 4, 3, 7 .— L. Varius, a tragic poet ,…

vărix.opening: and 1. varus , a dilated vein , varix , esp. in the thighs, Cels. 7, 8 ; 7, 17 fin. ; 7, 31; Varr. ap. Non. 26, 13 ; 167, 25 ; Cic. Tusc. 2, 15, 35 ; Sen. Ep. 78, 17 ; Plin. 11, 45, 104, § 252 ; Quint. 11, 3, 143 ;…

vāro.opening: v. a. 1. varus , to bend , curve (late Lat.): alveos pontium, Auct. Limit. p. 257 Goes.: flumen, id. ib. p. 285.

Varro.opening: a surname in the gens Terentia, e. g. M. Terentius Varro, a contemporary of Cicero , who wrote De Re Rusticā and De Linguā Latinā.— The poet P. Terentius Varro Atacinus, Hor. S. 1, 10, 46 .— The consul C. Terentius…

vārus.opening: adj. perh. root kar, kvar; whence Sanscr. kakras, wheel; Lat. circus, curvus, and vārus, for cvarus; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 412 , bent , stretched , or grown inwards , or awry. Lit. : (canes) debent esse cruribus rectis…

vărus.opening: an eruption on the face, a blotch , pimple , Gr. ἴονθος , Cels. 6, 5 ; Plin. 22, 25, 73, § 151 ; 23, 1, 14, § 19 ; 23, 4, 42, § 85 ; 23, 4, 45, § 89.

Vārus.opening: a surname , esp. in the gens Quintilia; e. g. P. Quintilius Varus, defeated by Arminius, Vell. 2, 117 ; Suet. Aug. 23 ; id. Tib. 17 ; Tac. A. 1, 3 ; 1, 43 ; 1, 55 ; 1, 60 al.—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to a Varus…

văs.opening: a bail , security , surety (in gen., while praes is confined to pecuniary matters; cf. also sponsio): vas appellatus, qui pro altero vadimonium promittebat, Varr. L. L. 6, 74 Müll.: vas factus est alter (Damon) ejus…

vās.opening: , vāsis; plur. , (anteclass. collat. form of the nom. sing. , Cato ap. Gell. 13, 23, 1 ; Fab. Pict. ap. Non. 544, 26 ; Plaut. Truc. 1, 1, 33 sq. : vasus fictilis, Petr. 57, 8 ; dat. plur. vasibus, Gargil. Martial.…

vāsārĭum.opening: 2. vas . Furniture-money , equipage-money , given to a governor of a province for his domestic establishment, Cic. Pis. 35, 86 .— Money given for the hire of an oil-mill , Cato, R. R. 145, 3 .— The furniture , movables…

Vā^sātes.opening: , and , , , a people of Aquitania , Aus. Parent. 24 ; Amm. 15, 11, 14 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Vasates : rheda, Aus. Ep. 7, 18 .

vāsātus.opening: 2. vas fin. , i. e. magnā mentulā instructus (late Lat.), Lampr. Heliog. 5 ; 8 ; 9, 31 .

vascellum.opening: dim. 2. vas , a small vase or urn , Inscr. Orell. 4555 .

Vascŏnes.opening: a people in Hispania Tarraconensis, on the Pyrenees , in the modern Navarra , the parent stock of the Basques , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 22 ; Juv. 15, 93 .—As adj. : , , of the Vascones : saltu, i. e. the Pyrenees, Paul. Nol.…

vascŭlārĭus.opening: (contr. VASCLARIVS, Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 291, 9 ; Inscr. Fabr. p. 17 , n. 75), , vasculum , one who makes vessels of metal , a worker in metals , a whitesmith , goldsmith , etc., Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 24, § 54 ; Dig. 19,…

vascŭlum.opening: dim. 2. vas , a small vessel. Lit. Cato, R. R. 111 ; Plaut. Aul. 2, 3, 3 ; id. Trin. 4, 2, 46 ; Quint. 1, 2, 28 ; 7, 10, 9 ; Juv. 9, 141 .— A small beehive , Pall. Jun. 7, 8 .— Transf. The seed-capsule of certain…

vascus.opening: adj. perh. incorrectly for vastus : tibia, a kind of flute, Sol. 5 ; Serv. Verg. A. 11, 737 .

vastābundus.opening: adj. vasto , wasting , desolating , devastating , Amm. 31, 8, 6 .

vastātĭo.opening: id. , a laying waste , desolating , ravaging , devastation : omnium, Cic. Cat. 2, 8, 18 : domuum, Sall. Or. ad Caes. 1, 4 : villarum, Tac. H. 4, 34 : agri, Liv. 7, 15 11; 10, 4, 7; Quint. 8, 4, 14 : Italiam a vastatione…

vastātor.opening: id. , a desolater , ravager , devastater (mostly poet. ): Arcadiae aper, Ov. M. 9, 192 : ferus (i. e. lupus), id. ib. 11, 395 : ferarum Amycus, destroyer, Verg. A. 9, 772 : Trojae, Stat. Achill. 2, 318 : gentium…

vastātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , wasting , ravaging , devastating (late Lat.): manus hostium, Amm. 18, 6, 9 : globus, id. 19, 9, 7 .

vastātrix.opening: vastator , a (female) waster , ravager , devastater; trop.: luxuria terrarum marisque vastatrix, Sen. Ep. 95, 19 .

vastesco.opening: v. inch. n. [vastus], to become desert or waste : ne scelere tuo Thebani vastescant agri, Att. ap. Non. 185, 10 .

vastĭfĭcus.opening: adj. vastus-facio , laying waste , ravaging , devastating : Erymanthia vastifica belua, Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 9, 22.

vastĭtas.opening: vastus , an empty place , a waste , desert. Lit. : te propter tot tantasque habemus vastitatis funerum, Att. ap. Non. 417, 12 (Trag. Rel. v. 175 Rib.): audistis, quae solitudo in agris esset, quae vastitas, quae fuga…

vastĭtĭes.opening: vastus , = vastitas, II. A., ruin , destruction : voluptatum omnium, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 68 .

vastĭtūdo.opening: id. . = vastitas, II. A., ruin , destruction (ante-class.): Mars pater, te precor ... ut tu morbos visos invisosque, viduertatem vastitudinemque, calamitates intemperiasque prohibessis, an old formula of prayer ap.…

vasto.opening: v. a. id.; hence, Ital. guastar, and Fr. gāter , to make empty or vacant , to leave untenanted or uninhabited , to desert. Lit. (rare but class.): lex erat lata de vastato ac relicto foro, Cic. Sest. 24, 53 : vastati…

vastŭlus.opening: adj. vastus, II. , rather huge or bulky : corpora, App. M. 2, p. 128, 14 .

vātĭcĭnĭus.opening: vaticinor , prophetic , vaticinal : libri, Liv. 25, 1, 12 ; 39, 16, 8 Weissenb. (al. vaticinos).

Vecilĭus.opening: a mountain in Latium , perh a spur of the Algidus, Liv. 3, 50 .

vēcordia.opening: vecors , want of reason , senselessness , silliness , folly; madness , insanity (not in Cic.): tanta vecordia innata cuiquam, Ter. And. 4, 1, 2 : prorsus in facie voltuque vecordia inerat, Sall. C. 15, 5 : alicui…

vectābĭlis.opening: adj. vecto , that can be carried , portable : materia insulae, Sen. Q. N. 3, 25, 9 .

vectācŭlum.opening: id. , a carriage , vehicle , Tert. Bapt. 3 ; id. Anim. 53 .

vectārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or for carrying or conveying : equus, a packhorse , draught-horse , Varr R. R. 2, 7, 15 (acc. to Schneid. we should read vectuarius).

vectātĭo.opening: id. , a carrying or being carried , a riding (post-Aug.): vectatio et iter reficiunt animum, Sen. Tranq. 17, 8 : assidua equi post cibum, Suet. Calig. 3 .—Also in act. sense, a carrying or bearing : sarcinae, Aug. Civ.…

vectĭārĭus.opening: 1. vectis , one who works the lever in machines, Vitr. 6, 9 med.

vectĭfer.opening: adj. , having a bolt , well bolted (late Lat.), Aldh. Virg. 447 .

vectīgālis.opening: adj [id.]. Of or belonging to imposts or taxes : pecunia, i. e. impost, tribute, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 35, § 89 , cf.: annuum tributum, Just. 13, 1, 9 .— Paying tribute , subject to imposts , tributary : civitas, Cic. Verr.…

vectĭtātus.opening: Part. [vectito, acc. to Gell. 9, 6, 3 ; Caper, p. 2246 P.], borne or carried about : curru quadrijugo vectitatus, Arn. 5, 183 ; Sol. 11, 9 .

Vectĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens, Tac. A. 11, 30 ; 11, 31 ; 11, 35 ; Plin. 2, 83, 85, § 199 .

vecto.opening: v. freq. a [veho], to bear , carry , convey (perh. not ante-Aug.): delphinum dorso super fluctus edito vectavisse (Arionem), Gell. 16, 19, 16 : corpora viva nefas Stygiā vectare carinā, Verg. A. 6, 391 : plaustris…

vectōrĭus.opening: adj [id.], of or for carrying : navigia, transport-ships, Caes. B. G. 5, 8 , Suet. Caes. 63 .
