verbĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. verbero , worthy of a beating : verberabilissime, Plaut. Aul. 4, 4, 6 .

verbĕrābundus.opening: adj. id. , whipping , flogging , Plaut. Fragm. p. 30 Mai ( id. Stich. v. 444 Ritschl).

verbĕrātĭo.opening: id. , a striking , beating. Lit. : flagellorum castigatio, vinculorum verberatio, Dig. 48, 19, 7 ; 47, 10, 5, § 1 .— Trop. , chastisement , punishment : mirificam mi verberationem cessationis epistulā dedisti, i. e.…

verbĕrātor.opening: id. , a beater , flogger , Prud. στεφ . 9, 38.

verbĕrātus.opening: id. , a beating : si (aqua) e sublimi dejecta verberatu corripiat aëra, Plin. 31, 3, 23, § 39 .

verbĕrĕus.opening: adj. verber , worthy of stripes (Plautinian): caput = 2. verbero, scoundrel, Plaut. Pers. 2, 2, 2 ; also called statua, id. Capt. 5, 1, 31 ; id. Ps. 4, 1, 7 .

verbĕrĭto.opening: v. freq. [1. verbero], to beat often , Cato, acc. to Fest. p. 379 Müll.

verbĕro.opening: 1. verbero , one worthy of stripes , a scoundrel , rascal : ain' tu vero verbero? Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 128 ; Cic. Att. 14, 6, 1 ; Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 187 ; id. Ps. 4, 7, 63 ; id. As. 2, 4, 10 ; 2, 4, 78 ; 3, 3, 79 ; id. Capt.…

verbĭālis.opening: adj. , verbal , derived from a verb , Pompei Comment. (Keil, Lat. Gram. 5).

verbĭfĭcātĭo.opening: verbum - facio , a talking , Caecil. ap. Don. Ter. Eun. 4, 4, 4 (Com. Rel. p. 37 Rib.).

verbĭgĕna.opening: verbum-gigno , he who was born of the Word , i. e. Christ , Prud. Cath. 3, 1 ; 11, 17 .

verbĭgĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. verbum-gero , to talk , chat , dispute : quoties inter nos verbigeratum sit, App. Mag. p. 321, 3 .

verbōsĭtas.opening: verbosus , multiplicity of words , wordiness , verbosity (postclass.), Prud. στεφ . 10, 551; Symm. Ep. 8, 47 .

verbōsus.opening: adj. verbum , full of words , wordy , prolix , verbose (rare but class.): verbosa simulatio prudentiae, Cic. Mur. 14, 30 : T. Livium ut verbosum in historiā carpebat, Suet. Calig. 34 ; Cat. 98, 1 .— Comp. : verbosior…

verbum.opening: ( gen. plur. verbūm, Plaut. As. 1, 3, 1 ; id. Bacch. 4, 8, 37 ; id. Truc. 2, 8, 14 ), from the root er; Gr. ΕΡω, whence εἴρω and ῥῆμα, what is spoken or said; cf. Goth. vaurd; Germ. Wort; Engl. word , a word; plur. ,…

Vercellae.opening: a town in Gallia Cisalpina, now Borgo Vercelli , Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 124 ; Brut. ap. Cic. Fam. 11, 19, 2 ; Tac. H. 1, 70 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Vercellœ : ager, Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 78 .— † , , adj. , of…

Vercingetŏrix.opening: a commander of the Gauls in the Gallic War , Caes. B. G. 7, 4 sq. ; Flor. 3, 10, 20 .

vercŭlum.opening: dim. ver , little spring , as a term of endearment: meum corculum, melliculum, verculum, Plaut. Cas. 4, 4, 15 .

vĕrēcundĭa.opening: verecundus , the natural feeling of shame , by whatever cause produced, shamefacedness , bashfulness , shyness , coyness , modesty , etc. In gen. (class.; syn.: pudicitia, castitas, pudor). Absol. : nec vero tam metu…

vĕrēcundor.opening: v. dep. n. [verecundus], to feel bashful or ashamed , to be shy or diffident (rare but class.): verecundari neminem apud mensam decet, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 77 : hi nostri amici verecundantur, capti splendore virtutis,…

vĕrēcundus.opening: adj. vereor , feeling shame (at any thing good or bad), shamefaced , bashful , shy , coy , modest , diffident , etc. Lit. : nimis verecunda es (uxor), Plaut. Am. 3, 2, 22 : decet verecundum esse adulescentem, id. As. 5,…

vĕrēdārĭus.opening: veredus , a postboy , courier (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 5, 7 med. ; Vulg. Esth. 8, 10 ; Firm. Math. 3, 13 fin. ; Paul. Nol. Ep. 9 .—Comically, of a priest eager for gossip, Hier. Ep. 22, 28 .

vĕrēdus.opening: A light horse for posting, a post-horse , courier's horse , Cod. Just. 12, 51, 4 ; 12, 51, 7 ; Aus. Ep. 8, 7 ; 8, 14 .— Transf. , a light , fleet huntinghorse , Mart. 12, 14, 1 ; 14, 86, 1 .

vĕrĕor.opening: ( part. pres. verens; rare in histt.; not in Cæs., Liv., Sall., or Curt., veritus being used instead; but freq. in Cic., Nep., and Just.; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 1192), 2, v. dep. a. and Greek root ορ-, ϝορ; οὖρος,…

vĕrētillum.opening: dim. veretrum , = parvum veretrum, App. Mag. p. 296, 28 .

vĕrētrum.opening: vereor; cf. verendus, 2. , the private parts , Phaedr. 4, 14, 1 ; Suet. Tib. 62 ; Arn. 5, 165 : muliebre, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 10, 16 ; Scrib. Comp. 234 ; App. Herb. 201 .

Vergellus.opening: a river of Apulia , Val. Max. 9, 2 , ext. 2; Flor. 2, 6, 18 .

Vergentum.opening: a town in Hispania Baetica, Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 11 .

Vergĭlĭae.opening: vergo , the constellation of the seven stars , that rises at the end of spring , the Pleiades , Cic. N. D. poët. 2, 44, 112; Auct. B. Afr. 47; Isid. Orig. 3, 70 ; cf. Fest. p. 372 Müll.

Vergĭlĭo-cento.opening: Vergiliuscento , a poem made up of scraps from Vergil , Hier. Ep. 103, 7 .

Vergĭlĭus.opening: (not ; the form Ver- is supported by the ancient MSS. and inscriptions in unbroken succession, to the fourth century A.D.; v. Ritschl, Opusc. Phil. 2, 779 sq.), , , the name of a Roman gens; so, esp., P. Vergilius Maro,…

vergo.opening: ( perf. and sup. wanting, acc. to Neue, Formenl. 2, pp. 507, 584; but versi is assumed as perf. by Prob. Cath. 1486, and is read, Ov. P. 1, 9, 52 , by Merkel, ex conj. for the MS. vertit; acc. to Charis. 3, 1, p. 218 ,…

Vergŏānum.opening: a town on the island of Lerina , near Gaul , Plin. 3, 5, 11, § 79 .

Vergŏbrĕtus.opening: , = Βεργόβρετος ; paraphr., the title of the chief magistrate among the Ædui, Caes. B. G. 1, 16 .

vērĭcŏla.opening: verus-colo , that cultivates or regards the truth : lex, Tert. Carm. ad Senat. 43 .

vĕrĭcŭlum.opening: (not ), , dim. veru; cf. corniculum, from cornu , a small javelin , Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 107 ; 35, 11, 41, § 149 ; Veg. Mil. 2, 15 .

vērīdĭcentĭa.opening: veridicus , truthtelling (late Lat.), Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 1, 14 ; 2, 2 .

vērĭdĭcus.opening: adj. verus-dico , that speaks the truth , truth-telling , veracious , veridical (rare but class.). Lit. , act. : os, Lucr. 6, 6 : voces, Cic. Div. 1, 45, 101 : sorores, Mart. 5, 1, 3 : interpres, Liv. 1, 7 .— Transf. ,…

vērĭlŏquĭum.opening: verus-loquor , a literal transl. of ἐτυμολογία , etymology , for which Cicero proposes the freer rendering, notatio, Cic. Top. 8, 35 .

vērĭlŏquus.opening: adj. id. , speaking truly , truth-telling (very rare): oraculum, Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 3, 12 Mai: lingua, Hier. adv. Ruf. 3, 42 .

vērĭsĭmĭlis.opening: , and , , , etc., v. under verus and similis, etc.

vērĭtas.opening: verus , truth , truthfulness , verity; the true or real nature , reality (always abstract; cf.: verum, vera). In gen.: veritas, per quam immutata ea, quae sunt aut ante fuerunt aut futura sunt, dicuntur, Cic. Inv. 2,…

vērĭverbĭum.opening: verus-verbum , a telling the truth , veracity , Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 36 .

vermesco.opening: v. n. (eccl. Lat.), Aug. in Joan. tr. 35, 8.

vermĭcŭlātĭo.opening: vermiculor , a being worm-eaten , of plants, Plin. 17, 24, 37 , §§ 218 and 230; 17, 11, 16, § 87.

vermĭcŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. [vermiculus], to be full of worms , wormy , to be worm-eaten , of trees: vermiculantur magis minusve quaedam arbores, Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 220 .—Hence, , , P. a. , in the form of worms : gummi, Plin. 13, 21,…

vermĭcŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of worms , wormy : poma, Pall. 12, 7, 14 .

vermĭcŭlus.opening: dim. vermis , a little worm , grub , in decaying things. Lit. , Lucr. 2, 899 ; Plin. 10, 65, 85, § 186 : in linguā canum, id. 29, 5, 32, § 100 .— Transf. A disease of dogs which drives them mad , Grat. Cyn. 386 .— In…

vermĭflŭus.opening: adj. vermisfluo , swarming with worms : vulnus, Paul. Nol. Carm. 22, 134 .

vermĭna.opening: vermis, gripings of the belly caused by worms; hence, in gen. , the gripes , belly-ache , stomach-ache. Lit. : saeva, Lucr. 5, 997 ; cf.: vermina dicuntur dolores corporis cum quodam minuto motu quasi a vermibus…

vermĭnātĭo.opening: vermino , the worms , a disease of animals, the bots. Lit. , Plin. 28, 11, 49, § 180 ; 30, 15, 50, § 144 . — Transf. , a crawling , itching pain , Sen. Ep. 78, 9 .— Plur. : cerebri aestuantis, Sen. Ep. 95, 17 .

vermĭno.opening: (in the dep. collat. form verminatur, Pompon. ap. Non. 40, 21 ; Sen. Vit. Beat. 17 fin. ), v. n. vermina . Lit. , to have worms , be troubled with worms , Sen. Q. N. 2, 31, 2 .— Transf. , in gen., to have crawling ,…

vermĭnōsus.opening: adj. vermis , full of worms , wormy : fici, Plin. 17, 28, 47, § 261 : ulcera, id. 26, 14, 87, § 145 : auris, id. 20, 14, 52, § 146 .

vermis.opening: Gr. ἕλμις; cf. Sanscr. krmis, worm; Goth. vaùrms, serpent , a worm , Lucr. 2, 871 ; 2, 928 ; 3, 719 ; 3, 723; Plin. 18, 17, 45, § 159 ; 24, 5, 11, § 18 ; 30, 13, 39, § 114 ; Col. 6, 30 fin.

verna.opening: root vas, to dwell; Sanscr. vāstu, house; Gr. ἄστυ, city , a slave born in his master's house , a homeborn slave. Lit. : vernas alere, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 104 ; id. Am. 1, 1, 24 ; Just. 38, 6, 7 ; Val. Max. 3, 4, 3 ;…

vernācŭlus.opening: adj. verna . (Acc. to verna, I.) Of or belonging to homeborn slaves. Adj. : multitudo, the rabble of slaves, Tac. A. 1, 31 ; so, plebs, Tert. Apol. 35 .— Substt. : , , (acc. to verna, I.), buffoons , jesters (postAug.…

vernālis.opening: adj. ver , of or belonging to spring , vernal : horae, Manil. 3, 258 : facies terrae, Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 25.

vernātĭo.opening: verno , the sloughing or shedding of the skin of snakes. Lit. , Plin. 29, 5, 32, § 101 ; 30, 3 8, § 24.— Transf. , concr., the slough cast off by a snake, Plin. 29, 6, 35, § 11 .

vernĭ-cŏmus.opening: adj. vernuscoma , having young leaves : oliva, Mart. Cap. 6, § 570 .

vernĭfer.opening: adj. vernusfero , flowering in spring , spring-blooming , = ἐαροτρεφής : comere verniferis florentia limina sertis (sc. coronis), Mart. Cap. 1, § 1 .

vernīlis.opening: adj. verna , of or belonging to a home-born slave (verna), slavish , i. e., Mean , fawning , servile : blanditiae, Tac. H. 2, 59 : corpora, Quint. Decl. 9, 12 .— * Jesting , pert , waggish : dictum, Tac. H. 3, 32…

vernīlĭtas.opening: vernilis (mostly post-Aug.). Cringing obsequiousness , servility , Sen. Ep. 95, 2 .— Coarse , pert , jesting , pertness , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Non. 342, 17 ; Quint. 1, 11, 2 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 79 .

vernisera.opening: Fest. p. 379 Müll. [perh. from ver-sero, auguries belonging to sowing in the spring].

verno.opening: v. n. ver , to appear like spring , to flourish , be verdant; to spring , bloom , grow young , renew itself , etc. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn. vireo). Lit. : humus, Ov. M. 7, 284 : arbores fruticesque, Plin.…

vernŭla.opening: comm. dim. [verna], a little or young home-born slave (post-Aug.). Lit. , Juv. 10, 117 ; Sen. Prov. 1, 6 ; Plin. 22, 17, 20, § 44 ; App. M. 4, p. 153, 25 al. — Transf. , adj. : = vernaculus. Jocular , pert , coarse :…

vernus.opening: adj. ver , of or belonging to spring , spring-. Adj. : tempus, Lucr. 5, 802 ; 6, 369 ; Cic. Sen. 19, 70 ; id. Tusc. 5, 13, 37 ; Hor. A. P. 302 al. : aequinoctium, Liv. 33, 3, 5 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 28, 2 ; Col. 9, 14, 4 :…

vēro.opening: v. n. verus , to speak the truth : satin' vates verant aetate in agendā? Enn. ap. Gell. 18, 2 fin. (Ann. v. 370 Vahl.).

Veromandŭi.opening: a people of Gallia Belgica, in the mod. Département de l' Aisne (the old Vermandois ), Caes. B. G. 2, 4 ; 2, 16 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 ; Epit. Liv. 104 .

Vērōna.opening: a city in Gallia Transpadana, the birthplace of the poet Catullus and of the elder Pliny , still called Verona , Liv. 5, 35 ; Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 130 , Cat. 35, 3 ; 67, 34 ; Ov. Am. 3, 15, 7 al. —Hence, , , adj. , of or…

verpa.opening: , = membrum virile, Cat. 28, 12 ; Mart. 11, 46, 2 ; Auct. Priap. 35 .

verpus.opening: a circumcised man , Cat. 47, 4 ; Juv. 14, 104 ; Mart. 7, 82, 6 ; 11, 94, 2 .

verres.opening: (collat. form of the nom. sing. , Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 8 ), Sanscr. root varsh-, to rain, wet; whence vrshabha, bull; cf. ἔρση, dew , a male swine , boar-pig (syn.: aper, porcus), Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 21 ; Col. 7, 9, 7 ; Hor.…

Verres.opening: the surname of the prœtor C. Cornelius, notorious for his bad government of Sicily; hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Verres , Verrian : lex, that originated with him, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 49, § 117 .— Subst. : , , (i.…

verrĭcŭlum.opening: verro , a drag-net , seine (more freq. called everriculum), Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 59 (but the true read., Val. Max. 4, 1 , ext. 7, is everriculum).

verrīnus.opening: adj. 1. verres , of a boar-pig , boar- , hog- , pork- : jecur, Plin. 28, 10, 42, § 152 : fel, id. ib. : adeps, id. 28, 9, 37, § 140 : sincipita, id. 8, 51, 77, § 209 .— In a punning lusus verbb.: jus, v. 2, Verres, B.

Verrĭus Flaccus.opening: a celebrated grammarian of the time of Augustus and Tiberius , Suet. Gram. 17 .

verro.opening: ( perf. versi, Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 59 : verri, Charis. p. 218 ; Prisc. p. 900 ; neither form in use, acc. to Macr. D. Diff. 23, 8 ), , v. a. root var-; cf. vello , to scrape , sweep , brush , scour; to sweep out ,…

verrūca.opening: a steep place , height. Lit. , Cato ap. Gell. 3, 7, 6 ; 3, 7, 13 (cf. also Quint. 8, 3, 48 ; 8, 6, 14 ).— Transf A wart on the human body, Plin. 20, 12, 48, § 123 ; 22, 21, 29, § 59 ; 33, 4, 25, § 85 .— An excrescence…

verrūcārĭa herba.opening: a plant that drives away warts , helioscopium, wartwort , turnsole , Plin. 22, 21, 29, § 58 .

Verrucius.opening: ( ), , , a fictitious name fraudulently used by Verres , Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 76, § 187 ; 2, 4, 61, § 137 .

verrūcōsus.opening: adj. verruca, II. , full of warts , warty. Lit. , an appellation of Q. Fabius Maximus Cunctator, Cic. Brut. 14, 57 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Illustr. 43 .— * Transf. , rough , rugged : verrucosa Antiopa, Pers. 1, 77 .

verrūcŭla.opening: dim. verruca . A little eminence , Arn. 2, 77 .— A small wart , Cels. 5, 28, 14 ; Col. 7, 6, 2 .

Verrugo.opening: a town of the Volsci , now Colle Ferro or Colle Sacco , near Segni , Liv. 4, 1 ; 4, 55 ; 4, 58 ; 5, 28; Val. Max. 3, 2, 8 .

verrunco.opening: v. n. , to turn , turn about; hence, in relig. lang., to turn out well , have a fortunate issue : bene, Att. and Pac. ap. Non. 185, 24 ; Att. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 22, 45 ; Liv. 29, 27, 2 ; cf. Fest. p. 373 .

versābĭlis.opening: adj. verso , movable , mobile; changeable , mutable , versatile (postAug.; cf.: mutabilis, variabilis). Lit. : aër, Sen. Q. N. 6, 16, 4 : repagulum, of a cage, Amm. 19, 6, 4 : acies, Curt. 4, 13, 32 . — Trop. : omnis…

versābundus.opening: adj. id. , turning round , revolving (very rare): turbo, Lucr. 6, 438 : sidera, Vitr. 9, 7, 4 .

versātĭlis.opening: adj. id. , that turns or moves round , revolving , movable (not in Cic.). Lit. : templum mundi, Lucr. 5, 1436 : laquearia cenationum, Sen. Ep. 90, 15 : tabulae, Suet. Ner. 31 : triclinia, Lampr. Heliog. 21 : molae,…

versātĭo.opening: id. , a turning round. Lit. : machinarum, Vitr. 10, 1 ; 10, 6 ; 10, 8 ; 10, 10; 10, 14: oculi, Plin. 8, 33, 51, § 121 .— Trop. , a changing , alteration , mutation : rerum sursum ac deorsum euntium, Sen. Tranq. 11, 10 .

versĭcăpillus.opening: verto-capillus , one who changes hair , i. e. whose hair grows gray , Plaut. Pers. 2, 2, 48 Ritschl (al. ubi capillus versipellis flat).

versĭcŏlor.opening: ( abl. versicolori, Liv. 7, 10 : versicolore, Prop. 4, 7, 50 ; Ov. F. 5, 356 ; post-class. collat. form of the nomsing. , Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 56 ; neutr. versicolorum, Dig. 32, 1, 70, § 12 Momms.; and , Dig. 34, 2, 32,…

versĭcŭlus.opening: dim. versus , a little line , a mere line : tribusne versiculis his temporibus Brutus ad me? Nihil scripsissem potius. Cic. Ep. ad Brut. 1, 14, 1 : epistulae versiculum, id. Att. 5, 1, 3 : cum senatus ei commiserit, ut…

versĭfĭcātĭo.opening: versifico , versemaking , versifying , versification (post-Aug.): quem in poëmate locum habet versificatio, eum in oratione compositio, Quint. 9, 4, 116 ; 9, 2, 35 ; Col. 11, 1, 2 .

versĭfĭcātor.opening: id. . Lit. , a verse-maker , versifier (post-Aug.): Cornelius Severus versificator quam poëta melior, Quint. 10, 1, 89 .— Transf. , a poet : versificatores meliores quam duces, Just. 6, 9, 4 .

versĭfĭco.opening: v. a. versusfacio , to put into verse , write in verse , versify (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.): portenta in Homero versificata, Lucil. ap. Non. 533, 14 : fatiloquia Sibyllae, App. de Deo Socr. p. 46, 5 : versificandi…

versĭfĭcor.opening: dep. collat. form of versifico, acc. to Prisc. 8, 15, 82, p. 830 P.

versĭfĭcus.opening: adj. versifico , written in verse , versified , poetic (late Lat.): ordo, Sol. 11, 6 .

versĭformis.opening: adj. verto-forma , changing its form , changeable (post-class.): totum, Tert. Pall. 2 : cupitor (Juppiter), Mart. Cap. 6, § 589 : puer (Cupido), id. 9, § 917 .

versĭlis.opening: adj. verto , that may be turned (post-class.): profunditas, Mart. Cap. 4, § 423 : scaena, Serv. ad Verg. G. 3, 24 .

versĭlŏquus.opening: adj. versus-loquor , speaking in verse , Ennod. Carm. 1, 6, 36 .

versĭpellis.opening: ( ), , adj. vertopellis, that changes its skin; hence, in gen. , that changes its shape or form , that alters its appearance , that transforms himself or itself. Lit. In gen.: eccum Juppiter In Amphitruonis vertit sese…

verso.opening: ( ), ( inf. vorsarier, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 53 ), v. freq. a. verto , to turn , wind , twist , or whirl about often or violently (freq. and class.; syn.: verto, contorqueo). Lit. : qui caelum versat stellis fulgentibus…

versōrĭa.opening: ( ), , verto , a rope that guides a sail , a sheet (Plautin.); hence, trop.: versoriam capere, to turn the sail , i. e. tack : cape vorsoriam, Recipe te ad erum, about ship! Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 19 : cape modo vorsoriam,…

versūra.opening: ( ), , verto , a turning round , twirling about , rotating. Lit. : foliorum, Varr. R. R. 1, 46 : ejus loci (coxendicum), id. L. L. 7, § 67 Müll.— Transf. The turning-place , turn at the end of a furrow, Col. 2, 2, 28 ;…

versus.opening: ( ), (ante-class. collat. form of the plur. versi, Laev. ap. Prisc. p. 712 P.: versorum, Laber. ib.: versis, Val. ib.), verto, a turning round, i. e. of the plough . A furrow , Col. 2, 2, 25 ; Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 177 .—…

versūtĭa.opening: versutus , cunning , slyness , craftiness , subtlety , ingenuity (very rare; cf.: dolus, astutia); sing. (late Lat.), App. Mag. p. 307, 41 ; p. 325, 25.— Plur. , Liv. 42, 47, 7 .

versūtĭlŏquus.opening: adj. versutusloquor , crafly-speaking , sly : malitiae, Poët. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 38, 154 , and ap. id. Or. 49, 164 .

versūtus.opening: ( ), , adj. a lengthened form of versus, from verto; cf. astutus init. . In a good sense, adroit , dexterous , versatile; shrewd , clever , ingenious (class.; syn. callidus): homo versutus et callidus (versutos eos…

Vertacomacori.opening: a tribe of the Vocontii , Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 124 .

vertăgus.opening: Celtic , a greyhound , Mart. 14, 200, 1 ; Firm. Math. 5, 8.— Called also or (also ), Grat. Cyn. 203 .

vertē^bra.opening: verto , a joint. In gen., Cels. 8, 1 , Plin. 11, 46, 106, § 255 ; Sen. Ep. 78, 8 .—Of insects, Plin. 11, 1, 1, § 1 .— In partic., a joint , vertebra of the spine, Cels. 8, 1 .— In late Lat. collat. form , , , = ἰσχίον ,…

vertebrātus.opening: adj. vertebra , jointed , articulated , vertebrated : ossa, Plin. 11, 37, 67, § 177 : dens, id. 34, 8, 19, § 75 .

vertex.opening: ( ; cf. Quint. 1, 7, 25 The archaic form vortex was already disused in Cicero's time; cf. Ribbeck, Prol. Verg. 436 sq. ; id. G. 1, 481 n. Wagn. The grammarian Caper distinguishes thus: vortex fluminis est, vertex…

vertĭbŭlum.opening: id. , a joint , for the usual vertebra, lact. Opif. Dei, 5 med.

vertĭcillus.opening: id. , the whirl of a spindle, Plin. 37, 2, 11, § 37 ; App. Herb. 9 .

Vertĭcordĭa.opening: verto-cor , the Turner of hearts , an epithet of Venus, who was supposed to restrain maidens from unchastity, Val. Max. 8, 15, 12 ; Jul. Obseq. 97 (cf. Ov. F. 4, 157 sq. ).

vertĭcōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. vertex, I. , full of whirlpools or eddies , eddying : mare, Sall. Fragm. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 121 ( Sall. H. 4, 22 Dietsch); cf. Sen. Q. N. 7, 8, 2 : amnis, Liv. 21, 5, 15 : fluvius, Amm. 14, 2, 9 .

vertĭcŭla.opening: dim. verto , a joint , = vertebra, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 207, 24 ; cf. Fest. p. 371 .—In machines, Vitr. 10, 13, 1 .— Called also , , , Sol. 4 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 242 ; , , , id. Acut. 3, 17, 138 .

vertīgĭno.opening: v. n. vertigo , to whirl round , revolve : puncta luminis, Tert. Pall. 3 .

vertīgĭnōsus.opening: id. , one who suffers from giddiness or vertigo , vertiginous , Plin. 23, 2, 28, § 59 .

vertīgo.opening: verto , a turning or whirling round (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : assidua caeli, Ov. M. 2, 70 : ponti, id. ib. 11, 548 : venti, Sen. Q. N. 5, 13, 3 : torti fili, Luc. 6, 460 : rotarum, Prud. Psych. 414 : assiduā…

verto.opening: ( ), ( inf. vortier, Plaut. Rud. 3, 6, 48 ; Lucr. 1, 710 ; 2, 927 ; 5, 1199 al. ), v. a. and n. Sanscr. root vart-, to apply one's self, turn; cf. vart-ukas, round . Act. , to turn , to turn round or about (syn.: verso,…

Vertumnus.opening: ( ), , qs. vertomenos, as a part. pass., from verto, that turns or changes himself , orig. an Etruscan deity, the god of the changing year , i. e. of the seasons and their productions , also of exchange and of trade ,…

vĕru.opening: (collat. form of the nom. sing. , Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 15 and 17; masc. collat. form of the plur. , Aur. Vict. Caes. 17 ; abl. verubus, Ov. M. 6, 646 ; Juv. 15, 82 al. : veribus, Charis. pp. 50 and 112; Prisc. p. 672 ;…

vĕrūcŭlātus.opening: adj. veruculum , furnished with a small pike : falces, Col. 2, 20, 3 .

Verudoctĭus.opening: a chief of the Helvetii , sent as an ambassador to Cœsar , Caes. B. G. 1, 7 .

vĕrŭīna.opening: veru , a small javelin , Plaut. Bacch. 4, 8, 46 ; Gavius Bassus ap. Fulg. 564, 22 .

Verŭlae.opening: a town of Latium, now Veroli , Flor. 1, 11, 6 .—Hence, , , adj. , of Verulœ , Liv. 9, 42 ; 9, 43 .— , , , the inhabitants of Verulœ , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 64 .

vērum-tămen.opening: ( ; in recent edd. more freq. as two words, ; sometimes separated, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 45 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 41, § 101 infra), conj. [verum-tamen], but yet , notwithstanding , however , nevertheless (class.): cum pugnabant…

vērus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; cf. Zend var, believe; Sanscr. var, choose, wish , true , real , actual , genuine , etc. (opp. falsus, fictus). Lit. : secerni blandus amicus a vero et internosci tam potest adhibitā diligentiā, quam…

vĕrūtum.opening: ( ), , veru , a dart , javelin : veruta pila dicuntur quod veluti verua habeant praefixa, Paul. ex Fest. p. 375 Müll.: cursus quingentos saepe veruti, Enn. ap. Fest. ib. (Ann. v. 356 Vahl.); Caes. B. G. 5, 44 ; Sall. H.…

vĕrūtus.opening: adj. id. , armed with a dart or javelin : Volsci, Verg. G. 2, 168 ; cf. verutum.

vervactum.opening: vervago , fallow ground , a fallow field , Cato, R. R. 27 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 44, 2 ; Col. 11, 2, 32 ; 11, 2, 52 ; Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 176 ; Pall. 4, 2 .

vervăgo.opening: v. a. etym. unknown; acc. to Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 176, from ver-ago , to break up land, i. e. to plough land for the first time after its lying fallow : agros, Col. 11, 2, 8 .

Vervēcĕus.opening: ( ), , vervex , that has the form of a wether , an epithet of Jupiter Ammon, Arn. 5, 171 ; Inscr. Murat. 1043, 3 .

vervēcīnus.opening: adj. id. , of a wether : pellis, Lampr. Comm. 1 : caput, Arn. 5, 157 .

vervex.opening: ( and ), , , a wether. Lit. , Varr. L. L. 5, § 98 Müll.; id. ap. Non. 189, 30 ; Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 40 ; Cic. Leg. 2, 22, 55 .— Transf. , a name for a stupid fellow, qs. mutton-head , Plaut. Merc. 3, 3, 6 ; Auct. ap.…

vēsānĭa.opening: ( ), , vesanus , madness , insanity (very rare): extimui, ne vos ageret vesania discors, Hor. S. 2, 3, 174 : simulata (Ulixis), Plin. 35, 11, 40, § 129 : formidabatur flagrans vesania manus, Amm. 14, 2, 15 .

vēsānĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. vesanus , to be insane , rave (late Lat.): dicebat contra deum vesanire Theodosium, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 9, 30 .—Hence, , , part. , raging , furious : vesaniente vento, Cat. 25, 13 .

vē-sānus.opening: ( ), , adj. , not of sound mind , mad , insane (mostly poet. ). Lit. : remex, Cic. Div. 2, 55, 114 : homo, id. Dom. 2, 3 : tribunus plebis, id. ib. 21, 55 : poëta, Hor. A. P. 455 : stella vesani Leonis, fierce, raging,…

Vescia.opening: a little town in Latium , on the river Liris , Liv. 8, 11 ; 9, 25 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Vescia , Vescinian : ager, Cic. Agr. 2, 25, 66 ; Liv. 10, 21 ; 10, 31 : caseus, Plin. 11, 42, 97, § 241 (al.…

Vescitānĭa.opening: a district of Hispania Tarraconensis, Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 24 .

vesco.opening: v. a. vescor , to feed with any thing: quis nos vescet carne, Tert. Jejun. 5 .— Pass. , Isid. Orig. 20, 2, 27 : vescendi pupilli causā, Dig. 42, 5, 33 .

vescor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [ve- and root ed- of edo; cf. esca], to fill one's self with food , to take food , feed , eat. Lit. (class.; syn. pascor), constr. usu. with abl. , rarely with acc. or absol. With abl. : di nec escis…

vescŭlus.opening: adj. dim. of vescus , little , trifling : vinarium, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 46 Ritschl, Fleck., Brix, Wagn. (al. vasculum); v. R ib. Lat. Part. p. 10 ; cf.: vesculi male curati et graciles homines. Ve enim syllabam rei…

vescus.opening: adj. contr. from veesca . Small , little , thin , weak , feeble : farra (opp. vegrandia), Ov. F. 3, 445 : papaver, Verg. G. 4, 131 : frondes, id. ib. 3, 175 Serv.: corpus, Plin. 7, 20, 19, § 81 : vires, Afran. ap. Non.…

Vesĕris.opening: a river in Campania , with a town of the same name , Cic. Off. 3, 31, 112 ; id. Fin. 1, 7, 23 ; Liv. 8, 8 ; 10, 28 ; Val. Max. 6, 4, 1 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 26, 4 ; 28, 4 .

Vēsi.opening: the Visigoths , Sid. Carm. 7, 399 ; in sing. , id. ib. 5, 476 ; 7, 431.

vēsīca.opening: (in MSS. often or ), , , the bladder in the body of animals, the urinary bladder. Lit. , Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 18 ; Cic. Fin. 2, 30, 96 ; Plin. 30, 8, 21, § 65 ; Hor. S. 1, 8, 46 ; Petr. 27 ; App. M. 1, p. 108, 30 .—…

vēsīcārĭus.opening: adj. vesica , of or belonging to the bladder , bladder-. Adj. : aqua, i. e. curing pain in the bladder, Marc. Emp. 26 ; cf. Scrib. Comp. 146 .— Subst. : , , (herba), a plant that cures pain in the bladder , bladder -…

vēsīcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little blister , vesicle; containing air, Lucr. 6, 130 ; containing seeds, on plants, Cic. Div. 2, 14, 33 .

vēsīcŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of bladders or blisters , vesiculous , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 171 .

Vĕsontĭo.opening: a city in Gallia Belgica, the chief town of the Sequani , now Besancon , Caes. B. G. 1, 38 ; 1, 39 ; Auson. Grat. 31 .

vespa.opening: Gr. σφήξ; O. H. Germ. wefsa; Engl. wasp , a wasp , Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 19 ; Plin. 11, 21, 24, § 71 ; 20, 13, 51, § 133 ; Phaedr. 3, 13, 3 .

vespae.grammar: et vespillones dicuntur, qui funerandis corporibus officium gerunt, non a minutis illis volucribus, sed quia vespertino tempore eos efferunt
vespae.opening: , qui funebri pompā duci propter inopiam nequeunt. Hi etiam vespullae vocantur. Martialis: qui fuerat medicus, nunc est vespillo Diaulus, Fest. p. 369 Müll.

Vespăsĭānus.opening: : Ti. Flavius Vespasianus, a Roman emperor , reigned between 69 and 79 A. D., Suet. Vesp. 1 sq. ; Sid. Carm. 5, 327 .

Vespasĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; e. g. Vespasia Polla, the mother of Vespasian, Suet. Vesp. 1 : Vespasius Pollio, the father of Vespasia Polla, id. ib. 1 .

vesper.opening: (in class. prose mostly acc. vesperum, and abl. vespere, or adverb. vesperi; the plur. not used), ( neutr. , Varr. L. L. 7, § 50 and 9, § 73 Müll. acc. to Lachm.) [Gr. ἕσπερος, ἑσπέρα ], the evening , even , eve ,…

vespĕra.opening: = ἑσπέρα, i. e. ϝεσπερα; cf. the preced. art. , the evening , eventide (much more freq. than vesper; used only in sing. ; in Cic. only adverb., ad vesperam): prima vespera, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 4 ; so Suet. Tib. 74 ;…

vespĕrālis.opening: adj. vespera , of or belonging to evening : plaga, the west, Sol. 9 .

vespĕrasco.opening: v. inch. n. [vesper], to become evening , grow towards evening : vesperascente jam die, Tac. A. 16, 34 : vesperascente caelo, Nep. Pelop. 2, 5 .— Impers. : vesperascit, Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 7 : ubi jam vesperaverat, Gell.…

vespĕrātus.opening: Part. [vespera], grown into evening : die jam vesperato, Sol. 11 med.

Vesperĭes.opening: a town of Hispania Tarraconensis, Plin. 4, 20, 34, § 110 .

vesperna.opening: Fest. p. 368 Müll.; cf. id. s. v. cena, p. 54; and s. v. scensas, p. 339 [vesper].

vespertīlĭo.opening: vesper , a bat , Plin. 10, 61, 81, § 168 ; 11, 37, 62, § 164 ; 29, 4, 26, § 83 ; Macr. S. 7, 16 ; Varr. ap. Non. 47, 3 ; Auct. Carm. de Philom. 39.

vespertīnālis.opening: adj. , = vespertinus (late Lat.), Adaman. Vit. Columb. 3, 30.

vespertīnus.opening: adj. vesper . Of or belonging to evening or even-tide , evening- : tempora (opp. matutina), Cic. N. D. 2, 20, 52 : litterae, received in the evening (opp. antemeridianae), id. Att. 13, 23, 1 : senatusconsulta, made or…

vespĕrūgo.opening: id. . The evening-star , Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 119 ; Vitr. 9, 4 ; cf. Quint. 1, 7, 12 ; and Fest. p. 368 Müll.; Mart. Cap. 8, 883 .—* A bat , Tert. Anim. 32 .

vespĕrus.opening: adj. vespera , of or belonging to the evening , evening- : his horae rigandi matutina atque vespera, Plin. 19, 12, 60, § 183 (dub.; al. matutino atque vespera): tempus vesperum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 15, 141 ; 1, 15, 151 .

vespices.grammar: frutecta densa dicta a similitudine vestis

vespillo.opening: dim. 2. vespa , a corpse-bearer who carried out the bodies of the poor at night, Suet. Dom. 17 fin. ; Mart. 1, 48, 1 ; cf. vespae.

Vesta.opening: Sanscr. root vas, to burn; vasaras, day; whence also Gr. Εστία . Another name for Ops, Cybele, Terra, the wife of Cœlus and mother of Saturn , Cic. N. D. 2, 27, 67 ; Ov. F. 6, 267 .— Her granddaughter , daughter of…

vester.opening: ( ), , pron. poss. [vos], your : voster senex, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 60 (dub.; al. noster): animi vostri, id. Am. prol. 58 : num sermonem vestrum aliquem diremit noster interventus? Cic. Rep. 1, 11, 17 : vestra quae…

vestĭārĭus.opening: adj. vestis , of or belonging to clothes. Adj. : arca, a clotheschest, Cato, R. R. 11, 3 : negotiator, a clothesdealer, Dig. 38, 1, 45 .— Substt. , , , a clothes-dealer , Dig. 14, 3, 5, § 4 ; Inscr. Orell. 3643 ; 4294…

vestĭbŭlum.opening: perh. for vesti-bulum, kindr. with Sanscr. vas, habitare, commorari; cf. Vesta , the enclosed space between the entrance of a house and the street , a fore-court , entrance-court (cf. atrium). Lit. , Gell. 16, 5, 2 ;…

vestĭceps.opening: vestis-capio, that has got the first covering of the chin, opp. investis , bearded , arrived at puberty , manly , virile (post-class.). Lit. : arrogari non potest nisi jam vesticeps, Gell. 5, 19, 7 ; Tert. Anim. 56 ;…

Vestĭcŏla.opening: Vesta-colo , a Vestal virgin (late Lat.), Drac. Carm. 7, 22.

vestĭ-contŭbernĭum.opening: vestis , a lying under the same coverlet , sleeping in the same bed , bed - companionship , Petr. 11 .

vestĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little garment (post-class.), Dig. 33, 7, 18, § 13 .

vestĭfĭca.opening: vestis-facio , she that makes garments , a tailoress , Inscr. Orell. 2437 .

vestĭfĭcīna.opening: † vestificus , a making of garments , tailoring , Tert. Pall. 3 fin.

vestĭfĭcus.opening: vestis-facio , a maker of garments , a tailor , Inscr. Grut. 578, 7 .

vestĭflŭus.opening: adj. vestis-fluo , that wears long , flowing garments (a late poet. word): Lydus, Petr. 133 : Ser, Aus. Technop. Hist. 24 .

vestīgātĭo.opening: vestigo , a tracing or searching after (post-class.): Psyche dies noctesque mariti vestigationibus inquieta, App. M. 6, p. 173 .

vestīgātor.opening: or , , vestigo , a tracker , spy , tracer , searcher (not in Cic.): vestigator a vestigiis ferarum, quas indagatur, Varr. L. L. 5, § 94 Müll. (where the read. is vestigiator); so Col. 9, 8, 10 ; Sen. Ben. 3, 26, 2 ;…

vestīgĭum.opening: id. , a footstep , step; footprint , foot-track , track. Lit. : currentium pes vestigium facit, Quint. 9, 4, 67 : hac socci video vestigium in pulvere, Plaut. Cist. 4, 2, 29 : hominis, Plin. 8, 4, 5, § 9 : in foro…

ve-stīgo.opening: , no perf. and sup. , , v. a. etym. dub.; perh. Sanscr. vahis (bahis), out, and stigh-, to climb; cf. Gr. στίχος, a row, etc.; Angl. -Sax. stīgan; Germ. steigen, to climb . Prop., to follow in the track of; to track ,…

vestīmentum.opening: vestis , clothing , a garment , vestment , bedclothes , tapestry , etc., Dig. 34, 2, 24 ; Cic. Mil. 10, 28 ; Liv. 4 , 25, 13; Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 32 : aestiva, hiberna, Sen. Ben. 1, 12, 3 ; Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 30 ; Sen. Ep.…

Vestīni.opening: a people of Central Italy , on the Adriatic Sea , Auct. Her. 2, 28, 45 ; Liv. 8, 29 ; 10, 3 ; Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 107 .— Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Vestini : Vestina virum vis, Enn. ap. Charis. p. 251 P.…

vestĭo.opening: ( imperf. vestibat, Verg. A. 8, 160 ; inf. vestirier, Prud. Psych. 39 ), v. a. vestis , to cover with a garment , to dress , clothe , vest (syn.: induo, amicio). Lit. : Vatinii strumam sacerdotii διβάφὡ vestiant, Cic.…

vestĭplĭca.opening: vestis-plico , a (female) clothes-folder , ironer , laundress (anteand post-class.), Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 26 ; Pseudo Quint. Decl. 363 ; Inscr. Orell. 3315 ; cf. vestiplicus and vestispica.

vestiplĭcus.opening: id. , a clothes-folder , ironer , Inscr. Orell. 2839 ; cf. the preced. art.

vestis.opening: Sanscr. root vas-, to put on; Gr. ἑσ-, ϝεσ-; cf. ἕννυμι, ἐσθής , the covering for the body , clothes , clothing , attire , vesture (syn. amictus; in class. prose only sing. ). Lit. : lavere lacrimis vestem squalam et…

vestĭspĭca.opening: vestis-spicio , she that has the care of clothing , a wardrobewoman , Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 22 (Ritschl, Fleck., and Brix, vestiplica, q. v.); Afran. and Varr. ap. Non. p. 12, 15 .

vestītor.opening: vestio . A maker of clothing , tailor (post-class.), Lampr. Alex. Sev. 41 ; Inscr. Grut. 1111, 3 ; Inscr. Murat. 1842, 2 .— A clother , dresser : divinorum simulacrorum, Firm. Math. 3, 11, 9.

vestītus.opening: vestio , clothing , clothes , dress , apparel , raiment , attire , vesture. Lit. : hoc cum vestitu, Enn. ap. Non. p. 537, 28 (Trag. v. 373 Vahl.): immutabilis, Plaut. Ep. 4, 2, 8 : muliebris, Cic. Att. 1, 13, 3 ; id.…

Vestorĭus.opening: An artist of Puteoli , Vitr. 7, 11 init. —Hence, , , adj. , of or pertaining to Vestorius , Plin. 33, 13, 57, § 162 ; Isid. Orig. 19, 17 . — A friend of Cicero , Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 8, 1 ; Cic. Att. 4, 6, 4 ; 4, 16 ,…

vestras.opening: vester , of your family or nation , acc. to Charis. p. 133 P.; Diom. p. 317 ib.; Prisc. p. 1095 ib.

Vĕsŭlus.opening: a mountain in Liguria , now Monte Viso , Mel. 2, 4, 4 ; Verg. A. 10, 708 ; Plin. 3, 16, 20, § 117 .

Vĕsŭvĭus.opening: ve and σβε-, root of σβέννυμι; v. Lidd. and Scott s. v. , a celebrated volcano in Campania , Liv. 8, 8, 19 ; Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 22 ; Col. 3, 2, 10 ; Plin. Ep. 6, 6, 12 .—Collat. form ( ), , , Suet. Tit. 8…

Vĕtĕra.opening: a town of Gallia Belgica, now Xanten , Tac. A. 1, 45 ; called also Vetera castra, id. H. 4, 18 and 21.

vĕtĕrāmentārĭus.opening: adj. vetus , of or belonging to old things : sutor, a mender of old shoes, cobbler, Suet. Vit. 2 .

vĕtĕrānus.opening: adj. id. , old , veteran (in technical lang.): boves, Varr. R. R. 1, 20, 2 : pecus, Col. 6, 2, 9 : gallinae, id. 8, 5, 6 : vitis, id. 3, 15, 3 : mancipia, Dig. 39, 4, 16 : hostis, Liv. 21, 6, 5 : miles veteranus, or…

vĕtĕrārĭus.opening: adj. id. , old , mature (very rare): quoniam non contenti vina diffundere, veteraria per sapores aetatesque disponere invenimus, Sen. Q. N. 4, 13, 3 ; cf.: veteraria nostra et plena multorum saeculorum vindemiis horrea,…

vĕtĕrasco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to grow old : veterascens ad gloriam, Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. p. 437, 29 : pati aliquid veterascere, Col. 2, 14, 2 : ut nec vestimenta veterascerent, etc., wear out , Ambros. de Fide, 2, 2, 23: cum…

vĕtĕrātor.opening: veteratus , one who has grown old , become gray , is practised , skilled in any thing. In gen.: in causis privatis satis veterator, Cic. Brut. 48, 178 : in litteris, Gell. 3, 1, 5 .— In partic. In a bad sense, a crafty…

vĕtĕrātōrĭus.opening: adj. veterator, II. A. , crafty. cunning , sly (Ciceronian): nihil ab isto tectum, nihil veteratorium exspectaveritis: omnia aperta, omnia perspicua reperientur, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 54, § 141 ; so, ratio dicendi, id. Brut.…

vĕtĕrātrix.opening: veterator , a sorceress , App. M. 9, p. 230, 24 (al. veratrix).

vĕtĕrētum.opening: vetus , ground that has long lain fallow , old fallow ground , = vervactum, Col. 2, 10, 4 and 5; 2, 13, 2.

vĕtĕrīnārĭus.opening: adj. veterinus , of or belonging to beasts of burden and draught. Adj. : medicina, farriery, Col. 7, 3, 16 .— Subst. , , , a cattle-doctor , farrier , veterinarian , Col. 6, 8, 1 ; 7, 5, 14 ; 11, 1, 12 .— , , , a place…

vĕtĕrīnus.opening: adj. contr. from vehiterinus, from veho; cf. Fest. p. 369 Müll. , of or belonging to carrying or drawing burdens. Adj. : bestia, a beast of burden or draught , Cato ap. Fest. p. 369 ; called also pecus, Arn. 3, 139 :…

vĕternōsĭtas.opening: veternosus , lethargy , somnolency , Fulg. Myth. 3, 4 fin.

vĕternōsus.opening: adj. veternus, II. C. , afflicted with lethargy , lethargic. Lit. , Plin. 20, 4, 13, § 24 ; 28, 17, 67, § 230 ; Cato ap. Gell. 1, 15, 9 ; id. ap. Fest. p. 369 . — Transf. , sleepy , drowsy , dreamy : homo, Ter. Eun. 4,…

vĕtĕro.opening: v. a. vetus , to make old (late Lat.): dicendo autem novum veteravit prius, Vulg. Heb. 8, 13 .— P. a. : , , old , inveterate : mederi ulceribus veteratis, Plin. 32, 10, 52, § 141 : caseus, mouldy, Scrib. Comp. 140 .

vĕto.opening: (old form : votes, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 56 : votitus, id. As. 4, 1, 44 ; cf. Non. 45, 4 ; perf. ( poet. and late Lat.) vetavit, Pers. 5, 90 : vetati sunt, Vulg. Act. 16, 6 ), v. a. etym. dub. , not to suffer a thing to…

Vettius.opening: the name of a Roman gens, Cic. Att. 2, 4, 7 ; 6, 1, 15 ; id. Vat. 10, 24 .

Vĕtŭlōnĭa.opening: a town of Etruria , Sil. 8, 485 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Vetulonia , Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 227 .— , , , the inhabitants of Vetulonia , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 52 .

vĕtŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [vetus], little old , old (class.) Adj. : vetulus, decrepitus senex, Plaut. Merc. 2, 2, 43 : gladiator, Cic. Quint. 7, 29 : filia, id. Att. 13, 29, 1 : equi, id. Lael. 19, 67 : arbor (opp. novella), id. Fin.…

Veturĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. L. Veturius Philo, a consul 548 A.U.C., Cic. Brut. 14, 57 .— T. Veturius Calvinus, a consul 433 A.U.C., Cic. Off. 3, 30, 109 ; id. Sen. 12, 41 ; Liv. 3, 8, 2 .— Fem. : Veturia, the mother of…

vĕtus.opening: (ante-class. collat. form of the nom. sing. , Enn. and Att. ap. Prisc. p. 607 P.; cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 2 Müll.; abl. regularly, vetere; but veteri, Juv. 6, 121 ; Stat. Th. 1, 360 ; 11, 582 ; 13, 374 ; comp. class.…

vĕtuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [vetus], somewhat old or ancient , oldish , rather antiquated : color, Fronto Eloqu. p. 232 Mai: dictio, Sid. Ep. 8, 16 .

vĕtustas.opening: id. , old age , age , long existence. Lit. In gen.: municipium vetustate antiquissimum, Cic. Phil. 3, 6, 15 : vetustate possessionis se, non jure defendunt, id. Agr. 2, 21, 57 : tantum aevi longinqua valet mutare…

vĕtustesco.opening: ( acc. to Nigid. ap. Non. p. 437, 27 ), ĕre, v. inch. n. [vetustus], to grow old : vina, Col. 1, 6, 20 .

vĕtustus.opening: adj. vetus , that has existed a long time , aged , old , ancient (in the posit. mostly poet. , and almost exclusively of things; for the comp. vetustior, v. vetus): veteris vetusti (vini) cupida sum, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2,…

vexābĭlis.opening: adj. vexo . Disturbed , plagued , vexed : membra, Lact. 7, 5, 10 Bünem. N. cr. — Causing annoyance , troublesome , vexatious , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11, 78 ; 2, 9, 39 .

vexābĭlĭter.opening: adv. vexabilis, II. , troublesomely , vexatiously : caput onerare, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9, 41 .

vexāmen.opening: vexo , a shaking , quaking : mundi, Lucr. 5, 340 .

vexātĭo.opening: vexo , a violent movement , shaking. Lit. (rare): partus, Plin. 28, 19, 77, § 253 : minima pomorum, Petr. 60 : ipsā enim vexatione constringitur (arbor) et radices certius figit, Sen. Prov. 4, 16 .— Trop. , agitation ,…

vexātīvus.opening: adj. id. , causing annoyance , vexatious , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 29, 156 ; id. Tard. 3, 4, 63 .

vexātor.opening: id. , a troubler , harasser , abuser , vexer (Ciceron.): custosne urbis an direptor et vexator esset Antonius, Cic. Phil. 3, 11, 27 : aetatulae suae, id. Sest. 8, 18 : furoris (Clodii), i. e. opposer, id. Mil. 13, 35 .

vexātrix.opening: vexator , she that vexes or molests , Lact. 3, 29, 10 : libido vexatrix hominum, Prud. Psych. 58 .

vexātus.opening: P. a. , v. vexo, II. A. fin.

vexillārĭus.opening: vexillum . A standard-bearer , ensign. Lit. , Liv. 8, 8, 4 ; Tac. H. 1, 41 .— Transf. , a leader , captain of a band of robbers, App. M. 4, p. 146 .— , , , in the times of the emperors, the oldest class of veterans ,…

vexillātĭo.opening: id. . A body of the vexillarii; acc. to others, a body of soldiers united under one flag (vexillum), a corps , battalion , Suet. Galb. 20 ; Inscr. Orell. 845 ; 2009 sq. al.— A division of cavalry , a troop , squadron ,…

vexillum.opening: dim. of vēlum , a military ensign , standard , banner , flag. In gen., Caes. B. G. 6, 36 ; Cic. Phil. 2, 40, 102 ; 5, 11, 29 ; id. Att. 10, 15, 2 ; id. Agr. 2, 32, 86 ; Tac. A. 1, 20 al. — In partic., a red flag placed…

vexo.opening: ( inf. vexarier, Verg. Cir. 480 ), , v. freq. a. veho , orig., to shake , jolt , toss in carrying; hence, in gen., to move violently , to shake , agitate. Lit. (rare; syn. quatio): vexasse grave verbum est, factumque ab…

vĭa.opening: ( , Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 14 ), ae ( gen. sing. vias, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 679 P., or Ann. v. 421 Vahl.; viāï, Enn. ap. Cic. Sen. 6, 16 , or Ann. v. 209 ib.; Lucr. 1, 406 ; 1, 659 ; 2, 249 et saep.; dat. plur. VIEIS, Inscr.…

vĭālis.opening: adj. via , of or belonging to the highways or roads : Lares, placed, worshipped by the road-side, Plaut. Merc. 5, 2, 24 ; called also dii, Serv. ad Verg. A. 3, 148 .

vĭārĭus.opening: (old form VIASIEIS, Lex Thor.), , adj. id. , of or belonging to the highways or roads : lex, for keeping the roads in repair , Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 6, 5 .

vĭātĭcātus.opening: adj. viaticum , furnished with travelling - money : viaticati hercle admodum aestive sumus, Plaut. Men. 2, 1, 30 .

vĭātĭcŭlum.opening: dim. id. , a small sum of money for a journey (post-class.), Dig. 5, 1, 18 fin. ; App. M. 7, p. 191, 16 .

vĭātĭcus.opening: adj. via , of or belonging to a road or journey , viatic. Adj. (very rare): cena, a parting meal, farewell repast, Plaut. Bacch. 1, 1, 61 ; so perh. factum, id. Trin. 4, 2, 45 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.— Subst. : , , ,…

vĭātor.opening: vio . In gen., a wayfarer , traveller , Cic. Fat. 15, 34 ; id. Mil. 21, 55 ; Caes. B. G. 4, 5 ; Verg. G. 4, 97 ; id. Fragm. ap. Don. Vit. Verg.; Hor. C. 3, 4, 30 ; id. S. 1, 5, 17 ; Ov. Tr. 2, 271 ; id. P. 4, 10, 34 ;…

vĭātōrĭus.opening: adj. viator , of or belonging to a journey : vasa, travellingdishes, Plin. 16, 10, 20, § 50 ; so, argentum, silver travelling-plate, Dig. 34, 2, 40 : horologia, Vitr. 9, 9 : medicamentum, Veg. Vet. 1, 61 ; 3, 65, 12 .—…

vĭātrix.opening: id. , a female traveller , Mart. Cap. 6, § 581 ; Inscr. Mur. 1058. 8.

vībex.opening: ( ), , , the mark of a blow or stripe , a weal , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 63 Müll.; Cato ap. Non. p. 187, 26 ; Plin. 30, 13, 39, § 118 ; Pers. 4, 48 ; App. M. 9, p. 222, 26 ; cf. Fest. p. 369 Müll.

vĭbĭa.opening: a plank , cross-piece supported on trestles (varae) so as to form a bank; hence the proverb: sequitur varam vibia, one error follows another, Aus. Idyll. 12 praef. monos.; v. vara.

Vĭbĭlĭa.opening: a goddess presiding over highways , the goddess of roads , Arn. 4, 131 .

Vibinātes.opening: a people of Southern Italy , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 105 .

Vibĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. C. Vibius Pansa, a consul , Caes. B. C. 1, 24 ; Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 8 .— Vibius Crispus, an orator , Quint. 5, 13, 48 .— Fem. , Anthol. Lat. 2, p. 132 .

vibo.opening: the flower of the herb called Britannica, Plin. 25, 3, 6, § 21 .

Vibo.opening: or , , , a town in the territory of the Bruttii , now Monteleone , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin. 3, 5, 10, § 73 ; Cic. Att. 16, 6, 1 ; Mart. Cap. 6, § 645 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Vibo : ager, Liv. 21, 51, 4 sqq.;…

vī^brābĭlis.opening: adj. vibro . * That may be brandished : ornus (i. e. hasta), Aus. Ep. 24, 108 .—* Quivering , glimmering : sidus, Mart. Cap. 1, § 29 .

vī^brābundus.opening: adj. id. , tremulous , glimmering : Mercurius (stella), Mart. Cap. 8, § 880 .

vī^brāmen.opening: id. , a tremulous motion , quivering : trisulca draconum, App. M. 6, p. 179, 17 .

vī^brātĭo.opening: id. , a brandishing , vibration : hastae, Fest. s. v. gradivus, p. 97: continuata tonitruum, Calp. ap. Vop. Carin. 8 .

vī^brātus.opening: vibro , a quivering , tremulous motion (post-class.): luminis, flickering, Mart. Cap. 8, § 887 : crebri ignium, id. ib. 1 , § 66.

vī^brissae.grammar: pili in naribus hominum, dicti quod his evulsis caput vibratur

vī^brisso.opening: v. n. , to shake the voice (in singing), to trill : vibrissare est vocem in cantando crispare, Fest. p. 370 Müll.; Titin. ap. Fest. l. l.

vī^bro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
vī^bro.opening: v. a. and n. cf. Sanscr. vip, to tremble . Act. , to set in tremulous motion , to move rapidly to and fro , to brandish , shake , agitate (class.; syn.: quatio, ventilo). Lit. : hastas ante pugnam, Cic. de Or. 2, 80,…

Vībullĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; e. g. L. Vibullius, a partisan of Pompey, Caes. B. C. 1, 15 ; 1, 23 ; Cic. Att. 8, 1 .

vīburnum.opening: the wayfaring-tree : Viburnum lantana, Linn.; Verg. E. 1, 26 .

vīcānus.opening: (post-class. collat. form , Cod. Just. 11, 56 ), , adj. vicus , of or dwelling in a village. Adj. : Tmolites ille vicanus, villager, Cic. Fl. 3, 8 : haruspices, who go about from village to village , Enn. ap. Cic. Div.…

Vĭca Pŏta.opening: vinco- potior , Victress-and-possessor , an appellation of the Goddess of Victory, Cic. Leg. 2, 11, 28 ; Liv. 2, 7, 12 : Diespiter, Vicae Potae filius, Sen. Lud. Most. Claud. 9, 4 ; Arn. 3, 25 .

vĭcārĭānus.opening: adj. vicarius , of or belonging to a deputy or vicar , vicarial : apparitores, Cod. Just. 1, 35, 1 : apex, the rank of a vicar, Sid. Ep. 1, 3 .

vĭcārĭus.opening: adj. vicis , that supplies the place of a person or thing, substituted , delegated , vicarious. Adj. : vicaria fides amicorum supponitur, Cic. Rosc. Am. 38, 111 : manus, Quint. Decl. 6, 21 : corpus, id. ib. 16, 7 :…

vīcātim.opening: adv. vicus . From street to street , through the streets , Sisenn. ap. Non. p. 188, 26 ; Suet. Caes. 41 med. ; Tac. H. 2, 95 ; Hor. Epod. 5, 97 .— From village to village , through the villages , in hamlets : habitare,…

vīcēnālis.opening: adj. viceni , containing the number twenty : sphaera, having twenty angles, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 5, 14 (just before, vigintiangula).

vīcēnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the number twenty , vicenary. Adj. : annorum lex me perdit quina vicenaria: metuunt credere omnes, i. e. the law by which young people under five-and-twenty were incapable of making…

vīcēni.opening: (collat. form , Col. 4, 30, 2 ), ae, a, num. distrib. adj. [viginti], twenty each , twenty distributively. Lit. : si duae res quae conferuntur, vicenas habent partes, Varr. L. L. 10, § 5 Müll.: annos nonnulli vicenos in…

vīcennālis.opening: adj. vicennium , of twenty years , every twenty years (postclass.). Adj. : votis vicennalibus, Num. Alex. Sev. ap. Eckhel. D. N. V. 7, p. 275.— Subst. : , , , a festival on the twentieth anniversary of an emperor's…

vīcennĭum.opening: vicies-annus , a period of twenty years : post decennii aut vicennii tempus, Dig. 50, 8, 8 .

vĭcĕquaestor.opening: vicis - quaestor , = proquaestor (late Lat.), Ps.-Ascon. ad Cic. Verr. 1, 38 .

vĭcĕquaestūra.opening: vicis-quaestura , = proquaestura (late Lat.), Ps.-Ascon. Arg. ad Cic. Verr. 2 . 2, 3.

vīcēsĭmāni.opening: vicesimus , soldiers of the twentieth legion , Tac. A. 1, 51 ; 1, 64 : vexillarii, id. ib. 14, 34 .

vīcēsĭmārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the twentieth part. Adj. : aurum, of the tax called vicesima (v. h. v.), Liv. 27, 10, 11 .— Subst. : , , , a receiver of the vicesima, Petr. 65 .

vīcēsĭmātĭo.opening: id. , a drawing by lot of every twentieth man for execution , vicesimation , Capitol. Macrin. 12 .

vīcēsĭmus.opening: or (collat. form , Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 21 ; Caes. B. C. 3, 34 ; Sall. C. 47, 2 ; Col. 5, 1, 10 ; Manil. 4, 462 al. ; but not in Cic.), a, um, ord. num. adj. [viginti], the twentieth. Adj. : annus, Plaut. Capt. 5, 3, 3 :…

Vīcētĭa.opening: ( ), , , a town in Gallia Transpadana, in the territory of Venetia , now Vicenza , Tac. H. 3, 8 ; Suet. Gram. 23 ; Inscr. Orell. 5152 ; Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 132 . — Its inhabitants are called or , , , Brut. ap. Cic. Fam.…

vĭcĭālĭa.opening: vicia , the stalks or haulm of vetches , Col. 6, 30, 5 Schneid. N. cr.

vĭcĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to vetches : cribrum, Col. 8, 5, 16 .

vīcĭens.opening: or , num. adv. [viginti], twenty times : viciens centena milia passuum, Caes. B. G. 5, 13 fin. : viciens tantum, Plin. 14, 4, 6, § 53 : superficiem aedium aestimarunt HS. viciens, i. e. two millions, Cic. Att. 4, 2, 5 :…

Vĭcĭlīnus.opening: vigil , the Watchful , the Vigilant , an epithet of Jupiter, Liv. 24, 44, 8 .

vīcīnālis.opening: adj. vicinus , neighboring , near : usus, Liv. 21, 26, 8 : bella, Just. 41, 1, 3 : via, a road over the fields used in common, a village-path, Dig. 43, 8, 2 ; 43, 7, 3 ; Front. Aquaed. 126 ; Sen. Ben. 5, 24, 9 .

vīcīnārĭus.opening: adj. vicinus , neighboring , near (post-class.): via, a by-way in a camp, Hyg. Grom. p. 5, 2 ; 12, 2 .

vīcīnĭa.opening: vicinus , neighborhood , nearness , vicinage , vicinity. Lit. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; but cf. vicinitas): proximae viciniae habitat, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 27 : hic proximae viciniae, id. Mil. 2, 3, 2 :…

vīcīnĭtas.opening: id. , neighborhood , nearness , proximity , vicinity (class.). Lit. : vel virtus tua me vel vicinitas Facit, ut te audacter moneam, etc., Ter. Heaut. 1, 1, 4 : propter vicinitatem totos dies simul eramus, Cic. Att. 5,…

vīcīnĭtus.opening: adv. id. , in the neighborhood , close by : omnes intra centum vicinitus arceantur, Cod. Th. 15, 1, 4.

vīcīnor.opening: v. dep. id. , to be neighboring , near (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 2, 11 ; 6, 9 ; 7, 2 : vicinantia capiti loca, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 6, 27 ; 2, 16, 97 ; 2, 34, 181 : plaustrum, Mart. Cap 6, § 608 .

vīcīnus.opening: adj. vicus , near , neighboring , in the neighborhood or vicinity. Lit. Adj. (mostly poet. ; cf.: contiguus, finitimus): taberna, Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 24 : silva, id. C. 3, 29, 39 : oppidum, id. Epod. 5, 44 : urbes, id. A.…

vĭcis.opening: (as a gen.; the nom. does not occur), vicem, vice; in plur. , vices ( nom. and acc. ) and vicibus ( dat. and abl. ), cf. Gr. εἴκω, to yield; root ϝικ-; v. Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 135 , change , interchange ,…

vĭcissātim.opening: adv. vicis , in return , again (ante-class. for the class. vicissim): ad argumentum vicissatim remigrare, Plaut. Poen. prol. 46 ; id. Stich. 4, 1, 27 ; Naev. ap. Non. p. 183, 15 .

vĭcissim.opening: adv. id. , on the other hand , on the contrary , again , in turn (freq. and class.; cf. in vicem): nunc mihi vicissim supplicabunt, Plaut. As. 3, 3, 92 : da te mihi vicissim, Ter. Heaut. 4, 3, 10 : terra uno tempore…

vĭcissĭtas.opening: id. , change , alternation , = vicissitudo: vicissitatemque imperandi tradidit, Att. ap. Non. p. 185, 18 (Trag. Rel. p. 181 Rib.).

vĭcissĭtūdo.opening: vicis, I. , change , interchange , alternation , vicissitude (class.; used alike in sing. and plur. ): omnium rerum vicissitudo est, Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 44 : ex alio in aliud vicissitudo atque mutatio, Cic. Tusc. 5, 24, 69…

Victa.opening: 2. victus , the goddess that presides over food , Arn. 3, 115 .

victĭma.opening: perh. root vig- of vigeo; with superl. ending; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 509 sq. , a beast for sacrifice adorned with the fillet (vitta), a sacrifice , victim (cf. hostia). Lit. , Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 93 ; Hor. C. 3, 23, 12 ;…

victĭmārĭus.opening: adj. victima , of or belonging to victims. Adj. : negotiator, a dealer in beasts for sacrifice, Plin. 7, 12, 10, § 54 (al. suarius).— Subst. : , , An assistant at sacrifices , Liv. 40, 29, 14 ; Val. Max. 1, 1, 12 ;…

victĭmo.opening: v. a. id. , to offer in sacrifice , to sacrifice (post-class.): hircum Marti, App. M. 7, p. 192, 30 : hostiam, id. ib. 7 , p. 197, 31: filium, Vulg. Ecclus. 34, 24 .

victĭto.opening: v. freq. a. vivo , to live , feed , support one's self , subsist on any thing (ante-class.): ficis victitamus aridis, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 59 ; so, sinapi, id. Truc. 2, 2, 60 : suco suo, id. Capt. 1, 1, 12 : parce, id.…

victor.opening: vinco . In gen., a conqueror , vanquisher , victor. Prop. Absol. : quod (sc. stipendium) victores victis imponere consuērint, Caes. B. G. 1, 44 : multa victori, eorum arbitrio, per quos vicit, etiam invito facienda…

Victor.opening: : S. Aurelius, a Roman historian of the fourth century A.D., Amm. 21, 10, 6 .

victōrĭa.opening: victor . Prop., victory. In war. Absol. : cernere de victoriā, Enn. ap. Non. p. 511, 9 (Trag. Rel. v. 206 Vahl.): insignia victoriae, non victoriam reportare, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 3, 8 ; cf.: exercitus plus victoriae quam…

victōrĭālis.opening: adj. victoria , of or belonging to victory (late Lat.). Adj. : dies, day of victory , i. e. when victories are celebrated , Treb. Gall. 3: scipio, Cassiod. Var. 6, 1 .— Subst. : , , , a plant , called also Idaea Daphne,…

victōrĭātus.opening: Part. [victoria], gained by victory (late Lat.): plus victoriatum est quam injuriatum, Tert. adv. Gnost. 6 .

Victōrĭŏla.opening: dim. victoria, II. A. , a little statue of Victory , Cic. N. D. 3, 34, 84 .

victōrĭōsus.opening: adj. victoria , victorious (ante- and post-class.; cf. victor, II. B.), Cato ap. Gell. 4, 9, 12 .—As an epithet of the emperor Probus, Nummus ap. Eckhel. D. N. V. 7, p. 505.— Sup. : vir, Sid. Ep. 5, 6 : PRINCIPES,…

victrix.opening: ( abl. victrice, Cic. Phil. 13, 3, 7 al. ; but victrici, Liv. 28, 6, 8 ; gen. plur. victricium, Tac. H. 2, 59 ; Suet. Tib. 14 : victricum, Fest. p. 178, 26 ), victor , she that is victorious , a conqueress , victress;…

victŭālis.opening: adj. 2. victus , of or belonging to nourishment or sustenance (postclass.). Adj. : ministerium, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 10, 17 : sumptus, Cod. Just. 8, 51, 20 .— Subst. : , , , provisions , victuals , Cassiod. Var. 3, 44…

victŭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to sustenance (post-class.): exhibitio, i. e. of provisions, Tert. Monog. 8 .

victus.opening: (ante-class. collat. form of the gen. sing. victuis, Varr. ap. Non. p. 494, 11 : victi, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 75 ; also cited ap. Non. p. 484, 10 ), vivo . That upon which one lives; sustenance , nourishment , provisions ,…

vīcŭlus.opening: dim. vicus , a little village , hamlet , Cic. Rep. 1, 2 ; Liv. 21, 33 .

vīcus.opening: Sanscr. vēcas, vēcman, house; Gr. οἶκος; O. H. Germ. wīch, village; and Engl. -wick or -wich, as in Berwick, Norwich . Collectively, a row of houses in town or country, a quarter of a city, a street , Cic. Mil. 24, 64 ;…

vĭdēlĭcet.opening: adv. contr. from videre licet; cf. scilicet from scire licet; v. scilicet init.; prop. it is easy to see, to comprehend , serving, like scilicet, to confirm and complete what precedes (but with the difference that…

vĭdens.opening: a seer , prophet (eccl. Lat.): eamus ad videntem, Vulg. 1 Reg. 9, 9 : Samuel videns, id. 1 Par. 9, 22 : Gad videns et Nathan propheta, id. 2 Par. 29, 25 et saep.

vĭdĕo.opening: (viden', i.e. videsne, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 37 ; Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 10 ; 2, 2, 34 ; 4, 6, 16 ; Cat. 61, 98 ; Tib. 2, 2, 17 ; Verg. A. 6, 779 ; inf. viderier, Cic. Dom. 53, 136 ; Ter. Hec. 5, 1, 33 : vidĕ, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 46…

vĭdŭālis.opening: adj. vidua , of or belonging to a widow , widow- : pudicitia, Aug. Civ. Dei, 15, 26: depeculator depositi vidualis, Ambros. in Psa. 40, 27 .

vĭdŭertas.opening: viduus , lack of fruits of the earth , dearth , sterility , Cato, R. R. 141, 2 ; cf. Fest. p. 369 Müll.

vĭdŭĭtas.opening: id. , bereavement , want , lack. * In gen.: omnium copiarum atque opum, Plaut. Rud. 3, 3, 2 .— In partic., widowhood , Cic. Caecin. 5, 13 ; Liv. 40, 4, 2 ; App. Mag. p. 291, 33 .

Vidularĭa.opening: the title of a lost comedy by Plautus.

vidŭlus.opening: a travelling-trunk , portmanteau , wallet , Plaut. Rud. 4, 3, 60 sq. ; 4, 4, 83 ; 4, 4, 86 ; 4, 4, 89 sqq.; id. Men. 5, 7, 47 ; id. Ep. 1, 1, 20 .

vĭdŭo.opening: v. a. viduus , to deprive , bereave of any thing ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). In gen.: civibus urbem, Verg. A. 8, 571 : ornos foliis, Hor. C. 2, 9, 8 : arva pruinis, Verg. G. 4, 518 : vitem pristino alimento, Col.…

vĭdŭus.opening: adj. Sanscr. vidhava, without a husband; cf. ve- in vecors, etc.; ἠΐθεος, single , deprived or bereft of a husband or wife , bereft of a lover , spouseless , mateless , widowed. Lit. : quae (Penelopa) tam diu vidua viro…

vĭdŭvĭum.opening: viduus , widowhood (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 6, 2 ; Inscr. Don. cl. 10, n. 51.

Vĭenna.opening: a city in Gallia Narbonensis, on the Rhodanus , now Vienne , Caes. B. G. 7, 9 ; Cic. Fam. 10, 9, 3 ; Mel. 3, 5, 2 ; Plin. 2, 47, 46, § 121 ; 3, 4, 5, § 36 ; Mart. 7, 88, 2 al. —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to…

vĭĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. root in Sanscr. vjā-, cover; Gr. ἴτυς, border; cf. Lat. vitex, vitta, vimen, vitis, etc. , to bend or twist together , to plait , weave (ante-class.): viere vincire: a quo est in Sota Ennii: Ibant…

vĭesco.opening: v. inch. n. [vieo], to shrink up , shrivel , wither (cf. vietus): viescens ficus, Col. 12, 15, 1 .

vĭgĕo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. ugras, mighty; Gr. ὑγιής, sound; cf. Lat. vegeo, vigil, augeo , to be lively or vigorous; to thrive , flourish , bloom; to be in honor , esteem , repute , etc. (class.; mostly of things, concrete and…

vĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. [vigeo], to become lively or vigorous; to thrive , to begin to flourish or bloom (class.): de niloque renata vigescere copia rerum, Lucr. 1, 674 ; 1, 757 : jam laeti studio pedes vigescunt, Cat. 46, 8 :…

vīgessis.opening: viginti-as , twenty asses, Mart. 12, 76, 1 ; Mart. Cap. 7, § 737 .

vĭgil.opening: ( gen. plur. vigilium, Liv. 10, 33, 6 ), adj. vigeo , awake , on the watch , alert (class.; cf.: insomnis, exsomnis). Lit. Adj. : prius orto Sole vigil calamum et chartas et scrinia posco, Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 113 ; 1, 2, 37…

vĭgĭlābĭlis.opening: adj. vigilo , wakeful , watchful : dormitio nostri pectoris, Varr. ap. Non. p. 100, 2 .

vĭgĭlans.opening: Part. and P. a. of vigilo.

vĭgĭlanter.opening: adv. , v. vigilo, P. a. fin.

vĭgĭlantĭa.opening: vigilans, from vigilo , wakefulness (class.). Lit. : erat (Plinii) incredibile studium, summa vigilantia, Plin. Ep. 3, 5, 8 .—Jocosely: fuit (Caninius) mirificā vigilantiā, qui suo toto consulatu somnum non viderit,…

vĭgĭlātĭo.opening: vigilo , wakefulness , sleeplessness , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 101 .

vĭgĭlax.opening: adj. id. , watchful. Lit. : canes, Col. 7, 12, 5 : Subura, Prop. 4 (5), 7, 15. — Trop. : curae, Ov. M. 2, 779 .

vĭgĭlĭa.opening: ( neutr. collat. form , Varr. ap. Non. p. 232, 4 ) [vigil]. Lit. In gen., wakefulness , sleeplessness , a lying awake : ut neque vigilia praecesserit neque ventris resolutio, Cels. 2, 6 : corporum robora nocturnā…

vĭgĭlĭārĭum.opening: id. . A watchtower , Sen. Ep. 57, 6 .— A small sepulchral monument in the shape of a watchtower , Inscr. Orell. 4557 .

vĭgĭlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
vĭgĭlo.opening: v. n. and a. [vigil]. Neutr. , to watch , i. e. to be or keep awake at night, not to sleep , be wakeful (class.; syn. excubo). Lit. : ad multam noctem vigilare, Cic. Rep. 6, 10, 10 : de nocte, id. Q. Fr. 2, 15, 2 :…

virgātor.opening: virga , one who beats with rods , a flogger , Plaut. As. 3, 2, 19 .

virgātus.opening: adj. id. . Made of twigs or osiers : calathisci, Cat. 64, 320 . — (Acc. to virga, II. C.) Striped : sagula, Verg. A. 8, 660 : vestes, Sil. 4, 155 : tigris, Sen. Hippol. 344 ; id. Herc. Oet. 146 ; cf.: virgato corpore…

virgētum.opening: id. , a thicket of rods or osiers , Cic. Leg. 2, 8, 21 .

virgĕus.opening: adj. id. , of rods or twigs , of brushwood : scopae, Cato, R. R. 152 : crates, Col. 1, 6, 22 : saepes, id. 11, 3, 7 : anuli ex myrto, Plin. 15, 29, 37, § 124 : supellex, Verg. G. 1, 165 : flamma, of brush set on fire,…

virgĭdēmĭa.opening: formed from virga, after the analogy of vindemia , a harvest of rods , i. e. of stripes or blows , Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 22 ; Varr. ap. Non. p. 187, 13 .

virgĭnālis.opening: adj. virgo , of or belonging to a maiden or virgin , maidenly , virgin , virginal. Adj. : habitus, vestitus, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 3, § 5 : forma, Gell. 14, 4, 2 : modestia, Poët. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 31, 66 : verecundia, Cic.…

virgĭnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to virgins : feles, virgin-cat , i. e. virgin-stealer , Plaut. Pers. 4, 9, 14 ; cf. virginalis.

Virgĭnensis.opening: or , , id. , the goddess that presided over the loosing of the bridal zone , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 11; 6, 9.

Virgĭnesvendŏnĭdes.opening: comically formed from virgo - vendo , virginseller , Plaut. Pers. 4, 6, 20 Ritschl.

virgĭnĕus.opening: adj. virgo , of or belonging to a maiden or virgin , maidenly , virgin ( poet. for virginalis): figura, Tib. 3, 4, 89 : forma, Ov. M. 3, 607 : vultus, id. ib. 5, 563 ; 10, 631: facies, id. ib. 8, 323 : comptus, Lucr. 1,…

virgĭnĭtas.opening: virgo , maidenhood , virginity , Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 59 ; Verg. A. 12, 141 ; Ov. M. 1, 487 ; 1, 695 ; 3, 255 ; Plin. 25, 13, 95, § 154 ; Stat. Achill. 1, 292 ; Val. Fl. 6, 449 ; App. M. 5, p. 160, 24 .— Transf. , concr. =…

virgĭnor.opening: v. dep. virgo , to act or behave like a virgin , to play the virgin , Tert. Virg. Vel. 12 fin.

virgo.opening: root varg-; Sanscr. ūrg, strength, ūrga-jami, nourish; Gr. ὀργάω, to swell, ὀργή, impulse , a maid , maiden , virgin (cf. puella). Lit. In gen.: cum Sabinas honesto ortas loco virgines rapi jussit, Cic. Rep. 2, 7, 12 :…

virgōsus.opening: adj. virga , full of twigs (late Lat.): frutex, Pall. 1, 24, 2 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 17, 9 fin.

virgŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little twig , a small rod , a wand , Nep. Thras. 4, 1 ; Cic. Phil. 8, 8, 23 ; Sen. Q. N. 1, 7, 1 : divina, a divining-rod, Cic. Off. 1, 44, 158 ; also, the title of a work by Varro , ap. Non. p. 550, 12 :…

virgŭlātus.opening: adj. virgula , striped (cf. virga, II. C., and virgatus, II.): concha, Plin. 9, 33, 52, § 103 .

virgultum.opening: contr. from virguletum, from virgula (only in plur. ), a bush , thicket , copse , shrubbery , Caes. B. G. 3, 18 fin. ; 7, 73 ; Cic. Div. 1, 24, 49 ; id. Cael. 18, 42 ; Liv. 1, 14, 7 ; id. E. 10, 7 ; id. A. 5, 661 ; Ov.…

virgultus.opening: adj. virgultum , full of bushes or thickets , shrubby : vallis, Sall. Fragm. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 3, 516 ; Sil. 12, 354 .

virguncŭla.opening: dim. virgo , a little maid , young girl , Petr. 18 ; 20 ; Sen. Q. N. 1, 17, 9 ; Curt. 8, 4, 25 ; Juv. 13, 40 .—In apposition: virguncula puella, Front. Aquaed. 10 .

vĭrĭae.opening: a kind of ornament for the arm , armlets , bracelets (syn. armilla), Plin. 33, 3, 12, § 40 ; Tert. Pall. 4 med. ; Ambros. Abrah. 1, 9, 88 .

Vĭrĭāthus.opening: or , , , a celebrated leader of the Lusitanians in the war against the Romans , Liv. Epit. 52 ; 54 ; Vell. 2, 1, 3 ; 2, 90, 3 ; Flor. 2, 17 fin. ; Cic. Off. 2, 11, 40 ; Val. Max. 6, 4, 2 ; Sil. 4, 354 ; 10, 219 .— or ,…

vĭrĭātus.opening: adj. viriae , adorned with bracelets , Lucil. ap. Non. p. 186, 30 ; Varr. ib. p. 187, 14 .

vīrĭcŭlae.opening: dim. vires, from vis , little strength , small force : patrimonii, small means, App. M. 11, p. 271, 24 .

vīrĭcŭlum.opening: a graving-tool , graver , burin , = cestrum, Plin. 35, 11, 41, § 149 .

vĭrĭdārĭum.opening: ( , , contr., ), , viridis , a plantation of trees , a pleasure-garden , Cic. Att. 2, 3, 2 ; Petr. 9 fin. ; Cels. 1, 2 ; Suet. Tib. 60 ; Plin. 18, 2, 2, § 7 ; Dig. 7, 1, 13 ; 33, 7, 26 ; Lampr. Heliog. 23 al.

vĭrĭdesco.opening: v. inch. n. [viridis], to grow or become green , Ambros. Hexaëm. 5, 1, 1; id. Spir. Sanc. prol. 16 .

vĭrĭdĭcātus.opening: Part. [id.], made green , green : silva, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2, § 3 dub.; v. Orell. N. cr. (Bait. virdicata).

vĭrĭdis.opening: ( gen. plur. viridum, Stat. Th. 2, 279 ), adj. vireo , green. Lit. (as the most general designation for every shade of that color). Adj. : color, Ov. M. 10, 137 ; Plin. Ep. 8, 20, 4 : smaragdi, Lucr. 2, 805 : collis,…

vĭrĭdĭtas.opening: viridis , green color , greenness , verdure , viridity. Lit. : herbescens viriditas, Cic. Sen. 15, 51 : pratorum, id. ib. 16, 57 : maris, Plin. 37, 5, 20, § 76 .— Transf. , freshness , briskness , vigor : senectus…

vĭrĭdo.opening: v. a. and n. id. . Act. , to make green , cause to grow green : hastas floribus, Val. Fl. 6, 136 : vada subnatis viridentur ab herbis, become green, Ov. Hal. 90 .—More freq., Neutr. , in the part. pres. viridans,…

Viridomărus.opening: ( ), , , a chief of the Ædui , Caes. B. G. 7, 38 ; Prop. 4, 10, 41 (called , Liv. Epit. 20 ).

vĭrīlis.opening: adj. vir , of or belonging to a man , manly , virile (cf.: mas, masculus). Lit. In respect of sex, male , masculine. In gen.: virile et muliebre secus, Sall. Fragm. ap. Macr. S. 2, 9 : virile secus, i. e. puer, Plaut.…

vĭrīlĭtas.opening: virilis , manhood (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. The age of manhood , Plin. 33, 12, 54, § 155 .— Abstr., manhood , virility : Gaiam C. Caesarem, quasi incertae virilitatis, dicere, Tac. A. 6, 5 : adempta, id. ib. 6, 31 .—…

vĭrĭŏla.opening: dim. viriae , a little bracelet , Plin. 33, 3, 12, § 40 ; Dig. 18, 1, 14 ; 34, 2, 40 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 31 .

vĭrĭōsē.opening: adv. viriosus , strongly , violently , Tert. Anim. 19 med.

vĭrĭōsus.opening: adj. vis , strong , robust , violent (post-class.): vitia usu, Tert. adv. Valent. 16 med. : spinae, App. M. 7, p. 196 dub.

Vĭrĭplāca.opening: vir-placo , a name of the goddess (Juno) who, in her temple on the Palatine Hill, reconciles husbands to their wives, appeaser of men , Val. Max. 2, 1, 6 .

vīrĭpŏtens.opening: adj. vis-potior , mighty in power , mighty , powerful , an epithet of Jupiter, Plaut. Pers. 2, 3, 1 .

vĭrĭpŏtens.opening: adj. vir-potior , fit for a husband , i. e. marriageable , nubile : puella, Dig. 24, 1, 65 ; 26, 7, 58 ; 35, 1, 99 : virgo, ib. 50, 16, 3 .

vĭrītānus.grammar: ager dicitur, qui viritim populo distribuitur

vĭrītim.opening: adv. vir , man by man , to each one separately , singly , individually (used only with distrib. numerals, never with card.; v. infra ). Lit. : viritim dicitur dari, quod datur per singulos viros. Cato: praeda, quae…

vĭror.opening: vireo , green color , greenness , verdure (post-class. for viriditas): pratorum, App. Flor. p. 348, 18 : superest aliquid de virore, Pall. Jun. 12 ; Vop. Prob. 19 .

vĭrōsus.opening: adj. vir , fond of men , longing after men : uxor, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 21, 30 ; Afran. ib.; App. M. 9, p. 223 med. : qui non modo vinosus, sed virosus quoque sit, Scipio Afric. ap. Gell. 7, 12, 5 .

vīrōsus.opening: adj. virus . Full of or covered with slime , slimy : loci, Cato, R. R. 257, 11 : pisces, Cels. 2, 21 .— Sup. : medicamentum adversus stomachum, Scrib. Comp. 103 .— Having a bad odor , stinking , fetid : virosi odoris…

virtŭōsus.opening: adj. virtus , virtuous , good (late Lat.), Aug. c. Sec. Man. 10.

virtūs.opening: ( gen. plur. virtutium, App. Mag. 73 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 10, 34 ; dat. and abl. VIRTVTEI, Inscr. Corp. Lat. 1, 30 and 34), vir , manliness , manhood , i. e. the sum of all the corporeal or mental excellences of man,…

vīrŭlentĭa.opening: virulentus , an offensive odor , a stench : hircorum, Sid. Ep. 8, 14 med.

vīrŭlentus.opening: adj. virus , full of poison , poisonous , virulent : serpentes, Gell. 16, 11, 2 .

vīrus.opening: Sanscr. visham; Gr. ἰός, poison , a slimy liquid , slime. In gen., of animals and plants, Verg. G. 3, 281 ; Col. 2, 14, 3 ; Plin. 19, 5, 27, § 89 ; 30, 6, 15, § 45 ; Stat. S. 1, 4, 104 .—Of animal sperm or semen , Plin.…

vīs.opening: plur. vīres, ĭum (class. only in nom. , acc. and abl. sing. and in plur.; gen. sing. very rare; Tac. Or. 26 ; Dig. 4, 2, 1 ; Paul. Sent. 5, 30 ; dat. sing. vi, Auct. B. Afr. 69, 2; C. I. L. 5, 837; collat. form of the…

viscātōrĭum.opening: visco , a snare (late Lat.), Manich. Cit. Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 3, 74.

viscātus.opening: Part. [id.], smeared with birdlime : virgae, limed twigs. Lit. , Varr. R. R. 3, 7, 7 ; Ov. M. 15, 474 : alae, id. A. A. 1, 391 .— Transf. : omnia viscatis manibus leget, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 332, 30 ; 396, 4 .— Trop. :…

viscellātus.opening: adj. 1. viscus , stuffed with the entrails of fishes or of birds: pisces, Plin. Val. 1, 24 : pullus, id. 2, 17 med.

Viscellīnus.opening: an agnomen of the consul Sp. Cassius, who was put to death for aiming at the sovereignty , Cic. Lael. 11, 36 ; cf. id. ib. 8, 28 .

viscĕrātim.opening: adv. 1. viscus , piecemeal : dissupat membra, Enn. ap. Non. p. 183, 17 (Trag. v. 145 Vahl.).

viscĕrātĭo.opening: id. , a public distribution of flesh cr mcat , Cic. Off. 2, 16, 55 ; Liv. 8, 22 ; 39, 46 ; Suet. Caes. 38 ; Inscr. Orell. 134 ; 3858 : sine amico visceratio, leonis ac lupi vita est, a feeding, Sen. Ep. 19, 10 .

viscĕrĕus.opening: adj. id. , consisting of flesh : arvum nondum viscereum, i. e. which had not yet been employed in the creation of man, Prud. Apoth. 1093 .

viscĭdus.opening: adj. viscum , clammy , sticky , viscid : acetum, Theod. Prisc. 1, 2 ; 1, 6 : viscidiores cibi, id. de Diaeta, 18.

visco.opening: v. a. , to smear , besmear : cum se inter articulorum conjunctiones usu commotionum viscaverit (sanies), Theod. Prisc. 2, 21 : spirat et hinc miseri viscantur labra mariti, are glued, smeared, Juv. 6, 463 .

viscōsus.opening: adj. viscum , full of birdlime , sticky , viscous : pastus, Prud. Ham. 824 ; Pall. 1, 14 .

viscum.opening: ( collat. form , , Plaut. Bacch. 1, 1, 16 ) [cf. Gr. ἰξός, ϝιξος ; Lat. viscus], the mistletoe. Lit. , Plin. 16, 44, 94, § 248 ; 24, 4, 6, § 11 ; Verg. A. 6, 205 .— Transf. , birdlime made from the berries of the…

vīsĭbĭlis.opening: adj. video . Pass. , that may be seen , visible (late Lat. for adspectabilis): exhalationes tenues vixque visibiles, App. de Mundo, p. 60, 37; id. de Deo Socr. p. 42, 22 : deus, Prud. Apoth. 146 : gloria, id. Cath. 5,…

vīsĭbĭlĭtas.opening: visibilis, I. , visibility , Tert. Carn. Chr. 12 fin. ; Fulg. ap. Contin. Verg. p. 750 Stav.

vīsĭfĭcus.opening: adj. video- facio , causing to see , conferring sight (late Lat.), Theod. Prisc. 4, 2 fin.

vīsĭo.opening: video , the act or sense of seeing , sight , vision. Lit. : ignes ... nostrae visioni occurrunt, App. de Mundo, p. 63 fin. ; id. M. 2, p. 120, 32 ; 8 , p. 203, 37: in caelestis sponsi visione requiescere, Greg. Mag.…

vīsĭtātĭo.opening: visito . * A sight , appearance , Vitr. 9, 4 fin. — A visit (postclass.), Tert. adv. Jud. 13 fin. — Trop. , a visitation , punishment , Vulg. Isa. 10, 3 ; id. 1 Pet. 2, 12.

vīsĭtātor.opening: id. , a visitor (late Lat.), Aug. Serm. in Fer. Pentec. 1, 2 ; a protector , Vulg. 2 Macc. 3, 39 .

vīsĭto.opening: v. freq. a. viso . To see (ante- and post-class.): quia te non visitavi, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 20 : aliquem, id. Curc. 2, 3, 64 ; id. Ep. 4, 1, 12 ; 4, 1, 24 : ignotā facie, quae non visitata sit, id. Trin. 3, 3, 37…

visĭum.opening: Gr. βδέσμα , a stench : βδέσμα , visio, Gloss.

vīso.grammar: si, sum, 3 v. freq. a. and n.
vīso.opening: v. freq. a. and n. video , to look at attentively , to view , behold , survey (class.). Lit. : ludos nuptiales, Plaut. Cas. 5, 1, 2 : ex muris visite agros vestros ferro inique vastatos, Liv. 3, 68, 2 : praeda…

visor.opening: a scout , only in a gloss ap. Tac. A. 16, 2 ; omitted by Draeg. and Halm.

vispellio.opening: a class of thieves who robbed corpses of their grave-clothes , Dig. 21, 2, 31 ; 36, 1, 7 fin. ; 46, 3, 72, § 5 Momms.

Vistŭla.opening: a river in Eastern Germany , the mod. Weichsel or Vistula , Mel. 3, 4, 1 ; Plin. 4, 12, 25, § 81 ; 4, 13, 27, § 97 ; 4, 14, 28, § 100 .—Called also , , , Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 100 .

vīsŭālis.opening: adj. visus , attained by sight (late Lat.): probatio, Cassiod. Var. 4 , 51.—Hence, subst. : , , , the power of vision , Theod. Prisc. 4, 2 .— Adv. : , visibly (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 36, 29 .

vīsŭālĭtas.opening: visualis , the power of seeing , the faculty of sight , vision (postclass.), Tert. Anim. 29 .

visŭla.opening: a kind of vine , Col. 3, 2, 21 ; Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 31 .

vīsum.opening: video , something seen , !*? sight , appearance , vision. In gen.: visa somniorum, Cic. Tusc. 1, 41, 97 : talia visa, Prop. 2, 26 (3, 21), 20: dic age ... visa quid ista ferant, Ov. Am. 3, 5, 32 : turpia, Prop. 2, 6, 28…

Vĭsurgis.opening: a river in Northern Germany , the mod. Weser , Mel. 3, 3, 3 ; Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 100 ; Tac. A. 2, 9 ; 2, 11 ; 2, 16 sq.; Sid. Carm. 23, 244 .

vīsus.opening: video , a seeing , looking; a look , glance; the faculty or act of seeing , sight , vision. Lit. : feminas omnes visu nocere, quae duplices pupillas habent, Cic. Fragm. ap. Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 18 : visu effascinare, Plin.…

vīta.opening: ( gen. sing. vitaï, Lucr. 1, 415 ; 2, 79 ; 3, 396 ), vivo; Sanscr. gīv, to live; Gr. βίος, life , life. Lit. In gen.: tribus rebus animantium vita tenetur, cibo, potione, spiritu, Cic. N. D. 2, 54, 134 : dare, adimere…

vītābĭlis.opening: adj. vito , that may or ought to be shunned : Ascra, Ov. P. 4, 14, 31 ; Arn. 5, 165 .

vītābundus.opening: adj. id. , shunning , avoiding , evading (rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.). With acc. : vitabundus classem hostium, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. p. 186, 17 ( id. H. 3, 19 Dietsch): Hanno vitabundus castra hostium consulesque, Liv.…

vītālis.opening: adj. vita , of or belonging to life , vital. Adj. : caloris natura vim habet in se vitalem, vital power, Cic. N. D. 2, 9, 24 : spiritus, id. ib. 2, 45, 117 : totum corpus vitalis calor liquit, Curt. 3, 5, 3 ; 7, 3, 14 ;…

vītālĭtas.opening: id. , vital force , life , vitality : durat in corde, Plin. 11, 37, 69, § 182 ; so id. 11, 38, 90, § 221 ; 11, 45, 103, § 250 .

vītātĭo.opening: vito , a shunning , avoiding , avoidance : doloris, Cic. Fin. 5, 7, 20 : oculorum, lucis, urbis, fori, id. Phil. 3, 10, 24 : periculi, Auct. Her. 3, 2, 3 .

Vitellĭa.opening: an ancient town of the Æqui , near the modern Valmontone , Liv. 2, 39 ; 5, 29 ; Suet. Vit. 1 .

Vĭtellĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So esp., A. Vitellius, a Roman emperor. —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the emperor Vitellius , Vitellian : via, so named after him, Suet. Vit. 1 ; Tac. H. 1, 1 ; 1, 57 .— , , adj. , of…

vĭtellus.opening: dim. vitulus . * A little calf , as a term of endearment, Plaut. As. 3, 3, 77 .— Transf. , the yolk of an egg, Cels. 6, 6, 1 ; Cic. Div. 2, 65, 134 ; Petr. 33 fin. ; Plin. 10, 53, 74, § 148 ; Hor. S. 2, 4, 14 ; 2, 4, 57…

vītĕus.opening: adj. vitis , of or belonging to the vine : coliculus, Varr. R. R. 1, 31, 4 : pocula, i. e. wine, Verg. G. 3, 380 : rura, planted with vines, Prud. Ham. 228 .

vītex.opening: Sanscr. vaja, twig; Gr. ἴτυς, rim; cf. Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 392 , the chaste-tree , Abraham's balm : Vitex agnus castus, Linn.; Plin. 24, 9, 38, § 59 .

vĭtĭābĭlis.opening: adj. vitium , that may be harmed , violable , corruptible : ne jam vitiabilis esset, Prud. Apoth. 1113 ; id. Ham. 216 .

vītĭārĭum.opening: vitis , a nursery for vines , Cato, R. R. 40 ; 47 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 31, 2 ; Col. 3, 4, 1 ; 3, 5, 1 .

vĭtĭātĭo.opening: vitio , an injuring , violation , corruption (post-Aug. and very rare): feminae, Sen. Contr. 3, 23, 6 .

vĭtĭātor.opening: id. , an injurer , violator , corrupter (post-Aug. and very rare): feminae, Sen. Contr. 2, 11, 1 ; 3, 23, 1 ; 3, 23, 4 : pupillae, Quint. Decl. 284 ; 309 .

vītĭcarpĭfer.opening: adj. vitiscarpo-fero , that serves for pruning vines : forcipes, Varr. ap. Prisc. p. 868 P.

vītĭcella.opening: a plant , otherwise unknown, Isid. Orig. 17, 9, 92 .

Viticīni.opening: a people in the territory of Picenum , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 108 .

vītĭcŏla.opening: vitis-colo , a cultivator of vines , a vine-planter , Sil. 7, 193 .

vītĭcŏmus.opening: adj. vitis-coma , adorned or crowned with vine-leaves : ulmus, Sid. Carm. 2, 328 : Lyaeus, Avien. Arat. 70 .

vītĭcŭla.opening: ( , Plin. Ep. 1, 24, 4 ), , dim. vitis . A little vine , Cic. N. D. 3, 35, 86 ; Tert. Carm. adv. Marc. 2, 230 ; Val. Cat. Dir. 11, 5 .— A tendril , in gen.: fruticis, Plin. 24, 11, 58, § 98 : cucumeris, Pall. 4, 9, 8 .

vītĭfer.opening: adj. vitis-fero , vinebearing , i. e. supporting or producing vines : arbores, Pall. 3, 13, 2 : colles, Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 60 ; cf. mons, Sil. 4, 349 : Vienna, Mart. 13, 107, 1 .

vītĭgĕnus.opening: adj. vitis-gigno , vine-born , produced from the vine : liquor, Lucr. 5, 15 : latices, id. 6, 1072 ; cf. vitigineus.

vītĭgĭnĕus.opening: adj. id. , produced by the vine , vine- : surculi, Cato, R. R. 41, 3 : folia, Col. 12, 16, 3 : ligna, Plin. 30, 6, 16, § 50 : columnae, id. 14, 1, 2, § 9 ; cf. vitigenus.

vĭtĭlēna.opening: vitium-lena; cf. vitilitigator , a bawd , procuress : malesuada, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 56 MSS. (Ritschl, invitam lena; Lorenz, viti malesuada plena, ex conj. Speng.).

vĭtĭlīgo.opening: vitium , a kind of cutaneous eruption , tetter , Cels. 5, 28, 19 ; Lucil. ap. Fest. p. 369 Müll.; Plin. 20, 15, 59, § 165 ; 21, 19, 75, § 129 ; 22, 25, 74, § 156 ; Just. 36, 2, 12 ; App. Mag. p. 306, 14 .

vītĭlis.opening: adj. vieo , platted , interwoven. Adj. : cola, Cato, R. R. 11, 2 : alvi apum, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 16 : cistae, Plin. 15, 17, 18, § 60 : naves corio circumsutae, id. 7, 56, 57, § 206 et saep.— Subst. : , , , things…

vĭtĭlītĭgātor.opening: vitium-litigator; cf. vitilena , a brawler , wrangler , Cato ap. Plin. praef. § 32; cf. vitilitigo.

vĭtĭlītĭgo.opening: v. n. vitium-litigo , to quarrel disgracefully , to brawl , wrangle to abuse , calumniate : scio ego, quae scripta sunt, si palam proferantur, multos fore qui vitilitigent, Cato ap. Plin. praef. § 30; cf. vitilitigator.

vītīnĕus.opening: adj. perh. contr. from vitigineus , of the vine , vine- : vincula, Flor. 3, 20, 4 .

vĭtĭo.opening: v. a. vitium , to make faulty , to injure , spoil , mar , taint , corrupt , infect , vitiate (class., esp. in the trop. sense; syn.: corrumpo, noceo). Lit. In gen.: dira lues quondam Latias vitiaverat auras, Ov. M. 15,…

vĭtĭōsĭtas.opening: vitiosus , faultiness , corruption , viciousness , vice. * Lit. : umoris, Macr. S. 7, 10, 10 .— Trop. (Ciceron.): hujus virtutis contraria est vitiositas. Sic enim malo quam malitiam appellare eam, quam Graeci κακίαν…

vĭtĭōsus.opening: adj. vitium , full of faults or defects , faulty , defective , bad , corrupt , etc. Lit. (very rare): pecus (with morbosum), Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 21 : locus (corporis pecudum), i. e. diseased, Col. 7, 5, 6 : nux, Plaut.…

vitiparra.opening: a small bird , otherwise unknown, perh. the titmouse , Plin. 10, 33, 50, § 96 .

vītis.opening: root in Sanscr. vjā, to cover; cf. Goth. vindan; Germ. winden, to bind; Lat. vieo; cf.: vitta, vitex , a vine , grapevine. Lit. , Plin. 14, 1, 2, § 9 ; Cic. Sen. 15, 52 sq. ; Col. 3, 1 sq. ; Cic. N. D. 2, 47, 120 ;…

vītĭ-sător.opening: vitis-sero , a vineplanter : Sabinus, Verg. A. 7, 179 .—Of Bacchus, Att. ap. Macr. S. 6, 5 .—Of Saturn, Arn. 3, 117 .

vĭtĭum.opening: ( gen. plur. vitiūm, Titin. ap. Non. p. 495, 13 ), from the same root with vieo, vitis, vitta; prop. a twist; hence , a fault , defect , blemish , imperfection , vice (syn. menda). Lit. : quomodo autem in corpore est…

vīto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
