ămĕthystĭnus.opening: adj. amethystus . Of the color of amethyst : vestes, Mart. 1, 97, 7 .—Also absol. : amethystina (sc. vestimenta), * Juv. 7, 136 .— Set or adorned with amethyst : trientes, Mart. 10, 49 .

ămĕthystīzōn.opening: adj. , , = ἀμεθυστίζων , resembling the amethyst in color : carbunculi, prob. our violet ruby , Plin. 37, 7, 25, § 93 .

ămĕthystus.opening: , = ἀμέθυστος . The amethyst , a precious stone of violet-blue color , Plin. 37, 9, 40, § 121 sqq.; Vulg. Exod. 28, 19 ; ib. Apoc. 21, 20 .— A kind of vine , Col. 3, 2, 24 ; cf. Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 31 .

ămĭa.opening: , and , , , = ἀμία , the tunny , a sea-fish : (piscem) amiam vocant cujus etc., Plin. 9, 15, 19, § 49 .—The form amias: acc. amian, Lucil. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 47 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 21 ib.

ămĭantus.opening: , = ἀμίαντος (unspotted, pure), the amianth , a stone which may be separated into threads and spun , and is inconsumable by fire; asbestos , earth-flax , Plin. 36, 19, 31, § 139 .

ămīcābĭlis.opening: adj. amicus , friendly , amicable (post-class. and rare), Firm. Math. 5, 5.— Adv. : , in a friendly manner , Jul. Epit. Nov. 63, § 211 .

ămīcālis.opening: adj. id. , friendly (postclass.): affectio, Dig. 17, 1, 10, § 7 : transactio, Cod. 6, 58, 15, § 5: Deus hospitalis, amicalis, App. de Mundo, p. 75, 9.

ămīcārĭus.opening: amica , one that procures a mistress , a procurer , Diom. p. 313 P.

ămĭcīmen.opening: amicio , a garment , = amictus (only post-class.): candidum, App. M. 11, p. 261, 9 : rude, id. ib. 11 , p. 268, 32.

ăm-ĭcĭo.grammar: ĭcui, or ixi, ictum, 4 v. a.
ăm-ĭcĭo.opening: v. a. ( fut. amicibor, Plaut. Pers. 2, 5, 6 ; perf. only in exs. below; inf. perf. amicisse, Front.) [jacio], to throw round , to wrap about (cf. ἀμφιβάλλω ); exclusively of upper garments (on the contr., induere , of…

ămīcĭtĭa.opening: ( gen. sing. amicitiāï, Lucr. 3, 83 ; acc. amicitiem, id. 5, 1019 Lachm.; cf. Charis. p. 94 P., and Neue, Formenl. I. p. 372) [amicus], friendship (very freq. in Cic., occurring more than 200 times). Lit. : Est autem…

ămīco.opening: v. a. amicus , to make friendly to one's self : Oeclides solitā prece numen amicat, Stat. Th. 3, 470 .

ămīcōsus.opening: adj. id. , rich or abounding in friends , Diom. p. 313 P.

ămictōrĭus.opening: adj. amicio , suitable for throwing about one: linteamen, Cod. Th. 8, 5, 48, § 1.—Hence, subst. : , , , a garment which is thrown about or over one, a light , loose garment , esp. of women, a scarf , a tie for the neck…

ămictus.opening: amicio , orig. a throwing about or on one of a garment; hence, The manner of dressing , fashion : amictum imitari alicujus, Cic. de Or. 2, 22, 91 (cf. Plin. Ep. 2, 3, 2 ): est aliquid in amictu, Quint. 11, 3, 156 .—…

ămĭcŭlum.opening: amicio , a garment that one throws about or on him , a mantle , cloak : amiculum genus est vestimenti, a circumjectu dictum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 28 Müll.: amicae amictus amiculo, Cic. Div. 2, 69 : agreste duplex amiculum,…

ămīcŭlus.opening: dim. amicus , a dear friend : quid de Docimo amiculo meo? * Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 34 : te nil miseret, dure, tui dulcis amiculi? Cat. 30, 2 ; * Hor. Ep. 1, 17, 3 .—Hence, , , , a dear ( female ) friend : de amiculà rixatus,…

ămīcus.opening: from amo, as φίλος from φιλέω, and from ( gen. plur. amicūm, Ter. Heaut. prol. 24 ). A friend; constr. with gen. or poss. adj.; v. Zumpt, Gram. § 410: est is (amicus) tamquam alter idem, Cic. Am. 21, 80 (cf. id. ib. 25,…

Ămīnaeus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = Ἀμιναῖος , of or pertaining to Aminœa , a region in the country of the Piceni , distinguished for the culture of the vine: vites, Verg. G. 2, 97 ; so Cato, R. R. 6, 4 ; 7, 2 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 25 Schneid.;…

Ămīsĭa.opening: , ae. Masc. , a river in Germany , now the Ems , Tac. A. 1, 60 ; 1, 63 ; 2, 23 ; in Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 100 , and Mel. 3, 3 , called , ii; cf. Mann. Germ. 419. — Fem. , a fortress built by the Romans upon the Ems (near…

Ămīsus.opening: , = Ἀμισός , a town in Pontus , now Samsoon , Cic. Imp. Pomp. 8 ; Plin. 37, 8, 37, § 115 ; Mel. 1, 19 .— , , , Plin. 6, 2, 2, § 7 . Cf. Mann. Asia Min. 2, 448 sq.— , , , the inhabitants of Amisus , Plin. Ep. 10, 93 .

ămĭta.opening: cf. abba, avus, and Engl. aunt (so the mother's sister is called matertera, from mater; cf. Dig. 38, 10, 10 ), a father's sister , a paternal aunt , Cic. Clu. 10 ; Liv. 39, 11 ; Tac. A. 12, 64 ; 27, 16 ; Vulg. Lev. 20,…

Ămĭternum.opening: acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, 5, 12, from am- = amb- and Aternus , = Ἀμίτερνον , a very ancient town built by the Aborigines , in the Sabine country , now San Vettorino; cf. Mann. Ital. 1, 509; the birthplace of the historian…

ămĭtīnus.opening: adj. amita , descended from a father's sister; hence, , , , and , , , cousins , cousins-german , Dig. 38, 10, 1 and 10.

ămo.opening: v. a. (amāsso = amavero, Plaut. Cas. 5, 4, 23 ; id. Curc. 4, 4, 22 ; id. Mil. 4, 2, 16 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 28 Müll.: amāsse = amavisse, Ter. Eun. 5, 1, 11 : amantum = amantium, Plaut. Men. 2, 3, 4 ; Lucr. 4, 1077 ;…

ămoebaeus.opening: adj. , = ἀμοιβαῖος . alternate (pure Lat. alternus); hence, amoebaeum carmen = ᾆσμα ἀμοιβαῖον , a responsive song , Fest.; Serv. ad Verg. E. 3, 28, 59, 66 al. —Hence in metre, pes amoebaeus: ex duabus longis et totidem…

Ămoebeus.opening: ( ), , , = Ἀμοιβεύς , a distinguished Athenian harp-player , Ov. A. A. 3, 399 .

ămoenĭtas.opening: amoenus , pleas antness , delightfulness , loveliness. Lit. , of places (as scenery, a garden, river, etc.; in the poets, except Plaut., rare; never in Ter., Lucr., or Hor.): nunc domus suppeditat mihi hortorum…

ămoeno.opening: v. a. amoenus , late Lat. Lit. , of places, to make pleasant : regio aut consita pomis aut amoenata lucis, Salv Gub. Dei, 7 med. — Trop. , to please , delight : amoenare oculos, Cypr. Ep. 2, 1 : amoenare felices animas,…

ămoenus.opening: adj. amo; some comp. ἀμείνων , lovely , delightful , pleasant , charming (in gen. of objects affecting the sense of sight only; as a beautiful landscape, gar dens, rivers, pictures, etc.: amoena loca.. quod solum amorem…

ămōmis.opening: , = ἀμωμίς , a plant similar to the genuine amomum , but inferior in fragrance , Plin. 12, 13, 28, § 49 .

ămōmum.opening: or , , , = ἄμωμον , an aromatic shrub , from which the Romans prepared a costly , fragrant balsam : Cissus vitiginea, Linn.; Plin. 12, 13, 28, § 43 ; 16, 32, 59, § 135 : Assyrium vulgo nascetur amomum, Verg. E. 4, 25 ;…

ămor.grammar: like honos, labos, colos ōris m.
ămor.opening: (old form , , etc., Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 2 ; v. Neue, Formenl. I. p. 170), , amo , love (to friends, parents, etc.; and also in a low sense; hence in gen., like amo, while caritas , like diligere, is esteem, regard, etc.;…

ămōrābundus.opening: adj. amor , loving , amorous : Laberius in Lacu Averno mulierem amantem verbo inusitatius ficto amorabundam dixit, Gell. 11, 15, 1 .

Ămorgus.opening: or , , , = Ἀμοργός , one of the Sporades in the Ægean Sea , the birthplace of the poet Simonides; under the Roman emperors, a place for the banishment of criminals; now Amorgo , Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 70 ; Tac. A. 4, 30 ;…

ămōrĭfer.opening: adj. amor-fero , producing , or awakening love : sagittae, Ven. 6, 2, 13.

ămōrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. amor-facio , causing love , App. Herb. 123 .

ămŭlētum.opening: (Arab. hamalet), a sympathetic preservative against sickness , etc., φυλακτήριον , an amulet (usu. hung around the neck): veneficiorum amuleta, Plin. 29, 4, 19, § 66 ; so id. 30, 15, 47, § 138 al.

Ămūlĭus.opening: , = Ἀμούλιος , son of Procas , king in Alba , who expelled his brother Numitor , and ordered his grandsons Romulus and Remus to be thrown into the Tiber; hence, dirus, Ov. F. 4, 53 ; cf. Liv. 1, 3 sq. : injustus, Ov. M.…

ămurca.opening: (better than ), , , = ἀμόργη (cf. Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 194 ), the watery part that flows out in pressing olives , the lees or dregs of oil , Cato, R. R. 91 ; 101 ; 103 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 64 ; Col. 12, 50, 5 ; Plin. 15, 8,…

ămurcārĭus.opening: adj. amurca , pertaining to the lees of oil (v. amurca): dolia, Cato, R. R. 10, 4 .

ămūsĭa.opening: , = ἀμουσία , ignorance of music , Varr. ap. Non. p. 171, 30 .

ămūsos.opening: , = ἄμουσος , one unskilled in music , * Vitr. 1, 1 med.

ămussis.opening: etym. unc.; perh. from am- and assis = axis, a plank, i. e. something flat, straight, moved about a surface in adjusting it ( acc. amussim, v. Neue, Formenl. I. p. 198; abl. and plur. not used; only ante- and…

ămussĭto.opening: v. a. amussis , to make according to rule , i. e. accurately , nicely : amussitata indoles, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 38 Ritschl.

ămussĭum.opening: id. , a horizontal wheel for denoting the direction of the wind , Vitr. 1, 6 .

Ămȳclae.opening: , = Ἀμύκλαι . A town in Laconia , in a beautiful , fertile region , the residence of Tyndarus and the birthplace of Castor and Pollux; also renowned on account of its temple and Colossus of Apollo , now Agios Kyriaki ,…

Ămȳclīdēs.opening: patr. , a male descendant of Amyclas , the builder of Amyclœ , i. e. Hyacinthus , Ov. M. 10, 162 .

ămyctĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀμυκτικός , scratching; hence, of medical remedies, sharp , biting , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 6 ; Theod. Prisc. 2, 5 .

Ămўcus.opening: , = Ἄμυκος . Son of Neptune , king of the Bebrycians , Val. Fl. 4, 148 .— A centaur slain in the contest with the Lapithœ , Ov. M. 12, 245 .— A Trojan , Verg. A. 10, 704 .

ămygdăla.opening: , = ἀμυγδάλη . An almond , Cato, R. R. 8, 2 ; Col. 6, 10, 12 ; Plin. 12, 9, 19, § 36 .— = ἀμυγδαλῆ , an almond-tree , Col. 5, 10 fin. ; Plin. 16, 26, 42, § 103 .

ămygdălācĕus.opening: adj. amygdala , similar to the almond-tree : folium, Plin. 26, 11, 69, § 111 .

ămygdăleus.opening: adj. id. , of an almond-tree : ramus, Pall. Insit. 157 .

ămygdălĭnus.opening: adj. id. . Of or from almonds : oleum, Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 26 .— Pruna, i. e. ingrafted on an almond-tree , Plin. 15, 13, 12, § 42 .

ămygdălum.opening: , = ἀμύγδαλον , i. q. amygdala. An almond , an almondkernel , Ov. A. A. 3, 183 ; Pall. 2, 15 fin. — An almond-tree , Col. Arb. 25 .

ămўlo.opening: v. a. amylum , to mix with starch (only post-class.): jus, Apic. 7, 6 : lac, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13 .

ămўlum.opening: or , , , = ἄμυλον , starch , Cato, R. R. 87 ; Cels. 2, 20 ; Plin. 18, 7, 17, § 76 .

Ămȳmōnē.opening: , = Ἀμυμώνη . Daughter of Danăus , and grandmother of Palamedes , Hyg. Fab. 169 ; Prop. 3, 22, 27 . — A fountain near Argos , Ov. M. 2, 240 .—Hence, , , pertaining to Amymone , Hyg. Fab. 169 .

Ămyntas.opening: , = Ἀμύντας . The father of the Macedonian king Philip , Nep. Reg. 2 ; Just. 7, 4 .—Hence, , , patr. , a descendant of Amyntas , i. e. Philip , Ov. Ib. 297 .— Name of a shepherd , Verg. E. 3, 66 .

Ămyntor.opening: , = Ἀμύντωρ , king of the Dolopians , and father of Phœnix , Ov. M. 8, 307 ; id. H. 3, 27 .—Hence, , , , son of Amyntor , i. e. Phœnix , Ov. A. A. 1, 337 .

ămystis.opening: , = ἄμυστις , the emptying of a cup at one draught , Hor. C. 1, 36, 14 .

Ămȳthāōn.opening: (also ), , , = Ἀμυθάων , a Greek , the father of Melampus , Ov. M. 15, 325 .—Hence, , , of Amythaon , Verg. G. 3, 550 ; Prop. 2, 4, 10 .

ăn.opening: conj. [etym. very obscure; v. the various views adduced in Hand, I. p. 296, with which he seems dissatisfied; if it is connected with the Sanscr. anjas, = Germ. ander, = Engl. other, we may comp. the Engl. other and or…

ănăbaptismus.opening: , = ἀναβαπτισμός , a second baptism , Aug. ad Psa. 38 .

ănăbăsĭs.opening: , = ἀνάβασις , a plant , horse-tail : equisetum, Linn.; Plin. 26, 7, 20, § 36 ; 26, 13, 83, § 133 .

ănăbathrum.opening: , i. , = ἀνάβαθρον , an elevated place for beholding public games : quae conducto pendent anabathra tigillo, tiers of benches that rest on hired beams , * Juv. 7, 46 .

ănăbŏlium.opening: ἀναβάλλω , a surgical instrument , Inscr. Orell. 1572 .

ănăcampsĕrōs.opening: , = ἀνακαμψέρως (love-restoring), an herb , the touch of which was said to have the power of bringing back lost love , Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 167 .

Ănăces.opening: , = Ἄνακες (v. ἄναξ , L. and S.), an epithet of the Dioscuri ( Castor and Pollux ), Cic. N. D. 3, 21 .

Ănăcharsis.opening: , = Ἀνάχαρσις , a distinguished Scythian philosopher in the time of Solon , Cic. Tusc. 5, 32, 90 ; Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 209 al.

ănăchōrēsis.opening: , = ἀναχώρησις , retirement , the life of an eremite , Sid. Ep. 7, 9 .

ănăchōrēta.opening: , = ἀναχωρητής , a hermit , an eremite , recluse , anchorite , Sulp. Sev. Dial. 1, 18 ; Sid. Carm. 16, 97 .

ănăclintērĭum.opening: , = ἀνακλιντήριον , a cushion for leaning upon , Spart. Ael. Ver. 5 .

Ănā^crĕōn.opening: , = Ἀνακρέων , a distinguished lyric poet of Teos , who fl. 540 B.C., Cic. Tusc. 4, 33, 71 ; Hor. C. 4, 9, 9 ; id. Epod. 14, 10 al. —Hence, , , adj. , Diom. p. 512 P.; , , adj. , Quint. 9, 4, 78 ; Gell. 19, 9 ; and , ,…

ănactŏrĭum.opening: , = ἀνακτόριον , a plant , sword-grass , App. Herb. 78 .

ănădēmă.opening: , = ἀνάδημα , a band , a fillet , an ornament for the head : Et bene parta patrum flunt anademata, mitrae, the well-earned property of fathers is converted into head-bands , etc., * Lucr. 4, 1129 ; Dig. 34, 2, 27 .

ănădiplōsis.opening: , = ἀναδίπλωσις , the reduplication or repetition of the same word (in pure Lat., conduplicatio); as, Sequitur pulcherrimus Astur, Astur equo fidens, Verg. A. 10, 181 ; cf. Aquila, Rom. 32; Jul. Rufin. 7 ; Mart. Cap. 5,…

Ănădўŏmĕnē.opening: , = ἀναδυομένη (she that emerges), an epithet of Venus emerging from the sea , a celebrated picture of the painter Apelles , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 12 .

ănăgallis.opening: , = άναγαλλίς , a plant , pimpernel or chickweed , Plin. 25, 13, 92, § 144 .

ănăglyptĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀναγλυπτικός , carved or engraved in bas-relief : metallum, Sid. Ep. 9, 13 .

ănăglyptus.opening: or , , adj. , = ἀνάγλυπτος or -φος ; in sculpture, wrought or carved in bas-relief , Inscr. Orell. 3838 .— Hence, subst. : , , , work in bas-relief , Plin. 33, 11, 49, § 139 , where the old form was anaglypha.

Ănagnĭa.opening: , = Ἀναγνία , a town in Latium , the chief seat of the Hernici , now Anagni , Cic. Att. 16, 8, 1 ; Liv. 45, 16 ; Plin. 34, 6, 11, § 23 ; cf. Mann. Ital. 1, 665.—Hence, , , belonging to Anagnia , Cic. Dom. 30 .— Subst. :…

ănăgnostēs.opening: , = ἀναγνώστης , a reader , com. among the ancients an educated slave (cf. acroama): noster, Cic. Att. 1, 12 , where Orell. would write it as Greek; Vatin. ap. Cic. Fam. 5, 9, 2 ; Nep. Att. 13, 14 ; Gell. 3, 19 ; 18, 5 .

ănăgȳros.opening: , = ἀνάγυρος , a strengscented , pod-bearing shrub , bean-trefoil : Anagyris foetida, Linn.; Plin. 27, 4, 13, § 30

Ănăītis.opening: an Armenian goddess , said to be the name of Diana read backwards (Anaid), Plin. 33, 4, 24, § 84 .

ănălecta.opening: , = ἀναλέκτης , he that collected the crumbs , etc., left after a meal , Mart. 7, 20 ; 14, 82 .— Trop. : grammaticos habere analectas, that picked up words (said of parasites), Sen. Ep. 27 .

ănălectris.opening: ἀνά-λέκτρον , perh. a cushion for the shoulders , used to improve the figure , a shoulder-pad , Ov. A. A. 3, 273 , where Merkel reads analeptrides; v. analeptris.

ănălemmă.opening: , = ἀνάλημμα , a sundial which showed the latitude and meridian of a place , Vitr. 9, 4 .

ănăleptris.opening: , = ἀναληπτρίς ( ἀναλαμβάνω , to hold up), a suspensory bandage , Ov. A. A. 3, 273 Merkel; v. analectris.

ănălŏgĭa.opening: , = ἀναλογία , the resemblance or agreement of several things; in gram., the analogy of language , analogy , Varr. L. L. 9, 4 al. (in Cic. Att. 6, 2 , written as Greek).

ănălŏgĭcus.opening: adj. analogia , = ἀναλογικός , pertaining to analogy : in libris analogicis, Gell. 4, 16 .

ănălŏgus.opening: adj. , = ἀνάλογος , analogous , proportionate , Varr. L. L. 10, § 37 (by Müll. written as Greek).

ănancaeum.opening: , = ἀναγκαῖον (that must be done), a large drinking-cup , which must be drained on a wager , a brimmer or bowl , Plaut. Rud. 2, 3, 33 ; Varr. ap. Non. p. 547, 33 dub.

ănancītes.opening: ἀν- ἄγχω, to free from distress , a name of the diamond as a remedy for sadness and trouble of mind : adamas et venena vincit et lymphationes abigit metusque vanos expellit a mente. Ob id quidam eum ananciten vocavere,…

ănancītis.opening: a precious stone used in hydromancy : Anancitide in hydromantiā dicunt evocari imagines deorum, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 192 .

ănăpaestĭcus.opening: adj. anapaestus , consisting of anapœsts , Sid. Ep. 4, 3 ; Serv. ad Verg. E. 8, 78 .

ănăpaestus.opening: adj. , = ἀνάπαιστος (struck back). Pes, the metrical foot , anapœst : ˘˘¯ (i. e. a reversed dactyl), Cic. Tusc. 2, 16, 37 ; id. de Or. 3, 47 ; also absol. without pes, id. Or. 56 .— , , (sc. carmen), a poem in anapœsts…

Ănăpauŏmĕnē.opening: , = ἀναπαυομένη (she that rests), a painting of the Theban Aristides , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 99 ; cf. Anapauomenos.

Ănăpauŏmĕnos.opening: , = ἀναπαυόμενος (he that rests), a painting of Protogenes , which represents a satyr as leaning idly against a tree , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 106 .

Ănăphē.opening: , = Ἀνάφη , an island that rose of itself (i. e. volcanic) in the Cretan Sea , now Namfi or Namfio , Ov. M. 7, 461 ; Plin. 2, 87, 89, § 202 ; Amm. 17, 7 .

ănăphŏră.opening: , = ἀναφορά . A rising or mounting up , the rising of the stars , Plin. 7, 49, 50, § 160 ; Firm. Math. 3, 3. — In rhet. The bringing up or repetition of a word at the beginning of successive clauses , e. g. Cic. Verr.…

ănăphŏrĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀναφορικός . In astronomy, adjusted according to the rising of the stars : horologium, Vitr. 9, 9 .— In medicine, bringing up blood , spitting blood , Firm. Math. 3, 13.

Ănāpis.opening: , or , , Brother of Amphinomus , q. v.— A river in Sicily , which empties into the bay of Syracuse , now Anapo or Fiume di Sortino , Ov. M. 5, 417 ; id. F. 4, 469 .

ănăplērōtĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἀναπληρωτικός , suitable for filling up , Veg. Vet. 2, 26 .

ănăs.opening: ( gen. plur. anatum, Cic. N. D. 2, 48, 124 ; Plin. 25, 2, 3, § 6 ; rarely anatium, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 14 ; 3, 11, 1 ) [kindr. with old Germ. Anut; Lith. antis; mod. Germ. Ente; perh. also with Sanscr. ātis, a waterfowl],…

ănās.opening: 3. anus , disease of old women : anatem morbum anuum dicebant, id est, vetularum sicut senium morbum senum, Paul. ex Fest, p. 29 Müll.; cf. Placid. p. 435 Mai.

Ănas.opening: a river in Spain , now Guadiana (Arab., i. e. Wadi-Ana, = river Anas), Caes. B. C. 1, 38 ; Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 3 ; 4, 22, 35, § 116 ; Mel. 2, 6 ; 3, 1 ; cf. Mann. Hispan. 325.

ănătārĭus.opening: adj. anas , relating to a duck : aquila, the duck-eagle , which stations itself by the water and carries off ducks: Falco haliaëtus, Linn.; Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 7 .

ănăthēmă.opening: , = ἀνάθημα , an offering , a gift , Prud. Psych. 540 : in anathema oblivionis, Vulg. Judith, 16, 23 .

ănăthĕmă.opening: , = ἀνάθεμα , a later form of ἀνάθημα , used in mal. part. (eccl. Lat.), pr. an offering not to be redeemed; and of a living thing, to be put to death, doomed; hence, an accursed thing , a curse. Concr., of things:…

ănăthĕmătīzo.opening: v. a. , = ἀναθεματίζω . Lit. , to anathematize , to put under the ban : aliquem or aliquam rem, Aug. Ep. 75 .— In gen., to curse , Vulg. 1 Macc. 5, 5 ; ib. Marc. 14, 71 .— To detest : aliquid, Hier. Ep. 75 .—Form , Aug.…

ănăthȳmĭāsis.opening: , = ἀναθυμίασις , a rising vapor , Petr. 47 ; Theod. Prisc. 2, 2, 1 .

ănătĭcŭla.opening: dim. anas . A little duck , a duckling , * Cic. Fin. 5, 15, 42 .— In Plaut., a term of endearment, duckie , * As. 3, 3, 103.

ănătīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to the duck : Utinam fortunam nunc [ego] anatinam uterer, Uti quom exivissem ex aquā, arerem tamen, * Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 49 .—Hence, , , (sc. caro), duck-flesh , duck , Petr. 56, 3 .

ănătŏcismus.opening: , = ἀνατοκισμός , interest upon interest , compound interest (twice in Cic.): centesimae cum anatocismo anniversario, Cic. Att. 5, 21, 11 ; 5, 21, 12 ; Inscr. Orell. 4405 .

ănĭcŭlāris.opening: adj. anicula , worthy of an old woman , after the manner of an old woman : verba, Aug. in Psa. 38 .

Ănĭensis.opening: adj. Anio , of or pertaining to the Anio : tribus, in the Tiburtine region, through which the Anio flows, Liv. 10, 9 fin. ; Cic. Planc. 22 .

Ănĭēnus.opening: adj. Anio , of or pertaining to the Anio : fluenta, Verg. G. 4, 369 : unda, Prop. 1, 20, 8 : lympha, id. 4, 15, 4 .

ănīlis.opening: adj. anus , of or pertaining to an old woman. Lit. : voltus, Verg. A. 7, 416 : passus, Ov. M. 13, 533 : aetas, Col. 2, 1, 2 .— Often in a contemptuous sense, like an old woman , old womanish , anile : ineptiae paene…

ănōmălŏs.opening: ( ), (um), adj. , = ἀνώμαλος , in gram., deviating from the general rule , irregular , anomalous , Diom. p. 314 P.; Prisc. p. 833 P.; Mart. Cap. 3, p. 71 al.

Ăphaea.opening: , = Ἀφαία , an epithet of Britomartis (q. v.), Verg. Cir. 303 , ubi v. Wagner.

ăphaerĕma.opening: , = ἀφαίρεμα , a coarse kind of grits , Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 2 .

ăphaerĕsis.opening: , = ἀφαίρεσις , a gram. fig., the dropping of a letter or syllable at the beginning of a word (e. g. ruere for eruere, temnere for contemnere, etc.), Prob. p. 1438 P.; Don. p. 1772 ib.; Charis. p. 248 ib.; Serv. ad…

Ăpĭa.opening: , = Ἀπία , an old name of the Peloponnesus , Plin. 4, 4, 5, § 9 (v. aqua init. ).

ăpĭăcus.opening: adj. apium , of or relating to parsley , similar to parsley : brassica, Cato ap. Plin. 19, 8, 41, § 136 Jan; cf. Cato, R. R. 157, 2 (others read in the first passage apianam , in the latter apia ).

ăpĭcātus.opening: Part. , as if from apico [apex], adorned with the priest's cap : Dialis, Ov. F. 3, 397 .

ăpīcĭus.opening: adj. apis , sought by bees , liked by bees; hence, sweet , dainty , = apianus, q. v.: uvae, Cato, R. R. 24, 1 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 58 ; Plin. 14, 4, 5, § 46 ; Macr. S. 2, 16 .—Hence, , , , sc. vinum, Cato, R. R. 6, 5 ; 7, 1…

ē-dŏlo.opening: v. a. , to cut or hew out , to prepare by hewing. * Lit. : lingulas, Col. 8, 11, 4 .— Trop. , to work out , prepare , finish (rare): libellum, Varr. ap. Non. 448, 17 : quod jusseras edolavi, Enn. ap. Cic. Att. 13, 47, 1…

Ē-dŏmĭno.opening: v. a. , to control absolutely; pass. , Arn. 5 , no. 11 init.

ē-dŏmo.opening: v. a. , to tame completely , conquer , overcome , vanquish , subdue (rare; mostly poet. and in postAug. prose). Prop.: (Roma) edomito sustulit orbe caput, Ov. F. 4, 256 ; cf. id. A. A. 3, 114 .— Transf. : pastinaca…

ēdŭcātĭo.opening: 2. edŭco , a breeding , rearing , training , bringing up , education (good prose). Of men, Cic. de Or. 3, 31, 124 ; id. Leg. 3, 13 ; Quint. 1, 1, 21 ; 1, 2, 6 ; Tac. A. 3, 52 ; id. G. 20 et saep.— Transf. Of animals,…

ēdŭcātor.opening: id. , a rearer , bringer - up (rare, but good prose). Prop., of a foster-father , Cic. Planc. 33, 81 ; Quint. 7, 1, 14 ; cf. Cic. N. D. 2, 34 .— Transf. , of tutors , pedagogues , Tac. A. 11, 1 ; 12, 41 ; 14, 3 ; Dig.…

ēdŭcātrix.opening: educator . She who brings up , a nurse , Col. 8, 11, 14 ; Inscr. Don. 14 , no. 39.— Transf. : earum (rerum) parens est educatrixque sapientia, Cic. Leg. 1, 24, 62 .

ēdŭcātus.opening: 2. edŭco , bringing up , Tert. Res Carn. 60 .

ē-dūco.opening: ( imper. , educe, Plaut. Pers. 4, 1, 11 ; id. Stich. 5, 6, 1 : educ, Cic. Cat. 1, 5, 10 ; Alcim. 5, 248 al. — Inf. pass. parag. , educier, Plaut. Truc. 5, 16 ), v. a. , to lead forth , draw out , bring away (very freq.…

ēductor.opening: 1. educo, II. A. 4. b. , a bringer-up , tutor (for the usual educator), Fronto Ep. ad Amic. 15 .

ē-dulco.opening: v. a. , to sweeten : vitam, Matius ap. Gell. 15, 25, 2 , and ap. Non. 106, 25 .

ē-dūresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow hard , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 34, 182 .

ē-dūrus.opening: adj. , exceedingly hard , very hard (very rare): pirus, Verg. G. 4, 145 . — Trop. , harsh , cruel : eduro ore negare, Ov. A. A. 3, 476 .

Ēĕtĭon.opening: , = Ἠετίων , the father of Andromache , and king of Thebe , in Cilicia , Ov. Tr. 5, 5, 44 ; id. F. 4, 280 .—Hence, , , pertaining to Eëtion : Thebae, Ov. M. 12, 110 .

ē-gĕlĭdo.opening: v. a. gelidus , to thaw away , Sid. Ep. 4, 1 .

ē-gĕlĭdus.opening: adj. ( Ex priv. as in effrenare.) Not cold; lukewarm , tepid ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): potio et frigidae propior, Cels. 4, 18 fin. ; cf. aqua (opp. frigida), id. 6, 18 ; cf. Suet. Aug. 82 : tepores, Cat. 46, 1 ;…

ē-gĕlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to take off the chill , make lukewarm : leviter egelatum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 5, 58 ; id. Tard. 4, 3 .

ēgĕrĭes.opening: egero , excrement , dung (late Lat.), Sol. 40, 11 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 32, 281 .

ē-germĭno.opening: v. n. , to put forth , shoot , sprout , Col. 4, 17, 4 ; 27, 4 ; 32, 5 .

ē-gĕro.opening: v. a. , to carry , bear or bring out , to lead or draw out , to discharge (not ante-Aug.). Lit. : praedam ex hostium tectis, Liv. 6, 3 Drak.; cf. id. 9, 31 ; 25, 25 : pecuniam ex aerario, id. 30, 39 fin. : fluctus (e…

ēgestĭo.opening: egero , a carrying out or off , an emptying , voiding (post-Aug. and rare): cadaverum et ruderum, Suet. Ner. 38 : ventris et urinae, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 10 ; for which simply egestio, Suet. Claud. 44 fin. ; Veg. Vet. 5,…

ēgestīvus.opening: adj. id. .—In medic. lang., purgative : vis, Macer de Anetho, 14.

ē-gigno.opening: to procreate , produce , bring forth : et altos interdum ramos egigni corpore vivo, Lucr. 2, 703 Lachm. N. cr.

ē-grānātus.opening: adj. granum , shelled , emptied : carinae, Plin. Val. 3, 14 .

ē-grĕdĭor.opening: ( inf. egredier, Plaut. Poen. 3, 4, 32 ), v. dep. n. and a. Neutr. , to go or come out , come forth (class.). Lit. In gen., with e or ex : foras e fano, Plaut. Rud. 2, 3, 4 ; cf.: e fano huc, id. ib. 3, 2, 49 : e…

ēgressĭo.opening: egredior , a going out or forth (post-Aug.). Lit. : nocturna (ex castello), App. M. 8, p. 208, 7 ; Hier. Ep. 78, 1 : eorum ex Aegypto, Vulg. Num. 1, 1 ; and so in gen. of the Exodus : filiorum Israel, id. ib. 33, 38 ; 1…

ē-lāmentābĭlis.opening: adj. , very lamentable : gemitus, Cic. Tusc. 2, 24, 57 Mos. N. cr.

ēlectārĭum.opening: (also ), , ecligma , a medicament that melts in the mouth , an electuary , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13 ; 169, 176 al. ; cf. Isid. Orig. 4, 9, 10 .

ēlectĭlĭs.opening: adj. eligo , choice , dainty (with probus): piscatus, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 41 : partes, App. M. 10, p. 245, 35 .

ēlectĭo.opening: id. , a choice , selection , * Cic. Or. 20, 68 ; Quint. 1, 12, 4 ; Prooem. § 2; 3, 4, 8; Vell. 2, 72 fin. ; Tac. A. 6, 22 ; id. Or. 23 al. : vitiatarum electiones, i. e. the option given to a violated maiden, whether…

ēlectrus.opening: adj. electrum , of amber : nummi, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 25, 9 .

ē-ructo.opening: v. a. To belch or vomit forth , to throw up (rare but class.). Prop.: unde tu nos turpissime eructando ejecisti, Cic. Pis. 6, 13 : saniem eructans, Verg. A. 3, 632 ; cf. Col. 8, 8, 10 .— Trop. : caedem sermonibus suis,…

ē-rūdĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to clear from rubbish (very rare). Lit. : solum, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 7 .— Trop. : volumen de supervacuis sententiis, Sid. Ep. 5, 15 ; 5, 7 ; Ambros. Ep. 22, 2 .

ē-rŭdĭo.grammar: īvi or ii, ītum, 4 v. a.
ē-rŭdĭo.opening: v. a. , qs. to free from roughness, i. e. to polish , educate , instruct , teach (freq. and class.; cf.: doceo, edoceo, praecipio, instituo). Prop.: studiosos discendi erudiunt atque docent, Cic. Off. 1, 44, 156 :…

ērŭdītĭo.opening: erudio , an instructing , instruction (cf.: doctrina, disciplina, scientia, intellegentia, cognitio). Prop.: de ejus eruditione quod labores, nihil est, quoniam ingenium ejus nosti, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 4 fin. ; cf. Quint.…

ērŭdītor.opening: id. , an instructor , teacher (post-class.), Tert. Pall. 4 ; Hier. Vit. Hil.; Vulg. Rom. 2, 20 al.

ērŭdītŭlus.opening: dim. 1. eruditus , somewhat skilled or experienced (in love), said jocosely, Cat. 57, 7 .

ērŭdītus.opening: erudio , instruction; in abl. sing. , Tert, adv. Val. 29.

ērūgātĭo.opening: 1. erugo , a clearing from wrinkles : cutis, Plin. 28, 12, 50, § 184 .

ē-rūgo.grammar: ĕre, semel factum significat, quod eructare saepius a, um P. a.
ē-rūgo.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 83, 1 Müll.—Hence, * , , P. a. , belched out; transf., impure , bad : vinum (with fetidum), Gell. 11, 7, 3 .

ē-rumpo.grammar: rūpi, ruptum, 3 v. a. and n.
ē-rumpo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to cause to break or burst forth; to burst , sunder (rare; mostly ante-class.). Lit. : (brassica) tumida concoquit, eadem erumpit, Cato, R. R. 157, 3 : ignes, Lucr. 1, 725 ; cf. id. 6, 583 ; Cic.…

ē-runco.opening: v. a. , to weed out : herbas, Col. 2, 10, 28 : areas, id. 11, 3, 14 .

ē-rŭo.opening: v. a. , to cast forth , throw out; to dig , tear , or pluck out (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: qui sciet, ubi quidque positum sit, quaque eo veniat, is, etiam si quid obrutum erit, poterit eruere, Cic. Fin. 4, 4 fin.…

ēruptĭo.opening: erumpo, II. , a breaking out , bursting forth. Lit. In gen.: (elephanti) universi eruptionem tentavere, Plin. 8, 7, 7, § 21 ; 16, 10, 19, § 45 ; 18, 17, 44, § 150 al. —In plur. , Plin. 24, 15, 86, § 136 .— In partic. In…

ēruptor.opening: erumpo , one who makes a sally , Amm. 24, 5, 9 .

ērŭtor.opening: eruo , a rescuer : erutor meus es tu, Domine, Vers. Lat. Psa. 69, 6, ap. August. in Psa. 69 (cf.: implicatus sum, erue, August. ib.).

ērynge.opening: , and , , , = ἠρύγγη and ἠρύγγιον , a sort of thistle; acc. to some, the eringo , Eryngium campestre, Linn.; acc. to others, the spotted yellow thistle , Scolymus maculatus, Linn.; Plin. 22, 7, 8, § 18 sq. ; Col. 6, 5,…

Ē^sāĭās.opening: Heb. , the Jewish prophet Isaian , Lact. 4, 11, 10 ; Prud. στεφ . 5, 524.—Hence, , , adj. , of Isaiah , Sulp. Sev. Ep. 2, 10 .

ē-scendo.grammar: di, sum, 3 v. n. and a.
ē-scendo.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. [scando]. Neutr. , to climb up , mount up , ascend from a place (cf. ascendo init. ; also: scando, peto, incedo, ingredior; rare but class.). In gen. Lit. : ex alto puteo ad summum, Plaut. Mil. 4, 4,…

ēscensĭo.opening: escendo , an ascension , a mounting , climbing , going up : adversus regem escensionem a Paesto facientem pugnare, Liv. 8, 17, 9 : in agrum Uticensem, id. 27, 5, 8 : ad urbem, id. 27, 29, 7 ; 28, 8, 8 ; 37, 17, 3 .—…

ēscensus.opening: id. , a mounting , ascending , only in abl. sing. , Tac. A. 13, 39 Nipperd. (al. ascensu).

ēsĭto.opening: v. freq. a. 1. edo , to be wont to eat , to eat (ante- and post-class.): brassicam, Cato R. R. 157, 10 (cited in Plin. 20, 9, 33, § 83 ; Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 85 ; id. Ps. 3, 2, 41 ; Gell. 4, 11, 1 and 9.

ēsor.opening: id. , an eater : prandiorum optimorum, Front. de Fer. Alsiens. 3 .

ēsŭrĭālis.opening: adj. esuries , of or belonging to hunger , comic.: venter gutturque resident esuriales ferias, are keeping hunger-holidays , i. e. have nothing to eal , Plaut. Capt. 3, 1, 8 ; quoted, Front. de Fer. Aliens. 3 .

ēsŭrĭenter.opening: adv. , hungrily , v. I. esurio fin.

ēsŭrĭes.opening: 1. esurio , hunger (postclass.). Lit. , Hier. Ep. 125, 33 ; Alcim. 2, 18 ; Vulg. Deut. 28, 20 .— Trop. : avida ignorantiae, Sid. Ep. 6, 6 .

ēsŭrĭo.opening: ( ), , 1. esurio , a hungry person , Petr. 44, 2 .—In a punning jest, with saturio, Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 23 .

ēsŭrītĭo.opening: id. , a hungering , hunger (rare; not in Cic.), Cat. 23, 14 ; Gell. 16, 3, 3 sq. ; Mart. 1, 100 .—In plur , Cat. 21, 1 .

ēsus.opening: 1. edo , an eating (anteclass. and post-Aug.): esui condi, Varr. R. R. 1, 60 ; cf.: esui dare alicui, Plin. 20, 17, 69, § 178 : agni, Vulg. Exod. 12, 4 : esui esse, Gell. 4, 1, 20 : esum et potum eximere, Tert. Anim. 43…

Ēsus.opening: ( ), , , a Gallic deity , to whom human blood was offered , Inscr. Orell. 1993 ; Luc. 1, 445 ; Lact. 1, 21, 3 .

ēta.opening: , indecl., the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet , Ter. Maur. Litt. 43 ; Aus. Idyll. 12, 12, 3 .

ēthĭcē.opening: , = ἠθική , moral philosophy , ethics , Quint. 2, 21, 3 ; 12, 2, 15 ; also , , , Lact. 3, 13 .

ēthĭcus.opening: , (scanned ĕthĭcīs, Prud. Hamart. 583 ), adj. , = ἠθικός , moral , ethic (post-class.): res, ethics, Gell. 1, 2, 4 : dictio, which shows the character, Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .— Hence adv. : = ἠθικῶς , morally : dicere, Sen.…

ēthŏlŏgĭa.opening: , = ἠθολογία , the art of depicting or imitating character , Quint. 1, 9, 3 ; Sen. Ep. 95, 66 ; Suet. Gramm. 4 .

ēthŏlŏgus.opening: , = ἠθολόγος , one who jestingly imitates the manners , actions , gestures , etc., of others , a mimic : mimus, Cic. de Or. 2, 59, 242 ; 2, 60, 244 .

ēthŏpoeĭa.opening: , = ἠθοποιΐα , rhet. t. t., an expression of character , Rutil. Lup. de Fig. 1, 21, p. 66 al. ; cf. the foll. art., II.

ēthos.opening: , = ἦθος . * Manners , morals , Sid. Carm. 15, 101 .—* A depicting of character. —In acc. plur. : ethē, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 98 ; in abl. plur. : in ethesin Terentius poscit palmam, Varr. ap. Non. 374, 9 .

Ē^trūrĭa.opening: ( ), , , a country of central Italy , Mel. 2, 4, 2 ; Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 50 ; Cic. Div. 1, 41, 92 ; id. Cat. 2, 3 fin. ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 32 Müll.; Liv. 1, 35, 9 ; Verg. A. 8, 494 ; 12, 232 et saep.—Deriv., , , adj. , of…

Ēva.opening: ( , Vulg. Gen. 4, 1 ; id. 2 Cor. 11, 3 al.), , , Eve , the first woman , Tert. Virg. vel. 5; Prud. Hamort. 741 .

ēvăcŭātĭo.opening: evacuo , an evacuating; trop., a weakening : fidei, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 24 .

ē-văcŭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to empty out , evacuate (post-Aug.). Lit. : alvum, Plin. 20, 6, 23, § 52 ; 32, 9, 33, § 104 . — Trop. To rid one's self of , lay aside : quae pueruli erant, Vulg. 1 Cor. 13, 11 .— To make void ,…

ē-vādo.opening: ( perf. sync. evasti, Hor. S. 2, 7, 68 ; Sil. 15, 796 ; perf. evadi. Treb. Poll. Trig. Tyr. 5, 6), v. n. and a. Neutr. , to go or come out , go forth (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: si (apes) ex alvo minus frequentes…

ēvăgātĭo.opening: evagor , a wandering , straying : stellarum, Plin. 2, 17, 14, § 72 ; Sen. Ep. 65, 17 .

ē-vāgīnātĭo.opening: evagino , a spreading out , extending , Arn. 1, 50 Orell.

ē-vāgīno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. vagina , to draw out of the scabbard , to unsheath (post-class.): gladio sua sponte evaginato, Just. 1, 9, 8 ; Hyg. Fab. 164 ; Vulg. Exod. 15, 10 : pugionem, id. Judith, 13, 9.

ē-văgo.opening: v. n. collat. form of depon. evagor, q. v. : Famae nam nobilitas late ex stirpe praeclara evagat, Att. ap. Non. 467, 28 (R ib. Fragm. Trag. p. 219 ).

ē-văgor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. Neutr. , to wander forth , to roam about; to scatter or spread about , to extend (class.). Lit. : ne longius evagatae (incubantes gallinae) refrigerent ova, Col. 8, 5, 14 : cappari evagatur per agros,…

ē-vălesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become strong , increase in strength , to increase , grow (cf.: vix illa, quae παραγόμενα vocant, nobis permittimus, sed hoc feliciter, evaluit, Quint. 8, 6, 32 ; not ante-Aug.). Lit. : cum evaluissent…

ē-vallo.opening: v. a. 2. vallus , to winnow out , to cleanse from the husks , to husk , to hull , Plin. 18, 10, 23 , §§ 97 and 99.

ē-vānesco.opening: ( part. fut. evaniturus, Lact. 5, 4 fin. ), v. inch. n. , to vanish or pass away , to die away , to disappear (class.). Lit. In gen.: Bacchi cum flos evanuit (with diffugere in auras), Lucr. 3, 222 : evanescere paulatim…

ēvangĕlĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = εὐαγγελικός , evangelical : scriptura, Tert. adv. Marc. 39 : vox, Prud. Apoth. 495 et saep.

ēvangĕlista.opening: ( ), , , = εὐαγγελιστής , an evangelist , Prud. Cathem. 6, 77 et saep.; Vulg. Act. 21, 8 .

ēvangĕlĭum.opening: ( ), , , = εὐαγγέλιον . Good news , Cic. Att. 2, 3, 1 , written as Greek, εὐαγγέλια .— The Gospel (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Matt. 4, 23 et saep.

ēvangĕlīzātor.opening: ( ), , evangelium , a preacher of the Gospel , Tert. Cor. Mil. 9 ; id. Praescr. 4 .

ēvangĕlīzo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ēvangĕlīzo.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n. , = εὐαγγελίζω (eccl. Lat.). Act. , to preach , declare , proclaim , always with the accessory notion of bringing good tidings , proclaiming the Gospel : vobis gaudium magnum, Vulg. Luc. 2, 10 :…

ēvānĭdus.opening: adj. evanesco , vanishing , passing away (not ante-Aug., and very rare). Lit. : pectora, Ov. M. 5, 435 : oleae, i. e. frail, without strength, Col. Arb. 17, 3 ; cf. arbores, Vitr. 2, 10 : materia vetustate, id. 2, 8 :…

ē-vanno.opening: v. a. vannus , to cast out the chaff of grain from the fan , to winnow. * Lit. : acus, Varr. R. R. 1, 52 fin. —* Transf. , to cast out : aliquem, Pompon. ap. Non. 19, 23 (R ib. Com. Fragm. p. 239 ).

ēvăpōrātĭo.opening: evaporo , an evaporating , evaporation : terrae, Sen. Q. N. 1, 1, 6 ; 6, 13, 1 : nivis, Gell. 19, 5, 6 .

ēvăpōrātīvus.opening: adj. id. , evaporating , apt to evaporate : virtus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8, 83 .

ē-văpōro.opening: v. a. , to disperse in vapor , to evaporate (post-class.), Gell. 19, 5, 7 and 8; Tert. Pall. 6 fin.

ēvāsĭo.opening: evado , a going out , Vulg. Judith, 12, 20 .

ē-vasto.opening: v. a. , to lay utterly waste , to devastate (a favorite word of Livy; elsewh. very rare): omnia, Liv. 10, 15 ; 5, 5 ; 8, 37 ; 28, 44; 32, 33, 14 Drak. et saep.; Vop. Aurel. 15 ; Sil. 15, 185 .

ēvectĭo.opening: eveho . * A going upwards , flying up , flight : sublimis, App. M. 5, p. 169 .— In jurid. lang., a permit to travel by the public post , a post-warrant , Cod. Just. 12, 51, 3 sq. ; Symm. Ep. 4, 6 ; Aug. Ep. 55 .

ēvectus.opening: eveho , a carrying out , exporting of goods from a place, Varr. R. R. 1, 16, 2 Schneid. N. cr.; Plin. 18, 5, 6, § 28 .

ē-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to carry out or forth , to convey out , lead forth (rare but class.). Lit. : omnia (signa) ex fanis, ex locis publicis palam plaustris evecta exportataque esse, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 20 : aquas ex planis locis, Liv.…

ēvēlātum.grammar: eventilatum, unde velabra, quibus frumenta ventilantur

ē-vello.opening: ( Cic. Sest. 28 ; id. de Or. 1, 53 fin. ), post-class., vulsi ( Flor. 4, 12, 38 ; Sen. ad Marc. Consol. 16, 7 al. ), , v. a. , to tear , pull , or pluck out (class.). Lit. : linguam se evellisse M. Catoni, Cic. Sest. 28…

ē-vĕnĭo.opening: ( praes. subj. evenat, Enn. ap. Non. 507, 20 ; Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 3 ; id. Mil. 4, 1, 19 : evenant, id. Ep. 3, 1, 2 ), v. n. , to come out , come forth. Lit. (very rare): merses profundo: pulchrior evenit, Hor. C. 4, 4,…

ē-ventĭlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to set in motion (the air), to fan (post-Aug.). Lit. : (aërem graviorem) emendant assiduo linteorum jactatu eventilando, Plin. 31, 3, 28, § 49 ; cf. Just. 44, 1 fin. : frumenta, to winnow , i. e.…

ēventus.opening: evenio, II. . An occurrence , accident , event; fortune , fate , lot (rare but class.): mihi a peritis in Asia praedictum est, fore eos eventus rerum qui acciderunt, Cic. Div. 1, 28 : in incerto reliqui temporis eventu,…

ē-verbĕro.opening: v. a. , to strike violently , to beat (rare and not ante-Aug.). Lit. : os oculosque hostis, Quint. 2, 4, 18 ; cf. pectus suis armis, Val. Fl. 6, 737 : clipeum alis, Verg. A. 12, 866 ; cf.: cineres alis, Ov. M. 14, 578 :…

ē-vergo.opening: v. a. , to send out , send forth : montes nullos apertos evergunt rivos, send forth, pour forth, Liv. 44, 33, 2 .

ēverrĭātor.grammar: vocatur, qui jure accepta hereditate justa facere defuncto debet, quae si non fecerit, seu quid in ea re turbaverit
ēverrĭātor.opening: , suo capite luat. Id nomen ductum a verrendo. Nam exverrae sunt purgatio quaedam domus, ex qua mortuus ad sepulturam ferendus est, quae fit per everriatorem certo genere scoparum adhibito, ab extra verrendo dictarum,…

ēverrĭcŭlum.opening: everro , a sweepnet , drag-net. Prop., for taking a large number of fishes, Varr. R. R. 3, 17, 7 ; App. Mag. p. 294 ; cf. Non. p. 34 ; and: everriculum, quod Graece σαγήνη dicitur, Dig. 47, 10, 13, § 7 .— Trop. :…

ē-verro.opening: v. a. , to sweep out (class.). Lit. : stercus ex aede Vestae, Varr. L. L. 6, § 32 Müll.; cf.: purgamenta salsamentorum officinis, Col. 8, 17, 12 : aedes, Titin. ap. Non. 192, 11 : solum stabuli, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 7 :…

ēversĭo.opening: everto, I. B. . Lit. An overthrowing. In gen.: columnae, Cic. Phil. 1, 2, 5 .—In plur. : eversiones vehiculorum, Plin. 22, 17, 20, § 43 .— Esp., a destructive overthrow , subversion , destruction : templorum, Quint. 5,…

ēversor.opening: everto , a subverter , destroyer. Prop.: Carthaginis et Numantiae, Quint. 8, 6, 30 ; cf.: regnorum Priami (Achilles), Verg. A. 12, 545 : regnorum cometes, i. e. presaging their destruction, Sil. 8, 639 .— Trop. :…

ēversus.opening: , um. Swept out , v. everro.— Overthrown , v. everto.

ē-verto.opening: or , , v. a. , to overturn , turn upside down (syn. demolior, destruo, extinguo, diruo, deleo, etc.). Lit. In gen. (very rare): aequora ventis, to upturn, agitate, Verg. A. 1, 43 ; cf. aquas, Ov. H. 7, 42 : mare, Sen.…

ē-vestīgātus.opening: Part. [vestigo], traced out , found out , discovered , investigated (very rare), Ov. M. 15, 146 ; Sen. Contr. 9 .

ēvexus.opening: adj. eveho , rounded off at the top , rounding upwards : mundus, Mart. Cap. 8, § 816 .

ē-vībro.opening: v. a. Lit. , to swing forwards , to hurl , throw : scorpiones rotundos lapides, Amm. 24, 4, 16 .— Trop. , to set in motion , to move , excite : animos, Gell. 1, 11, 1 : eum ad rabiem, Amm. 14, 1, 10 .

ēvictĭo.opening: evinco, II. A. 2. , jurid. t. t., a recovering of one's property by a judicial decision , a recovery , eviction , Dig. 21, tit. 2 ; Cod. Just. 8, 45 , De evictionibus.

ē-vĭdens.opening: adj. video , of things (like perspicuus), apparent , visible , evident , manifest , plain , clear (good prose; most freq. since the Aug. per.; syn. perspicuus, manifestus, apertus, dilucidus): flos (lappae) non evidens,…

ēvĭdentĭa.opening: evidens , clearness , distinctness. —In rhet. lang., clearness , perspicuity; used by Cicero along with perspicuitas, as a transl. of ἐνάργεια . Cic. Ac. 2, 6, 17 ; cf. Quint. 6, 2, 32 ; 4, 2, 63 ; 9, 2, 40 .— A proof :…

ē-vĭdĕor.opening: v. pass. [ex+video], to appear completely or plainly , with nom. and inf. , Arn. 2, 54 .

ē-vĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to lose liveliness or vigor , Tert. Anim. 38 .

ēvĭgĭlātĭo.opening: evigilo , a waking up , awakening , Aug. Solil. 1, 1 ; id. Civ. D. 17, 18, 1 .

ē-vĭgĭlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ē-vĭgĭlo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. To wake up , awak , Plin. Ep. 1, 5, 8 ; 9, 36, 1 ; Quint. 9, 4, 12 ; Suet. Aug. 78 ; Stat. S. 5, 3, 128 ; Vulg. Gen. 28, 16 .— To be wakeful , vigilant. — Trop. : in quo evigilaverunt curae et…

ē-vĭgōrātus.opening: Part. [vigoro], deprived of vigor or liveliness (post-class.), Tert. Pall. 4 ; id. Apol. 17 .

ē-vīlesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become vile , worthless , despicable (post - Aug. and very rare): nullis sordibus pretium carae pietatis evilescit, Val. Max. 5, 4, 7 : pericula, Tac. H. 3, 53 : propter quae usque eo eviluit, ut passim…

ē-vincĭo.opening: v. a. , to bind up , to bind or wind round with something (not ante-Aug., and mostly poet. ): simul diademate caput Tiridatis evinxit, Tac. A. 15, 2 ; cf. id. ib. 6, 43 .—More freq. in the part. perf. : viridi Mnestheus…

ē-vinco.opening: v. a. (not anteAug.). To overcome completely , to conquer , vanquish : evicit omnia assuetus praedae miles, Liv. 10, 17 fin. : imbelles, Aeduos, Tac. A. 3, 46 .— Transf. beyond the milit. sphere (freq.): lacrimis…

ēvĭŏlo.opening: v. a. , to violate , Prop. 1, 7, 16 (dub.; v. evolvo, B. 2.).

ēvĭrātĭo.opening: eviro , a depriving of manhood : pilorum, i. e. a removing, Plin. 29, 1, 8, § 26 .

ēvĭrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from eviro.

ē-vĭresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to fade , become pale , Varr. ap. Non. 101, 32 .

ē-vĭro.opening: v. a. vir , to deprive of virility , to emasculate , unman , (rare): omnes pueros, Varr. ap. Non. 46, 12 : corpus, Cat. 63, 57 ; Arn. 5, p. 187 .— Transf. , to weaken , make faint , deprive of strength : corpore evirato…

ē-viscĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. ( poet. and in post-class. prose). To deprive of the entrails , to disembowel. Lit. , Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 44, 107 (Trag. v. 413 ed. Vahl.); Pac. ap. Cic. Div. 2, 64 fin. — Hence, In gen., to tear…

ēvītābĭlis.opening: adj. 1. evito , avoidable. Prop.: telum, Ov. M. 6, 234 .— Trop. : mala (opp. inevitabilia), Sen. Q. N. 2, 50, 2 .

ēvītātĭo.opening: id. , an avoiding (post - Aug.): malorum, Quint. 5, 10, 33 : periculi, Sen. Q. N. 2, 39 : fastidii, Vop. Aur. 22 .

ē-vīto.opening: v. a. vita , to deprive of life , to kill (ante- and post-class.): vidi, Priamo vi vitam evitari, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 35, 85 (Trag. v. 129 ed. Vahl.): evitat vitam regi, Att. ap. Non. 449, 32 (R ib. Trag. Fragm. p.…

ēvŏcātĭo.opening: evoco , a calling out , calling forth (very rare). In gen.: inferorum, an evoking, Plin. 30, 1, 2, § 6 : deorum ex urbibus obsessis, Macr. S. 3, 9 . — In partic. A summoning of a debtor, Hirt. B. Alex. 56 fin. — A…

ēvŏcātīvus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to summoning : stipendia, Inscr. Orell. 3460 ; 4968 .

ēvŏcātor.opening: id. , one who calls to arms : servorum et civium perditorum, Cic. Cat. 1, 11, 27 .

ēvŏcātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , citing , summoning (late Lat.): epistola, Sid. Ep. 8, 12 .

ē-vŏco.opening: v. a. , to call out , call forth; to bring out , draw forth (class. —syn. invito, cito, etc.). Lit. In gen.: (Tullia) evocavit virum e curia, Liv. 1, 48 : gubernatorem a navi huc, Plaut. Am. 3, 3, 12 : aliquem huc…

ēvŏlātĭo.opening: evolo , an escaping , rising out of : mortis, Hier. in Psa. 54 .

ē-vŏlĭto.opening: v. freq. n. , to fly out frequently , Col. 8, 8, 1 .

ē-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly out or forth , to fly away , to fly up (class.). Lit. : ex quercu (aquila), Cic. Leg. 1, 1, 2 : extra septa, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 15 .— Absol. : evolandi potestas, Col. 8, 15, 1 : longius, Dig. 41, 1, 5, § 6…

ēvŏlūtĭo.opening: evolvo, I. B. 1. , an unrolling or opening of a book; hence, a reading : quid poëtarum evolutio voluptatis affert? Cic. Fin. 1, 7, 25 .

ē-volvo.opening: ( per diaeresin ēvŏlŭam, Cat. 66, 74 : ēvŏlŭisse, Ov. H. 12, 4 ), v. a. , to roll out , roll forth; to unroll , unfold (class.). Lit. : (vis venti) Arbusta evolvens radicibus haurit ab imis, Lucr. 6, 141 ; cf. silvas,…

ē-vŏmo.opening: v. a. , to spew out , vomit forth (class.). Lit. : (haec avis scribitur) conchas cum concoxerit, evomere, Cic. N. D. 2, 49 ; Suet. Claud. 44 ; id. Ner. 2 ; Tac. A. 12, 67 ; Vulg. Jonah, 2, 11 al. — Transf. : quod (urbs)…

ē-vulgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to bring out among the people , to publish , divulge (not ante-Aug., and very rare): civile jus repositum in penetralibus pontificum evulgavit, Liv. 9, 46 : arcanum, Tac. H. 1, 4 : injurias, id. A. 13, 19…

ēvulsĭo.opening: evello , a pulling out : dentis, Cic. N. D. 3, 22, 57 .— Eradication , utter destruction , Vulg. Jerem. 12, 17 .

ĕălē.opening: a large animal found in Ethiopia; acc. to Cuvier, the two-horned rhinoceros , Plin 8, 21, 30, § 73.

ĕā-propter.opening: (= propter ea), adv. , on that account , therefore , Ter. And. 5, 5, 3 Fleck. Pomp. Bon. Com. p. 238 Rib.

ĕapse.opening: , v. ipse init. † , , adj. , = ἐαρινός , of the color of spring, i. e. green : oves purpureas et earinas, Tert. Hab. mul. 8.

ĕā-tĕnus.opening: adv. is , designates the limit to which an action or condition extends, so far (rare; perh. not before Cic., for in Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 50 , the right reading is protenus); followed by quatenus , Cels. 2, 10 ; Dig. 47,…

ĕbĕnĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. hebenus, q. v. , of ebony , ebon (ante-class.), Mart. Capt. 1, § 80 .

ĕbŏrārĭus.opening: ( ), , ebur , a worker in ivory , Cod. Just. 10, 64, 1 ; Inscr. Orell, 4180; 4302.

ĕbŏrĕus.opening: adj. id. , made of ivory , ivory : Juppiter, Plin. 36, 5, 4, § 40 : mensae, Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 43 : oppida, Quint. 6, 3, 61 Spald.

ĕbŭlīnus.opening: adj. ebulum , of elder-wood , Plin. Val. 1, 64 .

ĕbŭlum.opening: , and , , , Dane-wort , dwarf-elder : Sambucus ebulus, Linn.; Cato R. R. 37, 2 ; Plin. 26, 11, 73, § 119 sq. ; Verg. E. 10, 27 ; Col. poët. 10, 10 al.

ĕbur.opening: (cf. Quint. 1, 6, 22 sq. ), Copt. ebu; cf. Sanscr. ibhas, elephant; whence Gr. ἐλέφας, Semit. article el being prefixed , ivory. Prop., Cic. Leg. 2, 18 ; id. Brut. 73 fin. ; id. Par. 1, 3 ; Quint. 2, 21, 9 ; Verg. G. 1,…

ĕbŭrātus.opening: adj. ebur , adorned or inlaid with ivory : lecti, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 53 : vehicula, id. Aul. 2, 1, 46 : sella, Lampr. Heliog. 4 fin.

ĕburnĕŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [eburneus], of ivory : fistula, Cic. de Or. 3, 60, 225 (for which, in Gell. 1, 11, 16 , eburnea).

ĕburnĕus.opening: (mostly poet. ) , , adj. ebur , of ivory. : signum, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 1 ; Ov. M. 4, 354 : lectus, Suet. Caes. 84 : praesepe, id. Calig. 55 : quadrigae, id. Ner. 22 : tabulae, id. ib. 31 al.; so, tulit eburneos dentes…

ĕchĕnēis.opening: , = ἐχενηΐς , the sucking-fish , remora , Echeneis remora, Linn.; Plin. 9, 25, 41, § 79 ; 35, 1, 1, § 2 sq.; Luc. 6, 675 ; Ov. Hal. 99 ; Isid. 12, 6, 34 .

ĕchidna.opening: , = ἔχιδνα , an adder , viper. The Furies were said to have them twined in their hair; hence: stipite te Stygio tumidisque adflavit Echidnis E tribus una soror, Ov. M. 10, 313 .— Nom. prop. Lernaea, the Lernaean hydra ,…

Ĕchīnădes.opening: , = Ἐχινάδες , a small group of islands in the Ionian Sea , at the mouth of the Acheloüs , Mel. 2, 7, 10 ; Plin. 2, 85, 87, § 201 ; 4, 12, 19, § 53 ; Ov. M. 8, 589 .

ĕchīnātus.opening: adj. echinus, a hedge-hog , set with prickles , prickly : calyx, Plin. 15, 23, 25, § 92 : capitula echinata spinis, id. 27, 9, 47, § 71 : folia, id. 22, 9, 11, § 24 .

ĕchīnŏmētrae.opening: , = ἐχινομῆτραι , a sort of sea-urchin , Plin. 9, 31, 51, § 100 .

ĕchīnŏphŏra.opening: , = ἐχινοφόρα , a sort of concha, Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 147 (Sillig, actinophoroe).

ĕchīnŏpūs.opening: , = ἐχινόπους , a kind of thorn , otherwise unknown , Plin. 11, 8, 8, § 18 .

ĕchīnus.opening: , = ἐχῖνος , a hedgehog , urchin. Prop., usually the (edible) sea-urchin , Echinus esculentus, Linn.; Varr. L. L. 5, § 77 Müll.; Afran. ap. Non. 216, 11 ; Plin. 9, 31, 51, § 100 sq. ; Hor. Epod. 5, 28 ; id. S. 2, 4, 33…

Ĕchīnus.opening: or , , , = Ἐχῖνος . A city of Phthiotis , in Thessaly , Mel. 2, 3, 6 ; Plin. 4, 7, 14, § 28 ; Liv. 32, 33 al. — A city of Acarnania , Plin. 4, 1, 2, § 5 .

ĕchĭon.opening: , = ἔχιον , a medicament prepared from the ashes of adders , Plin. 29, 6, 38, § 119 .

Ĕchīon.opening: One of the heroes who sprang up from the dragon's teeth sown by Cadmus; the husband of Agave and father of Pentheus , Ov. M. 3, 126 ; 10, 686 ; Stat. Th. 4, 569 ; Hyg. Fab. 178 .—Hence: Echione natus, for Pentheus , Ov.…

ĕchĭos.opening: , = ἔχιος , viper's bugloss , a plant which was taken as a remedy for the viper's bite , Plin. 25, 9, 58, § 104 .

ĕchis.opening: a plant , called also pseudoanchusa, and doris, Plin. 22, 20, 24, § 50 .

ĕdācĭtas.opening: edax , voracity , gluttony , Plaut. Pers. 1, 2, 7 ; Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 9, 9 ; id. Fam. 7, 26, 1 ; Ambros. Luc. 7, § 142 .

ĕdax.opening: adj. 1. edo; cf. Sanscr. adakas , voracious , gluttonous. Prop., Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 16 ; Ter. Eun. prol. 38 ; id. Heaut. prol. 38 ; Cic. Fl. 17, 41 ; id. Fam. 9, 20, 2 ( abl. edaci, as in Ov. M. 15, 354 ; Val. Fl. 6,…

Ĕdessa.opening: , = Ἔδεσσα . A city of Macedonia , the burial-place of the kings , Liv. 45, 29 ; Just. 7, 1, 7 .—Hence, , , adj. , of Edessa : Antiphilus (dux), Liv. 42, 51 .— A city of Mesopotamia , in the province of Osrhoëne, now…

ĕdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 1. edo , eatable , that may be taken as food : potio, Cassiod. Var. 12, 4 .

ĕdo.opening: 1. edo , a glutton , Varr. ap. Non. 48, 19 .

ĕdūlis.opening: adj. 1. edo , eatable (rare). Adj. : capreae, Hor. S. 2, 4, 43 .— Subst. , in the plur. , , , , eatables , food (for syn. cf.: alimenta, cibus, cibaria, esca, penus, victus, opsonium, pulmentum, etc.), Afran. ap. Non.…

Ĕdūsa.opening: 1. edo , the goddess that presides over children's food , Varr. ap. Non. 108, 22 ; August. Civ. D. 4, 34 ; called also , , , Don. Ter. Ph. 1, 1, 15 ; , , , August. Civ. D. 4, 11 ; and , , , Tert. ad Nat. 2, 11 .

ĕf-fulgĕo.opening: ( inf. effulgĕre, Verg. A. 8, 677 ; Claud. VI. Cons. Hon. 546 ), v. n. , to shine or gleam forth , to glitter (not anteAug.). Lit. : nova lux oculis effulsit, Verg. A. 9, 731 ; cf. Liv. 22, 1 ; 28, 15 ; 41, 21 : auro…

ĕgens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from egeo.

ĕgēnus.opening: adj. egeo , in want of , in need of , destitute or void of any thing (rare, and mostly poet. for egens). With gen. : (nos) omnium, Verg. A. 1, 599 ; Liv. 9, 6 : omnis spei, Tac. A. 1, 53 : aquarum (regio), id. ib. 15, 3…

ĕgĕo.opening: ( part. fut. egitura, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 24 ), v. n. cf. Gr. ἀχήν, poor; root αχ-, αγχ, in ἄχος, ἄγχω, etc.; Lat. angustus, angina , to be needy (for syn. cf.: indigeo, careo, vaco). Prop. Absol. (so usually in Plaut.…

ĕgersĭmon.opening: , = ἐγέρσιμον , a means of excitement , Mart. Cap. 9, § 911 .

ĕgestas.opening: egeo , indigence , extreme poverty , necessity , want (very freq. and class.; for syn. cf.: indigentia, inopia, penuria, paupertas, mendicitas): ista paupertas, vel potius egestas ac mendicitas, Cic. Parad. 6, 1, 45 ;…

ĕgestōsus.opening: adj. egestas , very poor , indigent , Aur. Vict. Epit. 12 al.

ĕgō^.opening: (ŏ always in poets of the best age, as Cat., Verg., Hor., etc.; ō ante-class. and post-Aug., as Juv. 17, 357 ; Aus. Epigr. 54, 6 , v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 483; gen. mei; dat. mihi; acc. and abl. me; plur. , nom. , and acc.…

ĕgŏmet.opening: v. the preced. art. and met.

ĕgŭla.opening: perh. kindr. with ἀχλύς , a kind of sulphur , Plin. 35, 15, 50, § 175 .

ĕhem.opening: interj. , an exclamation of joyful surprise, ha! what! ehem, optume! quam dudum tu advenisti? Plaut. As. 2, 4, 43 ; id. Most. 3, 2, 38 ; id. Mil. 4, 9, 5 ; id. Rud. 3, 5, 25 ; Ter. And. 2, 5, 6 : ehem, pater me, tu hic…

ĕhŏ.opening: interj. ; in the comic poets, used in asking, commanding, or scolding, ha? ho! holla! soho! In vehement questions, Plaut. Ep. 3, 4, 69 ; 5, 2, 22 ; id. Bacch. 4, 7, 5 : eho tu, id. Merc. 1, 2, 77 ; Ter. And. 5, 4, 5 ;…

Ĕlaea.opening: , = Ἐλαία , a city of Aeolis , Mel. 1, 8, 1 ; Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 121 ; Liv. 36, 43 al.

ĕlaeempŏrĭa.opening: , = ἐλαιεμπορία , traffic in oil , the oil-trade , Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 19 .

ĕlaeŏmĕli.opening: , = ἐλαιόμελι , a sort of manna which exudes from the branches of the olive-tree , Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 32 ; 23, 4, 50, § 96 .

ĕlaeōn.opening: , = ἐλαιών , a plantation of olives , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 39 fin.

ĕlaeŏthĕsĭum.opening: , = ἐλαιοθέσιον , the anointing-room in a bath , Vitr. 5, 11, 2 .

Ĕlaeūs.opening: , = Ἐλαιοῦς , a city on the Hellespont in the Thracian Chersonesus , Liv. 31, 16, 5 Drak. N. cr.; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 49 .— , Mel. 2, 2, 7 .

ĕlăte.opening: , = ἐλάτη , a sort of firtree , Lat. abies, Plin. 12, 28, 62, § 134 ; 23, 5, 53, § 99 .— The envelope or leaf of the palm-bud , Vulg. Cant. 5, 11 .

Ĕlătēa.opening: or , , , = Ἐλάτεια . A city of Phocis , Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 27 ; Liv. 28, 7 ; Plaut. Bacch. 4, 2, 9 al. — A city of Thessaly , Liv. 42, 54 .

Ĕlătēïus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to Elatus , a prince of the Lapithae : Caeneus, i. e. his son, Ov. M. 12, 497 : proles, the same, id. ib. 12, 189 ; v. Caeneus.

ĕlătērĭum.opening: , = ἐλατήριον , a medicine prepared from the juice of the wild cucumber , Cels. 5, 12 ; 6, 5 ; Scribon. Comp. 70, 224; Plin. 20, 1, 3, § 5 al.

ĕlătīne.opening: , = ἐλατίνη , a plant of the genus Antirrhinum, Plin. 27, 9, 50, § 74 .

ĕlătītes.opening: , = ἐλατίτης , a kind of blood-stone , Plin. 36, 20, 38, § 147 (dub. Jan. miltiten).

Ĕlăver.opening: a river in Gaul emptying into the Liger , now Allier , Caes. B. G. 7, 34 ; 35 ; 53 fin.

Ĕlĕa.opening: , = Ἐλέα , a city of Lucania , the birth-place of Parmenides and Zeno , the founders of the Eleatic philosophy , in Lat. also called Velia, Cic. N. D. 3, 33, 82 .— Hence, Zeno , of Elea , Cic. Tusc. 2, 22, 52 ; and: ,…

ĕlĕēmŏsўna.opening: , = ἐλεημοσύνη , alms (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Patient. 7 ; Aug. Civ. D. 21, 27 ; Vulg. Matt. 6, 2 al.

ĕlĕgātus.opening: an unknown kind of fish , Aus. Epigr. 4, 59 .

ĕlĕgi.opening: , = ἔλεγοι , elegiac verses , an elegy , Tib. 2, 4, 13 ; Prop. 4 (5), 1, 135 ; Hor. C. 1, 33, 3 ; id. Ep. 2, 2, 91 ; id. A. P. 77 ; Ov. F. 2, 3 ; Juv. 1, 4 ; Tac. Or. 10 al.

ĕlĕgīa.opening: ( , in Ov. ), , , = ἐλεγεία . An elegy : form elegia, Quint. 10, 1, 58 ; 93 ; Stat. S. 1, 2, 7 ; Mart. 5, 30, 4 ; Aus. Parent. 7, 1 ; form elegea, Quint. 1, 8, 6 ; form elegeia, Ov. Am. 3, 1, 7 ; 3, 9, 3 ; id. R. Am.…

ĕlĕgī^ăcus.opening: adj. , = ἐλεγιακός , elegiac : carmen, Diom. p. 507 P.; Serv. p. 1824 ib.; Mart. Cap. 5, 168 .

ĕlĕgīon.opening: (also ), , , = ἐλεγεῖον , an elegiac poem , an elegy , Aus. Epigr. 94, 2 .—In plur. , id. Parent. 29, 2 .

Ĕlĕleus.opening: , = Ἐλελεύς [from ἐλελεῦ , the cry of the Bacchantes], a surname of Bacchus , Ov. M. 4, 15 .—Hence, = Bacchae, Ov. H. 4, 47 .

ĕlĕmentārĭus.opening: adj. elementum, II. , belonging to the elements or rudiments , elementary (post-Aug. and very rare): senex, an old schoolmaster, Sen. Ep. 36 : litterae, elementary knowledge, Capitol. Pert. 1 .

ĕlĕmentīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. id. , elementary , elemental : substantiae, Tert. de Anima, 32.

ĕlĕmentum.opening: root al-, to nourish; Gr. ἄν-αλ-τος, ἄλσος; Lat. alo, alimentum, etc.; cf. Sanscr. al-akā, a girl , a first principle , element (cf.: initium, principium, exordium, primordium); Gr. στοιχεῖον . Lit. , in plur. : nec de…

ĕlenchus.opening: , = ἔλεγχος . A costly trinket , ear-pendant , Plin. 9, 35, 56, § 113 ; Juv. 6, 459 ; Dig. 34, 2, 32, § 8 ; cf. Boettig. Sabina II. p. 56.— Plur. , part of the title of a work of M. Pompilius Andronicus: adeo inops ut…

ĕlĕphantĭăsis.opening: ( , Veg. A. V. 4, 3, 4 ; August. de Gen. ad Lit. 9, 10 ), , , = ἐλεφαντίασις , a very virulent kind of leprosy , elephantiasis , Plin. 26, 1, 5, § 7 sq. ; 20, 10, 42, § 109 ; 20, 14, 52, § 144 ; Veg. A. V. 1, 9 ; 1, 16…

Ĕlĕphantīne.opening: , = Ἐλεφαντίνη , a small but very fertile island of the Nile , in the Thebaid , with a city of the same name , now Jezyret-Assuan , Mel. 1, 9, 2 ; 9 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 6 ; Tac. A. 2, 61 ; Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 163…

ĕlĕphantĭnus.opening: adj. elephas . Belonging to the elephant : tergum, Mel. 1, 5, 2 .— = ἐλεφάντινος , pure Lat. eburnĕus, of ivory : liber, consisting of ivory tablets, Vop. Tacit. 8 : atramentum, ivoryblack, Plin. 35, 6, 25, § 42 :…

Ĕlĕphantis.opening: (Gr. gen. ĭdos, Mart. 12, 43, 4 ), , = Ἐλεφαντίς . An island of the Nile , v. Elephantine.— The name of a licentious Greek poetess , Suet. Tib. 43 ; Mart. 12, 43, 4 ; Plin. 28, 7, 24, § 81 .

ĕlĕphantus.opening: , and , (rarely , , Plin. 8, 1, 1, § 1 ; Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 196 ; of the second form the nom. sing. , and of the first the oblique cases are most freq.), ( fem. , Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 14 ), = ἐλέφας , an elephant. —Form…

Ĕleusin.opening: ( acc. Eleusin, Front. Strat. 4, 7, 44 ; Lat. form , , Front. Ep. ad Ver. 1, p. 178 ; Cl. Mam. Grat. Act. Jul. 9, 3 ; Oros. 1, 7 ; and acc. to MSS. Eleusinam in Cic. N. D. 1, 42, 119 ; Liv. 31, 25, 2 ; cf. Salaminam…

Ĕleuthĕrĭus.opening: , = Ἐλευθέριος (Liberator), the surname of a god : Liber, Arn. 6, p. 207 .—Hence, , , , the festival of Jupiter Eleutherius , feast of liberty , celebrated in honor of the victory at Plataea, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 29 .

Ĕleuthĕrŏcĭlĭces.opening: (free Cilicians), a people (probably the aborigines ) in the mountains of Cilicia , Cic. Att. 5, 20, 5 ; id. Fam. 15, 4, 10 .

Ĕlĭmēa.opening: or , , , = Ἐλίμεια , a district to the southwest of Macedonia , Liv. 31, 40 ; 42, 53 al. ; also called , , , Liv. 45, 30, 6 .

Ĕlissa.opening: or , , , = Ἔλισσα , another name (occurring only in poetry) for Dido , Verg. A. 4, 335 ; 610 ; 5, 3 ; Ov. Am. 2, 18, 31 ; id. F. 3, 553 al. —Hence, (Elīsaeus), , adj. , poet. for Carthaginian : patres, Sil. 6, 346 :…

Ĕlŭsa.opening: a city in Gallia Aquitania , now Eauze , Claud. in Rufin. 1, 137 ; Amm. 15, 11, 14 .—Hence,

Ĕlymāis.opening: , = Ἐλυμαΐς , a district of Persia , in the west of the modern province of Iran , Plin. 6, 25, 28, § 111 al. — Hence, , , adj. , = Ἐλυμαῖος , Elymaean , Liv. 37, 40 .— Plur. subst. : , , , the inhabitants of Elymaïs ,…

ĕmācĭtas.opening: emax , a propensity to buy , a desire to be always buying , Col. 4, 3, 1 ; Plin. Ep. 3, 7, 8 .

ĕmax.opening: adj. emo; cf.: edax, bibax, etc. , eager to buy , fond of buying , Cato R. R. 2 fin. ; * Cic. Par. 6, 3, 51 ; Nep. Att. 13, 1 : domina, Ov. A. A. 1, 421 .— Poet. : non tu prece poscis emaci, i. e. that vows a price for…

ĕmo.opening: ( perf. subj. emissim, Plaut. Cas. 2, 5, 39 ), v. a. the same word with EMERE=accipere, Paul. ex Fest. pp. 4, 18, and 76, 1 Müll.; cf. adimo and demo; prop., to take; root yam; Sanscr. yamati, hold fast, Fick, Vergl.…

ĕmys.opening: , = ἐμύς , a kind of freshwater tortoise , Plin. 32, 4, 14, § 32 .

ĕnallăge.opening: , = ἐναλλαγή , a change of words (as, vos, O Calliope, precor, Verg. A. 9, 525 ), Gramm.

ĕnargīa.opening: , = ἐνάργεια , rhet. t. t., a vivid description , Rufin. de Schem. p. 275 ; Isid. Orig. 2, 20, 4 ; 2, 21, 33 .

ĕnarmŏnius.opening: ( , also ), , adj. , = ἐναρμόνιος , enharmonic; as subst. (sc. melodiae genus), = ἐναρμόνιον μέλος , the technical name in Greek music of a kind of melody , in which quarter-tones predominated, Mart. Cap. 9, § 930 :…

ĕnĕma.opening: , = ἔνεμα , a clyster , enema , Theod. Prisc. 2, 1 .

ĕnergēma.opening: , = ἐνέργημα , effect , efficacy (late Lat.), Tert. Praesc. 30 ; Carn. Christ. 34. In Prudentius written and scanned ĕnergĭma, Apoth. 468.

ĕnergūmĕnos.opening: , = ἐνεργούμενος , possessed of the devil (pure Lat.: a daemone correptus), Sulp. Sev. Dial. 1, 20, 9 ; 3, 6, 2 .

ĕnhaemon.opening: , = ἔναιμον (sc. φάρμακον ), a styptic medicine , Plin. 12, 17, 38, § 77 .

ĕnhȳ^dros.opening: ( ), , , = ἔνυδρος , an unknown gem , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 190 ; Sol. 37 ; 67 ; Isid. 16, 13, 9 .

ĕnim.opening: conj. [comp. of ĕ for pronom. stem i, and nam], a demonstrative corroborative particle. (Its position is regularly after the first word, or the first two or more closely connected words in the sentence; only in the…

Ĕnīpeus.opening: ( ), , , = Ἐνῖπεύς . A river in Thessaly that flows into the Penēus , Verg. G. 4, 368 ; Luc. 7, 116 ; as a river-god , the lover of Tyro , daughter of Salmoneus , and by her the father of Pelias and Neleus , Prop. 1,…

Ĕnispē.opening: a city of Arcadia , Sen. Troad. 844 ; Stat. Th. 4, 286 .

ĕnorchis.opening: , = ἔνορχις , an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 159 .

ĕo.opening: (īt, Verg. A. 9, 418 al. ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. vol. 2, p. 206 sq.: isse, issem, etc., for ivisse, etc., Ter. Hec. 2, 1, 25 ; Cic. Rosc. Am. 23, 64 ; id. Phil. 14, 1, 1 ; Ov. M. 7, 350 et saep.: isti, Turp. ap. Non. 4,…

ĕō.opening: adv. old dat. and abl. form of pron. stem i; cf. is . In locat. and abl. uses, Of place=in eo loco, there , in that place (rare): quid (facturus est) cum tu eo quinque legiones haberes? Cic. Ep. ad Brut. 1, 2, 1 : quo…

ĕōăd.opening: adv. inverted from adeo; cf. quoad , until : nuptias eludit, eoad dum puerorum avus fato concessit, App. Mag. 68, p. 318, 13 (cf. adeo, I. A. 2.).

ĕpactae.opening: , = ἐπακταί (sc. ἡμέραι ), intercalary days , Isid. Or. 6, 17, 29 and 31.

ĕpăgōge.opening: , = ἐπαγωγή , rhet. t. t. = inductio, induction , Rufin. de Fig. O. 26, p. 215 Ruhnk.

Ĕpămīnōndas.opening: , = Ἐπαμεινώνδας , the famous general of the Thebans , victor at Leuctra and Mantinea , Nep. Epam. ; Just. 6, 7 sq. ; Cic. de Or. 3, 34, 139 ; id. Tusc 1, 2, 4 ; 1, 15, 33 al.

ĕpănădiplōsis.opening: , = ἐπαναδίπλωσις , rhet. t. t., a repetition of the same word , Rufin. de Schem. § 9, p. 233 Ruhnk.

ĕpănăphŏra.opening: , = ἐπαναφορά , rhet. t. t., a repetition of the same word at the beginning of several successive clauses , Rufin. de Schem. Lex. 6, p. 231 al.

ĕpănŏdus.opening: , = ἐπάνοδος , rhet. t. t., a return to the same word , Rufin. de Schem. Lex. 19, p. 241 al.

ĕpănorthōsis.opening: , = ἐπανόρθωσις , rhet. t. t., a correction of one's self in speaking , Rufin. de Schem. 15, p. 238 al.

ĕpăphaerĕsis.opening: , = ἐπαφαίρεσις , a repeated removal : barbae, Mart. 8, 52 ; Veg. Vet. 5, 24, 5 .
