ĕpŏdĕs.opening: a kind of sea-fish , Ov. Hal. 126 ; Plin. 32, 11, 54, § 152 .

ĕpōdos.opening: , = ἐπωδός (singing to), a form of lyric metre invented by Archilochus , in which a longer verse is followed by a shorter one , not including the elegiac distich. So in Roman literature, the Epodi of Horace, Ter. Maur.…

ĕpogdŏŏs.opening: acc. ŏŏn or , adj. , = ἐπόγδοος , containing a whole and an eighth : numerus, the proportion of nine to eight, Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 1, 14 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 109 ; Fulg. Myth. 3, 9 .

ĕpomphălĭon.opening: , = ἐπομφάλιον , a plaster for the uterus , Fulg. Myth. 2, 5 fin.

Ĕpŏna.opening: from equus; cf. Gr. ἵππος; but referred to root ap- of apo by Fick, Wörterb. p. 425 , the protecting goddess of horses , asses , etc., Tert. ad Nat. 1, 11 ; id. Apol. 16 ; Juv. 8, 157 ; Prud. Apoth. 197 ; App. M. 3, p.…

ĕpops.opening: , = ἔποψ , the hoopoe , Ov. M. 6, 674 ; Verg. Cul. 251 ; cf. upupa.

ĕpoptae.opening: , = ἐπόπται , beholders; persons fully initiated into the Eleusinian mysteries , who attained the third and highest grade , that of intuition , Tert. adv. Val. 1 .

Ĕpŏrĕdĭa.opening: , = Ἐπορεδία , a Roman colony in Gallia Cisalpina , in the district of the Salassi, on the Duria , now Ivrea , Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 123 ; Brut. ap. Cic. Fam. 11, 20 fin. ; Vell. 1, 15, 5 ; Tac. H. 1, 70 .

Ĕpŏrĕdŏrix.opening: , = Ἐπορέδοριξ , Paraphr. A noble Aeduan , who served in Caesar's army , Caes. B. G. 7, 38 sq. ; 7, 54 sq.; 7, 76.— Another Aeduan of the same name , Caes. B. G. 7, 67 fin.

ĕpos.opening: (occurring only in the nom. and acc. ), , = ἔπος , a heroic poem , an epic; nom. , Hor. S. 1, 10, 43 ; acc. , Mart. 12, 95 ; Aus. Prof. 5, 10 .

ĕpŭlāris.opening: adj. epulum , of or belonging to a banquet. Adj. : epularis accubitio amicorum, at a banquet, Cic. de Sen. 13 fin. : sacrificium ludorum, id. de Or. 3, 19 fin. ; cf. 1. epulo, II.: sermo, App. M. 2, p. 123 .— Subst. :…

ĕpŭlātĭo.opening: epulor , feasting , eating (very rare), Lucil. ap. Non. 204, 18 ; Col. 12, 3, 2 ; Petr. 141, 10 ; Suet. Calig. 18 ; Val. Max. 2, 5, 4 extr.; Vulg. Sap. 19, 11 .

ĕpŭlātor.opening: id. , a feaster , carouser , Ambros. Cant. Cantic. 5, 5 init. al.

ĕpŭlātōrĭum.opening: id. , a feast , banquet , carouse , Ambros. Fragm. Saec. 8, 45 .

ĕpŭlo.opening: (also EPOLONUS, i, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 78, 11 Müll.), epulum , a guest at a feast or banquet , a feaster , carouser. In gen. (mostly post-class.), Cic. Att. 2, 7, 3 ; App. M. 2, p. 123 ; 9 , p. 235; Firm. Math. 5,…

ĕpŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [epulum], to hold an entertainment , to feast , banquet. Neutr. (class.): ut in voluptate sit, qui epuletur, Cic. Fin. 2, 5, 16 ; id. de Sen. 13, 45 ; id. Tusc. 1, 47, 113 ; id. Att. 5, 9 ; Liv. 42, 56…

ĕpŭlum.opening: , and in the plur. heterocl. , (EPULAM antiqui etiam singulariter posuere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 82, 14 Müll.), etym. dub.; perh. contr. from edipulum, from edo , sumptuous food or dishes (cf.: daps, commissatio, convivium,…

ĕqua.opening: equus , a mare , Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 4 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 10 ; Verg. G. 1, 59 ; 3, 266 ; Hor. C. 2, 16, 35 et saep.— Dat. and abl. plur. equis, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 19 ; Col. 6, 37, 8 ; Plin. 11, 41, 96, § 237 ; 8, 42, 64, §…

ĕquārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to horses (very rare). Adj. : medicus, a farrier, Val. Max. 9, 15, 2 .— Subst. , , , a stableboy , groom , Sol. 45, § 8 .— , , (sc. res), a stud of horses : grandes, Varr. R. R. 2 , prooem. §…

ĕquĕs.opening: id. , a horseman , rider. In gen.: it eques et plausu cava concutit ungula terram, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 1 (Ann. v. 419 ed. Vahlen); Liv. 26, 2 ; 28, 9 ; Dig. 9, 2, 57 ; Ov. F. 5, 700 (of Castor; cf. Hor. C. 1, 12, 26 ;…

ĕquester.opening: ( equestris, Liv. 27, 1, 11 ; Verg. A. 5, 667 al. ; v. Zumpt, Gram. § 100, A. 1.; like acris, celebris, celeris, etc.), adj. eques , belonging to a horseman , equestrian. In gen. (very rare): equestres statuae…

ĕquĭdem.opening: adv. comp. of the interj. ĕ and quidem enclit.; cf. edepol , a demonstrative corroborative particle, verily , truly , indeed , at all events , = certe, revera, etc. (freq. and class.). In gen. Without other particles.…

ĕquīle.opening: id.; cf.: bubile, caprile, ovile, etc. , a stable for horses , Cato, R. R. 14, 2 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 15 ; Suet. Calig. 55 .

ĕquīmentum.opening: id. , a fee for covering , Varr. ap. Non. 69, 27 .

ĕquīnus.opening: adj. equus , of or belonging to horses : pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 7 ; cf. genus, Col. 6, 27, 1 : lac, Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 1 : stercus, id. ib. 1, 38, 3 al.: cervix, Hor. A. P. 1 : cauda, id. Ep. 2, 1, 45 : ubera, id.…

ĕquĭo.opening: v. n. id. , of mares, to be in heat , Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 181 ; perh. also Col. 6, 38, 1 .

ĕquīrĭa.opening: id. , the annual horse-races , held on the 27 th of February and the 14 th of March in the Campus Martius, in honor of Mars , Varr. L. L. 6, § 13 Müll.; Ov. F. 2, 859 ; 3, 519 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 81, 12 , and 131, 13…

ĕquĭsaetum.opening: equus-seta , the plant horse-tail , equisetum arvense, Linn., Plin. 26, 13, 83, § 132 ; also called , , , id. 18, 28, 67, § 259 ; and , , , App. Herb. 40 , no. 1 al.

ĕquīso.opening: equus , a groom , stableboy (ante- and post-class.), Varr. ap. Non. 105, 14 ; 32 sq.; Val. Max. 7, 3 ext. 2; App. M. 7, p. 194 : equisones nautici, who draw vessels along by ropes , Varr. ap. Non. 106, 1 ; id. 451, 4 .

ĕquĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. equito , that may be ridden over , smooth : planities, Curt. 4, 9, 10 : campi, Amm. 22, 15 .

ĕquĭtātus.opening: equio , a being in heat , of mares (with hinnitus), Lucil. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 103 Müll.

ĕquĭtĭārĭus.opening: equitium , the inspector of a stud , Firm. Math. 8, 13.

ĕquĭtĭum.opening: equus , a stud of horses , Col. 6, 27, 1 ; Dig. 6, 1, 1 ; 7, 8, 12, § 4 al. ; cf. Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 10 .

ĕquĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ĕquĭto.opening: v. n. and a. [eques], to ride. Neutr. In gen. (class.): cum in illo nostro exercitu equitaret, Cic. Deiot. 10 ; Sall. J. 6, 1 ; Suet. Caes. 57 ; Hor. C. 2, 9, 24 al. : in equo, Dig. 9, 2, 57 ; cf.: in equuleis, Cic.…

ĕquŭla.opening: dim. equa . A little mare , a filly , Varr. ap. Non. 106, 12 .— Transf. , of a voluptuous woman, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 617 P.

ĕquŭlĕus.opening: or , , dim. equus , a young horse , a colt , foal. Lit. , Varr., Pompon., and Cic. ap. Non. 105, 11 sq. ; Liv. 31, 12 .— Transf. Eculeos argenteos nobilis aufert, horses wrought in silver , works of art, Cic. Verr. 2,…

ĕquŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a small young horse , a foal , Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 13 ; 2, 8 fin. ; * Cic. N. D. 2, 14, 38 .

ĕquus.opening: ( gen. plur. equūm, Verg. G. 2, 542 ; Stat. Th. 4, 409 al. ), Sanscr. acvas; Gr. ἵππος (ἴκκος); cf. Epŏna; root, ak-, to be sharp or swift; cf. Gr. ἄκρος, ὠκύς; Lat. acus, ocior , a horse , steed , charger. Prop. In…

ĕra.opening: (less correctly, ; v. erus), ae (archaic gen. sing. ĕrāï, Aus. Idyll. 7, 5 ), erus . Prop., the mistress of a house , with respect to the servants; the mistress , lady : nunquam era errans (i. e. Medea), etc., Enn. ap.…

Ĕrăna.opening: a town in Cilicia , near Mount Amanus , Cic. Fam. 15, 4, 8 .

ĕrănus.opening: , = ἔραϝος , a fund contributed for mutual protection against want : concessum est eranum habere ... si tali conlatione non ad turbas et ad inlicitos coetus, sed ad sustinendam tenuiorum inopiam utuntur, Plin. Ep. 10,…

Ĕrăsīnus.opening: , = Ἐρασῖνος , a river of Argolis , now Kephalari , Mel. 2, 3, 9 ; Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 225 ; Ov. M. 15, 276 ; cf. Sen. N. Q. 3, 26, 3 .

ĕrăsīnus.opening: † , , , = Ἐρασῖϝος , a favorite boy , Aus. Idyll. 7 praef.

Ĕrăsistrătus.opening: , = Ἐρασίστρατος , a famous physician of Alexandria in the time of Ptolemy Lagus , the founder of a medical school , Plin. 29, 1, 3, § 5 ; Val. Max. 5, 7 ext. 1; Cels. praef. 3, 4; 4, 4 et saep.

ĕrastes.opening: , = ἐραστής , a lover , M. Aurel. ap. Fronto Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 10 .

Ĕrătīnē.opening: , = Ἐρατειϝή , a nymph , a daughter of Venus , Mart. Cap. 9, § 905 .

Ĕrătō.opening: (occurring only in the nom. ), , = Ἐρατώ . The muse of lyric and amorous poetry , Ov. F. 4, 195 ; 349 ; id. A. A. 2, 16 ; 425 ; Aus. Idyll. 20, 6 .— Meton. , a Muse in gen., Verg. A. 7, 37 Serv.; Claud. Mall. Theod. 282…

Ĕrătosthĕnes.opening: , = Ἐρατοσθέϝης , a celebrated geographer , poet , and philosopher of Alexandria , under Ptolemy Euergetes , Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 3 ; Cic. Att. 2, 6 ; Caes. B. G. 6, 24, 2 ; Plin. Elench. 2 ; 5 ; 2, 108, 112 ; Quint. 1, 1,…

Ĕrĕbus.opening: , = Ἔρεβος . The god of darkness , son of Chaos , and brother of Nox , Cic. N. D. 3, 17 fin. ; Hyg. Myth. praef.; Verg. A. 4, 510 ; Ov. M. 14, 404 .— The Lower World , Verg. G. 4, 471 Serv.; id. A. 6, 247 ; 7, 140 ; Ov.…

Ĕrechtheus.opening: ( ), , , = Ἐρεχθεύς , a fabled king of Athens , father of Procris , Orithyia , Chthonia , and Creüsa , who devoted themselves to death for their country , Cic. Tusc. 1, 48, 116 ; id. Fin. 5, 22, 62 ; id. N. D. 3, 19 ;…

Ĕrembi.opening: , = Ἐρεμβοί , the Troglodytes in Africa , Avien. Descr. Orb. 271 ; Prisc. Perieg. 170 al.

ĕrēmīta.opening: , ae., , = ἐρημίτης , an eremite , hermit , Sulpic. Sever. Dial. 17.

ĕrēmītis.opening: adj. f. , = ἐρημιτίς , solitary , recluse , Sid. Ep. 9, 3 .

ĕrēmŏdĭcĭum.opening: , = ἐρημοδικίοϝ , a default of appearance before a court at the appointed time , Dig. 4, 4, 7 fin. ; 46, 7, 13 ; Cod. Just. 3, 1, 13, § 3 ; Tert. adv. Matyr. 3 .

ĕrēmus.opening: ( , Prud. Cathem. 5, 89 ; id. Psych. 371 ), , adj. , = ἔρημος , waste , desert (late Lat.). Adj. : loca, Cod. Just. 11, 57, 4 .— Subst. : , , (sc. locus), or (sc. regio), a wilderness , desert , Tert. Idol. 5 ; Sulpic.…

Ĕrĕtrĭa.opening: , = Ἐρετρία . The principal city on the island of Euboea , the birthplace of the philosopher Menedemus , now Palaeo Castro , Plaut. Merc. 3, 4, 59 ; Mel. 2, 7, 9 ; Plin. 4, 12, 21, § 64 ; Cic. Ac. 2, 42 ; Liv. 32, 16 ;…

ĕrīce.opening: , = ἐρείκη , heath , broom , ling , Plin. 24, 9, 39, § 64 ; 11, 16, 15, § 41 sq. —Hence, , , adj. , of the heath-flower , i. e. collected from it: mel (= mel sylvestre), Plin. 11, 16, 15, § 41 .

Ĕrichthō.opening: , = Ἐριχθώ , a Thessalian witch consulted by Pompey , Luc. 6, 508 ; hence transf., of another witch, Ov. H. 15, 139 .

Ĕrichthŏnĭus.opening: , = Ἐριχθόϝιος . A son of Vulcan , king of Athens , and the first who yoked four horses together to a chariot , Verg. G. 3, 113 Serv.; Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 202 ; Ov. M. 2, 553 ; 9, 424 ; Hyg. Fab. 166 .—Hence, , , adj. :…

ĕrĭ-fŭga.opening: (less correctly, ), , (erus-fugio), a runaway , a slave who absconds from his master : erifugae Famuli, Cat. 63, 51 .

Ĕrĭgōnus.opening: , = Ἐριγώϝ or Ἐρίγωϝ , a river of Macedonia , now Tzerna , Liv. 31, 39, 6 ; 39, 53 fin.

ĕrī^lis.opening: (less correctly , v. erus), , adj. erus , of the master or mistress of a family , the master's , the mistress's ( poet. ; esp. in Plaut.): erum fefelli, in nuptias conjeci erilem filium, Ter. And. 3, 4, 23 ; cf. id. Ad.…

ĕrīnĕos.opening: , = ἐριϝεός , a plant , perh. the Campanula Rapunculus, Linn., Plin. 23, 7, 65, § 131 .

Ĕrīnys.opening: (or, less correctly, ; cf. Wagner ad Verg. A. 2, 337 ), , , = Ἐριννύς ( Ἐρινύς ), one of the Furies , Verg. A. 7, 447 ; 570 ; Ov. M. 1, 241 ; 4, 490 ; 11, 14 et saep.— Acc. Erinyn, Ov. M. 1, 725 .—In plur. : Erinyes,…

ĕrĭŏphŏros.opening: , = ἐριοφόρος (woolbearer), a kind of bulbous plant , Plin. 19, 2, 10, § 32 .

Ĕrĭphȳla.opening: , or , , , = Ἐριφύλη , daughter of Talaüs , and wife of Amphiaraüs , whom she betrayed to Polynices for a golden necklace , for which she was slain by her son Alcmaeon. —Form -a, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 18, § 39 ; id. Inv. 1,…

Ĕris.opening: , = Ἔρις , the goddess of strife , Hyg. F. 92 .

ĕrisma.opening: , and , , , = ἔρεισμα , a buttress , Front. Aquaed. 18 ; Vitr. 6, 11, 6 ( heterocl. gen. plur. : eris matorum, id. 10, 1, 2 ).

ĕristălis.opening: an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 160 (dub.—Jan. erythallis).

ĕrĭthăce.opening: , = ἐριθάκη , bee-bread , sandarach , called also sandaraca and cerinthus, Plin. 11, 7, 7, § 17 (in Varr. R. R. 316, 8 and 23, written as Greek).

Ĕriza.opening: , = Ἔριζα , a town of Magna Phrygia , Liv. 38, 14, 1 .—Hence, , , adj. , of Eriza : regio, Plin. 10, 43, 60, § 124 .

Ĕros.opening: , = Ἔρως . Love as a person; Lat. Amor, Cupido, Nemes. Ecl. 4 lem. — In gen., a common name of Roman slaves or freedmen , Cic. Fam. 12, 26 ; id. Att. 10, 15 ; 15, 15 ; 20 ; Dig. 6, 1, 5 fin. et saep.— The name of an…

ĕrōtēma.opening: , = ἐρώτημα , an inquiry , a question , Mart. Cap. 5, § 524 .

Ĕrōtŏpaegnĭon.opening: , = ἐρωτοπαίγνιον , a love song , Aus. Edyll. 13 fin. —Esp. plur. : , , the title of a book of poems by Laevius, Gell. 2, 24, 9 .

ĕrōtўlus.opening: , = ἐρωτύλος , an unknown precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 160 .

ĕrus.opening: (less correctly, , v. infra ), , Sanscr. root, har-; har-āmi, I seize; har-anam, hand; Gr. χείρ, χέρης; Lat. heres, hirudo; but the form erus is that of the best MSS.; cf. Ritschl, Opusc. 2, 409; Brix ad Plaut. Trin. 1,…

Ĕrўmanthus.opening: , = Ἐρύμανθος . A chain of mountains in Arcadia , on the borders of Elis , where Hercules slew the boar named after the place , Ov. H. 9, 87 ; id. M. 5, 608 ; Mart. 11, 69 .— Derivv. , , adj. , Erymanthian : belua, Cic.…

Ĕrўsichthōn.opening: ( ), , , = Ἐρυσίχθων , son of the Thessalian king Triopas; he cut down the grove of Ceres, for which he was punished with a raging hunger, that caused him to devour his own flesh, Ov. M. 8, 471 sq. ; cf. Hyg. Astr. 2,…

ĕrўsĭmum.opening: , = ἐρύσιμον , a sort of grain , called also irio, Plin. 18, 10, 22, § 96 .

ĕrўsĭpĕlas.opening: , = ἐρυσίπελας , a reddish eruption on the skin, St. Anthony's fire , erysipelas , Cels. 5, 28, 11 ( id. 5, 26, 31 and 33, written as Gr.).

ĕrўsiscēptrum.opening: , = ἐρυσίσκηπτρον , a low thorny shrub , also called adipsatheon, Plin. 24, 13, 69, § 112 al. ; App. Herb. 109 .

ĕrўsĭthăles.opening: , = ἐρυσίθαλες , a plant with a yellow flower , Plin. 26, 13, 85, § 137 ; cf. id. 25, 13, 102, § 160 .

Ĕrўthēa.opening: or , , , = Ἐρύθεια , a small island in the Bay of Cadiz , where the giant Geryon dwelt , Mel. 3, 6, 2 ; Plin. 4, 21, 36, § 120 ; Prop. 5, 9, 2 .— Derivv. , , adj. , Erythean : ad litora Gades, Sil. 16, 195 .— , , ,…

ĕrўthīnus.opening: , = ἐρυθῖνος , a red kind of sea-mullet , Plin. 9, 16, 23, § 166 ; Ov. Hal. 104 .

Ĕrȳ^thrae.opening: , = Ἐρυθραί . A city of Boeotia , near Mount Cithaeron , Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 26 ; Stat. Th. 7, 265 .—By it was founded, One of the twelve chief cities of Ionia , Plin. 31, 2, 10, § 14 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 19, § 49 ; Liv.…

ĕrythraeus.opening: adj. , = ἐρυθραῖος , reddish : aries, Col. 7, 2 fin. ; 7, 3, 2 ; cf. Plin. 8, 48, 73, § 191 .— As an adj. prop. , v. Erythrae, II. B., and Erythras, II.

ĕrythrăĭcon.opening: , = ἐρυθραϊκόν , a species of the plant satyrion, Plin. 26, 10, 63, § 97 .

ĕrȳ^thrănos.opening: , = ἐρυθρανός , red : cissus erythranos similis hederae, Plin. 24, 10, 49, § 82 .—Hence, † , , , = ἐρυθρανόν , a kind of ivy with reddish berries , Plin. 16, 34, 62, § 147 .

Ĕrȳ^thras.opening: , = Ἐρύθρας , a fabulous king of southern Asia (Arabia or Persia), after whom the Red Sea , or the Arabian and Persian Gulfs , were named , Mel. 3, 8, 1 ; Plin. 6, 23, 28, § 107 ; Curt. 8, 9 . —Deriv., , , adj. ,…

ĕrythrŏcŏmos.opening: adj. , = ἐρυθρόκομος , red-haired : genus, a kind of pomegranate-tree, Plin. 13, 19, 34, § 113 .

ĕrythrŏdănus.opening: , = ἐρυθρόδανον , madder , Rubia tinctorum, Linn. (pure Lat. rubia); Plin. 24, 11, 56, § 94 .

ĕrȳthros.opening: adj. , = ἐρυθρός , red : rhus, Plin. 24, 11, 55, § 93 : venenum, id. 21 . 31, 105, § 179.

Ĕryx.opening: , = Ἔρυξ , the name of a high mountain in the northwestern angle of Sicily , and of a city near it famous for its temple of Venus. According to fable, it was named from the Sicilian king Eryx, son of Butes and Venus,…

ĕsox.opening: , = ἴσοξ , a fish of the Rhine , a kind of pike , Plin. 9, 15, 17, § 44 (dub. Jan. isox).

ĕt.opening: conj. [Sanscr. ati, beyond; Gr. ἔτι , besides, yet; Lat. et-iam, at-avus], serves to connect, in the most general manner, single words or entire sentences, and. In gen.: qui illius impudentiam norat et duritudinem, Cato…

ĕt-ĕnim.opening: conj. , subjoins a corroborative clause, or one which contains the reason of a preceding statement, for , truly , and indeed , because that , since (not freq. till class. times, esp. in Cic.): verum profecto hoc petere…

Ĕtĕōclēs.opening: , = Ἐτεοκλῆς , son of Oedipus and Jocasta , brother of Polynices; he was the cause of the Theban war, described by the Roman poet Statius in the Thebais, Cic. Off. 3, 21, 82 ; Hyg. Fab. 76 ; gen. Eteoclis, Stat. Th. 3,…

ĕtēsĭăcus.opening: adj. , = ἐτησιακός , of the trade-winds : vitis, Plin. 14, 3, 4, § 36 .

ĕtēsĭae.opening: , = ἐτησίαι (sc. ἄνεμοι ), the winds that blow annually during the dog-days for forty days , Etesian winds , trade-winds , Sen. Q. N. 5, 10 sq. ; Col. 11, 2, 56 ; 58 ; Lucr. 6, 716 ; Cic. N. D. 2, 53 ; id. Fam. 2, 15…

ĕtēsius.opening: adj. , = ἐτήσιος , yearly. Prop.: flabra aquilonum = etesiae, Lucr. 5, 742 ; 6, 730 Munro ad loc.; cf. id. 6, 715 sqq.— Transf. : lapis, a kind of stone, Plin. 36, 22, 43, § 157 .

ĕtĭam.opening: conj. [cf. Gr. ἔτι ; with ending -am, as in quoniam, nunciam, etc.; cf. Brix ad Plaut. Trin. prol. 3 ], annexes a fact or thought to that which has already been said, and also , and furthermore , also , likewise ,…

ĕtĭamdum.opening: (also written separately), hitherto , even till now , still , yet (rare; usually after a negative; cf.: etiamtum, etiamnum): dissimulabo, hos quasi non videam neque esse hic etiamdum sciam, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 2 : nihil…

ĕtĭam-num.opening: (more freq., always in Cic. and Caes.) (also written separately, etiam num ... nunc), conj. , yet , till now , still , even now , even to this time , even at this time. In gen. (in all periods): Ev. Etiamnunc mulier…

ĕtĭam-si.opening: (also written separately), a concessive conditional particle, = καὶ εἰ , more emphatic than etsi, even if , although , albeit. With indic. : etiamsi alterum tantum perdundum est, Plaut. Ep. 3, 4, 81 : etiamsi dudum…

ĕtĭam-tum.opening: (more rarely) , conj. , even then , till that time , till then , still. With imperf. tense (so usually): omnes etiamtum retinebant illum Pericli sucum; sed erant paulo uberiore filo, Cic. de Or. 2, 22 fin. : etiamtum…

ĕtўmŏlŏgĭa.opening: , = ἐτυμολογία , etymology , Cic. Ac. 1, 8, 32 ; Quint. 1, 6, 1 ; 28 ; 7, 3, 25 et saep. ( Cic. Top. 8, 35 , written as Greek, and transl. by veriloquium).

ĕtўmŏlŏgĭce.opening: , = ἐτυμολογική , etymology , Varr. L. L. 7, § 4 Müll. ( ib. 7, § 109 , written as Greek).

ĕtўmŏlŏgos.opening: , = ἐτυμολόγος , an etymologist , Varr. L. L. 6, § 39 Müll.

ĕtўmon.opening: , = ἔτυμον , the origin of a word : etymon habere, to be derived, Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 2 : etyma (with origines), Gell. 18, 4, 11 al.

ĭn-ănĭmālis.opening: adj. , lifeless , inanimate (post-class.): omnia (opp. animalia), App. Trism. p. 88 ; Macr. S. 4, 6 ; Tert. Apol. 48 .

ĭn-ănĭmans.opening: adj. , inanimate (post-Aug. and very rare): aut animantia sunt aut inanimantia, Sen. Ep. 58, 9 (al. inanimata).

ĭn-ănĭmātus.opening: adj. , lifeless , inanimate (late Lat.), Boëth. Arist. Anal. Prior. 1, 4, p. 471 sq. (but not in Cicero; v. Madv. ad Cic. Fin. p. 534 sq. ).

ĭnănĭmis.opening: adj. 2. in-anima , without breath or without life , breathless , lifeless , inanimate (Appuleian): ventus, i. e. that does not blow, App. M. 1, p. 103, 23 : humi projectus, inanimis, id. ib. p. 108, 25; cf. ib. 2, p.…

ĭnănĭmus.opening: adj. 2. in-animus , lifeless , inanimate (class.; cf. Madv. ad Cic. Fin. p. 534 ): cum inter inanimum et animal hoc maxime intersit, quod inanimum nihil agit, animal agit aliquid, Cic. Ac. 2, 12, 37 ; cf.: inanimum est…

ĭnānĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
ĭnānĭo.opening: v. a. inanis , to make empty , to empty out , evacuate ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): hoc ubi inanitur spatium, etc., Lucr. 6, 1005 ; cf.: locus inanitus magis ac vacuatus, ib. 1025 : herbacea arefacta per se inanit…

ĭnānis.opening: adj. etym. dub.; cf. 2. in- , empty , void (opp. plenus; freq. and class.). Physically: cum vas inane dicimus, non ita loquimur ut physici, quibus inane esse nihil placet, sed ita, ut verbi causa sine aqua, sine vino,…

ĭnānĭtas.opening: inanis . Lit. , emptiness , empty space (rare but class.): mihi inanitate Jamdudum intestina murmurant, Plaut. Cas. 4, 3, 5 : per inanitatem ferri, Cic. Fat. 9, 18 : oris, Quint. 1, 11, 6 .— Trop. , emptiness ,…

ĭn-ăpertus.opening: adj. , not open : fraudique inaperta senectus, not exposed, Sil. 7, 26 .

ĭn-apprĕhensĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , incomprehensible (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3, 38 ; Tert. adv. Val. 11 ; id. adv. Herm. 43 al.

ĭn-ăquo.opening: v. a. , to turn into water : nutrimenta corporis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 14, 118 .

ĭn-ăquōsus.opening: adj. , lacking water (post-class.): loca, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 1 : inaquosus ἄνυδρος, Gloss. Cyril.— As subst. : , , plur. , dry places , desert places : serpentes arida et inaquosa sectantur, Tert. Bapt. 1 .

ĭn-ărātus.opening: adj. , unploughed , untilled , fallow ( poet. ): terra, Verg. G. 1, 83 : tellus, Hor. Epod. 16, 43 : diu Pangaea, Stat. Th. 10, 512 .

ĭnarcto.opening: v. a. in-arctus , to circumscribe , limit ( post - class. ), Aug. contr. Ep. Manich. 25, 27.

ĭn-ardesco.opening: v. inch.n. , to kindle , take fire , burn , glow ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : nubes Solis inardescit radiis, Verg. A. 8, 623 : arbusculae in igne ut ferrum inardescentes, Plin. 13, 25, 51, § 140 : nec munus…

ĭn-ārĕfactus.opening: adj. , dried : sanguis ranarum, Plin. 32, 10, 42, § 121 dub.

ĭn-āresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become dry in any place, to dry up , become quite dry (post-Aug.). Lit. : in sole, Plin. 26, 8.40, § 66 ; for which: caenum illitum sole, id. 31, 6, 32, § 61 : opus, Vitr. 7, 3 : medicamenta, Cels. 5,…

ĭn-argento.opening: v. a. in-argentum , to overlay with silver , to silver : aes, Paul. Sent. 5, 25, 5 . — Mostly Part. : , , overlaid with silver , silvered over (post-Aug.): lamina aerea, Plin. 21, 2, 3, § 5 : lecti, Dig. 33, 10, 3…

ĭn-argūtus.opening: adj. , not acute , without acuteness (post - class.): sententia non inarguta, Dig. 7, 5, 5, § 1 .— Adv. : , not acutely : non mehercule inargute nec incallide opposuisti hoc Tullianum, Gell. 12, 13, 19 .

ĭn-armo.opening: v. a. , to arm (eccl. Lat.), Ven. Fort. Vit. Leob. 7.

ĭn-ăro.opening: v. a. , to plough in , cover by ploughing. Lit. : sarmenta, Cato, R. R. 37, 3 : fabalia pro stercore, Varr. R. R. 1, 23 . 3; cf.: disjectum fimum, Col. 2, 5, 2 : semina abjecta, Plin. 18, 18, 47, § 169 : arbores, Col.…

ĭn-artĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. , indistinct , inarticulate (post-class.), Arn. 2, 59 : vox, Prisc. 537 P.

ĭn-artĭfĭcĭālis.opening: adj. , inartificial , not according to the rules of art (post-Aug.): illas (probationes) ἀτέχνους, id est inartificiales; has ἐντέχνους, id est artificiales vocaverunt, Quint. 5, 1, 1 : probationes, id. 5, 5, 2 ; cf.…

ĭn-ascensus.opening: adj. , not mounted or ascended : locus (rostra), Plin. Pan. 65, 3 .

ĭnassĕro.opening: v. a. in-asser , to cover with beams , Inscr. Grut. 207, 2 .

ĭn-assignātus.opening: adj. , unassigned (post class.): inodus agrorum, Aggen. p. 70 Goes.

ĭn-assŭētus.opening: adj. , unaccustomed ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): equi, Ov. F. 4, 450 : manus, id. A. A. 1, 300 : at vestigia nuda sinusque Cingere, inassuetum, i. e. unusual, Sil. 3, 236 : opere inassueto Galliis, Fragm. Or. Claud.…

ĭnattāmĭnātus.opening: adj. 2. inattamino , uninjured , unhurt , Tert. de Cor. Mil. c. ult.

ĭn-attĕnŭātus.opening: adj. , undiminished , unweakened : fames, unappeased, Ov. M. 8, 846 .

ĭn-attrītus.opening: adj. , not rubbed away , not worn : aurum, Paul. Nol. Carm. 10, 254 .

ĭn-audax.opening: adj. , not daring , timorous : raptor, Hor. C. 3, 20, 3 .

ĭn-audībĭlis.opening: adj. , inaudible : melodia nobis, Censor. D. 13 .

ĭn-audĭo.opening: (arch. , cf. Ritschl Proleg. ad Plaut. p. 143 ), īvi or , v. a. , to hear , learn , esp. something secret (mostly ante-class. and in the tempp. perff. ): quod ego inaudivi, accipite, Pac. ap. Non. 126, 23 : unde hoc tam…

ĭn-audītĭuncŭla.opening: dim. , a little lecture or lesson : disciplinae grammaticae, Gell. 5, 21, 4 .

ĭn-audītus.opening: adj. , unheard. (On account of its novelty or strangeness.) Unheard-of , unusual , strange , new (freq. and class.; a favorite word of Cic.): nihil dicam reconditum, nihil aut inauditum vobis aut cuiquam novum, Cic. de…

ĭnaugŭrātĭo.opening: inauguro, a consecration; hence, transf. , a beginning (post-class.), Tert. adv. Valent. 11 .

ĭn-augŭro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ĭn-augŭro.opening: v. n. and a. Lit. To take omens from the flight of birds , to practise augury , to divine : per sacram viam augures ex arce profecti solent inaugurare, Varr. L. L. 5, § 47 Müll.: impetritum, inauguratum'st: quovis…

ĭnaurātor.opening: inauro , a gilder (post-class.), Firm. 4, 15; 8, 26; Inscr. Orell. 4201 ; Inscr. Grut. 1074, 12 .

ĭnaurātūra.opening: id. , a gilding , Front.— Piur. , Gromat. Vet. 97, 8.

ĭnaurātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from inauro.

ĭn-aurātus.opening: adj. , not gilded , not ornamented with gold : inauratae atque illautae mulieris, Titin. ap. Charis. p. 181 P.

ĭnaures.opening: in-auris , ear-drops , ear-rings , ornaments for the ear , Plaut. Men. 3, 3, 17 ; Plin. 9, 55, 81, § 172 ; 32, 2, 7, § 16 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 31 .

ĭnaurĭo.opening: v. a. id. , to give hearing to , to cause to hear (post-class.): surdos (Christus), Lact. Epit. 45, 2 .— To grant (in answer to prayer), Hilar. in Psa. 53, 54.

ĭn-aurītus.opening: adj. , without ears : animalia, Gell. 7, 6, 1 dub.; v. 2. inauditus, III.

ĭn-auro.opening: v. a. , to cover or overlay with gold , to gild (class.; most freq. in the part. perf. ). Lit. : tegulas aereas, Plin. 33, 3, 18, § 57 ; Vitr. 7, 8 : maurata statua, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 21, § 50 : columna extrinsecus, id.…

ĭn-auspĭcātus.opening: adj. At which no auspices were taken , without auspices : lex, Liv. 7, 6, 11 .—Hence, , adv. (lit. abl. absol. ), without consulting the auspices : quod inauspicato pomoerium transgressus esset (Ti. Gracchus), Cic. Div.…

ĭn-ausus.opening: adj. , not ventured , unattempted ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): ne quid inausum Aut intractatum scelerisve dolive fuisset, Verg. A. 8, 205 : nefas, Val. Fl. 1, 807 : quid enim per hosce dies inausum intemeratumve…

ĭnauxĭlĭātus.opening: 2. in - auxilior , not supported , Vulg. Sap. 12, 16 .

ĭnăvārus.opening: 2. in-avarus , not greedy , not avaricious , Cassiod. Var. 1, 3 .

ĭnāversĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-aversus , that cannot be turned aside , unalterable : aeternitas (with immobilis and insolubilis), App. Trim. p. 100 med. (al. inaversabilis or inversibilis).

ĭnēbrĭātĭo.opening: inebrio , inebriation (late Lat.), Aug. de Civ. Dei, 16, 1.

ĭnēbrĭātor.opening: inebrio , one who makes drunk (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 18 .

ĭn-ēbrĭo.opening: v. a. , to make drunk , inebriate ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : palma vescentes inebriat, Plin. 12, 22, 47, § 103 ; id. 14, 1, 3, § 17 ; Sen. Ep. 83, 27 . — Transf. , of colors, to saturate' amethystum inebriatur…

ĭn-ĕdax.opening: adj. , not voracious , that eats little , Gloss. Philox.

ĭnĕdĭa.opening: 2. in-edo , an abstaining from food , fasting (class.): tenebrae oboriuntur, genua inediā succidunt, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 30 : vigiliis et inedia necatus, Cic. Fin. 5, 27, 82 : inediam sustinere, Cels. 1, 3 : inediā vitam…

ĭn-ēdĭtus.opening: adj. , not made known , unknown : cura, Ov. P. 4, 16, 39 .

ĭn-effābĭlis.opening: adj. , unutterable , unpronounceable (Plinian): nomina, Plin. 5 praef. § 1: verba, id. 28, 2, 4, § 20 .— Adv. : , unutterably , ineffably (late Lat.): Deus ineffabiliter artifex, Aug. Enchir. 89 .

ĭn-effābĭlĭtas.opening: id. , unutterableness , ineffableness (late Lat.): visionis, Aug. Ep. 147 .

ĭneffectus.opening: adj. 2. in-efficio , not carried out , incomplete , Hier. in Didym. de Spir. Sanc. 5, 8 init.

ĭn-effĭcācĭa.opening: inefficax , inefficacy (late Lat.): libertatis, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 94.

ĭn-effĭcax.opening: adj. , ineffectual , inefficient (post-Aug.). With gen. : vox inefficax verborum, unproductive of, unable to produce, Sen. Ira, 1, 3 .— Absol. : ratio, Sen. Ira, 1, 10 : dii, id. Ben. 4, 4 .— Comp. , Plin. 34, 11, 25, §…

ĭn-effĭgĭābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-effigio , that cannot be portrayed or delineated (late Lat.): anima, Tert. Anim. 24 .

ĭn-effĭgĭātus.opening: adj. id. , without form , shapeless (post-class.): fetus (with informis), Gell. 17, 10, 3 : anima, Tert. Anim. 9 .

ĭn-effrēnātus.opening: adj. , unbridled , trop. (late Lat.): cupiditates, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 6, 4.

ĭn-effŭgĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-effugio , unavoidable , inevitable (post-class.): necessitas ultionis, App. de Mundo, p. 75 fin.

ĭn-ēlăbōrātus.opening: adj. , unlabored , unstudied , trop. (post-Aug.): oratio, Sen. Tranq. 1, 9 : deliciae, Cassiod. Var. 8, 31 .— Obtained without labor : pabulum, Ambros. ap. Luc. 7, § 124 .

ĭn-ēlĕgans.opening: adj. , not choice or elegant; tasteless , inelegant (class.): orationis non inelegans copia, Cic. Brut. 81, 282 : deliciae (with illepidae), Cat. 6, 2 : odor non inelegans, a not unpleasant odor, Plin. 21, 25, 98, § 169…

ĭn-ēlĕgantĭa.opening: tastelessness , inelegance; only as law t. t., want of harmony , inconsistency (with the general system of law; cf. Austin, Jurisprud. Lect. XXX. p. 552): inelegantia juris motus, Gai. Ins t. 1, 84; 85.

ĭn-ēlŏquax.opening: adj. 2. in-eloquor , unutterable (late Lat.): gemitibus ineloquacibus, Novat. de Trin. 29 .

ĭn-ēlŏquens.opening: adj. id. , ineloquent (eccl. Lat.): indocti et ineloquentes, Lact. Opif. D. 20, 5 .

ĭn-ēlŏquĭbĭlis.opening: adj. id. , unutterable , ineffable , for ineffabilis (eccl. Lat.): fructus, Lact. 7, 11 : praemium, id. 7, 5, 9 .

ĭn-ēluctābĭlis.opening: adj. , from which one cannot extricate one ' s self , unavoidable , inevitable ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : caenum, Stat. Th. 9, 502 .— Trop. : tempus, Verg. A. 2, 324 : fatum, id. ib. 8, 334 ; Vell. 2, 57 fin.

ĭn-ēlŭĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-eluo , that cannot be washed out , indelible (eccl. Lat.): fucus, Lact. 7, 20, 9 : maculae, id. Ira D. 23, § 24 .

ĭn-ēmendābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be amended , incorrigible (post-Aug.): pravitas, Quint. 1, 1, 37 : incommoda oris, id. 11, 3, 12 : affectus, Sen. Ira, 3, 41 .

ĭn-ēmendātus.opening: adj. , unamended , incorrect (late Lat.): dum de inemendatis scribuntur inemendatiora, Hier. in Ezech. 40, 5 ; Serv. Verg. A. 1, 565 .

ĭnēmĕrĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-emereor , that cannot be merited , cannot be earned (late Lat.), Tert. Res Carn. 18 .

ĭn-emptus.opening: ( ), , adj. , unbought , unpurchased ( poet. and postAug.): dapes, Verg. G. 4, 133 ; Hor. Epod. 2, 48 : consulatus, Tac. H. 2, 60 .

ĭn-ēnarrābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be related or described , indescribable (mostly post-Aug.): mira quadam et incredibili atque inenarrabili pietate, Vell. 2, 99, 2 : labor, Liv. 44, 5, 1 : tabes (jecoris), id. 41, 15, 2 : natura…

ĭn-ēnarrātīvus.opening: adj. 2. inenarro , not adapted for relation , Tert. adv. Val. 27 .

ĭn-ēnarrātus.opening: adj. , unexplained (late Lat.): quod reliquimus inenarratum, Gell. 12, 6, 1 : verba, id. 19, 14, 5 .

ĭnēnătābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-enato , from which one cannot swim out (post-class.): profundum, Tert. Idol. 24 .

ĭnēnōdābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-enodo , that cannot be freed from knots , cannot be unravelled (only in the trop. signif. class.). Lit. : capillus, App. Mag. p. 276, 15 .— Trop. , that cannot be explained , inexplicable , Att. ap. Non. 15,…

ĭn-ēnormis.opening: adj. , not irregular , not immoderate (post-class.): proceritas, App. M. 2, p. 115, 22 .

ĭnēnuntĭābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-enuntio , unspeakable (post-class.): quiddam, Censor. de Die Nat. 19 .

ĭn-ĕo.opening: (iniri only ap. Vop. Procul. 12, 7 ; fut. iniet, Sen. Ben. 21, 2 ), v. a. and n. To go into , to enter a place (class.). Lit. In gen., constr. with acc. , or with in and acc. With acc. : illius domum, Cic. Deiot. 3, 8 :…

ĭneptĭa.opening: ineptus , silliness , folly , absurdity (in sing. ante- and post-class.): tua, Ter. Ad. 4, 7, 31 ; Plaut. Merc. prol. 26 . — Plur. : , , sillinesses , fooleries , trifles , absurdities (class.): omnium ineptiarum haud…

ĭneptĭo.opening: v. n. id. , to talk or act absurdly , to trifle , play the fool ( poet. ): ineptis, Ter. Ad. 5, 8, 11 ; id. Phorm. 2, 3, 73 : desinas ineptire, Cat. 8, 1 .

ĭneptĭŏla.opening: dim. ineptiae , an absurdity , folly , Aus. Idyll. 11 .

ĭneptĭtūdo.opening: ineptus , for ineptia, absurdity : homo ineptitudinis cumulatus, Caecil. ap. Non. 128, 15 (Com. Fragm. v. 61 Rib.).

ĭneptus.opening: adj. 2. in-aptus , unsuitable , impertinent , improper , tasteless , senseless , silly , pedantic , absurd , inept , without tact (class.): quem enim nos ineptum vocamus, is mihi videtur ab hoc nomen habere ductum, quod…

ĭn-ĕquĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be ridden upon , unfit for riding : campi, Curt. 8, 14, 3 .

ĭn-ĕquĭto.opening: v. n. and a. , to ride upon or over any thing (post-class.). Lit. , with dat. : Sarmatae patentibus campis inequitant, Flor. 4, 12, 20 : horrenti fascino, Arn. 4, 7 .— Transf. , with acc. : Aurora caelum inequitabat,…

ĭn-ermis.opening: , and , (v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 88), adj. 2. in-arma , unarmed , without weapons , defenceless. Form inermis. Lit. : si spoliatum, inermem recepisset Antonium, Cic. Fam. 12, 10, 3 : inermibus vim facere (opp. arma.…

ĭn-errābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-erro , unerring (post-class.): meatus, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 7, 27 : orbis, id. de Mundo, p. 58, 6: computatio, August. Civ. Dei, 21, 8.

ĭn-errans.opening: adj. , not wandering , immovable , fixed; of the fixed stars: stellae eae, quae inerrantes vocantur, Cic. N. D. 2, 21, 54 ; 3, 20, 51 ; Lact. 2, 5, 18 .

ĭn-erro.opening: v. n. , to wander or ramble about in a place ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : Diana montibus, Plin. Ep. 1, 6, 3 ; cf.: ignis aedibus, Stat. S. 1, 5, 58 .— Trop. : memoria imaginis oculis inerrabat, swam before the eyes,…

ĭners.opening: ( abl. inerti, Plin. 16, 43, 83, § 227 : inerte, Ov. P. 1, 5, 8 ; 1, 10, 14 ), adj. 2. in-ars , unskilled in any art or trade, without skill , unskilful (class.): ut perhibetur iners, ars in quo non erit ulla, Lucil.…

ĭnersĭtūdo.opening: iners , for inertia, inactivity , idleness , Gloss. Philox.

ĭnertĭa.opening: id. , want of art or skill , unskilfulness , ignorance. Lit. (rare but class.): animi (spectantur), quemadmodum affecti sint, virtutibus, vitiis; artibus, inertiis, Cic. Part. 10, 35 ; Petr. 135, 6 . — Transf. , in…

ĭnertĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], inactive , that produces no effect; a term applied to a sort of grape that yields a good but not intoxicating wine, Col. 3, 2, 24 ; Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 31 .

ĭn-ērŭdītĭo.opening: want of learning , Vulg. Eccl. 4, 30 ; cf.: ineruditio ἀπαιδευσία, Gloss. Philox.

ĭn-ērŭdītus.opening: adj. , uninstructed , unlearned , illiterate , ignorant , awkward (class.): non ergo Epicurus ineruditus, sed ii indocti, qui, etc., Cic. Fin. 1, 21, 72 : ne quis illud tam ineruditum absurdumque respondeat, id. Ac. 2,…

ĭnērumpĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-erumpo , not to be torn (late Lat.): tunica Christi, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 14 .

ĭnescātĭo.opening: inesco , an alluring , a satiating , Aug.

ĭn-esco.opening: v. a. To allure with bait , to entice (syn.: prolecto, illicio; mostly post- Aug.). Lit. : sicut muta animalia cibo inescantur, Petr. 140 ; cf.: velut inescatam temeritatem ferocioris consulis, Liv. 22, 41, 5 .— Trop. ,…

ĭn-ēvectus.opening: adj. in-evehi , borne or mounted upon ( poet. ): ne quisquam ... Iret inevectus caelum super, Verg. Cul. 339 : tendit inevectus radios Hyperionis ardor, id. ib. 100 .

ĭn-ēvītābĭlis.opening: adj. , unavoidable , inevitable (post-Aug.): fulmen, Ov. M. 3, 301 : mala, Sen. Q. N. 2, 50 : fatum, Curt. 4, 6, 11 ; cf.: sors fati, id. 10, 1, 14 : crimen, Tac. A. 1, 74 .— Plur. subst. : , Sen. Ep. 30, 6 .— Adv. : ,…

ĭn-ēvŏlūtus.opening: adj. , not rolled out , unopened , of book-rolls: liber, Mart. 11, 1, 4 .

ĭn-ēvulsĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-evulsus , that cannot be torn away , inseparable (eccl. Lat.): membrum Ecclesiae, Aug. contra Don. 3, 10.

ĭn-exāmĭnātus.opening: adj. , unexamined (post-class.): mulieres, Mart. Cap. 9, § 895 ; Firm. 1, 2.

ĭn-excĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. , from which one cannot be aroused : somnus, Sen. Ep. 83, 13 .

ĭn-excītus.opening: adj. , unmoved , quiet , calm : Ausonia atque immobilis ante, Verg. A. 7, 623 .

ĭn-excoctus.opening: adj. , unexhausted (late Lat.): glaeba, Sid. Carm. 7, 380 .

ĭn-excōgĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-excogito , inconceivable , incomprehensible (eccl. Lat.), Lact. Inst. 1, 8 ; Tert. adv. Val. 37 .

ĭn-excōgĭtātus.opening: adj. , not thought of , not found out , not invented (postAug.): remedium, Plin. 36, 15, 24, § 107 (but not in Suet. Dom. 14 , where the correct read. is excogitatus).

ĭn-excultus.opening: adj. , unadorned; with rudes villae, Gell. 13, 23, 1 .

ĭn-excūsābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be excused , inexcusable ( poet. and post-class.): ne te retrahas, et inexcusabilis absis, Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 58 : tempus, Ov. M. 7, 511 : onera, that cannot be refused, Dig. 5, 1, 50 : necessitas, Cod.…

ĭn-excūsātus.opening: adj. , not excused , Ambros. de Jac. et Vit. Beat. 2, 2, 1 init.

ĭnexcussus.opening: adj. 2. in-excutio , unshaken , not terrified , Verg. Cul. 302 .

ĭn-exercĭtātus.opening: adj. Untrained , unexercised , unpractised , unskilful (class.): rudis et inexercitatus miles, Cic. Tusc. 2, 16, 38 ; so, miles, Front. Strat. 2, 1, 9 : homo non hebes, neque inexercitatus, Cic. de Or. 2, 17, 72 :…

ĭn-exercĭtus.opening: adj. , unemployed , for inexercitatus (post-class.), Macr. S. 7, 8, 1 .

ĭn-exhaustus.opening: adj. , unexhausted ( poet. and post-Aug.): metalla, Verg. A. 10, 174 : urbes, not plundered, Sil. 14, 686 : pubertas, not enfeebled, Tac. G. 20 ; id. H. 5, 7 (but not in Cic. Fin. 3, 2, 7 ; v. Madv. ad h. l.).

ĭn-exoptābĭlis.opening: adj. , not desirable , Not. Tir. p. 106 .

ĭn-exōrābĭlis.opening: adj. That cannot be moved by entreaty , inexorable (class.). Of persons, constr. with in , adversus , contra , or dat. With in and acc. : qui inexorabilis in ceteros esse visus sum, Cic. Sull. 31, 87 .— With adversus :…

ĭn-exōrātus.opening: adj. , not entreated , not prayed for , unasked (post-class.): beneficia praebere, Arn. 3, 114 .

ĭn-exortus.opening: adj. , that has not originated , without a beginning , = ἄναρκτον, Gloss.

ĭn-expĕdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-expedio , unavoidable , inevitable (late Lat.): morae, Amm. 31, 13, 15 .

ĭn-expĕdītus.opening: adj. , not free. Entangled , confused : sicut pugna inexpeditior in angustiis, ita caedes atrocior fuit, Liv. 24, 16, 3 (al. impeditior).— Not ready , not quick at any thing (postclass.). Of persons: in rebus obeundis,…

ĭn-experrectus.opening: adj. , unawakened : sopitus vinis et inexperrectus, Ov. M. 12, 317 .

ĭn-expers.opening: adj. , unacquainted with , having no share in; with gen. : Bacchi, Avien. Descr. Orb. 920 : famae, id. ib. 1391 .

ĭn-expertus.opening: adj. , untried (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Act. , that has not made trial of , unacquainted with , inexperienced in , unaccustomed to a thing: qui lascivia inexperti advenerant, Tac. A. 16, 5 : exercitus bonis inexpertus…

ĭn-expĭābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-expio , that cannot be atoned for , inexpiable (class.): religio, Cic. Tusc. 1, 12, 27 : scelus, Auct. Har. Resp. 27.— Transf. , implacable , irreconcilable , obstinate : bellum, Liv. 4, 35, 8 ; 41, 24, 7 ;…

ĭn-expĭātus.opening: adj. , not atoned for , unexpiated (late Lat.): dedecus, Aug. Ep. ad Dioscor. 56 .

ĭn-explācābĭlis.opening: adj. , implacable , irreconcilable : explacabilis, inexplacabilis, Not. Tir. p. 106 .

ĭn-explānātus.opening: adj. , indistinct , inarticulate (post-Aug.): linguae esse, to speak indistinctly, Plin. 11, 37, 65, § 174 .

ĭn-explēbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-expleo , that cannot be filled , insatiable (class.). Lit. : inexplebilis potu, Plin. 11, 25, 30, § 88 . stomachus, Sen. Ep. 89 fin. ; cf.: populi fauces, Cic. Rep. 1, 43, 66 .— Trop. : cupiditas, Cic. Tusc.…

ĭn-explētus.opening: adj. , not filled , unsatisfied , unsated ( poet. ). Lit. : alvus, Stat. Th. 2, 518 .— Transf. : lumen, Ov. M. 3, 439 .— Trop. : questus, Stat. S. 3, 3, 8 : amor, id. Th. 6, 703 : caedes, id. ib. 667 ; Hier. in Isai.…

ĭn-explĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be unfolded or loosened , inextricable , intricate (class. only in the trop. signif.). Lit. : vinculum, Curt. 3, 1, 13 : error viarum, Plin. 36, 13, 19, § 87 : laquei, Quint. 5, 10, 101 .— Transf. :…

ĭn-explĭcĭtus.opening: adj. Not to be unfolded or traced : (anguis) tractus, Prud. Cath. 3, 153 .— Unexplained , inexplicit , obscure ( poet. ): dicta, Stat. Th. 2, 510 : Platones, Mart. 9, 48, 1 .

ĭn-explōrātus.opening: adj. , unexplored , not examined , unknown (not in Cic. or Cæs.): vada, Liv. 26, 48, 4 ; 39, 51, 6 ; 43, 4, 6 : inventio mihi, Plin. 35, 6, 25, § 43 .— Advv. , without examining beforehand : non temere, nec inexplorate,…

ĭn-expugnābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be taken by assault , impregnable , inexpugnable (class.) Lit. : arx, Liv. 2, 7, 6 : urbes, id. 5, 6, 9 ; Vell. 2, 115, 3 .— Trop. , unconquerable , in assured safety : homo, Cic. Tusc. 5, 14, 41 :…

ĭn-expugnātus.opening: adj. , unconquered (late Lat.), in a trop. sense: voluntas, Paul. Nol. Ep. ad Vitric. 18, 5 .

ĭn-expŭtābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-exputo , incalculable , incomputable : numerus, Col. 9, 4, 6 .

ĭn-exsecrābĭlis.opening: adj. , not execrable , not accursed , Not. Tir. p. 152 .

ĭn-exsĕcūtĭo.opening: pursuit , prosecution : inefficax, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 2, 34 .

ĭn-exsŏlūbĭlis.opening: adj. in-exsolvo , indestructible , Ambros. Ep. 9, 70 al.

ĭn-exspectātus.opening: ( ), , adj. , unexpected (class.). Of persons: in armis Hostis adest, Ov. M. 12, 65 .— Of inanim. and abstr. things: quanta vis! quam inexspectata! Cic. Or. 2, 55, 225 : nihil insolitum, nihil inexspectatum est, Sen.…

ĭn-exquīsītus.opening: adj. , not to be inquired into , unsearchable (eccl. Lat.): judicia Dei, Hilar. in Psa. 118, 12, 14.

ĭn-exstinctus.opening: ( ), , adj. , unextinguished , unextinguishable (Ovidian). Lit. : ignis, Ov. F. 6, 297 .— Trop. : fames, unappeasable, Ov. Ib. 6, 428 : nomen, imperishable, id. Tr. 5, 14, 36 : libido, insatiable, id. F. 1, 413 .

ĭn-exstinguĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. , unextinguishable (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : flamma, Lact. 7, 19 : ignis, Vulg. Matt. 3, 12 ; ib. Marc. 9, 42 .— Trop. : mala consuetudo, indelible , Varr. ap. Non. 131, 6 .

ĭn-exstirpābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-exstirpo , that cannot be rooted out : radices, Plin. 15, 20, 22, § 84 .

ĭn-exsŭpĕrābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. , that cannot be crossed or passed over , insurmountable (a favorite word with Livy). Lit. : Alpes, Liv. 5, 34, 6 : ripa, id. 44, 35, 8 : serrae, id. 21, 30, 7 : manu, Vell. 2, 32, 4 ; cf. id. 2, 120, 2 .—…

ĭn-extermĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-extermino , that cannot be exterminated , immortal (post-class.): homo, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 10 .

ĭn-extrīcābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-extrico , that cannot be disengaged or disentangled , inextricable ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : error (of the mazes of the labyrinth, from which one could not find his way out), Verg. A. 6, 27 : cortex,…

ĭn-hăbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be managed , unmanageable , unwieldy. Lit. : navis inhabilis prope magnitudinis, Liv. 33, 30, 5 : telum inhabile ad remittendum imperitis, id. 24, 34, 5 ; cf.: telum pondere, Curt. 8, 9 med. :…

ĭn-hăbĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. , uninhabitable : regiones, Cic. N. D. 1, 10, 24 : Indi ostia inhabitabilia, Mela, 3, 7 fin. ; Plin. 6, 17, 20, § 53 .

ĭnhăbĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. inhabito , inhabitable : per inhabitabiles oras terrae, Arn. 1, 3 .

ĭnhăbĭtācŭlum.opening: id. , a dwelling-place : inhabitat inhabitaculum, Not. Tir. p. 11 .

ĭnhăbĭtātĭo.opening: id. , a dwelling , habitation (late Lat.), Tert. ad Marc. 3, 24 ; id. ex Gen. 27, 40.

ĭnhăbĭtātor.opening: id. , a dweller , inhabitant (post-class.): aedium, Dig. 9, 3, 5 ; Hier. ad Helv. 1 .

ĭn-hăbĭto.opening: v. a. , to dwell in , to inhabit (post-Aug. for habito, incolo). Lit. : inhabitatur illa regio, Plin. 6, 17, 20, § 53 ; Sen. Ep. 102, 27 : Dorienses oceani locos inhabitasse confines, Amm. 15, 9, 3 : nobile solum, Petr.…

ĭn-haerĕo.opening: v. n. , to stick in , to stick , hang , or cleave to , to adhere to , inhere in. Lit. With abl. : sidera suis sedibus inhaerent, Cic. Univ. 10 : animi, qui corporibus non inhaerent, id. Div. 1, 50, 114 : visceribus, id.…

ĭnhaeresco.opening: v. inch. n. [inhaereo], to stick fast , cleave , adhere to. Lit. : in sordibus aurium, tamquam in visco, Cic. N. D. 2, 57, 144 : ne quid emineret ubi ignis hostium inhaeresceret, Caes. B. C. 2, 9 : sucus villis, Plin.…

ĭnhaesĭo.opening: id. , a hanging or adhering to , Aug. Conf.

ĭnhālātus.opening: inhalo , a breathing at , breath : oris, App. M. 2, 119, 15 .

ĭn-hālo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ĭn-hālo.opening: v. n. and a. , to breathe at or upon : cerae, Lact. Ira D. 10 , 20: alicui popinam, the smell of food that has been eaten, Cic. Pis. 6, 13 . — To breathe the odor of something: inhalantes horti floribus, Ambros. Hexaëm.…

ĭn-hāmo.opening: v. a. hamus , to fasten by a hook. —Hence, transf., to entangle (late Lat.): linguam, Sid. Ep. 9, 9 med.

ĭn-hērēdĭto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to appoint an heir (late Lat.), Vulg. 4 Esdr. 7, 67.

ĭnhērēdo.opening: ( ), , v. a. heres , to appoint as an heir (late Lat.), Salv. contra Avar. 2, p. 384.

ĭnhĭanter.opening: adv. inhio , with open mouth , eagerly (late Lat.): aliquid inhianter haurire, Aug. Conf. 9, 8 : ardescere, id. ep. 112, 8.

ĭnhĭātĭo.opening: id. , an opening of the mouth , gaping , e. g. in astonishment (late Lat.), Treb. Poll. Gall. 9.

ĭn-hĭbĕo.opening: v. a. in-habeo , to lay hold of a thing, in order to keep it back or to put it forward. To keep back , restrain , curb , check. Lit. : tela, Verg. A. 12, 693 ; Liv. 30, 10, 15 : crudelissimas manus, Petr. 105 : frenos,…

ĭnhĭbĭtĭo.opening: inhibeo , a restraining : remigum, a rowing backwards : inhibitio autem remigum motum habet, et vehementiorem quidem remigationis navem convertentis ad puppim, Cic. Att. 13, 21, 3 ; v. inhibeo, I. A.

ĭn-hinnĭo.opening: v. n. , to neigh at (late Lat.): puellis, Prud. ap. Symm. 1, 57 .

ĭn-hĭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ĭn-hĭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to stand open , to gape. In gen. Lit. : ora inhiasse luporum, Stat. Th. 1, 626 .— Trop. , to gape with amazement, etc.: inhians Cerberus, Verg. G. 4, 483 : attonitis inhians animis, id. A. 7, 814 .— In…

ĭnhŏnestāmentum.opening: inhonesto , dishonor , disgrace , shame (ante- and postclass.): pueritia tua adulescentiae tuae inhonestamentum fuit, Gracch. ap. Isid. Orig. 2, 21 ; App. Mag. p. 275, 13 .

ĭn-hŏnestas.opening: inhonestus , dishonor , disgrace (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 5 fin. ; id. adv. Jud. 14 .

ĭnhŏnesto.opening: v. a. inhonestus , to dishonor , disgrace : palmas adeptas, Ov. Tr. 4, 8, 19 .

ĭn-hŏnestus.opening: adj. Dishonorable , disgraceful , shameful (class.): eho, impure, inhoneste, labes popli! Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 4 : simus, Cic. Rosc. Am. 18 : ignotā matre inhonestus, Hor. S. 1, 6, 36 : vita, Sall. C. 20, 9 : exitus nobis…

ĭn-hŏnōrābĭlis.opening: adj. , unhonored (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 17 .

ĭnhŏnōrātĭo.opening: inhonoro , a dishonoring , Vulg. Sap. 1, 38 ; Hilar. Trin. 4, 41.

ĭn-hŏnōrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. , not honorable , dishonorable : factum dictumque, Sen. Const. Sap. 10, 1 .

ĭnhŏnōris.opening: adj. 2. in-honorus , unhonored , without honor : ipse quoque non inhonoris hoc labore, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 35 Mai.

ĭn-hŏnōro.opening: v. a. inhonorus , to dishonor , Tert. Res. Carn. 10 ; id. Fug. in Persec. 5 .— Hence, , , P. a. Unhonored , disregarded : vita inhonorata et ingloria, Cic. Tusc. 3, 34, 81 : inhonoratior triumphus, Liv. 33, 23, 8 :…

ĭn-hŏnōrus.opening: adj. , without honor , not respected or esteemed , of no account , inconsiderable : civitates, Plin. 5, 30, 33, § 126 : pomum, id. 15, 24, 28, § 99 : Hercules, to whom no divine honors are paid, id. 36, 5, 5, § 39 :…

ĭn-horrĕo.opening: v. n. , to stand on end , stand erect , bristle. Lit. : haud secus quam vallo saepta inhorreret acies, Liv. 8, 8, 10 : spicea jam campis cum messis inhorruit, Verg. G. 1, 314 : aper pilis inhorrentibus corio squalidus,…

ĭn-horresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to send forth sharp points , to rise erect , to bristle up. Lit. : gallinae inhorrescunt edito ovo excutiuntque sese, Plin. 10, 41, 57, § 116 : inhorrescit mare, Pac. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 14, 24 (Trag. Rel. v.…

ĭn-hortor.opening: v. dep. , to incite , instigate to a thing: alicui canes, to set on, App. M. 8, p. 209, 9 .— Hence, , , with pass. signif. , instigated , set on : canes in eorum exitium inhortati, App. M. 9, p. 234, 15 .

ĭn-hospĭtālis.opening: adj. , inhospitable. Lit. : Caucasus, Hor. C. 1, 22, 6 : litus, Plin. Pan. 34 ext. : regnum, Sen. Troad. 215 . — Transf. : Pontus Euxinus antea ab inhospitali feritate Axenos appellatus, Plin. H. N. 6 praef. § 1.—Of a…

ĭnhospĭtālĭtas.opening: inhospitalis , inhospitality : ut inhospitalitas sit opinio vehemens, valde fugiendum esse hospitem, Cic. Tusc. 4, 11, 27 .

ĭn-hospĭtus.opening: adj. , inhospitable. Adj. : tecta, Ov. M. 15, 15 : Syrtis, Verg. A. 4, 41 : saxa, id. ib. 5, 627 : deserta et inhospita tesqua, Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 19 : terra Baccho, i.e. not bearing the vine, Sil. 1, 237 . — Subst. : , ,…

ĭnhostus.opening: , false read. in Tac. for inhonestus, v. Orell. ad Tac. H. 2, 31 .

ĭnhūmānātĭo.opening: a being made man , incarnation : unigeniti Dei Filii, Cod. Just. 1, 1, 5 and 6 fin.

ĭnhūmānātŭs.opening: in-humanus , made man , incarnate : Jesus Christus, Cod. Just. 1, 1, 6 : Christus, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 10, 10 .

ĭnhūmānĭtas.opening: inhumanus , inhumanity. Inhuman conduct , savageness , barbarity : crudelitas inhumanitasque, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 44, § 115 ; id. Deiot. 12, 32 . — Want of good breeding. Incivility , impoliteness : quod ego non superbia…

ĭn-hūmānus.opening: adj. , not suitable to the human condition , that does not befit a human being. Inhuman. Rude , savage , barbarous : quis tam fuit durus et ferreus, quis tam inhumanus, qui non illorum miseria commoveretur, Cic. Verr.…

ĭnhŭmātus.opening: adj. 2. in-humo , not inhumed , unburied : ossuum inhumatūm aestuosam aulam, Pac. ap. Prisc. p. 710 P. (Trag. Rel. v. 102 Rib.): is cum esset projectus inhumatus, Cic. Div. 2, 69, 143 : corpora, Verg. A. 11, 22 : funus,…

ĭn-hūmectus.opening: adj. , not moist : corpus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 207 .

ĭn-hūmĭgo.opening: v. a. , to moisten , wet : campum totum, Liv. Andron. ap. Non. 62, 22 (Trag. Rel. p. 2 Rib.).

ĭn-hŭmo.opening: v. a. , to bury in the ground , cover with earth , inhume : taleas, Plin. 17, 18, 30, § 130 .

ĭn-ĭbi.opening: adv. , therein , there. Lit. , of place, in that place , there : superbia nata inibi (Capuae) esse videtur, Cic. Agr. 1, 7, 20 : marsupium habeat, inibi paulum praesidii, in that matter, Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 45 ; Cato, R.…

ĭn-ĭdōnĕē.opening: , false read. in App. for idonee.

ĭnĭgo.opening: v. a. in-ago . To drive into or to a place, to drive : grege jumentorum inacto, Varr. R. R. 1, 52, 2 : in stabula, id. ib. 2, 2, 15 : equum in oves, Fronto ad M. Caes. 2 , ep. 15 Mai.: feras ad nocendum, Sen. Ep. 103, 2…

ĭnĭmīcālis.opening: adj. inimicus , inimical , hostile (late Lat.): stimuli, Sid. Ep. 1, 3 .

ĭnĭmīcĭtĭa.opening: inimicus , enmity , hostility , usu. in plur. : capere inimicitias in aliquem, Ter. Phorm. 2, 3, 23 : suscipere, Cic. Fam. 2, 18, 2 : intercedunt mihi inimicitiae cum aliquo, id. Cael. 13, 32 : erant ei veteres…

ĭnĭmīco.opening: v. a. inimicus , to make enemies , to set at variance ( poet. and rare): miseras inimicat urbes, Hor. C. 4, 15, 20 : hostiles inimicant classica turmas, urge on to fight, Stat. Th. 2, 419 : pectora, Aus. Ep. 24, 63 ;…

ĭnĭmīcus.opening: ( gen. plur. : , Plaut. As. 2, 2, 14 ), adj. 2. in-amicus , unfriendly , hostile , inimical. Adj. Of persons: quod eos infenso animo atque inimico venisse dicatis, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 61, § 149 ; id. Phil. 10, 10, 21 ;…

ĭn-ĭmĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be imilated , inimitable (post-Aug.): auctoritas, Quint. 8, 3, 25 : mellis inimitabilis humanae rationi sapor, id. 1, 10, 7 : dulcedo morum, Vell. 2, 97 .

ĭn-ĭnĭtĭātus.opening: adj. , not begun : ininitiato substantiarum cardine (al. in initiato), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 23 .

ĭn-intellĭgĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , unintelligible , incomprehensible : dei splendor, Ambros. Off. 1, 14 .

ĭn-interprĕtābĭlis.opening: adj. , inexplicable : nomen, Tert. adv. Val. 14 : sermo, Vulg. Heb. 5, 71 .

ĭn-interprĕtātus.opening: adj. , uninterpreted , unexplained : ininterpretatum (al. non interpretatum), Hier. Ep. 29, 4 .

ĭn-inventĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-invenio , not to be found out , inscrutable , Tert. adv. Herm. 45 .

ĭn-invĭcem.opening: adv. , not by turns , continually , Not. Tir. p. 84 .

ĭnīquĭtas.opening: ( gen. plur. iniquitatium, Tert. Spect. 2 ), iniquus , unequalness. Lit. Unevenness , of the ground: loci, Caes. B. G. 7, 45 : in talibus iniquitatibus locorum, Liv. 38, 22, 3 .— Inequality , of weight: ponderis, App.…

ĭnīquo.opening: v. a. id. , to render unfavorable : aequum animum alicui, Laber. ap. Non. 126, 31 (Com. Fragm. v. 65 Rib.).

ĭnīquus.opening: adj. 2. in-aequus , unequal. Lit. Uneven , not level , steep : puppis, inflicta vadis, dorso dum pendet iniquo, Verg. A. 10, 303 : juga montis iniqui, Ov. M. 10, 172 .— Not of the right measure , too great or too small…

ĭnĭtālĭa.opening: plur. [initium], opening or initial ceremonies : initalia Cereris adiit (al. initialia and inter alia Cereris templum), Capit. Marc. Aur. 27.

ĭnĭtĭālis.opening: adj. id. , initial , incipient , original (post-class.). Adj. : elementorum origo initialis, App. M. 4, p. 156, 9 : saeculorum progenies, id. ib. 11 , p. 259: controversiae status, Aggen. ap. Front. de Limit. p. 63…

ĭnĭtĭāmenta.opening: plur. [inito], an initiation into secret rites; trop.: sapientiae, Sen. Ep. 90, 29 .

ĭnĭtĭātĭo.opening: id. , a participation in secret religious rites: Eleusiniorum sacrorum, Suet. Ner. 34 .

ĭnĭtĭātor.opening: id. , an originator , founder (late Lat.): novi testamenti, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 14 .

ĭnĭtĭātrix.opening: initiator , she who originates , a foundress (late Lat.): litteraturae, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 7 med. : virtutum omnium, Salv. de Avarit. 4 post med. p. 165 Rittersh.

ĭnĭtĭo.opening: v. a. initium . To begin , originate (only late Lat.): ver tunc initiatur, Firm. 2, 12: brassicam seremus vel irriguo loco, vel pluviā initiante madefacto, when the rainy season begins (which begins again after the…

ĭnĭtĭum.opening: ineo , a going in , en trance. A beginning , commencement (syn.: principium, exordium). Lit. : bonis initiis orsus tribunatus, tristes exitus habuit consulatus, id. Brut. 34, 128 : initio accusationis, id. de Or. 1, 26,…

ĭnĭto.opening: v. freq. [ineo], to go into , to enter : loca horrida initas, Pac. ap. Diom. 336 P. (Trag. Rel. v. 1 Rib.); cf. inito, ἐμβατεύω, Gloss. Philox.

ĭnĭtus.opening: ineo , a coming in , entrance. Lit. An approach , arrival , advent : volucres te, diva, tuumque Significant initum, Lucr. 1, 13 .— A beginning , commencement : movendi, Lucr. 1, 383 : motūs, id. 2, 269 .— Transf. ,…

ĭn-objurgātus.opening: adj. , not scolded , not blamed , Charis. p. 41 P.

ĭn-oblector.opening: v. dep. , to take delight in any thing (late Lat.): in filiis hominum, Tert. adv. Hermog. 18 .

ĭn-oblītĕrātus.opening: adj. , not obliterated , unforgotten : scientia, Tert. Anim. 24 .

ĭn-oblītus.opening: adj. , not forgetful , mindful , Ov. P. 4, 15, 37 .

ĭn-ŏboedĭentĭa.opening: disobedience (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 14, 17; Hier. Quaest. Hebr. ad Reg. 2, 1 .—In the form , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 17 fin.

ĭn-ŏboedĭo.opening: (or , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 16 ), , v. n. , to disobey , be disobedient , Ambros. Serm. Epiph. 1 . — Hence, , , P. a. , disobedient , Vulg. Interp. Deut. 8, 20 ; ib. Tit. 1, 10 . — Adv. : , disobediently , Aug. Civ. Dei ,…

ĭnŏboedus.opening: adj. inoboedio , disobedient : cessatio (al. in obeundo), Arn. 7, 248 .

ĭn-obsaeptus.opening: adj. in-obsaepio , not hedged up , not closed , open : foramina aurium, Lact. Opif. D. 8, 7 .

ĭn-obscūrābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be obscured (late Lat.): regula, Tert. Anim. 3 .

ĭn-obscūro.opening: , a false read. in Cic. Phil. 9, 5, 10 , instead of obscurabit.

ĭn-obsĕquens.opening: adj. , not yielding , uncomplying , disobedient , Sen. praef. Q. N. fin. : equi frenis, id. Hippol. 1068 .— Absol. : contumaces et inobsequentes, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 17 fin.

ĭn-obsĕquentĭa.opening: disobedience , Jul. Valer. Res Gest. Alex. M. 2, 21 Mai.

ĭn-observābĭlis.opening: , e. adj. , that cannot be observed , unobservable : cursus, Plin. 2, 17, 15, § 77 : error, Cat. 64, 115 .

ĭnobservantĭa.opening: inobservans , inattention , negligence , irregularity : quae ne fecisse inobservantia quadam videatur, Quint. 4, 2, 107 ; Suet. Aug. 76 .

ĭn-observātus.opening: adj. , unobserved , unperceived , Ov. M. 2, 544 ; 4, 341 : et incertum tempus, Sen. Q. N. 3, 26 med. : sidera, Ov. F. 3, 111 : columba, Mart. 8, 32, 3 .

ĭn-obsŏlētus.opening: adj. , not grown old : vestimenta, Tert. Res. Carn. 58 .

ĭn-occĭdŭus.opening: adj. , never setting. Lit. : axis, the north pole, Luc. 8, 175 .— Transf. : visus, ever open eyes, Stat. Th. 6, 277 : ignes, inextinguishable, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 400 : vita continua et inoccidua, Arn. 2, 68 .

ĭn-occo.opening: v. a. , to harrow in : semen inoccatum, Col. 2, 8, 4 ; 11, 2, 82 : pastinatio inoccata, id. 3, 15, 1 .

ĭn-occultus.opening: adj. , not secret , Quint. 7, 9, 5 dub. (al. incultus).

ĭnŏcŭlātĭo.opening: inoculo , an inoculating , ingrafting , Col. 5, 11, 1 ; 11, 2, 54 ; Pall. 7, 5 . (An earlier method of inoculating is described in Plin. 17, 14, 23, § 100 ; cf. id. 17, 16, 26, § 118 .)

ĭn-ŏcŭlo.opening: v. a. , to inoculate , i. e. to ingraft an eye or bud of one tree into another (post-Aug.). Lit. : arbores ficorum, Col. 11, 2, 59 .— Transf. To implant : justitiae affectum pectoribus, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 1 .— To…

ĭnŏdĭātus.opening: adj. 2. in-odium , not hated : odiosus, inodiatus, Not. Tir. p. 77 .

ĭn-ŏdōro.opening: v. a. , to scent , cause to smell : mandentium halitus, Col. 11, 3, 22 .

ĭn-ŏdōror.opening: , formerly regarded as v. dep. , to smell out , trace out : mirabiliter inodoratus est, Cic. Att. 2, 25, 1 , where Orell., B. and K., al. now read moratus.

ĭn-ŏdōrus.opening: adj. Without smell , inodorous : ossa, unperfumed, Pers. 6, 35 : flos, App. M. 4, p. 143, 16 .— Without the sense of smell : animalia, Gell. 7, 6 (also ap. Non. 129, 11 ).

ĭn-offensus.opening: adj. , not struck; without stumbling , without hinderance , unobstructed , uninjured ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : cogit inoffensae currus accedere metae, untouched, not grazed, Luc. 8, 201 : voluptatis…

ĭnoffĭcĭōsĭtas.opening: inofficiosus , disobligingness , Salv. Ep. 3 : Ruricius, Ep. 2, 15.

ĭn-offĭcĭōsus.opening: adj. , undutiful , inofficious. In gen. Not observant of his duty , undutiful : humana gens inofficiosa dei, Tert. Apol. 40 : libertus inofficiosus patrono, Dig. 37, 14, 1 .— Contrary to one ' s duty : testamentum, i.…

ĭn-ŏlens.opening: adj. , without smell , inodorous : olivum, Lucr. 2, 850 .

ĭn-ŏlesco.grammar: lēvi, ŏlĭtum, 3 v. n. and a.
ĭn-ŏlesco.opening: v. n. and a. (inolesti, Aus. Grat. Act. § 36). Neutr. , to grow in , on , or to any thing. Lit. : udo libro, Verg. G. 2, 77 : necesse est multa diu concreta modis inolescere miris, id. A. 6, 738 ; Sil. 8, 583 : tradux a…

ĭn-ōmĭnālis.opening: adj. , unlucky , illomened , inauspicious : dies, Gell. 5, 17, 3 ; Macr. S. 1, 16, § 26 .

ĭn-ōmĭnātus.opening: adj. , ill-omened , inauspicious : cubilia, Hor. Epod. 16, 38 .

ĭn-ŏpācus.opening: adj. , not shady : inopacus, ἄσκιος, Gloss. Philox.

ĭn-ŏpĕrātus.opening: adj. , unoccupied , inactive : bonitas, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 11 .— Not wrought , Ambros. de Fid. 3, 14, 113 .

ĭn-ŏpĕro.opening: v. a. , to effect , produce (eccl. Lat.): hoc inoperatur per Deum Patrem, Rufin. Orig. de Principp. 1, 3, 7 .

ĭn-ŏpĕror.opening: v. dep. , to effect , operate , produce (eccl. Lat.): ille inoperatus est in Christum valentiam suam, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 17 (ex adv. Ephes. 1).

ĭn-ŏpertus.opening: adj. , uncovered , bare. Lit. : corpora, Prud. Cath. 3, 117 : capite inoperto, Sen. Vit. Beat. 13 .— Trop. , naked : ac confessa veritas, Sen. Ot. Sap. 30 .

ĭn-ŏpĭa.opening: inops , want , lack , scarcity. In gen.: argenti, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 55 : summa rerum omnium, Caes. B. G. 5, 2 : frumenti commeatusque, id. ib. 3, 6 : frumenti, Sall. J. 91, 1 ; cf.: frumentaria, Caes. B. G. 5, 24 : et…

ĭn-ŏpīnābĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be supposed or expected , inconceivable : latebra, Gell. 17, 9, 18 : id (dictum), id. 11, 18, 11 : res, Aur. Vict. Caes. 39 .— Esp., rhet. t. t., surprising , paradoxical : infames materias, sive quis…

ĭn-ŏpīnans.opening: adj. , not expecting , unaware (freq. in the historians; not in Cic.): inscios inopinantesque Menapios oppresserunt, Caes. B. G. 4, 4 : impeditos et inopinantes aggressus, id. ib. 1, 12 : imprudente atque inopinante…

ĭn-ŏpīnātus.opening: not expected , unexpected (class.). Adj. : cum hoc illi improvisum atque inopinatum accidisset, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 28, § 69 : nova tibi haec sunt et inopinata? id. ib. 2, 2, 8 , § 24: neque novum neque inopinatum mihi…

ĭn-ŏpīnor.opening: v. dep. , to suppose , think , opine : Alexander facilius inopinatus, Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 52 Mai. (but a false read. for opinor, Gell. 18, 7, 5 ).

ĭn-ŏpīnus.opening: adj. , unexpected ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose = in-opinatus, insperatus): quies, Verg. A. 5, 857 : nova inopinave facies laborum, id. ib. 6, 104 : fors, id. ib. 8, 476 : visus, Ov. M. 4, 232 : siccitas, Plin. Pan.…

ĭnŏpĭōsus.opening: adj. inops , in want of something: res inopiosae consilii, Plaut. Poen. 1, 1, 2 .

ĭn-oppĭdātus.opening: adj. , that has no town , not dwelling in a town (late Lat.): Gabalitani sparsi, inoppidati, Sid. Ep. 5, 13 ; cf.: inoppidatus ἀοίκητος, Gloss. Philox.

ĭn-opportūnus.opening: unfitting (late Lat.), Oros. c. Pelag. p. 618 (also a false reading in two places for importunus, Cic. de Or. 2, 5, 20 ; 3, 5, 18 ). — Hence, , adv. , unsuitably , untimely , Aug. c. Faust. 22, 72.

ĭnops.opening: adj. 2. in-opis , without resources , helpless , weak (class.). In gen.: ab ope inops, qui ejus indiget, Varr. L. L. 5, § 92 Müll.: inopes relicti a duce, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 34 : nihil cum potentiore juris humani…

ĭn-optābĭlis.opening: adj. , undesirable , unpleasant : officinae disciplina, App. M. 9, p. 222, 24 .

ĭn-optātus.opening: adj. , undesired , unpleasant : res, Sen. Exc. Contr. 8, 6, § 5 .

ĭnōrābĭlis.opening: , Att. ap. Non. 487, 15 ; v. Att. Trag. Fragm. v. 158 Rib.

ĭn-ōrātus.opening: adj. , not pleaded : incertā re atque inoratā, i. e. without obtaining a hearing , Enn. ap. Non. 166, 23 (Trag. v. 12 Vahl.): legati Ameriam re inorata reverterunt, Cic. Rosc. Am. 9, 26 .

ĭnordĭnālĭter.opening: adv. 2. in-ordinalis , irregularly : scarificandum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 36 .

ĭn-ordĭnātĭo.opening: disorder , App. Trism. p. 92, 1 ; Cod. Just. 3, 43, 3 .

ĭn-ordĭnātus.opening: adj. , not arranged , disordered , irregular : inordinati et incompositi milites, Liv. 22, 50, 8 : hostes, id. 35, 29, 5 : inordinati in proelium ruunt, id. 23, 27, 5 : ordo, App. M. p. 292 Oud. — Sup. : inordinatissimi…

ĭn-ordĭno.opening: v. a. , to arrange , bring into order : inordinandi soli duo sunt tempora, Col. 11, 3, 9 dub. (al. ordinandi).

ĭn-ōris.opening: adj. ōs , without a mouth , Paul. ex Fest. p. 114 Müll. N. cr.

ĭnormis.opening: adj. 2. in-norma , immoderate , enormous , Spart. Anton. Get. 6, 2 ; Ael. Ver. 1, 3 acc. to Salmas (al. enormis).

ĭn-ornātus.opening: adj. , unadorned (syn. incomptus): mulieres, Cic. Or. 23, 78 ; cf. capilli, Ov. M. 1, 497 ; 5, 472 ; and, crines, id. ib. 9, 3 : Lysias tenuis atque inornatus, Cic. Or. 9, 29 ; so Quint. 4, 2, 46 ; 8, 3, 50 ; 59 al. :…

ĭn-orno.opening: v. a. , to adorn (late Lat.): flosculi inornantur, Tert. Anim. 19 ; id. adv. Val. 12 .

ĭn-ōro.opening: v. a. , to crown the brim of a drinking-vessel: calix de coronis quoque potatoris inorabitur (al. inornabitur), Tert. Res. Carn. 16 .

ĭnōrus.opening: adj. 2. in-os , without a mouth : ostreae, Turp. ap. Non. 216, 8 (Com. Rel. v. 23 Rib.; cf. Müll. ad Fest. p. 114 ).

ĭn-ōtĭōsus.opening: adj. , not idle , busy ( ἄσχολος ): actio, Quint. 11, 3, 183 .

ĭn-ūber.opening: adj. , not full , ill-fed , ill-conditioned , poor : ostreae, Gell. 20, 8, 3 .

ĭn-ūdo.opening: v. a. , to wet , moisten : manus labris, Paul. Nol. Carm. 18, 418 .

ĭnŭla.opening: ἑλένιον , elecampane , a plant (Inula helenium, Linn.), Plin. 19, 5, 29, § 91 ; Col. 11, 3, 35 ; Hor. S. 2, 2, 44 ; 2, 8, 51 .

ĭn-ulcĕro.opening: v. a. , to ulcerate , Veg. Vet. 2, 59 .

ĭnultē.opening: adv. , false read. for inulti, Curt. 4, 4, 9 ; v. Mütz. ad h. 1.

ĭn-ultus.opening: adj. For whom no revenge is taken , unavenged , unrevenged , not vindicated. Of persons: Marius ne inultus esset, Cic. Sest. 22, 50 : ne inultos imperatores suos jacere sinerent, Liv. 25, 37, 10 : moriemur inultae?…

ĭnumbrātĭo.opening: inumbro , an overshadowing , darkness , Mart. Cap. 1, § 79 .

ĭn-umbro.opening: v. a. , to cast a shadow upon , to shade (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn. opaco). Lit. : terraque inumbratur, Lucr. 5, 289 : toros obtentu frondis, Verg. A. 11, 66 : forum velis, Plin. 19, 1, 6, § 24 ; Curt.…

ĭn-unco.opening: v. a. 2. uncus , to hook , catch with hooks; to clutch , seize , grasp (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : aquila unguibus agnum, leporem, App. Flor. 2 , p. 349, 9; Ccl. 7, 3, 10.— Transf. : nummos, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 124,…

ĭnunctĭo.opening: inunguo , an anointing , besmearing with unguents; a spreading on , applying (post-Aug.): tridui, Plin. 23, 8, 29, § 117 : matutina, id. 28, 4, 7, § 37 : medicamentorum, Cels. 7, 7, 14 : suci plantaginis, Col. 6, 33, 2 .

ĭnundātĭo.opening: inundo , an overflowing , inundating , inundation (postAug.): fluminum, Col. 3, 11, 8 : coërcere, Suet. Aug. 30 : inundationes Tiberis, id. Oth. 8 : Nili, Plin. Pan. 30 fin. ; Cassiod. Var. 3, 42 : terrarum, the deluge,…

ĭn-undo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ĭn-undo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to overflow , inundate (class.). Lit. : terram inundet aqua, Cic. N. D. 1, 37, 103 : imbres campis inundantes, Liv. 8, 24 : Tiberis agros inundavit, id. 24, 9 ; 28, 28 ; 24, 38 : Ciliciam cruore…

ĭnungĭto.opening: v. a. freq. [inunguo], to besmear (ante-class.): capillum cinere, Cato ap. Charis. p. 78 P.

ĭn-unguo.opening: (not ), , v. a. , to anoint ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : oculos, Varr. L. L. 5, 8 : non tamen idcirco contemnas lippus inungui, Hor. Ep. 1, 1, 29 ; id. S. 1, 3, 25 ; Plin. 28, 9, 37, § 141 : inunguendum primo…

ĭn-ūnĭo.opening: v. a. , to unite , Tert. adv. Val. 29 .

ĭn-urbānus.opening: adj. , rustic , boorish , rude , unpolishcd , unmannerly (class.): habitus orationis non inurbanus, Cic. Brut. 63, 227 : non essem tam inurbanus ac paene inhumanus, id. de Or. 2, 90, 365 : gestus, Quint. 6, 3, 26 :…

ĭn-urgĕo.opening: v. a. , to push , thrust; to obtrude ( poet. and post-class.): vitulus cornibus, Lucr. 5, 1035 : susurros, to be always whispering, App. M. 8, p. 205, 6 .

ĭn-ūrīno.opening: v. n. , to plunge or dive under the water (post-Aug.): piscinis, Col. 8, 14, 2 .

ĭn-ūro.opening: v. a. , to burn in , to burn. Lit. : foramen, i. e. to make an uneven hole, such as is made by burning, Col. 4, 29, 16 .—Of encaustic painting: Nicias scripsit se inussisse, Plin. 35, 4, 10, § 27 : cerae tinguntur isdem…

ĭn-ūsĭtātus.opening: adj. , unusual , uncommon , extraordinary , very rare (class.): pro di immortales! speciem humanam inusitatam, Att. ap. Non. 226, 2 : nova et inusitata belli ratio, Caes. B. C. 3, 47 : magnitudo, Cic. Off. 3, 9, 38 :…

ĭn-usquĕ.opening: (separately, ), adv. for usque in, even unto , all the way to , as far as , into ( poet. ), Stat. Th. 1, 440 ; Avien. Per. 525 ; 641 .

ĭnustus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. inuro.

ĭn-ustus.opening: adj. uro , not burned , unconsumed : ossa inustis plena medullis, Luc. 8, 787 .

ĭn-ūsus.grammar: ūs, false reading for in usu

ĭn-ūtĭlis.opening: adj. , useless , unserviceable , unprofitable; constr. absol. , with ad , or with dat. (class.). In gen. Of persons. Absol. : homo iners atque inutilis, Cic. Off. 3, 6, 31 ; Verg. A. 2, 647 ; 10, 794 : dum meliorem ex…

ĭnūtĭlĭtas.opening: inutilis . Uselessness , unprofitableness , Lucr. 5, 1274 .— Hurtfulness , injuriousness , Cic. Inv. 2, 52, 158 : facti, id. ib. 2, 26, 77 .

ĭnŭus.opening: ineo; the fructifying god , the god Pan, who gave fruitfulness to the herds , Liv. 1, 5 ; Arn. 3, p. 143 ; Macr. S. 1, 22 . — , a sea-coast town in Latium , near Antium , Verg. A. 6, 775 ; cf. Serv. ad loc.

ĭn-uxōrus.opening: adj. 2. in-uxor , unmarried (late Lat.): virginitas, Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 9 .

ĭō.opening: interj. ἰώ , expressing joy, ho! huzza! hurra! io hymen hymenaee, io hymen, Plaut. Cas. 4, 3, 3 ; id. Ps. 2, 4, 11 : miles, io, magna voce, triumphe, canet, Tib. 2, 5, 121 (118): io triumphe! Hor. C. 4, 2, 49 : io, io,…

Ĭŏcasta.opening: ( ), , and , , , = Ἰοκάστη, the wife of Lāïus , and mother of Œdipus , whom she married unknowingly , and had by him Eteocles and Polynices. —Form Iocasta, Stat. Th. 1, 681 ; Hyg. Fab. 66 .—Form Iocaste, Hyg. Fab. 67 ;…

Ĭŏlāŭs.opening: , = Ἰόλαος, a son of Iphiclus , and constant companion of his uncle Hercules , Ov. M. 8, 310 ; 9, 399 ; 430 .

Ĭolcos.opening: or , , , = Ἰωλκός, a town and harbor of Thessaly , in Magnesia , on the Pelasgic Gulf , whence Jason is said to have sailed with the Argonauts , Liv. 44, 13, 4 ; Hor. Epod. 5, 21 ; Col. 10, 368 ; Mel. 2, 3, 4 ; Plin. 4,…

Ĭŏlē.opening: , = Ἰόλη. A daughter of Eurytus , king of Œchalia , whom Hercules , after killing Eurytus , married to his son Hyllus , Ov. M. 9, 140 ; 278 ; 394 ; Hyg. Fab. 35 .— The name of a female slave , Prop. 4 (5), 5, 35 .

ĭon.opening: ἴον . A kind of violet , Plin. 21, 11, 38, § 64 ; plur. : ia, id. 21, 6, 14, § 27 . — A precious stone of a violet color , Plin. 37, 10, 61, § 170 .

Ĭōnas.opening: (or , Vulg. Jon. 1, 1 al. ), , , = Ἰωνᾶς, the Hebrew prophet Jonah , Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 169 ; Sid. Carm. 16, 25 . — Deriv.: , , adj. , of or belonging to Jonah , Juvenc. 2, 711 .

Ĭōnes.opening: plur. , = Ἴωνες, the inhabitants of Ionia , the Ionians , Mel. 1, 17, 1 ; Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 113 ; Cic. Fl. 27 ; Nep. Milt. 4, 1 ; also applied to the Athenians, Isid. Orig. 9, 2, 77 .

ĭōnĭăcus.opening: adj. , = Ἰωνιακός, Ionian : puellae, Ov. H. 9, 13 ; id. A. A. 2, 219 .

Ĭōnĭcus.opening: adj. , = Ἰωνικός, of or belonging to Ionia , Ionic. In gen.: gens, Plin. 6, 2, 2, § 7 : attagen, Hor. Epod. 2, 54 ; Mart. 13, 61, 2 : motus, i. e. the Ionic dance, Hor. C. 3, 6, 21 .— Subst. , , , an Ionic dancer : qui…

Ĭōnis.opening: adj. f. , = Ἰωνίς, Ionian : Ionides insulae, Avien. Perieg. 722 .— Subst. , an Ionian woman , Sen. Troad. 362 .

Ĭos.opening: , = Ἴος, a small island of the Sporades , in the Ægean Sea , now Nio , Mel. 2, 7, 11 ; Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 69 .— , , , = Ἰῆται, the inhabitants of Ios, Varr. ap. Gell. 3, 11, 6 .

ĭōta.opening: indec. , = ἰῶτα, the name of the Greek ι, iota (in Gr. trisyl., in Lat. dissyl.): ut iota litteram tollas, Cic. de Or. 3, 12, 43 : unum de titulo tollere iota, Mart. 2, 93, 4 . — Sometimes (on account of littera) , , ,…

ĭōtăcismus.opening: , = ἰωτακισμός, iotacism , a too frequent repetition of the letter i , Mart. Cap. 5, § 514 ; or a doubling of its sound in pronunciation , Isid. Orig. 1, 31, 7 .

Ĭsăra.opening: a river of Gaul that falls into the Rhone , now Isère , Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 33 ; Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 15, 3 ; 10, 23, 3 ; Luc. 1, 399 .

Ĭsauri.opening: an Asiatic tribe between Pamphylia , Lycaonia , and Cilicia , Isaurians , Liv. Epit. 93 ; Mel. 1, 2 ; Amm. 14, 2, 1 ; also, of their country, Cic. Fam. 15, 2, 1 ; Flor. 3, 6 .— Hence, , , , the country of the Isauri ,…

ĭta.opening: adv. pronom. stem i-; cf. is; Sanscr. itthā; Zend, itha , in the manner specified, in this manner , in this wise , in such a way , so , thus. In gen. Referring to what precedes, as has been said , thus , so : des operam…

ĭtă-que.opening: conj. ( = et ita.) And so , and thus , and accordingly : ita dolui, itaque ego nunc doleo, Plaut. Truc. 2, 6, 45 : si cetera ita sunt ut vis, itaque ut esse ego illa existimo, Ter. Hec. 4, 2, 28 : cum quaestor in…

ĭtă-tĕnus.opening: adv. , so far , to such a degree (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 10 .

ĭtem.opening: adv. i- (cf. is) and -tam, acc. fem. corresponding to tum (is), -tud; cf. tam; Sanscr. ittham, so . Implying comparison, just so , in like manner , after the same manner , likewise , also (cf.: ita, pariter, eodem…

ĭter.opening: (archaic forms: nom. ĭtĭner, Enn. Pac. Att. Varr. ap. Non. 482, 20 ; Plaut. Merc. 5, 2, 72 ; Lucr. 6, 339 ; Mart. Cap. 9, § 897 .— Gen. iteris, Naev. ap. Prisc. p. 695 P.; id. ap. Non. 485, 3 ; Jul. Hyg. ap. Charis. p.…

ĭtĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. itero , that may be repeated (late Lat.): injuria, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 28 .

ĭtĕrātĭo.opening: id. , a repetition : ver borum, Cic. Or. 25, 85 ; esp., in rhet., itera tion , = ἐπαναφορά, Mart. Cap. 5, § 533 al. ; cf.: et reditus ad propositum, et iteratio (dictorum), id. de Or. 3, 53, § 203 : lectio non cruda,…

ĭtĕrātīvum.opening: , i. e. verbum frequentativum, Diom. pp. 335 and 336, and Charis. p. 226 P.

ĭterdūca.opening: iter-duco , she who guides on a journey , an epithet of Juno, as the goddess who guides the steps of the child into the world, and of the bride to her new home, Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 3; Mart. Cap. 2, § 149 .

ĭtĕro.opening: v. a. , to do a thing a second time , to repeat (syn.: duplico, repeto). In gen.: quae audistis, si eadem hic iterem, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 99 . — Also pleonastically: bis iterare, Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 154 ; and: iterum…

ĭtĕrum.opening: (collat. form † ĭtĕro, Inscr. ap. Fea Framm. di Fast. Cons. Tav. 10, n. 26), adv. acc. sing. n. of compar. form from pronom. stem i- of is; cf. Sanscr. itara, the other; Hibern. itir , again , a second time , once more…

Ĭthăca.opening: ( , , Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 41 ), , = Ἰθάκη, an island in the Ionian Sea , the kingdom of Ulysses , Mel. 2, 7, 10 ; Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 54 ; Cic. Off. 3, 26, 27 ; id. Leg. 2, 1, 3 ; id. de Or. 1, 44, 196 al. : effugimus…

Ĭthōmē.opening: , = Ἰθώμη, a city of Messenia , Plin. 4, 5, 7, § 15 ; Liv. 32, 13 ; Stat Th. 4, 179.

ĭtĭdem.opening: adv. ita; suffix -dem for diem; cf. pridem, etc. , in like manner , so , just , in the same way. As correl. (cf. item). With ut : itidem, uti catapultae solent, Plaut. Curc. 5, 3, 12 : ut filium bonum patri esse…

ĭtĭnĕrārĭus.opening: adj. iter , of or belonging to a journey or march , itinerary (late Lat.): sumptus, Lampr. Commod. 9 : motus, the motion of travelling, Amm. 21, 15, 2 .—Hence, Subst. : , , An account of a journey , an itinerary , Veg.…

ĭtĭnĕrātor.opening: a traveller (late Lat.), Ven. Fort. Mauril. 24.

ĭtĭnĕror.opening: v. n. iter , = ὁδοιπορέω, to travel , Gloss. Lab.—Hence, part. as subst. : , , a traveller (late Lat.), Ambros. in Psa. 1, § 25 : Salv. de Gub. Dei, 1, p. 33.

ĭtĭo.opening: eo , a going , walking , travelling : itiones crebrae, Ter. Phorm. 5, 8, 23 : de obviam itione ita faciam, ut suades, Cic. Att. 11, 16, 1 : quaeris quod cogitem de obviam itione, id. ib. 13, 50, 4 : reditum ac domum…

ĭtĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [ito], to go : exsequias ititant, Naev. ap. Calp. Pis., acc. to Merul. Fragm. Enn. p. 417 .

ĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [eo], to go : ad legionem cum itant. Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 48 : ad cenas itare, Cic. Fam. 9, 24, 2 : pedibus itavisse in curiam, Gell. 3, 18, 4 ; Plin. 9, 8, 8, § 24 ; Edict. ap. Suet. Rhet. 1 .

Ĭtōnē.opening: ( ), , , and , , , a city and mountain in Bœotia (or Thessaly ), with a temple of Pallas , Stat. Th. 2, 720 ; Cat. 64, 228 .— Hence, † (an error for ), , Paul. ex Fest. p. 105 Müll.— ( ), , , the inhabilants of Itone ,…

Ĭtūraea.opening: ( ), , A district of Cœlesyria , the inhabitants of which were celebrated as archers , now El-Jeidoor , Vulg. Luc. 3, 1 .— Deriv. ( ), , adj. , of or belonging to Ituræa , Ituræan : arcus, Verg. G. 2, 448 : sagittae,…

ĭtus.opening: eo , a going , gait. In gen.: nec repentis itum cujusviscumque animantis Sentimus, Lucr. 3, 388 : itum, gestum, amictum qui videbant ejus, Titin. ap. Non. 123, 10 .— In partic. A going away , departure : noster itus,…

Ĭtўlus.opening: , = Ἴτυλος, the son of Ze thus , Cat. 65, 13 (where Itylus is confounded with Itys).

Ĭtys.opening: , = Ἴτυς. Son of Tereus and Progne; he was killed by his mother and served up to his father for food; whereupon he was changed into a pheasant , Progne into a swallow , and Tereus into an owl , Ov. M. 6, 652 sq. — A…

ĭūlis.opening: , = ἰουλίς, a kind of rockfish , Plin. 32, 9, 31, § 94 .

ĭūlus.opening: , = ἴουλος, the down or woolly part of many plants, a catkin , Plin. 16, 29, 52, § 120 .

ĭynx.opening: , = ἴυγξ, the wryneck , a bird made use of in conjurations and charms, with which it was thought that slighted lovers could procure a return of affection, Plin. 11, 47, 107, § 256 ; Laev. ap. App. Mag. p. 294 .

ō.opening: (long also before an initial vowel: o ego, Ov. M. 8, 51 ; Hor. A. P. 301 ; but also short: ŏ Alexi, Verg. E. 2, 65 ), interj. The commonest exclamation of joy, astonishment, desire, grief, indignation, etc.; O! Oh!…

Ōărĭon.opening: , = Ὠαρίων , a poet. collat. form for Orion, Cat. 66, 94 .

ōbex.opening: (objĭcis), and (of either gender indifferently; very rare in nom. sing.; acc. not found, v. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 489) [obicio, that which is cast or placed before; hence], a bolt, bar; a barrier, wall (mostly poet. and…

ōbĭcĭo.opening: and , (cf. abicio, etc.; perf. subj. objexim, Plaut. Poen. 1, 3, 37 : objexis, id. Cas. 2, 6, 52 ), v. a. ob-jacio , to throw or put before or towards, to throw to, to hold before or out, to offer, present, expose;…

Ōcĕănĕŏlus.opening: the name of a Roman gens, Inscr. Grut. 882, 10 .

Ōcĕănus.opening: (rarely , , ), = Ὠκεανός , the great sea that encompasses the land , the ocean : omnis terra parva quaedam insula est, circumfusa illo mari, quod Atlanticum, quod magnum, quem Oceanum appellatis in terris, Cic. Rep. 6,…

Ōcēlis.opening: , = Ὤκηλις , a city on the Arabian Gulf , Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 104 .

Ōcĕlum.opening: , = Ὤκελον , a city in Gallia Cisalpina , now perh. Usselio , Caes. B. G. 1, 10 .

ōchra.opening: , = ὤχρα , ochre , yellow ochre , a kind of earth that yields a yellow color, Plin. 35, 6, 12, § 30 ; Cels. 5, 18, 19 ; Vitr. 7, 7 .

Ōchus.opening: , = Ὦχος . A river in Bactriana , that empties into the Oxus , Plin. 6, 16, 18, § 49 ; Curt. 7, 10, 15 ; Amm. 23, 6, 57 .— A surname of Artaxerxes III. , king of Persia , Curt. 10, 5, 23 .— Son of Darius Codomannus ,…

ōcĭmŏīdes.opening: adj. , = ὠκιμοειδές , ocimum-like , of the ocimum kind : carduum silvaticum alii ocimoides vocant, App. Herb. 109 .

ōcĭnum.opening: (also , , and ), , , = ὤκινον , an herb which serves for fodder , perh. a sort of clover , Cato, R. R. 54 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 31 ; Plin. 17, 22, 35, § 198 ; 18, 16, 42, § 143 .

ōcĭor.opening: ( sup. ocissimus), adj. comp. [kindr. with Gr. ὠκύς , Sanscr. ācu, from the root ac, sharp; cf.: acer, acutus, ἀκωκή ], swifter , fleeter ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : et ventis, et fulminis ocior alis, Verg.…
