ō^crĕa.opening: ὄκρις, a prominence , x greave or leggin (made of mixed metal, and used to protect the legs of foot-soldiers, and also of hunters and country people; it was sometimes worn only on one leg): ocrea, quod opponebatur ob…

ō^crĕātus.opening: adj. 1. ocrea , greaved : in nive Lucanā dormis ocreatus, Hor. S. 2, 3, 234 : crura, Plin. 19, 2, 7, § 27 .

Ōcўălē.opening: one of the Amazons , Hyg. Fab. 163 .

Ōcўdrŏmē.opening: , = ὠκυδρόμη , Swiftrunner , one of Actæon's hounds, Hyg. Fab. 181 .

Ōcўdrŏmus.opening: , = ὠκύδρομος , Swiftrunner , one of Actæon's hounds, Hyg. Fab. 181 .

Ōcўpĕtē.opening: f , = ὠκυπέτη , Swift-flier , one of the Harpies, Serv. Verg. A. 3, 209 .

Ōcўpŏtē.opening: , = ὠκυπότη , Swift-flier , one of Actæon's hounds, Hyg. Fab. 181 .

Ōcyrrhŏē.opening: or , , , = Ὠκυρρόη , a daughter of Chiron , Ov. M. 2, 638 .

Ōcўthŏus.opening: , = ὠκύθοος , Swiftrunner , one of Actæon's hounds, Hyg. Fab. 181 .

ōdărĭārĭus.opening: odarium , a teacher of singing : MAGISTER ODARIARIVS, Inscr. Orell. 2634 .

ōdē.opening: or , , = ᾠδή , a song , esp. a lyric song , an ode (post-class. for carmen), Auct. Carm. Philom. 13; 25.

ōdēum.opening: , = ᾠδεῖον , a public building aesigned for musical performances , an odeon , Vitr. 5, 9 ; Suet. Dom. 5 ; cf. Eutr. 7, 24 ; Tert. Res. Carn. 42 ; Amm. 16, 10, 14 .

ōdi.opening: (old form of the pres. , odio: osi sunt ab odio, declinasse antiquos testis est C. Gracchus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 201 Müll. From this are formed: odis, Ambros. in Psa. 118, 17 ; odiant, Arn. in Psa. 37 ; odiebant, id. Psa.…

Ōdĭcē.opening: , = Ὠιδική , one of the Hours , Hyg. Fab. 183 .

ōdĭcus.opening: adj. , = ᾠδικός , of or belonging to song , odic , in prosody, Mart. Vict. p. 2501 P.

ōdīnŏlўtes.opening: ὠδινολύτης, from ὠδίς and λύω , he who or that which alleviates the pangs of childbirth (epithet of the fish called mora. Plin. 32, 1, 1, § 6 ).

Ōgўges.opening: , and , , , = Ὠγύγης, Ὤγυγος, Ὠγύγιος , the mythic founder and king of Thebes , in Bœtia , in whose reign a great deluge is said to have occurred : oppidum Thebae, quod rex Ogyges aedificarit, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 2 : ante…

Ōgўgĭa.opening: One of the seven daughters of Amphion and Niobe. Hyg. Fab. 69 .— A gate at Thebes , Hyg. Fab. 69 .— An island near Italy , in which Calypso was said to have dwelt , Plin. 3, 10, 15, § 96 .

Ōlĕăros.opening: ( ) or ( ), , , = Ὠλέαρος, Ὠλίαρος , one of the Cyclades , near Paros , now Antiparos , Mela, 2, 7, 11; Plin. 4, 12, 22, § 67 ; Verg. A. 3, 126 .—Form Oliaros, Ov. M. 7, 469 .

Ōlĕnos.opening: or , , , = Ὤλενος , an ancient city in Achaia , between Patrœ and Dymo , now Kato Akhaia , Plin. 4, 5, 6, § 13 . — A city in Ætolia , Hyg. Astr. 2, 13 ; Sen. Troad. 826 .—Hence, , , adj. , Olenian; poet. for Achaian ,…

ōlim.opening: adv. ole, olle, ollus or olus, archaic for ille, with locative ending -im, = illo tempore, v. Brix ad Plaut. Trin. 523 , lit., at that (sc. remote) time; hence, Of past time, some time ago , once upon a time , once ,…

ōmen.opening: (old form ), , omen quod ex ore primum elatum est, osmen dictum, Varr. L. L. 6, § 76 Müll.; cf.: osmen, e quo s extritum, id. ib. 7, § 97: omen velut oremen, quod fit ore augurium, quod non avibus aliove modo fit, Fest.…

ōmentātus.opening: adj. omentum , filled with omentum (post-class.): isicia omentata, Apic. 2, 1 .

ōmentum.opening: the fat-skin , adipose membrane; fat , esp. in men (post-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: ast illi tremat omento popa venter, Pers. 6, 74 .— In partic. The membrane which encloses the bowels , the caul , Cels. 4, 1 ; Plin. 11, 37,…

ōmĭnālis.opening: , a false read. for inominalem, Gell. 5, 17 fin.

ōmĭnātĭo.opening: ominor , a foreboding , prognostic , Paul. ex Fest. p. 88 Müll.

ōmĭnor.opening: v. dep. (ante-class. act. collat. form , āre: ut tibi bene sit, qui ominas, Pompon. ap. Non. 474, 11 ) [omen], to forebode , prognosticate , to augur , presage , predict , prophesy (class.; syn.: divino, auguro,…

ōmĭnōsus.opening: adj. omen , full of foreboding , portentous , ominous (post-Aug.): mons avibus obscenis ominosus, Messala ap. Gell. 13, 14, 6 : res, Plin. Ep. 3, 14, 11 . — Adv. : , ominously : ominose retentus, Ps.- Quint. Decl. 6, 5 .

ōmŏphăgĭa.opening: , = ὠμοφαγία , the eating of raw flesh (eccl. Lat.), Arn. 5, 169 .

Ōnītus.opening: , = ὠνειτός (purchased), the name of a slave , Inscr. Grut. 633, 6 .

Ōphĭăs.opening: the daughter of Ophius , Ov. M. 7, 383 .

ōpĭlĭo.opening: and , , for ovilio, from ovis , a shepherd : etiam opilio, qui pascit alienas oves, Plaut. As. 3, 1, 36 .— Form upilio, Verg. E. 10, 19 ; Col. 7, 3, 13 ; Dig. 32, 1, 60 ; Vulg. Gen. 38, 12 .— A kind of bird , otherwise…

Ōpis.opening: , = Ὦπις . A nymph in the train of Diana , Verg. A. 11, 836 ; cf. Macr. S. 5, 22 .— A Naiad , Verg. G. 4, 343 .

ōra.opening: kindred with Sanscr. avāra, ripa citerior fluminis , the extremity of a thing; the border , brim , edge , margin , end , boundary. Lit. In gen. (class.; syn.: limbus, fimbria, instita, margo): omnes avidi spectant ad…

ōrābĭlis.opening: adj. oro , exorable , Not. Tir. p. 106 .

ōrācŭlārĭus.opening: oraculum , dealing in or uttering oracles; prophetic : habuit autem oracularios servos, qui illum pessum dederunt, Petr. S. 43 .

ōrācŭlum.opening: (sync. oraclum: ex oraclo, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 21, 42 , or Trag. v. 65 Vahl.; plur , oracla, Att. ap. Non. 488, 2 , or Trag. Rel. p. 185 Rib.; Ov. M. 1, 321 ), , oro , a divine announcement , an oracle (class.). Lit.…

ōrārĭum.opening: 1. ōs , a napkin , handkerchief , Lucil. ap. Non. 539, 22 : oculum ligavit orario, Aug. Civ. Dei, 22, 8, 7.—Used in signifying applause, Vop. Aur. 48 fin.

ōrārĭus.opening: adj. 1. ora , of or belonging to the coast (post-Aug.): naves, coasting-vessels, coasters, Plin. Ep. 10, 15 (26); cf. naviculae, id. ib. 10, 28, 2 .

Ōrāta.opening: an appellation bestowed on a certain Sergius , on account of his fondness for the gilt bream (aurata, orata, v. auro, P. a. fin. ), Varr. R. R. 3, 3, 10 , Col. 8, 16, 5 ; Fest. p. 182 Müll.

ōrātim.opening: adv. 1. ora , coastwise , from coast to coast , Sol. 3 dub. (al. moratim).

ōrātĭo.opening: oro , a speaking , speech , discourse , language In gen., the connection of words to express thought : non est autem in verbo modus hic, sed in oratione, id est, in continuatione verborum, Cic. 3, 42, 167 . Speech , the…

ōrātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. oratio , a little speech , a brief oration (class.), Cic. Brut. 19, 77 ; id. Att. 13, 19, 2 ; 15, 3, 2 ; Quint. 4, 3, 17 : aureola, Cic. N. D. 3, 17, 43 .

ōrātor.opening: oro, one who speaks . A speaker , orator (very common in all periods and styles of writing): eum (oratorem) puto esse, qui et verbis ad audiendum jucundis et sententiis ad probandum accommodatis uti possit in causis…

ōrātōrĭus.opening: adj. orator . Of or belonging to an orator , oratorical (class.), Cic. de Or. 1, 54, 231 : ornamenta, id. Brut. 75, 261 : vis dicendi, id. Ac. 1, 8, 32 : ars, Quint. praef. § 17: gestus, id. 11, 3, 125 : compositio, id.…

ōrātrix.opening: id. . She that prays or beseeches , a female suppliant (rare but class.): me oratricem haud sprevisti, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 80 : pacis et foederis, * Cic. Rep. 2, 8, 14 .— A transl. of ῥητορική , rhetoric , oratory ,…

ōrātum.opening: oro , a prayer , entreaty , supplication : cum orata ejus reminiscor, Ter. Hec. 3, 3, 25 ; 4, 1, 60 .

ōrātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. and plur. ), oro , a praying , entreating; a request , entreaty (very rare but class.): oratu tuo, Cic. Fl. 37, 92 : illarum oratu, Plaut. Cas. 2, 2, 17 ; Sid. Ep. 9, 14 init. : magnis oratibus,…

ōrĕae.opening: 1. os , the bit of a bridle (ante-class.), Titin. ap. Fest. p. 182 Müll.: oreas equo detrahere, Cael. ib.

Ōrētāni.opening: , = Ὠρητανοί , the inhabitants of Oretum in Spain , Liv. 21, 11 ; Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 19 .

Ōrēus.opening: ( ), , , a city in Eubœa , formerly Histiœa , Liv. 28, 5, 18 ; 31, 40, 10 ; Plin. 4, 12, 21, § 64 .

ōrĭcilla.opening: ( ), , dim. auricula, auris , an ear-lap : mollior ... imula oricilla, Cat. 25, 2 .

Ōrĭcos.opening: or , , , or , , , = Ὠρικός and Ὠρικόν , a seaport town of Illyria Grœca , now Ericho , Caes. B. C. 3, 8 sq. ; Liv. 24, 40 ; Mel. 2, 3, 12 ; Prop. 1, 8, 20 ; Luc. 3, 187 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Oricum , the…

ōrĭdūrĭus.opening: adj. 1. os-durus , hard-mouthed , of horses: oridurius, σκληρόστομος , Gloss. Philox.

ōrĭfĭcĭum.opening: 1. os-facio , an opening , orifice (post-class.): ventris sunt duo orificia, Macr. S. 7, 4 : cistulae, App. M. 9, p. 236, 41 ; 11 , p. 262, 27.

ōrīga.opening: , an old form for auriga, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 8 ; 2, 8, 4 Schneid.

Ōrĭgĕnes.opening: , = Ὠριγένης , Origen , a famous Greek Christian writer of the early part of the third century , A.D., Hier. Ep. 100 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 17.—Hence, , , , a follower of Origen , Hier. Ep. 84, 3 ; id. ib. 3 in Rufin. 18…

Ōrīon.opening: (ŏrīōn, Verg. A. 1, 535 ; 4, 52 ), ŏnis and , , = Ὠρίων , the constellation Orion , whose rising and setting are attended by storms; acc. to the myth, a hunter transported to heaven, Ov. F. 5, 493 ; Hyg. Fab. 195 ;…

ōrĭpūtĭdus.opening: adj. 1. os-putidus , that has a stinking mouth : oriputidus, ὀζόστομος , Gloss. Philox.

Ōrīthȳīa.opening: ( ), , , = Ὠρείθυια , a female proper name. A daughter of Erechtheus , king of Athens; who became by Boreas the mother of Calaïs and Zetes , Ov. M. 6, 683 ; Verg. G. 4, 463 ; id. A. 12, 83 ; Sil. 8, 5, 16 ; Cic. Leg. 1,…

ōro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ōro.opening: (orassis for oraveris, Plaut. Ep. 5, 2, 63 ), v. a. and n. 1. os, to speak : oro ab ore, Varr. L. L. 6, § 76 Müll. In gen. (so obsol.): orare antiquos dixisse pro agere testimonio est, quod oratores dicti et causarum…

Ōrŏmĕdon.opening: , = Ὠρομέδων , one of the giants , Prop. 3, 9 (4, 8), 48.

Ōrōpus.opening: , = Ὠρωπός , a town of Bœotia , on the borders of Attica , now Oropo , Cic. Att. 12, 23, 2 ; Liv. 45, 27 ; Plin. 4, 7, 11, § 24 .

ōs.opening: (no gen. plur. ), kindr. with Sanscr. āsya, os, vultus, facies , the mouth (syn. bucca): quam tibi ex ore orationem duriter dictis dedit, Enn. ap. Non. p. 512, 8 : ex ore in ejus os inflato aquam dato palumbo, Cato, R.…

ōsor.opening: ( , Plaut. l. l. infra), , odi , a hater (ante- and post-class.): uxoris suae ossor, Plaut. As. 5, 2, 9 Fleck. (Ussing, osor): hominum, App. de Deo Socr. p. 48, 15 ; Pacat. Pan. Th. 20, 5 ; Aus. Ep. 4, 24 : mulierum,…

ōtăcustes.opening: , = ὠτακουστής , a listener , eavesdropper , spy (post-class.): otacustarum relatio, App. de Mundo, p. 69, 31.

ōtĭa.opening: , = ὠτίον (little ear), a kind of mussel , Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 149 .

ōtĭābundus.opening: adj. otior , having or enjoying leisure , keeping holiday (postclass.). Sid. Ep. 4, 18 .

ōtĭŏlum.opening: dim. otium , a little leisure : otiolum meum, my little bit of leisure , Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 3, 1 .

ōtĭor.opening: v. dep. id. , to have or enjoy leisure , to be at leisure , to keep holiday (rare but class.): cum se Syracusas otiandi, non negotiandi causā contulisset, * Cic. Off. 3, 14, 58 : domesticus otior, I idle about at home,…

ōtĭōsĭtas.opening: otiosus , leisure , idleness (late Lat.). Lit. : multam mahtiam docuit otiositas, Vulg. Ecclus. 33, 29 . — Transf. , a writing composed at leisure moments (post-class.): suas otiositates edere, the fruils of leisure,…

ōtĭōsus.opening: adj. otium , at leisure , unoccupied , disengaged , unemployed , idle (class.; cf. feriatus, immunis; opp. negotiosus). Of persons. In gen.: nimis otiosum te arbitror hominem esse, Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 34 ; 40 : quamvis…

ōtis.opening: , = ὠτίς , a species of bustard , Plin. 10, 22, 29, § 57 ; 30, 14, 45, § 131 .

ōtĭum.opening: In gen., leisure , vacant time , freedom from business (class.; opp. negotium; cf.: immunitas, vacatio): otio qui nescit uti plus negoti habet, Quam, etc., Enn. ap. Gell. 19, 10, 12 (Trag. v. 252 Vahl.): fecero;…

ōtŏpĕta.opening: , = ὠτοπετής , longear (pure Lat. auritus) poet. for hare , Petr. 35 .

ōtus.opening: , = ὦτος or ὠτός , a kind of owl , the horned owl , Plin. 10, 23, 33, § 66 .

Ōtus.opening: (also , , and ), , , the name of a giant : immanis Otos, Verg. Cul. 233 ; cf. Hyg. Fab. 28 .

ōvārĭus.opening: ovum , an egg-keeper (who took charge of the new-laid eggs), Inscr. Collect. Ferrar. Opusc. 9, p. 179.

ōvātus.opening: adj. ovum . Eggshaped , ovate (post-Aug.): aliis ovata species, Plin. 15, 21, 23, § 85 ; App. M. 10, p. 254 med. — Having ovate spots : lapis Numidicus, Plin. 35, 1, 1, § 3 .

ōvĭco.opening: v. a. ovum , to mix with the white of an egg , Plin. Val. 1, 17 .

ōvĭpărus.opening: adj. ovum-pario , that lays eggs , oviparous (post-class.): vivipari et ovipari: ita enim appello, quae Graeci ζωοτόκα, καὶ ὠοτόκα , App. Mag. p. 298, 24 : fetus, Fulg. Myth. 1, 12 ; Aus. Idyll. 10, 132 .

ōvum.opening: ὠόν, i. e. ΩϝΟΝ . Lit. , an egg : ovum parere, to lay, Cic. Ac. 2, 18, 57 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 8 : edere, Col. 8, 3, 4 : ponere, Ov. M. 8, 258 : efferre, Verg. G. 1, 379 : eniti, Col. 8, 11, 8 sq. : facere, Varr. R. R.…

Ŏăsis.opening: , = Ὄασις [orig. a Coptic word], an inhabited spot, a fertile piece of land in the Libyan desert, an oasis; esp. the great oasis in Upper Egypt, to which criminals were banished by the emperors , Cod. Just. 9, 47, 26 ;…

Ŏaxes.opening: or , , , = Ὄαξις , a river in Crete , now Axus : rapidum Cretae veniemus Oaxen, Verg. E. 1, 66 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the Oaxes; poet. for Cretan : capiens tellurem Oaxida, Varr. Atacin. ap. Serv. Verg.…

ŏb.opening: (old form , v. III.), prep. with acc. (in late Lat. also with the abl. : OB PERPETVO EIVS ERGA SE AMORE, Inscr. Orell. 106 ) [Osc. op; kindr. with Sanscr. api; Gr. ἐπί ]. Lit. With verbs of motion, towards, to (only…

ŏbăcĕro.opening: v. a. , to contradict, interrupt : obacerare obloqui atque alterius sermonem moleste impedire; quod sumptum videtur a paleis, quas Graeci ἄχυρα vocant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 187 Müll.

ŏb-aemŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. (lit. to excite to jealousy against, i. e.), to stir up, irritate, provoke (eccl. Lat.): illi obaemulati sunt me in non Deo, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 31 (a translation of Deut. 32, 21).

ŏbaerārĭus.opening: ob-aes , a debtor who must work out his debt (ante-class.): (agros colunt) ii, quos obaerarios nostri vocitārunt, Varr. R. R. 1, 17, 2 Schneid. N. cr .

ŏb-aerātus.opening: adj. id. , involved in debt, in bondage on account of debt (class.): liber, qui suas operas in servitute pro pecuniā quādam debebat, dum solveret, nexus vocatur, ut ab aere obaeratus, Varr. L. L. 7, § 105 Müll.: tenuis…

ŏb-ambŭlātĭo.opening: obambulo , a going or walking about : obambulatio hominum, Auct. Her. 3, 19, 31 .

ŏb-ambŭlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ŏb-ambŭlo.opening: v. n. and a. , to walk before or near any thing, to go past (not in Cic. or Cæs.); constr. with dat. or acc. : obambulare adversum alios ambulare, et quasi ambulanti sese opponere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 187 Müll. With dat.…

Ŏb-ărātor.opening: the god of ploughing , Fab. Pict. ap. Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 21 .

ŏb-ardesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to burn before one, to blaze out : obarsit Dryas, Stat. Th. 9, 856 .

ŏb-āresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow dry, to dry up (post-class.): membrana quam siccari et obarescere non oportet, Lact. Opif. D. 10, 3 (al. arescere).

ŏb-armo.opening: v. a. , to arm ( poet. and post-class.). Lit. : securi Dextras, Hor. C. 4, 4, 20 : clipeo filium, Aus. Epigr. 25, 1 : manus impias contra aliquem, App. M. 9 init. — Trop. : perfrictis oculis, et obarmatis ad vigilias,…

ŏb-ăro.opening: v. n. , to plough around, plough up : cum hostes obarāssent quicquid herbidi terreni extra murum erat, Liv. 23, 19, 14 .

ŏb-ātrātus.opening: adj., obscured, black, blackish : nascens luna si cornu superiore obatrato surget, pluvias decrescens dabit, Varr. ap. Plin. 18, 35, 79, § 349 Sillig. N. cr. (al. obatro).

ŏb-ātresco.opening: v. inch. n. [obatratus], to become black , Firm. Math. praef.

ŏb-audĭentĭa.opening: obaudio , obedience (eccl. Lat. for the class. oboedientia), Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 2 .

ŏb-audĭo.opening: v. a. , for oboedio, to obey (post-class.); constr. with dat. or absol. With dat. : alicui, App. M. 3, p. 136, 11 .— Absol. : Adam non obaudiit, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 2 .—With acc. : obaudite me, Vulg. Eccles. 39, 17…

ŏbaudītĭo.opening: obaudio , obedience : obauditio, ύπακοή , Gloss. Philox.

ŏbaudītus.opening: abl. , , id. , a listening : auris, Aug. Civ. Dei , 22, 29.

ŏb-aurātus.opening: adj., gilded (postclass.): socci obaurati, App. M. 11, p. 260, 34 .

ŏbēdĭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. oboedio.

ŏbēdĭenter.opening: adv. , v. oboedio, P. a. fin .

ŏb-ĕdo.opening: to eat, eat away, devour (used only in the part. perf. and P. a. ).— Trop. : nec obesa cavamine terra est, Auct. Aetn. 344 .—Hence, P. a. : , a, um. Wasted away, lean, meagre : corpore pectoreque undique obeso, Laev.…

ŏbĕliscus.opening: , = ὀβελίσκος (a small spit; hence), An obelisk : trabes ex Syenite marmore fecere reges, obeliscos vocantes Solis numini sacratos, Plin. 36, 8, 14, § 64 sq. ; cf. Amm. 17, 4, 17 ; Isid. Orig. 18, 31 ; Tac. A. 3, 60 .—…

ŏbĕlus.opening: , = ὀβελός (a spit), a critical mark shaped like a spit (†), placed opposite suspected passages in books, an obelisk (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 104 ; 108 ; 112 ; Aus. Sap. 13 prooem.; Isid. Orig. 1, 20, 2 .

ŏb-ĕo.opening: (obivi, Verg. A. 6, 801 ; Aus. Epit. 32, 4 ; Anthol. Lat. 4, 97, 1 ; contr. obit for obiit, Lucr. 3, 1042 ; Luc. 9, 189 ; Juv. 6, 559 ), ĭtum, 4 (lengthened form, obinunt obeunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 189 Müll.), v. n. and…

ŏb-ĕquĭto.opening: v. n. , to ride towards, ride up to (not ante-Aug.). With dat. : obequitando castris, Liv. 2, 45 : portis, id. 21, 54 ; 29, 34 : moenibus, Curt. 8, 10, 6 : peditibus, id. 10, 9, 16 : agmini, id. 3, 10, 4 : ordinibus,…

ŏb-erro.opening: v. n. , to wander, rove , or ramble about a place ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : oberrare tentoriis, Tac. A. 1, 65 : ignotis locis, Curt. 6, 5, 18 : mustela quae in domibus nostris oberrat, Plin. 29, 4, 16, §…

ŏbēsĭtas.opening: obesus , fatness, stoutness, corpulence, obesity (post-Aug.): et obesitas ventris, Suet. Dom. 18 ; id. Claud. 41 ; Col. 6, 24 .—Of trees: (arbores) laborant obesitate, Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 219 .

ŏbēso.opening: v. a. id. , to fatten : madefacto triticeo pane obesant avem, Col. 8, 7, 4 (al. obescant).

ŏbēsus.opening: Part. and P. a. of obedo, q. v.

ŏb-haerĕo.opening: v. n. , to stick fast to a thing: navis obhaerens vado, Suet. Tib. 2 : ne qui forte obhaereant ac resistant, Lact. Opif. D. 11 .

ŏb-haeresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to stick fast, remain stuck; in the tempp. perf., to be stuck fast, to cleave or adhere to a thing ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : aurum stirpibus obhaerescit, App. M. 6, p. 178, 19 : ubi in medio…

ŏb-herbescĕre.opening: ( to become grass ), Paul. ex Fest. p. 190 and 191 Müll.

ŏb-horrĕo.opening: v. n. , to bristle with any thing: prasii alterum genus sanguineis punctis obhorret, Plin. 37, 8, 34, § 113 dub. (Sill. abhorret).

ŏb-hŭmo.opening: v. a. , to cover with earth , Tert. Pall. 2 .

ŏb-īrascor.opening: v. dep. n. , to be angry at any thing (mostly post-Aug.; but cf. obiratio): obirascens fortunae animus, Sen. Tranq. An. 2, 11 : cum male audiunt, obirascuntur. App. Mag. p. 275, 18 ; id. Flor. 3, p. 357 .—Hence, , , P.…

ŏbīrātĭo.opening: obirascor , a becoming or being angry, anger : hujus nebulonis obiratione, Cic. Att. 6, 3, 7 dub.; v. Orell. ad loc. (B. and K., oratione).

ŏb-ĭter.opening: adv., on the way, in going or passing along (except in Laber., not anteAug.; cf. Charis. 187 P. Augustus found fault with Tiberius for using per viam instead of obiter, Charis. l. l.). Lit. : obiter leget aut scribet,…

ŏbĭtus.opening: ( gen. obiti, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 24 med. ), obeo . A going to, approaching; an approach, a visit (perhaps only ante- and post-class.; syn. adventus): obitu dicebant pro aditu, Paul. ex Fest. p. 188 Müll.: ecquis est…

ŏboedĭens.opening: P. a. , and , adv. , v. oboedio, P. a. fin .

ŏboedĭentĭa.opening: ( ), , oboediens , obedience (class.). Of persons. With gen. : servitus est oboedientia fracti animi, Cic. Par. 5, 1, 35 .— Absol. : relinquunt enim et abiciunt oboedientiam, Cic. Off. 1, 29 . 102.— Of bees: mira plebi…

ŏb-oedĭo.opening: (better than , Cic. Rep. 3, 29, 41 ; Front. Ep. ad Verr. 7 Mai.; id. Fer. Als. 3 ; cf.: oboedire, obaudire, Paul. ex Fest. p. 187 Müll. and Bramb. s. v.— Ante-class. form of the fut. , oboedibo: oboedibo tibi, Afran.…

ŏboedītĭo.opening: ( ), , oboedio , obedience (post-class.): per unius oboeditionem justi constituentur multi, Vulg. Rom. 5, 19 : ad justitiam, id. ib. 6, 16 ; Ambros. de Fug. Saec. 2, 12 fin.

ŏb-ŏlĕo.opening: v. a. , to smell of any thing (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : oboluisti allium, Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 38 : maluissem allium oboluisses, Suet. Vesp. 8 : antidotum, id. Calig. 23 : res mihi obolet. I smell a thing , App.…

ŏbŏlus.opening: , = ὀβολός . Lit. , an obol, a small Greek coin, the sixth part of a drachm , equivalent to three and a half cents Federal currency, Vitr. 3, 1 : siclus viginti obolos habet, Vulg. Exod. 30, 13 .— Transf. , as a weight,…

ŏb-ōmĭnātus.opening: Part. , from the obsol. obominor, wishing ill to one (postclass.): crurum ei fragium obominata, App. M. 9, p. 227, 36 (al. abominata).

ŏb-ŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. , to arise, appear, spring up (class.): oboritur, nascitur, nam praepositionem ob pro ad, solitam poni, testis hic versus: tantum gaudium oboriri ex tumultu maximo, Paul. ex Fest. p. 190 Müll.: tenebrae…

ŏb-orsus.opening: Part. , from the obsol. obordior, beginning : orsus, oborsus, exorsus, Not. Tir. p. 151 .

ŏb-ortus.opening: , a false read. for odores, Lucr. 4, 218 ; v. Lachm. ad h. l.

ŏb-oscŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to kiss (postAug.): quae flagellorum vestigia obosculantur (al. osculantur), Petr. 126 .

ŏbrōbŏrātĭo.opening: ob-roboro , rigidity of the nerves (post-class.), Veg. Vet. 3, 85 .

ŏb-ultrōnĕus.opening: adj. , voluntary , spontaneous : ultroneus, obultroneus, Not. Tir. p. 83 : † obultroneus, αὐθαίρετος , Gloss. Philox.

ŏbumbrācŭlum.opening: obumbro , an obscuration , darkening : aversionis, Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, § 39 .

ŏbumbrātĭo.opening: id. , a shading , darkening; trop., an obscuring (postclass.): allegoricae caecitatis obumbratio, Arn 5, 186: vicissitudinis, Vulg. Jacob. 1, 17 .

ŏbumbrātrix.opening: id. , she that shades or darkens (eccl. Lat.): arbores templi obumbratrices scelerum, Tert. Apol. 9 .

ŏb-umbro.opening: v. a. , to overshadow , to shade ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: opaco, obscuro). Lit. : gramineus madidam caespes obumbrat humum, Ov. Am. 2, 16, 10 : coma umeros obumbrat, id. M. 13, 845 : templum, id. ib. 14, 837…

ŏb-uncātus.opening: adj. , bent inward (post-class.): obuncatis unguibus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 198 .

ŏb-unctŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [obunctus]. slightly anointed , soiled : tunica obunctula, with panni fetidi, Titin. ap. Non. 536, 18 , acc. to Com. Rel. v. 138 Rib. (al., less correctly, obuncula).

ŏb-unctus.opening: Part. [ungo], anointed (post-class.): capillus guttis Arabicis, obunctus, App. M. 2, p. 118, 32 : oculi, id. ib. 8 , p. 214, 4

ŏb-uncus.opening: adj. , bent in , hooked ( poet. ): rostroque immanis vultur obunco, Verg. A. 6, 597 : pedes, Ov. M. 6, 516 : falx, Arn. 6, 197 .

ŏb-undans.opening: Part. [ob-undo], overflowing : semper obundantes hastas frangit, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 3 (Ann. v. 435 Vahl.).

ŏbundātĭo.opening: id. , an overflowing , inundation : fluminis, Flor. 4, 2, 27 dub. (Duker, abundatio.).

ŏbustus.opening: Part. [ob-uro]. Lit. , burnt around , burnt , hardened in the fire ( poet. ): hic torre armatus obusto, Verg. A. 7, 506 : sudes, id. ib. 11, 894 .— Transf. : glaeba gelu, burnt by frost. Ov. Tr. 5, 2, 66 .

Ŏcella.opening: ocellus, small-eyed , a Roman surname , Cic. Att. 10, 17, 3 ; 10, 17, 2 ; Plin. 11, 37, 55, § 150 ; Suet. Galb. 4 ; Inscr. Grut. 431, 2 .

ŏcellātus.opening: adj. ocellus , having little eyes (ante class. and post-Aug.).—Only as subst. : , , , a small stone marked with eyes or spots : altera exorat patrem libram ocellatorum ( like dice ), Varr. ap. Non. 213, 30 : ocellatis…

Ŏcellīna.opening: Ocella , a female surname : Livia Ocellina, Suet. Galb. 3 .

ŏcellŭlus.opening: dim. ocellus , a little eye , acc. to Diom. p. 313 P.

ŏcellus.opening: dim. oculus , a little eye , eyelet (mostly poet. ). Lit. : blanda quies furtim victis obrepsit ocellis, Ov. F. 3, 19 : ut in ocellis hilaritudo est! Plaut. Rud. 2, 4, 8 : turgiduli, Cat. 3, 17 : ebrii, id. 43, 11 :…

Ŏcrēsĭa.opening: ( ), , , a female slave of Tanaquil , the mother of king Servius Tullius , Ov. F. 6, 627 ; Plin. 36, 27, 70, § 204 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 7, 1 .—Form Ocrisia Arn. 5, 18 .

ŏcŭlārĭārĭus.opening: adj. ocularis , of or belonging to the eyes , eye- : FABER OCVLARIARIVS, who inserted artificial eyes (of glass, silver, etc.) in statues , Inscr. Grut. 645, 1 .

ŏcŭlāris.opening: adj. oculus , of or belonging to the eyes , eye- (post-class.): ocularis medicus, an eye-doctor, oculist, Veg. Vet. 2, 17, 2 .— Subst. : , , , a medicament for the eyes , eye-salve , Pelag. Vet. 30.— Adv. : , with the…

ŏcŭlārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the eyes , eye- : CHIRVRGVS, Inscr. Grut. 400, 7 : claritas, of the eyes, Sol. 24, 9 : aegritudo, a disease of the eyes, id. 4, 6 : ocularius medicus, an oculist, Cels. 6, 6, 8 .—As subst.…

ŏcŭlāta.opening: oculatus , a kind of fish , perh. a lamprey , Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 149 ; Cels. 2, 18, 25 .

ŏcŭlātus.opening: adj. oculus . Lit. , furnished with or having eyes , seeing (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.): pluris est oculatus testis unus quam auriti decem, an eye-witness, Plaut. Truc. 2, 6, 8 ; cf. inspectio, Arn. 2, 48 :…

ŏcŭlĕus.opening: adj. id. , full of eyes (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : Argus, Plaut. Aul. 3, 6, 19 .— Transf. , sharpsighted : oculeus totus, App. M. 2, p. 124 fin. ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 810 .

ŏcŭli-crĕpĭda.opening: , a false read. for collicrepidae, Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 14 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

ŏcŭlissĭmus.opening: adj. , a comically formed sup. , from oculus, dearest (cf. ocellus): oculissime homo, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 28 : valuistin' oculissimum ostium? id. ib. 1, 1, 17 ; cf.: oculissimum, carissimum, Plautus: oculissimum ostium…

ŏcŭlĭtus.opening: adv. oculus , as one's own eyes , i. e. most dearly : amare, Plaut. ap. Non. 147, 27 sq. ; cf.: oculitus quoque dicitur, ut funditus, penitus, quo significatur tam carum esse, quam oculum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 179 Müll.

ŏcŭlo.opening: v. a. id. . To furnish with eyes , make to see (eccl. Lat.). Lit. : pullos, Tert. Poen. 12 .— Trop. , to enlighten : homines in agnitionem veritatis oculare, Tert. Apol. 2 : caecos, Cypr. Idol. Van. 7, 6 .— To make…

ŏcŭlus.opening: (sync. oclus, Prud. στεφ . 10, 592 dub.), , kindr. with Sanscr. akshi and aksha, from the root ītsh, videre; Gr. ὄσσομαι, ὄσσε; Goth. augō; Germ. Auge; Engl. eye , an eye. Lit. : quae (natura) primum oculos membranis…

Ŏdessos.opening: or , , , = Ὀδησσός , a city of Lower Mœsia , on the Pontus Euxinus, now Varna , Mel. 2, 2 ; Plin. 4, 12, 18, § 45 .—Also written ( ), Amm. 32, 9 .

ŏdiātus.opening: adj. odium , hated , hateful : odiosus, odietas (odiatus), inodiatus, perodiatus, Not. Tir. p. 77 .

ŏdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. odi , that deserves to be hated , hateful , odious (ante- and post-class.), Poët. ap. Prisc. p. 709 P.: improbitate ita odibilis, ut, etc., Lampr. Heliog. 18 ; Ambros. Ep. 33, 1 : superbia, Vulg. Ecclus. 10, 7 :…

ŏdĭōsĭcus.opening: adj. odiosus , a comically formed word for odiosus, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 19 .

ŏdĭōsus.opening: adj. odium , hateful , odious , vexatious , offensive , unpleasant , disagreeable , annoying , troublesome , etc. (class.; syn.: invisus, offensus). Of persons: odiosus mihi es, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 28 : infestum et odiosum…

Ŏdītes.opening: The name of a Centaur , Ov. M. 12, 457 .— Another proper name , Ov. M. 5, 97 .

ŏdĭum.opening: odi (syn.: simultas, inimicitia) Lit. , hatred , grudge , illwill , animosity , enmity , aversion : odium (est) ira inveterata, Cic. Tusc. 4, 9, 21 : in odium alicujus irruere, to become hated by him, to incur his…

Ŏdŏmantes.opening: , or , , , = Οδομαντες , a people of Thrace , on the Strymon , Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 40 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Odomantes , Liv. 45, 4 .

ŏdontītis.opening: , = ὀδοντῖτις , a plant good for the toothache , tooth-wort , Plin. 27 . 12, 84, § 108.

ŏdontŏtyrannus.opening: , = ὀδοντοτύραννος (tooth tyrant), the name of an animal , Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 3, 33 .

ŏdor.opening: (old form , , etc., Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 35 ; id. Ps. 3, 2, 52 ; Sall. J. 44, 4 ), , root od-; Gr. ὄζω, ὄδωδα, ὀδμή; whence oleo, olfacio , a smell , scent , odor (class.; cf. fragrantia). Lit. In gen.: omnis odor ad…

ŏdōrābĭlis.opening: odoror , perceptible by smell , Ambros. Noë, 15, 22.

ŏdōrāmen.opening: odoro , a perfume , spice , balsam (post-class.), Macr. S. 1 praef.

ŏdōrāmentum.opening: id. , an odoriferous substance , a perfume , spice , balsam (post-Aug.), Col. 11, 2 : pretiosiora, Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 29 : STATVTA EX HS., etc., Inscr. Orell. 4413 : phialae plenae odoramentorum, Vulg. Apoc. 5, 8 .

ŏdōrārĭus.opening: adj [odor], of or for perfuming (post-Aug.): odoraria myrrha, Plin. 12, 16, 35, § 70 : MAGISTER, a vender or preparer of spices , Inscr. Rhein. cl. 11, n. 81; cf.: odorarius, ἀρωματοπώλης , Gloss. Phil.

ŏdōrātĭo.opening: odoror . Lit. , a smelling , smell (very rare): qualis est haec aurium delectatio, tales sunt oculorum et tactionum et odorationum et saporum, Cic. Tusc. 4, 9, 20 .— Transf. , the smell , the sense of smelling :…

ŏdōrātīvus.opening: adj. odoro , fragrant , odoriferous (post-class.): semen, App. Herb. 79 .

ŏdōrātus.opening: odoror , a smelling , smell. Lit. (class.), eorum jucundus non gustatus solum. sed odoratus etiam, et spectatus, Cic. N. D. 2, 63, 158 .— Transf. The sense of smell : nihil necesse est de gustatu et odoratu loqui, Cic.…

ŏdōrĭfer.opening: adj. odor-fero , bringing or spreading odors , fragrant , odoriferous ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : panacea, Verg. A. 12, 419 : flores, Sil. 16, 309 .— Producing perfumes or spices : gens odorifera, i. e.…

ŏdōrĭfĭcātus.opening: adj. odor-facio , made to emit pleasant odor , Ambros. Ep. 8, 64 .

ŏdōrĭsĕquus.opening: adj. odor-sequor , that follows the scent (of a trail): canes, Liv. Andron. ap. Ter. Metr, p. 2426 P.; cf. Serv. Verg. A. 4, 132 .

ŏdōro.opening: v. a. odor , to give a smell or fragrance to , to perfume a thing ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: oleo, fragro): odorant aëra fumis, Ov. M. 15, 734 : mella, Col. 9, 4, 4 : caelum sulfure, Avien. Arat. 1430 .—Hence,…

ŏdōror.opening: v. dep. id. , to smell at , examine by smelling (cf. olfacio). Lit. : pallam, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 55 .— Transf. , to smell out , detect by the scent; to scent : ibo odorans, quasi canis venaticus, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 113 :…

ŏdōrus.opening: adj. id. , emitting a scent or odor , odorous (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose for odoratus). Lit. Sweet-smelling , fragrant : flos, Ov. M. 9, 87 : arbor, i. e. myrrha, id. A. A. 1, 287 : res, Varr. L. L. 6, § 83…

Ŏdyssēa.opening: , = Ὀδυσσεία . The Odyssey of Homer , Ov. Tr. 2, 375 .—Gr. acc. Odyssian, Varr. Sat. Men. 11, 14 ; Petr. 29, 4 .— A poem of Livius Andronicus , Cic. Brut. 18, 71 ; Gell. 3, 16, 11 .— ( Ὀδυσσεία ἄκρα , Ptol.), a…

ŏfella.opening: dim. offa , a bite , bit , mouthful , morsel (post-Aug.). Lit. , Juv. 11, 142 ; Mart. 10, 48, 15 ; 14, 221, 1 ; Prud. στεφ . 10, 383.— Transf. , a little piece or bit , Ser. Samm. 46, 840 .

ŏhē.opening: interj. , ho! holloa! soho! ho there! ohe, inquam, si quid audis, Plaut. As. 2, 3, 4 : ohe, Jam satis est, id. Stich. 5, 4, 52 ; Hor. S. 1, 5, 12 ; id. ib. 2, 5, 96 ; so Mart. 4, 91, 1 and 9.

ŏho.opening: interj. , an exclamation of surprise or joy, oho! aha! oho, amabo, quid illuc non properas? Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 51 ; id. Ps. 4, 2, 32 (dub. in both passages; al. ohe).

Ŏīleus.opening: ( ), (ēī) and , , = Ὀϊλευς . A king of Locris , father of the Ajax who violated Cassandra , and who was called , from his parentage , Ajax Oilei (to distinguish him from Ajax Telamonius), Cic. Tusc. 3, 29, 71 : nec mihi…

ŏlax.opening: adj. oleo , smelling , having a smell , odorous (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 1, § 82 .

ŏlĕa.opening: ( dat. plur. oleabus, Gell. ap. Charis. 1, 40 ), = ἐλαία . Lit. , an olive , olive-berry : olea ab elaea, Varr. L. L. 5, § 108 Müll.: oleas caducas, et albas condire, Cato, R. R. 58 : oleam cogere, legere, stringere,…

ŏlĕācĕus.opening: adj. oleum , of the olive-tree; hence, like oil , oily (Plinian): liquor, Plin. 35, 15, 51, § 179 (al. oleique): folia oleacea (al. folia violae), id. 21, 4, 10, § 18 .

ŏlĕāgĭnĕus.opening: , and , , adj. olea . Of or belonging to the olive-tree (for the class. olearius): oleagineum seminarium, Cato, R. R. 48 : radix, Verg. G. 2, 31 : virgulae, Nep. Thras. 4, 1 : oleagineis coronis ministri triumphantium…

ŏlĕāmen.opening: , and , , oleum , an oil-ointment , Scrib. Comp. 222 ; 269 .

ŏlĕāris.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to oil , oil- : oleares cotes, i. e. which are moistened with oil, oil-stones, Plin. 34, 14, 41, § 146 .

ŏlĕārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to oil , oil- (class.): cella vinaria, olearia, Cato, R. R. 3 ; Cic. Sen. 16, 56 : dolia, Plin. 15, 8, 8, § 33 : mercatores, Dig. 50, 4, 5 .— Subst. : , , , an oilgrinder or oil-seller : in…

ŏlĕastellus.opening: dim. oleaster , a Calabrian species of olive-tree , Col. 12, 49, 3 .

ŏlĕaster.opening: olea , the wild olivetree , oleaster : oleaster, ἀγριελαία , Gloss. Philox.; Verg. G. 2, 182 ; 314 ; Ov. M. 14, 525 ; Plin. 17, 18, 30, § 129 ; 16, 44, 89, § 240 ; 15, 4, 5, § 19 ; Vulg. Rom. 11, 17 and 24.

ŏlĕātus.opening: adj. oleum , moistened with oil , put up in oil (post-class.): pultes oleatae, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 208 ; Vulg. Num. 11, 8 .

ŏlĕĭtas.opening: olea , the olive-gathering , olive-harvest (ante- and post-class.): ubi vindemia et oleitas facta erit, Cato, R. R. 68 ; id. ib. 144 ; Minuc. Fel. 17, 9; Mamert. Grat. Act. 22 .

ŏlens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from oleo.

ŏlentĭa.opening: oleo , a smell , scent (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 22 .

ŏlentĭca.opening: id. , stinking places , Paul. ex Fest. p. 192 Müll.

ŏlentĭcētum.opening: id. , a stinking place , a dungheap , in trop. signif. (postclass.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 9 : olenticeta et fetutina, App. Mag. p. 278, 7 .

ŏlĕo.opening: root al-; Sanscr. ar-, to rise; cf.: indoles, almus, alumnus. etc. , to increase , grow , found only in the compounds: adoleo, aboleo, etc.

ŏlĕŏmella.opening: oleum-mel , a fruittree peculiar to Syria , Isid. Orig. 17, 7, 11 .

ŏlĕŏsĕlīnum.opening: oleum-selinon , a plant resembling parsley , Isid. Orig. 17, 11, 3 .

ŏlĕōsus.opening: adj. oleum , oily , full of oil (Plin.): semen, Plin. 27, 12, 81, § 106 : butyrum, id. 28, 9, 35, § 134 .

ŏlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [2. oleo], to grow : suboles ab olescendo, id est crescendo dictae, Paul. ex. Fest. p. 309 Müll.

ŏlēto.opening: v. a. 2. oletum , to foul , defile , Front. Aquaed. 97 .

ŏlētum.opening: oleo , filth , dirt , excrement (very rare): oletum, stercus humanum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 203 Müll.: veto quisquam faxit oletum, Pers. 1, 112 .

ŏlĕum.opening: , = ἔλαιον , oil , olive-oil. Lit. , Cato, R. R. 64 sq. ; Varr. R. R. 1, 55 ; Col. 12, 50 ; Plin. 15, 6, 6, § 21 ; Lex. Thor. lin. 95 Rudorff. p. 191: instillare oleum lumini, Cic. Sen. 11, 36 : juventus Nudatos umeros…

ŏlĭdus.opening: adj. oleo , smelling , emitting a smell (mostly post-Aug.): vasa picata bene olida, Col. 12, 17 : bene olidae amphorae, id. 12, 38, 4 .—Of a bad smell, stinking , rank : olida capra, Hor. Ep. 1, 5, 29 : praesaepia, Juv.…

ŏlĭgochrŏnĭus.opening: adj. , = ὀλιγοχρόνιος , lasting but a short time , shortlived (post-class.), Firm. Math. 3, 5.
